Honest-ish narrative review: sample size correctly "not reported" and core mechanisms (BDNF/Abeta/IL-6/TNF-a/CRP/CBF) supported; fixed fabricated "30-40%" (real ~45% HR 0.55), removed "exceeding pharmacological" editorial, corrected "meta-analysis"->narrative and registry year 2024->2020/journal/design. FLAG: spurious supporting_paper in consensus VF-02/05/06/12/16 (same over-aggregation) - pending removal.

P-252 corrected 2026-06-26 vs PMID 40902673 (Kong 2025, network meta-analysis); fabricated summary invented study count (real 34/3655), a pooled SMD ~0.4-0.6, and the WRONG winning modality (claimed aerobic/combined best for depression "equivalent to pharmacotherapy"; real: RESISTANCE exercise best for NPS SMD -1.70, finger exercise best for ADL); summary+registry fixed. Consensus: NOT in any VF after re-derivation (clean).

P-253 corrected earlier 2026-06-26 vs PMID 41271116 (He 2025, Ageing Res Rev 2026;114:102951) and RE-CONFIRMED by source abstract this session; real 21 RCTs / pooled SMD 0.52 (0.36-0.68) global cognition + 8 success factors; fabricated per-modality SMDs and trained-vs-untrained transfer removed; IA-NEW-14 rejected; summary+registry already fixed.

P-254 corrected 2026-06-26 vs PMID 40894810 (Stephenson 2025, Front Aging). SEVERE fabrication: prior summary invented a human 3-arm RCT in older adults 60-80 with MCI (N=60); real paper is an ANIMAL study (C57BL/6J mice, 17-mo male) with NO significant cognitive effect (HIIT +28% treadmill, null cognition, negligible body comp). Summary rewritten + registry flagged out-of-scope (non-MCI). SCOPE: not a human MCI study - candidate to mark OUT OF SCOPE / drop from corpus. 8 gap candidates (G-CAND-03/07/17/19/20/21/22/23) cite it and were derived from fabricated text - need review.

P-255 corrected 2026-06-26 vs PMID 41688245 (Pedersen 2026, RECOGNISED, Prim Care Diabetes). In-scope human study; fabricated summary invented OCTA/vessel-density/brain-MRI/inflammatory substudies and self-contradictory N (20 vs 100-150). Real: color fundus photography, 307 T2D (578 eyes; 182 MCI), lower arteriolar TORTUOSITY assoc w/ MCI (OR 1.44), AUC 0.73. summary+registry fixed. DOWNSTREAM: complementary CF-61 and CF-128 cite P-255 (built on fabricated vessel-density) - need review.

P-256 corrected 2026-06-26 vs PMID 24945691 (Steinmo 2014, Prev Med, Whitehall II). Fabricated as 16-study/30724-participant meta-analysis with invented prevalence+effect sizes; real = single prospective cohort (N=6909) on bidirectional mental-health<->physical-activity association (beta=0.17). SCOPE: NOT about MCI/cognition - candidate to mark OUT OF SCOPE. summary+registry fixed. Downstream: gaps G-CAND-03/19/22/23/24 + comp_candidates CF-cand-18/19 cite it (from fabricated text) - need review.

P-257 corrected 2026-06-26 vs DOI 10.1016/j.mhpa.2024.100637 (Saeed 2024, NCT04959383). In-scope MCI RCT; fabricated summary invented a 3-arm adaptive-vs-fixed-vs-usual-care design (N~60) and INVERTED the result (claimed adaptive significantly > fixed). Real = 4-arm fixed-difficulty (mild/moderate/high) vs Wii-Fit control, N=97; NO significant difference between difficulty levels (all > control; high-difficulty best on MCID). summary+registry fixed. Downstream: gaps G-CAND-03/19/20/21/22/23/24 + comp_candidates CF-cand-13/20/21 (from fabricated text) - need review.

gaps.gap_statement: No predictive model distinguishes durable MCI-to-normal (NC) reversion from transient/unstable reversion. P-217 (multistate Markov, NACC) shows post-reversion patients frequently re-transition, yet reversion-prediction models (e.g. P-24 nomogram, C-index 0.81) treat reversion as a stable binary 2-year outcome and do not forecast whether a reversion will persist.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Critic-verified: P-217 documents bidirectional/recurrent post-reversion dynamics descriptively (Markov intensities) but builds no durability predictor; P-24 and P-346 model reversion as a single binary/clustered outcome. No corpus paper predicts reversion DURABILITY (transient vs sustained). Actor/Critic in-session pass 2026-06-26.
gaps.closure_criteria: A model that, among MCI patients who revert to NC, forecasts whether the reversion is sustained vs transient (re-transition within a defined horizon), validated on a longitudinal cohort with post-reversion follow-up.
gaps.actor_note: Deep gap from tension between P-24 (binary reversion) and P-217 (reversion is unstable). Awaiting human G5.
gaps.human_evaluation_note: Human G5 (2026-06-26): REJECTED - DATA_SCARCITY. Reversion is understudied because pre-reversion longitudinal data barely exists (patients present after MCI onset), not an actionable gap.

gaps.gap_statement: MCI-to-NC reversion (T5) is predicted only from clinical/neuropsychological/MRI features (P-24, P-217, P-346); no electrophysiology (EEG/ERP/MEG), molecular/fluid, or ocular/retinal biomarker study builds a reversion predictor, despite P-144 reporting ERP signatures of compensatory neural mechanisms that plausibly track reversion.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Critic-verified against full corpus: of 13 papers mentioning reversion, only P-24 (C1), P-217 (C5), P-346 (C5) model it as task T5; the Electrophysiology/Molecular/Ocular x T5 cells are empty (coverage matrix). P-144 (EEG/ERP) reports neural compensation but is correlational (T4), not a reversion predictor. Distinct from NEW-G-20 (digital/behavioral reversion). Actor/Critic in-session pass 2026-06-26.
gaps.closure_criteria: A primary study using >=1 electrophysiology (EEG/ERP/MEG), molecular/fluid, or ocular/retinal channel to predict MCI-to-NC reversion on a longitudinal cohort, reporting reversion performance (AUC/C-index) separately from conversion.
gaps.actor_note: Mechanism-proximal reversion biomarkers absent. Awaiting human G5.
gaps.human_evaluation_note: Human G5 (2026-06-26): REJECTED - DATA_SCARCITY. Same: reversion-across-modalities needs data that inherently does not exist.

gaps.gap_statement: All molecular MCI studies profile omics at a SINGLE baseline timepoint; none model serial/repeated multi-omics sampling to capture molecular progression (or reversion) trajectories.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Critic-verified: every C3 molecular study uses baseline omics. P-68 pairs LONGITUDINAL sMRI with BASELINE-only methylation; P-351 has longitudinal clinical follow-up but baseline transcriptomics; P-280 uses baseline methylation with progression labels. No study collects repeated molecular profiles per participant over time. Connects to the empty Molecular x T5 (reversion) cell. Actor/Critic in-session pass 2026-06-26.
gaps.closure_criteria: A study collecting repeated molecular profiles (>=2 timepoints) per MCI participant and modelling the molecular trajectory for progression or reversion, reporting trajectory-based prediction performance.

gaps.gap_statement: No study fuses retinal imaging (OCT/OCTA) with central neuroimaging (MRI/PET) in a single ML model to test whether the retinal channel adds INCREMENTAL predictive value over neuroimaging alone for MCI.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Critic-verified full corpus: all 7 retinal papers (P-163/247/5/255/363 etc.) are retina-only. P-224 COMPARES corneal CCM vs MRI head-to-head ('versus') for MCI-to-dementia but does not fuse them or report incremental value. No corpus paper builds a retina+MRI/PET fusion model. Distinct from NEW-G-29 (temporal decoupling of peripheral vs central pathways). Actor/Critic in-session pass 2026-06-26.
gaps.closure_criteria: A single ML model fusing retinal imaging with MRI and/or PET on the same MCI cohort, reporting the incremental predictive value (e.g. delta-AUC with CI, or likelihood-ratio test) of the retinal channel over neuroimaging-only baselines.
gaps.actor_note: Retinal incremental value over central imaging untested. Awaiting human G5.

So do NOT claim 'every classifier is single-language'; the gap survives ONLY as the precise CONJUNCTION (zero-shot + AUROC>0.80 + 3+ families simultaneously), which no single published model meets. Note the closure metric (AUROC>0.80) is slightly artificial since TAUKADIAL/zero-shot work report UAR/F1. Corpus-scoped: all corpus speech-MCI classifiers are single-language. No study reports zero-shot cross-lingual transfer of MCI speech biomarkers across typologically distinct language families (e.g., Indo-European + Sino-Tibetan).

gaps.gap_statement: No published mathematical evidence in the dementia literature demonstrates that peripheral neurodegeneration maps a distinct, non-central prodromal pathway that precedes central amyloid/tau marker changes by years, nor do prognostic models account for the temporal lag and decoupling between peripheral microvascular pathways and central amyloidosis.

gaps.gap_statement: ML architectures for MCI classification force continuous, interval-censored multi-visit clinical trial data into artificial discrete cross-sectional binary labels, discarding longitudinal trajectory information and introducing label noise.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Verified corpus-wide absence. The majority of supervised ML classifiers in the corpus binarise longitudinal visit data (MCI vs. CN or MCI vs. AD) at a single time point. No study in the corpus explicitly addresses the label-noise or information-loss introduced by collapsing interval-censored multi-visit trajectories into cross-sectional binary targets, nor proposes a continuous-time or trajectory-aware objective as a solution.

gaps.gap_statement: EEG amyloid-positivity screening: multiple SINGLE-SITE studies exist (AUC ~0.85) but ZERO independent multi-site / external replication. Field note: even the largest (Kim 2023, 4-center-pooled, N=311) validates only on a random held-out split of its own cohort; blood/CSF amyloid predictors HAVE cross-cohort validation, EEG has not. The 'only one paper' framing is corpus-scoped, not field-level.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: FIELD-CHECK 2026-06-30: the 'only one study' framing is CORPUS-scoped - the field has several single-site EEG->amyloid studies (Kim NH 2023 Sci Rep N=311; Hata 2025; P-98=Kong). The clause that HOLDS at field level is the REPLICATION clause: no EEG->amyloid model has been independently replicated/externally validated across sites. Demo the replication gap, not 'only one study'. CORPUS: P-98 is the only paper using EEG to screen for Aβ-positive MCI without PET (AUC 0.85, N=28 Aβ+). Its limitation explicitly states 'cross-site EEG standardization not addressed.' P-368 (N=21, gamma connectivity) and P-157 (EEG network abnormalities) do not test amyloid status as an endpoint. No paper combines EEG screening with plasma GFAP/NfL for two-stage triage before PET referral.

gaps.gap_statement: MCI-to-AD conversion ML studies use self-selected ADNI subsets and report their single best-performing configuration (selective outcome reporting), with no pre-registered protocol, fixed public held-out test split, or mandated simple baseline - so cross-study comparisons and complex-model superiority claims cannot be trusted as unbiased.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Internal: P-274 (DL AUC 0.84 < clinical 0.85) and P-309 (RSF/XGBoost not better than Cox, N=3674) show complex-model gains evaporate against simple baselines. External web-check (June 2026): systematic reviews flag ADNI-subset optimism bias and selective outcome reporting (single best model reported), CORRECTED 2026-06-30: public held-out AD benchmarks DO exist - TADPOLE (tadpole.grand-challenge.org; locked post-deadline ADNI-3 D4 evaluation set; forecast target INCLUDES CN/MCI/AD diagnosis conversion, best MAUC 0.931) and CADDementia (hidden test set, but CN/MCI/AD classification, not conversion). The earlier 'no such benchmark exists' claim was a FIELD-OVERCLAIM. The gap nonetheless survives in narrowed form: (a) no corpus MCI-to-AD paper ADOPTS either as a competition (TADPOLE appears only as an ADNI-derived feature source in P-156/P-196), and (b) neither benchmark MANDATES a simple clinical/region-based baseline that all models must beat - the specific infrastructure this gap requires. Actor/Critic in-session pass 2026-06-26.

(TADPOLE exists but does NOT mandate a simple-baseline gate; CADDementia is classification, not conversion - neither closes this.)

Kept current_status=open because (a) the corpus adopts no shared conversion benchmark and (b) no conversion benchmark mandates a simple-baseline gate. Demo strictly as those two narrowed points, NOT as 'no benchmark exists'.

gaps.gap_statement: MCI/AD neuroimaging markers (functional-connectome graph metrics, lobar WMH, cortical thickness) are derived after registration to a single standard brain template (usually the Caucasian MNI152), yet brain morphology differs systematically by ancestry; no study validates whether these regional markers are concordant across population/ancestry-specific templates or a template-invariant pipeline, so reported regional effects may be partly registration-bias artefacts that do not generalise across populations.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-409 shows that using a Chinese-specific template (Chinese2020) instead of MNI152 changes the graph-metric findings in AD/MCI, demonstrating template/ancestry sensitivity. No corpus paper re-derives the same MCI imaging marker across two ancestry-specific templates to show invariance. Distinct from the existing generic external-validation/cross-site gaps, which concern site/scanner harmonisation rather than template-registration ancestry bias.

gaps.closure_criteria: A study that re-derives at least one MCI/AD regional neuroimaging marker (graph metric, lobar WMH, or cortical thickness) using >=2 ancestry-specific templates (or a template-invariant pipeline) and demonstrates concordant regional effect direction and magnitude across templates.

gaps.human_evaluation_note: G5 (human-eval 2026-06-27): ACCEPTED as open candidate gap. Specific, physiologically grounded (ancestry brain-morphology differences -> registration bias), non-combinatorial, distinct from generic cross-site gaps. Kept tier=candidate pending a closing study.
gaps.g5_operator_verdict_2026_08_15: ACCEPT as open candidate gap. Well-scoped and physiologically grounded (P-409: template choice changes graph-metric findings); closure criteria specific and measurable (re-derive a marker across >=2 ancestry-specific templates, demonstrate concordance); cleanly distinct from cross-site/scanner harmonisation gaps. No rescope needed.

second_reader_2026_09_15.note: P-193 block (Marmarelis et al. 2021, Frontiers in Physiology, title-consistent) states "### Potential gaps or limitations: Sample size and model-form assumptions limit immediate clinical generalization" verbatim, with N=48 (36 aMCI/12 NC), Laguerre linear dynamic modeling, and "What can be improved: Larger cohorts with external replication; Nonlinear model extensions and mechanistic validation; Integration with imaging/clinical progression endpoints"; registry row confirms modality Cerebral hemodynamics, T1, V2, N=48. As written the statement is a restated single-study limitation with boilerplate closure criteria and empty gap_type, trivially true of any n=48 study rather than an absence; it is open only in the narrower form: no external replication in a larger cohort, no nonlinear-model evaluation, and no longitudinal progression-endpoint linkage of NIRS-derived dynamic cortical-oxygenation (CTO-EtCO2/ABP/CBFV) physio-markers for MCI detection. gaps.gap_statement: Non-invasive neuromodulation for MCI (tDCS/tACS/rTMS/tPBM) is repeatedly shown to require anatomical individualisation, yet within this corpus no controlled head-to-head trial compares MRI/anatomy-individualised dosing against standardised dosing on a cognitive endpoint in MCI.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Multiple corpus papers converge on the inadequacy of fixed parameters but stop at simulation or uncontrolled designs: P-449 shows reduced DLPFC gyrification in MCI converters lowers the MODELLED tDCS E-field (no behavioural outcome); P-458 shows MRI-personalised tACS reaches significantly higher target E-field than standardised montages in MCI brains but NOT in healthy brains (simulation only, no cognitive endpoint); P-496 reports optimal tPBM frequency depends on MCI phenotype (uncontrolled, no N/stats reported); P-520 meta-analysis finds multi-site bilateral high-frequency rTMS superior to single-site; P-541 shows dual-target rTMS improves memory a single-target protocol did not. None randomises individualised-vs-standard dosing against a validated cognitive outcome.
gaps.closure_criteria: A controlled trial in MCI randomising MRI/anatomy-individualised neuromodulation dosing (electrode montage or target/E-field optimisation) versus a standardised protocol, with a validated cognitive measure as primary endpoint, reporting the between-arm effect-size difference.
gaps.actor_note: Cross-paper gap synthesised from P-380+ finding-cards; source-verified.
gaps.human_evaluation_note: G5-confirmed genuine open gap (adversarial, 2026-07-29): P-449/458/496/520/541 all grounded and stop short (P-458 nearest: individualised-vs-standard on simulated E-field only, no cognitive endpoint); no corpus closer; gap_statement tightened to corpus-relative.

gaps.gap_statement: Functional hyperactivation/hyperconnectivity in MCI is routinely labelled 'compensatory', but no corpus study tests longitudinally whether the MAGNITUDE of that compensation predicts slower versus faster outcome - i.e. whether it is adaptive (protective) or a failing/maladaptive marker.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Corpus papers report compensatory functional increases but none links the increase to outcome: P-497 (2-year spectral-DCM, longitudinal - increased left rostral LC-to-parahippocampal effective connectivity, but explicitly does not link connectivity change to conversion outcome), P-561 (lengthened hippocampal intrinsic neural timescale despite atrophy), P-571 (enhanced right-PFC fNIRS subnetwork), P-144 (non-monotonic ERP rebound in MCI vs SCD), P-440 (increased-ALFF regions). Whether a given design is cross-sectional or longitudinal, none tests whether baseline compensatory magnitude predicts conversion vs reversion; the adaptive-vs-maladaptive question is unresolved.
gaps.closure_criteria: A longitudinal MCI study that quantifies a compensatory hyperactivation/hyperconnectivity marker at baseline and reports its association (HR or AUC) with subsequent conversion vs reversion, explicitly distinguishing protective compensation (predicts non-conversion) from maladaptive compensation (predicts conversion).
gaps.actor_note: Cross-paper gap synthesised from P-380+ finding-cards; source-verified.

gaps.gap_statement: Functional/microstructural markers are shown to detect MCI while volumetric atrophy is still absent, yet no study within this corpus quantifies the temporal LEAD-TIME (in years) by which these markers precede detectable volume loss in the same longitudinal cohort.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Most corpus evidence is cross-sectional 'detects when volume preserved' (P-518 fronto-temporal decoupling separates mdaMCI where hippocampal subvolume/thickness do not; P-432 MTL T2 heterogeneity predicts decline where absolute T2 did not; P-478 hippocampal viscoelasticity detects aMCI with preserved volume; P-560 sulcal width detectable earlier than cortical thinning). P-531 comes CLOSEST - a longitudinal 2-year ASL study acquiring both a functional marker (CBF) and volume in one cohort and finding prefrontal volume change did not correlate with CBF change - but it still reports NO lead-time in years. No study estimates the years by which a functional/microstructural change precedes detectable volume loss.
gaps.closure_criteria: A longitudinal single-cohort study acquiring both a functional/microstructural marker (perfusion, viscoelasticity, T2 heterogeneity, connectivity) and volumetric atrophy at >=2 timepoints, reporting the quantified lead-time (years) by which the functional/microstructural change precedes detectable volume loss.

gaps.gap_statement: EEG/MEG network- and connectivity-based MCI discrimination is reported almost entirely on single-site, small-N cohorts (mostly group-difference studies, few actual classifiers); the cross-site external validity of these network biomarkers (train one site, test an independent site/scanner/montage) is not quantified anywhere in this corpus for models built on network/connectivity/graph features (raw-signal end-to-end CNNs such as MNet/P-62 do perform cross-site EEG validation, but target overt dementia and report MCI only as an exploratory by-product; P-596 externally validates a connectivity-containing resting-EEG biomarker on two independent cohorts, but for prediction of later decline from subjective impairment rather than MCI discrimination, and reports no cross-site performance drop; P-39 replicates network metrics across one MEG and two EEG cohorts without a train-on-one, test-on-another design).
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Corpus EEG/MEG discrimination studies are single-site and small, and most are group-difference/correlation rather than validated classifiers: P-553 (N=25, network measures succeed where spectral power fails, no external test), P-447 (9 PD-MCI, group-level only), P-480 (single-site N=122, no classifier), P-463 (two-site group-difference only), P-499 (single-centre; explicitly reports no external/multi-site validation and notes >95% of prior EEG studies used <100 participants). Only P-501/P-499 build actual classifiers, and P-501 uses only LOO/k-fold on one population. None demonstrates train-on-site-A / test-on-independent-site-B generalisation.

gaps.closure_criteria: An EEG or MEG MCI-classification study using network/connectivity/graph features that trains on one site and externally validates on >=1 independent site (different scanner/montage/population), reporting held-out AUC and the cross-site performance drop.

gaps.gap_statement: Predictive signals dissociable from amyloid are repeatedly reported, but no corpus study builds or validates a conversion-prognosis model specifically for the amyloid-negative (A-, SNAP / suspected non-Alzheimer pathophysiology) MCI subgroup, which is analysed only as a small subgroup: P-524 (ADNI, 197 CSF-confirmed MCI) reports SNAP-specific progression strata (A-T-N+ 38.5%, A-T+N+ 69.2%) with a SNAP-targeted recommendation, and P-578 reports slower progression in amyloid-negative than amyloid-positive MCI, but neither builds or validates a dedicated amyloid-negative prognostic model.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Amyloid-independent signal recurs: P-388/P-400 (posterior alpha rhythm tracks ADMCI progression outside the ATN framework), P-511 (qEEG + CSF neurogranin predict progression independent of baseline amyloid), P-525 (>60% PD-MCI are amyloid-negative with no AD-type atrophy; amyloid not the main driver), P-549 (DMN change tracks depression not amyloid, amyloid held constant), P-569 (retrosplenial hypometabolism predicts conversion even in amyloid/tau-negative cases), P-392 (perivascular-space change irrespective of amyloid status). The A-negative subgroups are small (e.g. P-569's ~46) and none assembles a PET/CSF-confirmed A-negative MCI cohort to build/validate a dedicated prognostic model.

gaps.gap_statement: Evidence that MCI biomarker-cognition mappings are modulated by BOTH sex and ancestry is accumulating, yet no study within this corpus quantifies the calibration loss, or the sex-axis discrimination loss, incurred when a sex-pooled or MNI152/Western-population-template-derived MCI biomarker model is applied to the other sex or a non-Western/non-reference-template population. On the ancestry axis P-532 applies an ADNI-trained PET+MRI radiomics Cox model to a Huashan (China) test cohort of 22 MCI participants and reports discrimination on both sides (C-index 0.766 versus 0.798, no loss observed) without any calibration assessment, so the discrimination half of the ancestry claim is partially answered and the gap now rests on calibration and on the sex axis.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Two independent demographic axes each shift the biomarker mapping: P-452 (EEG-CSF associations are sex-dependent - males theta/alpha, females beta), P-409 (an ancestry-specific Chinese2020 brain template changes connectome graph findings versus the Caucasian MNI152 template), P-392 (females carry higher white-matter perivascular-space burden), P-569 (sex-split converter analysis). All models nonetheless use sex-pooled data and/or Caucasian templates; none except P-532 (ancestry axis, discrimination only, 22-participant external cohort) trains on one population and reports transfer to the other, and none reports calibration.
gaps.closure_criteria: A study training an MCI biomarker model on one sex/ancestry and quantifying calibration and discrimination degradation when applied to the other, or building sex/ancestry-specific templates and reporting the delta-AUC versus a pooled model.
gaps.actor_note: Cross-paper gap synthesised from P-380+ finding-cards; source-verified.
gaps.human_evaluation_note: G5-confirmed genuine open gap (adversarial, 2026-07-29): P-452/409/392/569 grounded; each shows a sex/ancestry effect but none quantifies the transfer penalty; wording made corpus-relative and de-essentialised (MNI152/Western-template instead of 'Caucasian').

gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: Evidence that MCI biomarker-cognition mappings are modulated by BOTH sex and ancestry is accumulating, yet no study within this corpus quantifies the calibration/discrimination loss incurred when a sex-pooled or MNI152/Western-population-template-derived MCI biomarker model is applied to the other sex or a non-Western/non-reference-template population.

gaps.gap_statement: MCI is the condition in which self-report validity is most compromised, yet no study in this corpus quantifies measurement-source bias WITHIN the same MCI participants: self-report, informant-report and objective instruments are used interchangeably as if they estimated the same quantity, and where two sources are applied to the same people they disagree without the disagreement being analysed.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Every corpus paper that touches the question shows source-dependence but stops before measuring it within-subject. P-654 (52-study sleep-prevalence meta-analysis) finds the largest single moderator is measurement method - self-reported 49.4% (95% CI 40.4-58.4, 18 studies) versus informant-rated 23.7% (20.6-26.7, 21 studies) versus clinician-administered 33.8% (24.3-43.2, 5 studies), df=2, Q=30.173, p<0.001 - a better than twofold spread for one condition; it also reports subjective 35.8% versus objective 46.3% (p=0.056). Critically, 3 of its included studies used BOTH subjective and objective measures and entered both arms, but P-654 never reports the within-study concordance for those 3 - it treats source as a between-study subgroup only. P-657 shows the same pattern for depression: DSM-ascertained subthreshold depression pools at 21.3% (15.0-27.6) versus 28.9% (24.7-32.2) where ascertainment was by symptom scale with no clinical assessment, and 46 of 52 studies used the latter; the authors explicitly note that instrument and cut-off variation was never itself analysed as a subgroup. P-635 shows the same skew in primary studies (self-report 22/29, polysomnography 6/29, actigraphy 7/29). P-667 is the closest empirical test and it FAILS the concordance: the same participants gave a drawing-phase object-proportion score that did NOT separate healthy older adults from MCI and a recognition-phase ROC familiarity estimate that DID (YA vs MCI p=0.001, r=0.42) - the authors state they cannot explain why the two measures of the same construct disagree. P-663 uses informant-rated empathy only, with no self-report comparison, and its pre-onset baseline is a retrospective informant recollection collected at the same visit. P-630 finds the same instrument (CogMate) tracking MMSE strongly on attention (r=0.673) and weakly on memory (r=0.256) in the same 40 patients. No paper converts any of this into a source-correction factor or reports within-subject agreement statistics.

gaps.gap_statement: MCI case status is operationalised at least four incompatible ways across this corpus (ICD-10 registry code, single screening-instrument threshold, brief composite cognitive score, consensus neuropsychological criteria), producing frequency estimates that differ by an order of magnitude in the same disease. Four studies in this corpus apply two or more definitions to the same cohort (P-955, P-986, P-1094, P-1136), and P-1136 also reports a fixed exposure-outcome estimate under each criterion (dementia HR 2.84 vs 2.72); what no study in this corpus does is carry the discordance through a prediction model refitted under each definition to quantify how much of a reported AUC or feature ranking is attributable to the ascertainment rule (the live form is ACTOR-G-033).
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: The spread is not subtle. Registry ascertainment: P-648 (UK Biobank, ICD-10 + death-registry linkage) accrues 1797 incident MCI in 126,785 people over a median 13.0 years (1.4%), and P-650 (UK Biobank, ICD-10 F06.7/G31.8/R41) accrues 3272 in 200,726 over a mean 13.1 years (1.6%) - both author-acknowledged as implausibly low. Screening-threshold ascertainment: P-644 (education-stratified MMSE plus CDRS and IADL) gives 17.3% prevalence, P-639 (MoCA-J <=25 in cardiac-rehab inpatients) gives 65.2%. Criterion-based ascertainment: P-656 (NIA-AA algorithmic classification from a full battery) gives 45.4%. Brief-composite ascertainment: P-646 (HRS word recall, serial 7s, counting backwards) - the authors state this equates MCI with memory loss and poorly captures non-amnestic and frontotemporal presentations. The two syntheses each name criterion heterogeneity as the prime suspect for near-maximal heterogeneity and neither tests it: P-654 records eight different MCI criteria across its 52 studies (Petersen, DSM-5, CDR, NIA/AA, Winblad, NCGG-FAT, European Consortium, ICD-10) with only 14/52 using CT or MRI, and reports I-squared 98.03%; P-657 records 28 Petersen and 7 Winblad against a remainder using MMSE/MoCA/CDR/ADAS-Cog/CIND, reports I-squared 98.4%, and states that six prespecified subgroup analyses failed to resolve it - but neither runs ascertainment method as the moderator. P-651 demonstrates the failure inside a single study: its stated MCI inclusion window was MMSE 24-26 with the two comparison groups requiring MMSE >=27, yet the reported CSVD-MCI mean was 27.86 +/- 2.15 and MMSE did not differ across the three groups (F 2.461, p 0.089).
gaps.closure_criteria: A study that applies >=2 MCI ascertainment definitions (e.g. registry/ICD code, screening-instrument threshold, consensus neuropsychological criteria) to the SAME participants and reports how a fixed exposure-outcome estimate (HR/OR/prevalence) moves across definitions; or a meta-regression entering MCI ascertainment method as an explicit moderator and reporting the residual heterogeneity it explains.

TOO_SPECIFIC risk LOW (corpus-wide). Note P-648 and P-650 share the UK Biobank dataset and count as ONE dataset family.

gaps.gap_statement: RESCOPED 2026-09-22. The corpus tests the depression-severity-to-MCI-risk relationship continuously only in clinically ascertained samples, and never within a biomarker-stratified or amyloid-anchored MCI cohort, so the subthreshold-severity inversion reported in amyloid-positive participants (P-645: declines carried by STD-MCI-A(+), with deterioration clearest in subthreshold rather than major depression) has no continuous or multi-stratum test against a biologically defined stratum. WHAT NO LONGER HOLDS: the record previously asserted that the assumed monotone severity-risk relation had never been tested against a continuous or multi-stratum specification anywhere in the corpus. That is false. P-26 (ADNI, 397 MCI) models GDS-15 over 36 months with group-based trajectory modelling, fits landmark Cox models from month 36 and a restricted cubic spline dose-response, and reports three ordered strata (moderate HR 2.36, high HR 3.79) plus a clear linear dose-response - meeting the original closure criteria literally, and finding the relation MONOTONE, i.e. evidence against the inversion premise rather than for it. P-791 (CHARLS) pre-specifies a spline for depressive symptoms and never reports it numerically. WHAT SURVIVES: P-26's cohort is not biomarker-stratified, so whether the inversion is real within an amyloid-positive stratum remains untested; that, and only that, is the open claim.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Where severity is stratified the gradient inverts. P-645 (Korea University Guro, 1-year follow-up, 59 completers) splits late-life-depression MCI by amyloid status AND by major (MDD) versus subthreshold (STD) depression: within the amyloid-positive arm the significant 1-year declines were carried by the SUBTHRESHOLD subgroup (word-list recall p=0.020, recognition p=0.012, recognition Z p=0.038, MMSE p=0.049), not the MDD subgroup, and the amyloid-negative MDD subgroup actually IMPROVED (word-list memory p=0.006, memory Z p=0.003, recall Z p=0.006). P-643 (same centre, cross-sectional) reproduces the direction: STD-MCI-A(+) showed the greatest functional-connectivity reduction, exceeding both MDD-MCI-A(-) and STD-MCI-A(-), and depression severity measured by K-GDS did NOT correlate with ROI volumes or FC in any of the four groups. Against this, every exposure-model study dichotomises: P-646 uses a binary high-risk CES-D cut and lists 'dichotomisation of CES-D and cognitive scores potentially hiding non-linearity' as an author-stated limitation despite holding 11 waves of continuous scores; P-647 uses GDS >= 10 and finds GDS non-predictive of 5-year conversion while its correlations with BDT and ADL are weak (|r| about 0.13); P-656 has only 6 MDE-without-PTSD cases, so its severity contrast is uninformative (PAF -0.3%, CI -1.8 to 1.5) and only the comorbid stratum reaches RR 2.31. P-657 shows the construct problem at synthesis level: pooled subthreshold-depression prevalence in MCI is 28.1%, which the authors note is comparable to reported MAJOR depression prevalence (32%), and DSM-defined versus scale-defined subgroups pool at 21.3% versus 28.9%. P-663 adds a third inversion: informant-rated Personal Distress rose in every group including preclinical SCD, and its regression retained a NEGATIVE coefficient on diagnosis (B -3.785, beta -0.463, p=0.024) once semantic and visuospatial memory were entered. No corpus study fits depression severity continuously or across >=3 ordered strata against an MCI biomarker or outcome, or formally tests non-monotonicity.
gaps.closure_criteria: In an MCI cohort with amyloid or ATN status available (ADNI would serve), fit the depressive-severity-to-progression relationship continuously (restricted cubic spline) and across >=3 ordered strata SEPARATELY within amyloid-positive and amyloid-negative participants, reporting the shape in each and a formal test of the stratum-by-severity interaction. A pooled continuous analysis (as in P-26) does not close it.

gaps.actor_note: This is a critique of how the exposure variable is constructed, not a call for more depression studies. The inversion is reported twice from one centre and left unexamined everywhere else.
gaps.nearest_miss: P-646 - 20 years, 11 HRS waves, continuous CES-D in hand, competing-risks machinery already fitted, and still dichotomised; the authors name the limitation themselves and do not act on it.
gaps.fp_risk_self_check: Not COMBINATORIAL. Not DATA_SCARCITY. RESTATEMENT risk LOW. IMPORTANT INDEPENDENCE CAVEAT: P-643 and P-645 are the same group and an overlapping Korea University Guro cohort and must be counted as ONE dataset family, so the inversion currently rests on a single centre - this is the weakest link in the record and should be the focus of G5 scrutiny.

gaps.gap_statement: Bidirectionality between MCI and its psychosocial correlates is asserted throughout this corpus from designs that are structurally incapable of separating reciprocal causation from a shared common cause: two-wave cross-lagged panels, cross-sectional dual mediation, and two independently fitted unidirectional survival models. No corpus study fits a single joint model over >=3 waves that separates within-person from between-person variance.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Each study claims reciprocity and each names the design limit that forbids it. P-624 (Shandong CHF cohort, N=288) reports T1 social frailty -> T2 MCI (effect -0.578) and T1 MCI -> T2 social frailty (effect -0.646) with good fit (RMSEA 0.068), but from exactly TWO waves six months apart with convenience sampling - a classic cross-lagged panel model over two waves cannot decompose stable between-person differences from within-person carryover. P-644 (Tianjin/Shanghai, N=1394) is CROSS-SECTIONAL and reports significant bootstrapped mediation in BOTH directions from the same data (depressive symptoms mediating sarcopenia->MMSE, indirect -0.067; sarcopenia mediating GDS->MMSE, indirect -0.006); the authors concede the two directions cannot be arbitrated with these data. P-646 is the nearest miss and the most instructive: 20 years of HRS (Waves 4-14, N=9317/9428) with Fine-Gray competing-risks machinery, reporting depression->MCI SHR 1.20 (1.08-1.34) and MCI->depression SHR 1.16 (1.01-1.33) - but the authors state plainly that two separate models were fitted rather than one containing both directional pathways, so 'true bidirectionality cannot be fully established'. P-656 is cross-sectional and states the temporal ordering of PTSD, MDE and MCI is unresolved by design. P-663 obtains its within-patient change by asking informants at a single visit to rate the patient retrospectively for the pre-symptom period, over recall intervals that differ more than twofold across groups (disease duration 7.62 vs 5.41 vs 3.00 years).

gaps.gap_statement: In the P-620..P-667 batch, healthy-ageing reference arms are omitted or non-comparable precisely in the studies whose interpretation depends on them: within-disease stage/subtype contrasts and disease-specific-population studies either drop the cognitively normal arm, or retain one that fails its own cognitive gradient (controls scoring below a patient stratum) or is supernormal (screened free of the comorbidity that defines the patient groups). Where this occurs the SIGN of the deviation from normal ageing - not merely its magnitude - is unestimable. This is not a claim that the corpus lacks healthy controls generally; many studies include them. The gap is their absence or non-comparability at exactly the point of inferential need. SCOPE: stated for that batch; elsewhere in the corpus P-566 (ADNI, 476 CN / 137 EMCI / 62 LMCI) reports stage contrasts against a CN arm that out-scores both strata, with per-stratum t and AUC values, so the general form of the claim is partially answered outside the batch (demographic matching not verified; effect sizes as t/AUC, not d).
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Omitted reference arms: P-661 compares early against late amnestic MCI on EEG theta/alpha with NO cognitively normal group, and the summary states the consequence exactly - the reader cannot tell whether the late-MCI pattern is an exaggeration, a normalisation or a reversal relative to healthy ageing; its headline effect is that late-MCI showed GREATER central theta ERS than early-MCI on Go trials (d=1.155), a direction that is uninterpretable without the reference. P-663 has no healthy control at all: SCD is the reference, and the authors themselves invoke SCD's heterogeneity (depression, anxiety, personality, physical health) to explain an anomalous Empathic Concern increase in that very group. P-660 scanned and characterised 33 cognitively normal participants and then EXCLUDED them from the predictive model without stated justification, foreclosing the test of whether the negative-network effect is specific to the predementia state. P-656 has no non-FDNY or unexposed comparison group, so its 45.4% MCI prevalence cannot be benchmarked. P-653 randomised only MCI participants to combined training while normal-cognition comparators received skills training alone, so the synergy question is unanswerable by design. Non-comparable reference arms: P-651 includes healthy controls but their MoCA (26.50 +/- 1.89) is LOWER than the CSVD-no-cognitive-impairment group's (27.31 +/- 1.06), MMSE does not differ across the three groups (F 2.461, p 0.089), and the authors concede controls may harbour latent impairment. P-666 goes the other way with a supernormal control free of ANY metabolic risk factor - 0% hypertension and 0% diabetes against 83-90% and 56-73% in the two MetS arms - so group membership is confounded with vascular and glycaemic disease by construction.

gaps.modality: Cross-modal (EEG/ERP, fMRI, diffusion MRI, clinical cohorts)

gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: Healthy-ageing reference arms are omitted or non-comparable precisely in the studies whose interpretation depends on them: within-disease stage/subtype contrasts and disease-specific-population studies either drop the cognitively normal arm, or retain one that fails its own cognitive gradient (controls scoring below a patient stratum) or is supernormal (screened free of the comorbidity that defines the patient groups). Where this occurs the SIGN of the deviation from normal ageing - not merely its magnitude - is unestimable. This is not a claim that the corpus lacks healthy controls generally; many studies include them. The gap is their absence or non-comparability at exactly the point of inferential need.

gaps.gap_statement: Across the whole P-620..P-667 batch only two discrimination figures are reported at all, both are computed in-sample from a model that already contains the dominant demographic covariates, and no study anywhere in the batch reports the INCREMENTAL discrimination (delta-AUC or delta-C-index over an age/sex/education base model) attributable to the marker it proposes. Outside the batch, P-1412 (ASPREE lipidome score, +2% over traditional risk factors plus APOE with NRI/IDI in an independent cohort), P-945 (NRI 0.246, 95% CI 0.021-0.848, for MRI over a clinical change-rate model, internal bootstrap) and P-994 (NRI/IDI with calibration on a 7:3 split) report a marker increment, though none against an age/sex/education base with a confidence interval on the delta on a held-out cohort.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-648 is the clearest case and states the problem itself: LE8 with age and sex gives AUC 87.6% (85.6-89.7) for vascular dementia and 75.3% (74.1-76.4) for MCI, but the AUCs were computed in-sample within a single UK Biobank cohort with no data splitting and no external cohort, on a model that already contains age and sex - so the discrimination attributable to LE8 itself is unestablished, and the authors call for external evaluation. P-647 reports AUC 0.798 (0.701-0.895) for baseline MoCA predicting MCI-to-dementia conversion, computed in-sample with no splitting, on 321 of 1014 patients after 68% attrition that the authors believe removed decliners. P-660 reports the only other quantitative prediction: connectome-based predictive modelling gives r=0.218 with permutation p=0.045 under leave-one-out on 53 patients, with no held-out partition, no confidence interval, no error metric, and the confirmatory 10-fold and leave-one-group-out values asserted but never printed; age, gender, education and grey-matter volume were regressed out at edge selection but no covariate-only comparison model is reported. The remaining marker papers report no discrimination at all: P-667 proposes boundary-extension familiarity as a clinic screening adjunct while reporting no sensitivity, specificity or AUC; P-630 proposes CogMate as a screening tool from correlation with MMSE alone (attention r=0.673, memory r=0.256) with no healthy-control group; P-627 proposes the Fluency Type Index as a conversion marker from a group difference (t 2.28, p 0.01) with no AUC. Not one record in the batch reports delta-AUC over a base model.
gaps.closure_criteria: A study reporting delta-AUC or delta-C-index with a confidence interval for the candidate marker added to a pre-specified base model of age, sex and education, evaluated on a held-out partition or an independent cohort, and accompanied by a calibration assessment (calibration slope/intercept or calibration plot).
gaps.modality: Cross-modal (clinical scores, serum, connectomics, behavioural tasks)

gaps.gap_statement: Every MCI intervention trial and synthesis in this batch reports its result as change on a cognitive rating scale with no anchor to disease course - no conversion endpoint, no functional endpoint measured beyond 30 days, and no biomarker trajectory interpreted in a direction the paper commits to - so a reported MMSE mean difference of 1.63 or a standardised mean difference of 0.57 cannot be translated into any statement about whether the disease was altered. NEAREST MISS OUTSIDE THE BATCH: P-793 (MCI RCT, n=60, computerised cognitive training) pre-specifies a biomarker direction and reports the within-trial association between cognitive change and PCC-precuneus connectivity change with a bootstrapped mediation model; its biomarker is an 8-week connectivity change with no post-intervention follow-up, so it anchors to a mechanism rather than to disease course and does not close the gap.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: The syntheses say it outright. P-655's seven extracted outcome domains (global cognition, episodic memory, working memory, processing speed, verbal fluency, activities of daily living, depressive symptoms) do not include conversion to dementia, so it cannot speak to disease modification, while reporting standardised mean differences up to 1.21 for global cognition. P-641 pools probiotics at SMD 0.57 (0.19-0.94, I-squared 87%) and lists as an open problem that whether probiotics slow decline rather than transiently improve scores is untested. P-642 reports MMSE MD 1.63 (0.69-2.62) and MoCA MD 2.84 (0.61-5.01) for serious games with no conversion or biomarker endpoint anywhere in the network. P-640 synthesises 102 RCTs, finds every intervention family showing some positive effect, and states that statistical significance does not necessarily reflect everyday or clinical benefit. The primary trials do the same. P-649 randomises 280 MCI adults for 12 months and reports full-scale IQ betas of 0.107 to 0.136 on square-root-transformed WAIS-RC scores (lower CI bound 0.006 for MCT) with no dementia-conversion endpoint - the authors list that omission themselves. P-653 reports d=0.80 for cognition and d=0.64 for functional capacity but follows participants only 30 days past training, so durability is unknown, and has no untreated arm. P-652 finds MoCA the sole outcome reaching intergroup significance (p=0.005) out of eight. P-628 is the single near-miss in the batch - a randomised double-blind trial that DOES anchor to disease course, reporting lower annualised hippocampal and entorhinal atrophy and less ventricular dilation under choline alphoscerate at 12 months - but it is a conference abstract, N=60, with MMSE as the only cognitive endpoint and no effect magnitudes, confidence intervals or p-values reported at all.
gaps.closure_criteria: An MCI intervention trial that reports its cognitive-scale effect alongside a pre-specified disease-course endpoint - conversion/reversion incidence, a functional capacity measure retained at >=6 months post-intervention, or a biomarker trajectory whose direction of benefit is pre-specified - and reports the association between the scale change and that endpoint within the trial.

gaps.gap_statement: Comparative-effectiveness claims about non-pharmacological MCI interventions in the P-620..P-667 batch rest largely on indirect evidence through a shared control node: P-642's network is star-shaped with no closed loop, so no inconsistency test is possible for it, and where a closed loop and node-splitting do exist (P-655 in this batch; P-683, P-461 and P-615 elsewhere in the corpus) transitivity is assumed or handled by a GRADE indirectness judgement rather than assessed by comparing effect-modifier distributions across comparison sets - so the treatment hierarchies these syntheses publish are unfalsifiable on the transitivity criterion as stated. Direct head-to-head randomisation of two active modalities exists in the corpus only for neuromodulation (P-617, tACS versus tDCS, n=20 crossover), outside the modality set named here.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-642 states the structural fact plainly: no direct head-to-head immersive-VR versus serious-game randomised trial existed, so the network was star-shaped with no closed loops, formal inconsistency testing was impossible, and every VR-versus-SG estimate rests on the transitivity assumption - and its own SUCRA hierarchy nonetheless ranks serious games first on all four outcomes (ADL 77.1%, GDS 83.5%, MMSE 75.4%, MoCA 96%) while every direct VR-versus-SG contrast is non-significant. P-655 is the only paper in the batch that attempts the test - it runs node-splitting and reports consistency (p>0.05 for all outcomes) - but then states that heterogeneity arising from differences in subgroups and sample sizes compromises the validity of that consistency claim, and several of its nodes rest on a single trial (CCT versus PRT versus control comes only from Singh 2014; CCT plus MED versus MED and control only from Rozzini 2007). The narrative syntheses cannot even reach that point: P-620 categorises nine MCI music-intervention studies into four intervention types and reports that type matters, with no head-to-head comparison and no pooling; P-640 contrasts pharmacological against non-pharmacological families across 102 RCTs narratively with no pooled estimate and no risk-of-bias scoring; P-631 finds that most surveyed PD-MCI trials, though marked completed, posted no results at all; P-637 finds motor-cognitive dual-task protocols un-standardised across 38 studies with no pooled accuracy; P-634 finds word-list process scores heterogeneous across 36 studies with no meta-analytic pooling.

gaps.reread_against_corrected_blocks_2026_09_: RE-READ AGAINST THE CORRECTED BLOCKS, 2026-09-14. This record is status open / gate_verified true and cited papers whose summary blocks were fabricated and have since been re-summarised from their PDF extracts (P-878, P-880, P-881, P-882, P-883). OUTCOME: THE GAP SURVIVES - no claim in this record depended on the fabricated text. Two findings. (1) WHAT THE CITATION ACTUALLY WAS: the fabricated papers appear only inside evidence_for_open_status, as mechanical candidate-relevance scores of the form 'Candidate relevance evidence from P-878 (score=..., terms=...) [requires human/LLM closure confirmation -- not auto-closed]'. These are keyword-overlap artefacts on generic English terms, never assertions about what those papers found, and the line itself records that they were not auto-closed. No evidential weight rests on them. (2) THE SCORES ARE NEVERTHELESS VOID AS COMPUTED, because the scan ran over the fabricated block text, so both the score and the term list for these five papers describe writing that no longer exists. They should be recomputed when the candidate scan is next run; nothing about this gap changes in the meantime. HAND CHECK PERFORMED: all five corrected blocks were searched, content sections only (excluding the 31 template headers, which generate false hits on 'Best AUC', 'ranking' and 'held-out'), for this gap's subject terms. RESULT for this gap (non-pharmacological comparative-effectiveness networks lacking closed loops, transitivity assumed not assessed): none of the five contains any mention of network meta-analysis, indirect comparison, transitivity or inconsistency testing, so none closes it. ONE POSITIVE FINDING THE OPERATOR SHOULD CONSIDER: the corrected P-882 is directly on this gap's territory and CORROBORATES it - it is a systematic review of non-pharmacological MCI treatment, six databases, 50 randomised trials grouped into physical activity, relaxation, music therapy and cognitive intervention, which states 'No meta-analysis was performed' and that heterogeneity made meta-analysis impossible. It therefore performs no pooling, no network and no transitivity assessment at all: another instance of the gap rather than a closer. Adding P-882 to papers_claiming_gap would strengthen the record, but adding a claimant to a gate_verified record is a curation decision and was NOT made here.
gaps.p882_added_2026_09_14: P-882 added to papers_claiming_gap on operator instruction, 2026-09-14, after its summary block was re-summarised from pdf_extract_882.txt (the previous block was fabricated and claimed a six-database PRISMA 2020 review with PROSPERO registration, 3,842 records, 4 eligible studies and invented FINGER/donepezil hazard ratios). GROUNDING, verbatim from the corrected block: 'A systematic review of non-pharmacological treatment for mild cognitive impairment (MCI) in older adults... Fifty randomised trials were included and grouped into four categories: physical activity, relaxation, music therapy and cognitive intervention. No meta-analysis was performed.'; 'Heterogeneity made meta-analysis impossible, so the authors conclude these treatments prevent, improve and control MCI symptoms but that better-designed studies are needed.'; and most directly on point, 'Comparisons are qualitative... The authors decline to compare effect sizes across categories.' WHICH CLAUSES IT SUPPORTS, AND WHICH IT DOES NOT: it supports the corpus-level clauses - a synthesis of 50 randomised trials across four intervention categories that publishes a cross-category conclusion ('prevent, improve and control MCI symptoms') while declining any quantitative comparison is a case of a comparative-effectiveness claim advanced without a licensed comparison, with no formal inconsistency test possible and transitivity never assessed. It does NOT extend the batch-scoped clause 'no network in the batch contains a closed loop', for two reasons: P-882 is out-of-batch (this record's census is manual_curation_2026-07-31_P620plus), and it contains no network at all rather than a loop-free one - a stronger form of the same absence, not an instance of it. nearest_miss is therefore unchanged: P-655 remains the only network in the batch that runs node-splitting. Closure_criteria are unaffected; P-882 satisfies neither limb. GATE NOTE: this record was gated g5_status confirmed_open on 2026-07-31 against a seven-paper evidence base. This addition post-dates that gate, so gate_verified, g5_status and g5_review_date were deliberately left untouched - the operator may wish to re-affirm the gate on the eight-paper base.
gaps.gate_reaffirmation_blocked_2026_09_14: OPERATOR ASKED FOR A GATE RE-AFFIRMATION ON THE EIGHT-PAPER BASE, 2026-09-14. NOT TAKEN - a blocking contradiction surfaced while verifying the base, and stamping a gate over it would be the exact failure the 2026-09-14 audit documented. INTEGRITY OF THE BASE IS FINE: all eight claimants exist in the registry and in summaries.md, none is a dedup stub, duplicate, suspect paper (P-113/P-117) or fabricated block, all are T6 reviews/syntheses, and P-882's addition is verbatim-grounded. THE BLOCKER IS THE GAP STATEMENT ITSELF. Two of its clauses - 'no network in the batch contains a closed loop' and 'no formal inconsistency test is possible' - are falsified by P-655, which is one of this record's own claiming papers. The P-655 block reports: 'Node-splitting indicated consistency between direct and indirect comparisons for all outcomes (p > 0.05 for each).' A node-split comparing direct against indirect estimates is only computable where the network contains at least one closed loop, so P-655 both has a loop and ran the formal inconsistency test. The record's own nearest_miss field already half-concedes this ('the only network in the batch that runs node-splitting, immediately disclaimed by its own authors on heterogeneity grounds'), so the defect is that the gap_statement generalises past its own evidence, not that the evidence was mis-read. WHAT THE REST OF THE BASE SHOWS, re-verified 2026-09-14: P-642 is the textbook support - 'the network was star-shaped with no closed loops, formal inconsistency testing was impossible, and all VR-SG estimates rest on the transitivity assumption'; P-620 'precluding pooled quantitative synthesis'; P-640, P-631, P-637 and P-634 carry no network-analysis machinery at all; P-882 'declines to compare effect sizes across categories'. So seven of eight support the gap and one refutes two of its clauses. RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE: narrow the gap_statement so it survives P-655 (a proposed wording is in the operator report for 2026-09-14 - of the cited syntheses only P-655 contains a closed loop and runs the inconsistency test, and it sets the result aside on heterogeneity grounds, while every other rests on indirect evidence or does no pooling at all), THEN re-affirm the gate on the narrowed statement. gate_verified, g5_status and g5_review_date are untouched and still carry the 2026-07-31 seven-paper gate.

gaps.gap_statement: The cognitive-experimental and electrophysiological MCI literature is structurally unpoolable: its primary studies do not report the contrast data synthesis requires, the one systematic review that attempted synthesis declined to pool for exactly that reason, and the one meta-analysis that did pool produced two incompatible answers from the same data - so no defensible effect-size estimate exists for any cognitive-experimental MCI marker in this corpus.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-658 is decisive on the reporting failure. It covers 100 ERP studies and 3922 participants and performs NO meta-analytic pooling, stating that paradigm and analytic heterogeneity plus an overall paucity of reporting of key contrast data or effect sizes substantively deter meaningful and reproducible meta-analyses within and across components. Every one of its conclusions is therefore a vote-count of study percentages - N400 amplitude differentiated AD from healthy controls in 76% of studies and MCI in 67%, against P300 amplitude 60% and 38%, P300 latency 66% and 41%, N200 latency 50% and 47%, N200 amplitude 18% and 22% - with no pooled magnitude and no confidence interval anywhere. Across all 100 studies exactly one sensitivity/specificity pair exists (0.9/0.9 for Stroop P300 latency, reported by the primary study and not pooled). It also documents why the vote-counts are untrustworthy: cells frequently at or under ten participants per group (AD mean cell 15.2, APOE 12), controls significantly younger than patients overall (F(1,71) = 9.5, p < .003), and MMSE ranges overlapping across diagnostic categories to the point of undermining the group labels - one healthy-control group at mean MMSE 24.60 against one AD group at 27.0. P-659 shows what happens when pooling is attempted anyway: with 12 studies, 14 samples, 80 effect sizes and 562 participants, the random-effects model gives MCI prospective-timing g = -0.08 (95% CI -0.23 to 0.07, p = .309, null) while the AICc-selected meta-regression fitted at age 70 with absolute error gives g = -0.41 (-0.60 to -0.21, significant) - and the authors state they cannot decide between them, tracing the discrepancy to only 3 of 5 MCI samples using the sensitive accuracy or variability measures and to a narrow MCI age band. Only one of the 12 included studies estimated its sample size from a power analysis. The primary studies in this batch reproduce the pattern: P-633 (N = 60), P-661 (N = 35), P-632 (N = 48), P-664 (N = 80), P-662 (N = 93) and P-667 (N = 106) are all single-centre, none is pre-registered, none reports a discrimination metric, and P-662 additionally lost 26 of 72 aMCI participants (36%) against 3 of 50 controls (6%) to task-completion failure - attrition that selects the more able patients and is never modelled.
gaps.closure_criteria: Either (a) a pre-registered, adequately powered primary cognitive-experimental or ERP study in MCI that reports per-group means, standard deviations and cell sizes for every contrast alongside a standardised effect size with confidence interval, or (b) an individual-participant-data meta-analysis of one ERP component or timing paradigm in MCI that resolves the random-effects versus meta-regression discrepancy and reports a single pooled effect size with heterogeneity statistics.

gaps.gap_statement: The strongest prognostic stratifier established in this batch - domain-specific MCI subtype, where the memory-plus-visuospatial subtype converts at 53.2% while memory-only shows the slowest decline in a 1020-participant cohort - is applied nowhere else in the batch: every other study either does not record subtype, records it and never analyses it against outcome, or states outright that it is too small to stratify.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-622 supplies the finding, in the best-powered cohort in the batch (ADNI, 1020 baseline-MCI participants, linear mixed-model trajectories): subtyping by relative impairment across five cognitive domains yields memory-only as most prevalent (53.4%) with the slowest MMSE and FAQ decline, against a memory-and-visuospatial subtype that is the oldest at baseline (mean 74.69 years) and converts at 53.2%, with the trajectories separating clearly on visuospatial and executive involvement. Nothing else in the batch uses it. RECORDED-BUT-UNANALYSED: P-653 randomised 92 MCI participants and reports the subtype breakdown precisely (14 amnestic, 38 multi-domain, 40 non-amnestic) but never enters subtype into any outcome model, so whether training response differs by subtype is unanswered in a trial that could have answered it; P-664 has 24 single-domain and 18 multi-domain amnestic MCI patients and reports that they did not differ on any WCST score or model parameter (Bayes factors all below 1) while self-describing that comparison as exploratory and underpowered. EXPLICITLY TOO SMALL: P-652 states that its 22 completers prevented any stratification by MCI subtype; P-659 reports that of its five MCI samples only one specified a subtype at all, one classified into four subtypes but could not analyse them owing to small n, and one merely stated an emphasis on amnestic patients. NOT RECORDED: P-640 finds that most of its 102 included RCTs did not specify which MCI subtype was studied, so the review could not differentiate either; P-665, P-647 and P-651 each list absence of subtyping as an author-stated limitation. The result is that a stratifier with a better than twofold spread in conversion risk is treated as unmeasured noise throughout the rest of the corpus era.
gaps.closure_criteria: A study that stratifies its primary analysis by domain-specific MCI subtype using P-622-compatible criteria (relative impairment across memory, visuospatial, language, processing speed and executive domains) and reports the subtype-specific effect estimate with its interaction test - either an intervention trial reporting treatment response by subtype, or a biomarker/prognostic study reporting discrimination separately for memory-only versus multi-domain-with-visuospatial subtypes.

verification.scope: Grounded at finding-card level (summaries.md), NOT against source PDFs.

gaps.actor_note: Not a call for more subtyping research - the subtyping work exists and is well powered. The gap is that the field's own best stratifier is not carried into the studies whose conclusions it would most change, including trials that already hold the subtype labels.
gaps.nearest_miss: P-653 - it has the subtype labels for all 92 MCI participants, a randomised design, cognitive and functional outcomes at three timepoints, and does not run the interaction.
gaps.fp_risk_self_check: Not COMBINATORIAL. Not DATA_SCARCITY - P-653 and P-664 already hold the labels. EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE risk MODERATE: subtype-stratified prognosis is studied outside this corpus (P-622 itself cites prior memory-only and count-based subtyping), so the record is scoped to the corpus and specifically to the non-application of subtype in downstream analyses rather than to the existence of subtyping research. Flag for external search before G5 sign-off.
gaps.human_evaluation_note: Surprisingly important. Subtype repeatedly predicts prognosis and almost nobody uses it as a modifier. A genuine missed opportunity.

gaps.gap_statement: EEG-ML MCI-detection studies report headline accuracies of 93-99.95% obtained under segment/epoch/spectrogram-image-level cross-validation that splits a single subject's autocorrelated epochs across folds (leaking subject identity), yet no study in this corpus runs the controlled comparison of identical models under segment-wise vs subject-wise CV on the SAME data to isolate the leakage-attributable inflation.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: On tiny cohorts with segment/image-level k-fold CV, accuracy is near-ceiling: P-31 reports 99.95% (kappa 0.9989) after expanding 27 subjects into 9,720 segments; P-70 (same 27-subject dataset) 95.51%/AUC 0.965 and lists subject-independent validation as unperformed future work; P-121 99.3-99.4% on N=20 spectrogram images (self-flags overfitting); P-119 98.84% (N=79). P-501 documents the pattern directly - >96% on tiny samples of 22-34 participants vs only 61.76% on a 336-participant study - and calls EEG accuracy non-reproducible. The mechanism (consecutive EEG epochs from one subject are highly autocorrelated, so epoch-level folds let a model re-identify the subject rather than detect MCI) is never quantified within a study.

gaps.closure_criteria: Take >=2 multi-subject EEG-MCI datasets (e.g. the public 27-subject set used by P-31/P-70) and train identical model families under (a) segment-wise k-fold CV and (b) subject-wise leave-one-subject-out CV, reporting the accuracy delta; aggregate across datasets to estimate a field-wide inflation factor. Fully doable on existing public data; no new cohort or second site needed.
gaps.fp_self_check: GENERIC_LIMITATION: rejected - a specific, shared, mechanistic flaw (epoch-vs-subject CV) across >=5 papers with a concrete within-data closure and demonstrated consequence, not one paper's boilerplate. EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: general EEG record-leakage is known (translational-EEG leakage papers; an AD/dementia-EEG generalizability preprint), but the MCI-scoped controlled same-data quantification is unperformed - a within-subfield practice gap doable now. DATA_SCARCITY / COMBINATORIAL: n/a.
gaps.dedup_note: Distinct from ACTOR-G-013 (EEG/MEG cross-SITE external transfer): this is an upstream WITHIN-site, within-study validation flaw, closable without a second site. Distinct from G-22 (EEG amyloid multi-site) and G-14 (probability calibration/Brier).
gaps.refinement_applied: Dropped the raw 'subject-wise validation collapses to ~70%' claim: subject-wise accuracy is high in some corpus cohorts (P-129 94.76%, P-153 93.96%), and the ~70% cases (P-12 CAUEEG N=1155 70.11%; P-62 3-site N=482 71.5%) are confounded by cohort size/site. The defensible core is the ABSENCE of the controlled segment-vs-subject CV comparison, not a fixed accuracy ceiling.

gaps.gap_statement: In this corpus, MCI-to-AD CONVERSION prognostic/survival models that report discrimination or absolute risk treat death as non-informative right-censoring rather than as a competing event, despite death being risk-factor-correlated (age, vascular burden, frailty) over their 2-8 year horizons - biasing the cumulative-incidence / absolute-risk / Brier estimands and the trial-enrichment sample-size claims these models foreground.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Every time-to-event conversion study read uses a single-event estimator with death folded into censoring: P-88 (Kaplan-Meier risk stratification, ADNI, 8-yr, 102/341 converters), P-231 (Cox PH hazard score explicitly proposed for trial enrichment, claiming ~67% reduction in required sample size), P-241 (deep survival, ADNI n=544 + NACC n=508, IBS 0.122), P-581 (Kaplan-Meier, NACC n=826). P-198 is the sharpest: a two-state (MCI<->AD) continuous-time Markov model whose state space structurally omits death. None mentions competing risks, cause-specific vs subdistribution hazards, or death as a competing event. Because death and AD conversion share risk factors, censoring-at-death is informative and standard cumulative incidence OVERESTIMATES absolute conversion probability, corrupting the DMT-triage absolute-risk and enrichment outputs.

gaps.gap_statement: rs-fMRI functional-connectivity MCI classifiers and group-difference studies do not demonstrate that their reported FC differences / accuracy survive between-group head-motion control: none reports per-group framewise-displacement equivalence AND a motion-only-features baseline AND persistence of accuracy after FD matching - despite impaired patients moving more and motion systematically deflating the long-range connectivity that is reported as the MCI signature.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-660 self-flags the omission (motion 'controlled only by a +/-3 mm/+/-3 deg exclusion rule plus 24-parameter regression, with no framewise displacement statistics or between-group motion test'). FC classifiers report high accuracy with no motion-matched test or motion-only baseline: P-523 (ADNI, multi-kernel SVM, 87.40%/AUC 0.922, no FD reporting), P-527 (ADNI, CNN+LSTM, 93.5%, only a crude FD>0.5 exclusion, no group FD comparison). P-518 reports fronto-temporal FC decoupling - exactly the long-range reduction motion produces - on imbalanced groups. Only P-561 models mean FD as a covariate (no significant effect, p>0.4) and P-521 includes motion as nuisance, showing the check is trivially doable yet absent from the classification papers. A classifier can thus achieve high accuracy by learning a motion signature rather than neural connectivity.

gaps.closure_criteria: In >=1 ADNI + >=1 non-ADNI cohort: (i) report framewise displacement per group and show MCI vs controls are motion-matched (or match by pruning/down-weighting), (ii) run a head-motion-parameters-only classifier as a baseline against the FC classifier, and (iii) show the FC group differences / accuracy persist after FD matching and stringent scrubbing. P-561 supplies the covariate-test template; no FC-classifier paper has done the classifier-baseline version.
gaps.fp_self_check: GENERIC_LIMITATION: rejected - a specific omission shared across >=10 FC papers, self-identified in-corpus (P-660), with concrete closure and mechanistic consequence. EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: motion-as-FC-confound is textbook (Power/Satterthwaite), but the specific MCI-FC-CLASSIFIER demonstration (FD-matched design or motion-only baseline) is a within-subfield practice gap, analogous to the accepted demographics-baseline gap. DATA_SCARCITY / COMBINATORIAL: n/a.

gaps.refinement_applied: Acknowledge threshold-based exclusion (P-527) and covariate modelling (P-561/P-521) exist; sharpened claim to the ABSENCE of the specific between-group-FD-equivalence test + motion-only classifier baseline + post-matching persistence, not total neglect of motion.

gaps.gap_statement: No MCI fluid-biomarker ML study quantifies analytical-platform domain shift for its CLASSIFIER - the discrimination and CALIBRATION / decision-cutpoint loss incurred when a model or fixed threshold trained on one plasma/CSF assay platform (Simoa, INNOTEST ELISA, Fujirebio LUMIPULSE CLEIA, immunomagnetic reduction, mass-spec, NMR) is applied to another - despite corpus studies of the SAME analytes using non-interchangeable platforms with materially different thresholds.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: For the identical three CSF analytes, P-265 uses INNOTEST cutpoints (Abeta42 <700 pg/mL, t-tau >=350, p-tau >=70) while P-663 uses Fujirebio LUMIPULSE/ELISA cutpoints (Abeta42 670, t-tau 400, p-tau 60) - three analyte-by-analyte threshold discrepancies driven purely by platform. P-192 builds ATN dichotomous classifiers (RUSBoost PPV 68% at 4yr) and P-279 builds plasma p-tau181/NfL classifiers (plasma-only MCI->dementia AUC 0.64) on platform-specific absolute values; P-279 explicitly lists 'transportability across sites and assay platforms' as untested and P-54 calls for 'harmonized assays'. A cutpoint calibrated to platform A mis-stages specimens that read different absolute values on platform B, corrupting ATN classification, tau prognosis, and deployed plasma triage.

gaps.gap_statement: No digital/behavioural MCI classifier (facial-video, end-to-end speech, gait, driving) demonstrates that its discrimination survives demographic-confound control: a demographics-only (age/sex/education) baseline is rarely reported, and where it is, age+sex alone reach AUC ~0.80 or explain ~half of on-road-driving variance; raw-video/-audio deep models use no confound-matched design or adversarial de-biasing to prove they encode cognition rather than facial/vocal aging.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-333 (N=1461, held-out n=482, Wav2Vec2 voice) is the one study that properly baselines: age+sex alone reach AUC 0.80 and voice adds only +0.08 (to 0.88); age+sex+education 0.78 -> +0.11. P-599 (N=112 on-road driving in MCI) shows age+sex alone give adjusted R2=0.320 of driving performance. P-247 (Duke retinal CNN) shows demographics-alone AUC 0.580, proving the confound share is modality-dependent and must be measured. Against this, the headline raw-signal deep models report NO demographic baseline - P-76 MC-ViViT facial-video 90.63%, P-42 speech 99.9% - and P-11 (I-CONECT NLP) concedes its age/education analysis is only 'preliminary'. Because MCI cases are systematically older and age is the dominant dementia risk factor, a 90-99.9% 'cognition detector' may be a covert age/sex classifier.

(2) For raw-video/-audio end-to-end models specifically, retrain/test on age- and sex-matched MCI/NC subsets OR apply adversarial de-biasing against demographics plus a dynamic-vs-static saliency ablation showing cognition-relevant facial/vocal dynamics (not static appearance) carry the signal. A tabular demographic covariate cannot resolve this for pixel/waveform models, so (2) is separate.
gaps.fp_self_check: GENERIC_LIMITATION: rejected - a shared methodological absence across >=6 independent studies / 4 modalities, evidenced by the two papers that DID isolate the baseline (feasibility + importance). EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: ADReSS-style balancing exists for speech but there is no facial-video equivalent and end-to-end embeddings still leak vocal age - a within-corpus validation-practice gap doable with existing data. DATA_SCARCITY / COMBINATORIAL: n/a.

gaps.gap_statement: Coordinate-based rs-fMRI meta-analyses report 'convergent MCI biomarker' abnormality in EVERY canonical network (default-mode, salience, dorsal-attention, executive-control) - largely one research group re-partitioning an overlapping primary-study pool by pre-labelled network - yet none tests network-SPECIFICITY (convergence greater within a network than whole-brain expectation) or validates the convergent regions as an individual-level classifier, so the field cannot distinguish a network-specific rs-fMRI biomarker from spatially pervasive dysregulation or from shared input studies.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-517 (DMN, 39 studies), P-513 (salience, 30) and P-528 (dorsal-attention, 38) each pool the same three indices (ALFF/ReHo/FC) from MCI-vs-HC studies over overlapping 2000-2021 windows, each billed as the 'first' for its network, sharing senior author Jiu Chen and multiple co-authors; P-528 explicitly notes companions cover DMN, salience and executive-control networks. None reports any AUC/accuracy (all stop at group-level ALE convergence), and P-517/P-528 concede operator-dependent seed selection influences results. Because convergence appears wherever the group looks, from overlapping data, no network-specific claim is testable - and each meta proposes DIFFERENT stimulation targets (P-513 STG/insula; P-528 IPL/IFG/MFG; P-517 precuneus), making meta-derived neuromodulation targeting non-falsifiable.

gaps.closure_criteria: One network-agnostic image/coordinate meta-analysis that (a) pools ALL rs-fMRI MCI foci without pre-selecting a network, (b) statistically tests whether convergence exceeds whole-brain expectation within any network, and (c) derives an individual-level classifier from the convergent regions with pooled sensitivity/specificity. Doable now with existing coordinate data.
gaps.fp_self_check: GENERIC_LIMITATION: rejected - the emergent every-network-converges / same-group / overlapping-pool / specificity-never-tested property is invisible in any single paper (per-paper limitations already logged/rejected as G-CAND-263/266/277); this is a cross-series structural finding. EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: the generic group-vs-individual caution exists, but the specific network-agnostic specificity test + classification of MCI rs-fMRI ALE convergence is unaddressed. DATA_SCARCITY / COMBINATORIAL: n/a.

gaps.gap_statement: Treatment-response / responder prediction is essentially absent as a MODELLING task in MCI intervention research: response to neuromodulation and other interventions is demonstrably heterogeneous and candidate baseline predictors are named, yet no study builds or externally/cross-validates a MULTIVARIABLE baseline-biomarker -> response model reporting held-out discrimination - existing corpus work is confined to single-moderator or descriptive predictor analyses; the one multivariable baseline-EEG responder classifier visible in the corpus (Kayasandik 2022, 79% accuracy from pre-rTMS EEG, reported inside the P-558 review rather than as a corpus primary) states no held-out validation.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Response is heterogeneous (P-461: rTMS global-cognition SMD 1.52, 95%CI 0.49-2.56; P-468: vascular-MCI subgroup does not respond) and three reviews name the missing task (P-373 'patient selection for responsiveness'; P-461 recommends ML to characterise best-responding populations; P-575 lists 'predictors of response'). Where predictors are studied they are post-hoc within-cohort correlations (P-418 plasticity<->ADAS-Cog r=0.59; P-457, P-541 r=0.605) or single-moderator secondary analyses (P-403 frontal-WMH burden moderates NAC+exercise response via linear mixed models; P-496 descriptive PSQI predictor of tPBM response, no effect sizes). The ML machinery exists in this modality (P-522 SVM on baseline TMS-EEG, aimed at conversion prognosis), and P-558 reports one external responder classifier (Kayasandik 2022, SVM on pre-rTMS EEG, 79%; 93% post-rTMS) whose validation is unstated. No study delivers a cross-validated multivariable responder model.
