gaps.gap_statement: The MCI / conversion OUTCOME LABEL is operationalised non-comparably across studies - conversion defined over inconsistent and frequently unreported minimum-follow-up windows (2/3/4/8 yr or unstated), contaminating the 'stable' negative class with right-censored future converters; and prevalent-MCI defined by different criteria (MoCA<25, age-standardised MMSE, education-stratified Petersen, EHR/ICD code, self-report) - yet no study in this corpus holds one cohort fixed and refits the identical pipeline under each operational definition to partition how much reported AUC / SHAP ranking is a labelling artifact rather than model quality (P-1136 varies only the label but reports each criterion's AUC without refitting a model).
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Conversion window: P-507 labels sMCI at 2 yr, P-3 at 3 yr (74.61% Acc, N=593), P-512 at 48 mo, P-88 at 8 yr, while P-41 (91% Acc, AUC 0.92, N=192) and P-334 report no window; P-41 self-flags 'progression-window definitions can influence apparent performance' and P-512 warns some 'stable' patients convert later. A leaderboard ranking P-41 (91%, unstated window, N=192) above P-3 (74.61%, clean 3-yr, N=593) confounds an easier label with a better model. Prevalent-MCI criterion: AUC spans ~0.65-0.93 tracking label leniency - P-96 age-standardised MMSE 0.93, P-258 MoCA<25 0.87, P-270 education-stratified Petersen 0.75, P-165 EHR-code 0.65; P-646 states 'the constant redefinition of MCI may explain heterogeneity' and P-293 (4 tools across ARIC/Whitehall II/PATH, N>14,000) concludes tools are 'interchangeable' while conceding MCI definitions differed and recommending 'standardize MCI definitions'. There is also a circularity: education is the dominant predictor (VF-19) yet the label is variably education-adjusted, so education's importance is partly a labelling artifact.

gaps.gap_statement: Test-retest / scan-rescan reliability (ICC) and practice/learning effects of the ML INPUT feature are essentially never reported across EEG, digital-behavioural and structural biomarker studies, despite these biomarkers being explicitly pitched for longitudinal / repeated monitoring - and the one corpus biomarker-feature study that measures cross-session reliability (P-420) shows it is STAGE-DEPENDENT (lower in patients), so differential measurement noise can itself become a spurious discriminative signal and 'change' cannot be separated from noise. (Reliability figures that exist elsewhere in the corpus do not close it: P-709 reports test-retest ICC 0.937-0.956 for a stopwatch clinical balance test in MCI, not an ML input feature and not stage-stratified; P-719 reports spectral-ratio test-retest r = 0.98 in controls and 0.86 in patients without an MDC.)
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-420 (rs-fMRI, ADNI, N=111, two scans ~1 yr apart, motion-controlled) reports RSN-amplitude test-retest ICC of 0.44-0.77 in healthy elderly but 0.31-0.62 in MCI and -0.06-0.44 in AD - reliability declines with disease stage. Yet longitudinal/monitoring studies report none: P-400 dichotomises patients by an 'arbitrary +/-10% posterior alpha-reactivity threshold' against a single healthy recording; P-424 interprets a 2-month qEEG shift as a treatment effect in an uncontrolled pre-post design; P-167/P-76/P-282 pitch repeated/passive monitoring but give only single-session cross-sectional classification; P-354 holds 6,771 I-CONECT sessions across 74 subjects (~91/person) yet uses them only to boost classification, never to report test-retest ICC or model practice effects. (P-651's reported ICC>0.8 is INTER-RATER segmentation QC, not scan-rescan reliability - it does not close this.)

Because ADNI spans 1.5T (ADNI1) and 3T (ADNI-GO/2/3), field strength correlates with cohort/era; if the fine-grained edge partly encodes acquisition differences it is confounded and will not transport.

gaps.gap_statement: MCI multi-omics subtypes are confounded with the clustering pipeline: multiple ADNI subtyping studies each report a different number of subtypes with different biology using different fusion/clustering methods, yet none tests whether subtype ASSIGNMENTS are concordant across methods on the SAME subjects (e.g. adjusted Rand index), so subtype identity may be an algorithm artifact.

Since these subtypes are proposed for precision stratification, method-dependent assignment would mean patients enter different 'high-risk' strata purely by algorithm choice.

gaps.gap_statement: Cross-sectional survey/tabular MCI-ML models rank psychosocial/functional variables (depression, loneliness, social frailty, functional disability, life satisfaction) as their top SHAP 'risk predictors' for prevention targeting, while two independent longitudinal studies in the SAME corpus show those exact factors are bidirectionally caused BY MCI - yet no cross-sectional model quantifies or corrects the reverse-causation inflation of its feature importances.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Longitudinal bidirectionality is explicit: P-646 (HRS, N~9,300, competing-risks) shows depression->MCI (SHR 1.20) AND MCI->depression (SHR 1.16); P-624 (CHF, N=288, cross-lagged) shows T1 social-frailty->T2 MCI (-0.578) AND T1 MCI->T2 social-frailty (-0.646). Meanwhile cross-sectional ML models present these as leading actionable predictors: P-25 (CHARLS, N=6,434) tops on social events; P-27 (CHARLS depressed, N=1,964) on loneliness and IADL disability; P-323 (functional-disability cohort) on life satisfaction/depressive symptoms; P-35 (CHF, AUC 0.94) on psychosocial-adaptation and depression - each single-wave and framed as a prevention roadmap, none acknowledging its headline drivers are partly downstream of the outcome.

gaps.gap_statement: In MCI neuromodulation trials the delivered electric-field dose is not modelled-as-exposure in any sham-controlled design; dose-response is analysed on nominal parameters (mA, session count, sites), yet cortical atrophy attenuates the field at target and that attenuation is correlated with disease severity, so nominal dose-response and apparent non-response are confounded by anatomy-dependent under-dosing. The one corpus study that does use modelled E-field as the exposure, P-1243 (open-label gamma tACS pilot, n=13, no sham), reports memory gains most pronounced at the highest modelled field - a feasibility demonstration without a controlled dose-response estimate.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-458 (149 participants, 33 MCI) shows a standardised (MNI) montage delivers a target field significantly off the intended 0.3 V/m specifically in MCI patients (personalised modelling restores it), with no such gap in healthy adults - nominal dose != delivered dose in atrophic brains. P-449 shows ageing-related left-DLPFC gyrification loss in MCI converters both predicts 3-year decline AND lowers the modelled tDCS field, so attenuation tracks severity/progression. Meanwhile dose-response is inferred from NOMINAL dose: P-520 (>10 sessions g=1.25 vs <=10 g=0.46; multi-site 1.08 vs single 0.75); P-461/P-373 list 'optimal dose-response' as open - all without any measured/modelled delivered field.

gaps.closure_criteria: Within an RCT, compute per-participant personalised modelled delivered E-field from the structural MRI already acquired (as P-458 does), then use delivered field - not nominal protocol - as the exposure/covariate in the dose-response model and stratify responder analyses by delivered dose.
gaps.fp_self_check: GENERIC_LIMITATION: rejected - synthesises P-458+P-449 (MCI-specific severity-correlated field attenuation) with the nominal dose-response practice in P-520/P-461/P-373 (the single-paper versions were already rejected as G-CAND-97/104). DATA_SCARCITY: rejected - delivered field is computable from routine structural MRI. EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: E-field modelling tools exist broadly, but using modelled delivered dose as the exposure in MCI dose-response/responder analysis, where attenuation is severity-correlated, is absent here and physiologically specific to progressive atrophy (hence medium).
gaps.dedup_note: Distinct from ACTOR-G-010 (whether individualised TARGETING beats standard on a cognitive endpoint - montage comparative-effectiveness). gaps.gap_statement: In early-decline classification the clinically decisive adjacent-stage contrast (SCD-vs-MCI, or same-age-cognitively-normal-vs-MCI) is markedly harder and systematically under-evaluated relative to the easy extreme contrasts (dementia-vs-SCD, MCI-vs-young-healthy) that dominate reporting, and reviews propagate easy-contrast performance as evidence of biomarker readiness; no study reports the spectrum-induced inflation as a computed quantity with age-matched controls on a fixed cohort. P-85 (fNIRS, 246 participants: MCI-vs-NC 97.0%, MCI-vs-SCD 87.0%, SCD-vs-NC 79.2%) and P-170 (206 participants; adjacent-stage classifiers with MCI-vs-SCD AUROC about 0.90, i.e. no inflation observed) do report easy and hard contrasts on one cohort, but neither quantifies the inflation or age-matches.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-538 shows WITHIN one model on one sample that dementia-vs-SCD reaches AUC 0.96 but MCI-vs-SCD is only 0.79 (dementia-vs-MCI 0.86) - a 0.17 AUC collapse driven purely by contrast difficulty. P-548 documents that only 10 of 30 SCD electrophysiology studies include a cognitively-normal comparator at all, and only 4 of 30 are longitudinal. P-562 reports that contradictory MTL-activation findings across t-fMRI studies are attributed to mixed MCI/AD samples - spectrum composition distorts the biomarker signal. Headline extreme-contrast AUCs thus overstate clinical readiness by an amount the field never quantifies.

gaps.gap_statement: No corpus paper reports a head-to-head measurement of how much MCI diagnostic or conversion performance shifts when the PET SUVR intensity-normalisation reference region is changed (cerebellum vs pons vs white matter vs composite). The single-reference practice is a corpus-level pattern - P-569 normalises 'to mean cerebellar voxel intensity' (N=399, ADNI), P-505 uses SUVRs referenced to cerebellar gray matter, P-525 uses a cerebellar GM reference - while the corpus simultaneously gives reason to doubt the cerebellum's neutrality in MCI (P-570 builds MCI-discriminative classifiers from cerebellar radiomic/connectome features; P-327 asserts white matter is 'superior to cerebellum as reference region' and 'more stable longitudinally').
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: SINGLE-REFERENCE PRACTICE (3 papers, verified verbatim): P-569 'SUVr was normalized to mean cerebellar voxel intensity' with no alternative reference tested; P-505 'SUVRs referenced to cerebellar gray matter'; P-525 'cerebellar GM reference'. CEREBELLUM-NOT-NEUTRAL (verified): P-570 derives MCI-discriminative classifiers from cerebellar radiomic/connectome features, i.e. the cerebellum carries MCI signal. ISSUE RAISED BUT NOT QUANTIFIED: P-327 (N=341) states 'white matter superior to cerebellum as reference region' and 'white-matter reference region more stable longitudinally than cerebellum' - BOTH quotes verified verbatim, BUT they appear in the significance / why-is-it-important fields as unquantified assertions. P-327's reported results cover ONLY the white-matter arm (AUC 0.868 train / 0.865 test); there is no cerebellum-referenced comparator statistic, and its DeLong test compares the integrated model against individual predictors (CDR, ADAS), not against a cerebellar reference. White matter was 'chosen as stable reference region' a priori - a design premise, not a tested outcome. SELF-REBUTTAL DISPOSED OF: P-327's novelty field claims it 'demonstrates reference-region choice impacts radiomics stability and predictive value'; the gap survives because no comparative number for the cerebellum arm is reported anywhere in the record - the issue is raised, never measured. ABSENCE RE-CHECK (receiver-side): regex sweep over all 687 paper blocks found ZERO papers pairing a reference-region discussion with a sensitivity analysis; only 4 blocks mention reference-region / intensity normalisation at all (P-327, P-537, P-665, P-540), and P-665's 'intensity normalisation' is FreeSurfer structural-MRI preprocessing (white-matter scaling), a different construct, not PET SUVR.

gaps.gap_statement: Two corpus studies apply Lempel-Ziv complexity to DISCRETE NEURAL STATE SEQUENCES along the AD continuum and report OPPOSITE signs, with no reconciliation: P-480 finds microstate-sequence LZ complexity DECREASED in MCI vs SCD (H=9.02, p=0.011; SCD vs MCI p=0.026, d=0.45), while P-463 finds meta-band sequencing complexity (SR, BLZC) INCREASED with pathology progression (significant HC-AD only). Because both are Lempel-Ziv applied to state-label sequences, the divergence cannot be attributed to different measurement families; candidate mediators (4-microstate vs 3-meta-band alphabet, topographic vs frequency-community sequence construction, EEG vs MEG, MCI vs AD stage) are untested. Separately, no study IN THE CITED SET computes signal-level entropy AND sequence-level Lempel-Ziv complexity in the same MCI cohort, so the sign relationship between those two constructs is untested.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status:
OPPOSITE SIGNS, SAME MEASUREMENT FAMILY (both verified verbatim): P-480 (EEG; 122 = 57 SCD / 46 MCI / 19 HC) 'LZ complexity decreased in MCI vs SCD (H=9.02, p=0.011; SCD vs MCI p=0.026, d=0.45)' - and its novelty field confirms 'First use of LZ complexity and Hurst exponent on EEG MICROSTATE SEQUENCES'. P-463 (MEG; 161 = 67 HC / 44 MCI / 50 AD) 'SR and BLZC increased with pathology progression, with significant HC-AD differences, indicating less stable meta-bands and increased sequencing complexity'. STAGE CAVEAT: P-463's SR/BLZC rise is significant only HC-AD; the HC-MCI contrast is carried by meta-band 1 assignment and DoD standard deviation, NOT by BLZC - so at the MCI stage the 'complexity rises' arm is not established. gaps.gap_statement:
GAP (corpus-absence, EEG/ERP MCI discrimination): Affective acquisition context - both the emotional valence of the eliciting stimulus and the participant's own depressive status - is a MEASURED modulator of the exact EEG/ERP feature families that MCI classifiers consume, yet no corpus study statistically tests the resulting performance shift or corrects a classifier for it.

MEASURED MODERATION, from TWO INDEPENDENT PROGRAMMES (not three independent papers):
(A) Zhejiang visual-oddball programme - P-485 (N=150; 51 Controls / 52 MCI / 47 AD) and P-133 (N=90; 30/30/30). NOTE: SAME GROUP - six shared authors including first author (C./Chu Wang) and senior author (M./Ming Tao), same Neutral/Happiness/Sadness IAPS visual-oddball paradigm, same region, 2024/2025; cohorts may overlap. Treat as ONE source. P-485 `### What are the outcomes? (Results)`: 'Under Happiness, MCI P3 latencies were significantly delayed vs Controls (frontal electrodes, p=0.005~0.020)'; 'During N2 window under Happiness, right inferior frontal gyrus activation was significantly attenuated in MCI vs Controls' - i.e. the MCI-vs-Control ERP marker is emotion-specific, not stimulus-general.
(B) Shanghai Tongji programme - P-533 (N=43; 26 MCI / 17 MCI+depressive symptoms) and P-662 (N=93; 46 aMCI / 47 HEC, ADDED BY VERIFIER - same lab and same 90-image IAPS reappraisal paradigm, cited inside P-533 as the authors' own Xiao et al. 2021; also ONE source). P-533 `### What are the outcomes? (Results)`, WITHIN the MCI label: left frontal-occipital alpha connectivity 0.393+/-0.05 vs 0.444+/-0.05, p=0.001; clustering coefficient 0.33+/-0.02 vs 0.39+/-0.044, p<0.0001; LPP to negative stimuli win4 3.06+/-0.92 vs 0.49+/-0.51, p=0.01 and win5 3.13+/-0.92 vs 0.69+/-0.49, p=0.015. Two participants both carrying the MCI label yield systematically different band-power, connectivity and graph features as a function of affective status.

CORRECTED ABSENCE CLAUSE (narrower than proposed - the proposed headline is FALSE): P-133 DOES quantify per-condition discrimination - `### What are the outcomes? (Results)`: 'GCN achieved accuracies of 90.17 +/-5.58 %, 86.73 +/-2.34 %, and 84.73 +/-4.28 % under Neutral, Happiness, and Sadness, respectively' (a 5.44-point spread). So 'no corpus study quantifies the discrimination loss' is retracted. What is absent from the corpus record is: (a) any significance test of the between-condition performance difference; (b) any condition-agnostic pooled estimate; (c) any cross-condition transfer test (train under one affective condition, test under another); (d) any calibration / operating-threshold comparison across conditions; (e) any classifier stratified by depressive status within MCI - P-485 and P-533 build no classifier at all (P-485 `### Potential gaps or limitations`: 'No diagnostic classifier or accuracy metrics'; P-533 `### Best AUC`: 'Not reported'), and P-662 handles affective status by EXCLUSION (MDD and HAMD>=14 excluded, groups matched at HAMD 5.28 vs 5.26, p 0.97) rather than by quantifying its cost.

TWO CAVEATS THE REVIEWER MUST CARRY: (1) P-133's accuracies are NOT attributable to MCI specifically - its block says only 'binary classification tasks distinguishing HC from MCI and AD', which may be a pooled MCI+AD contrast; and P-133's block is abstract-only with several fields containing author affiliations rather than content, so (a)-(d) are absences in the CORPUS RECORD for P-133, not verified absences in the published paper. (2) Within the depressive-status half, only the STATUS contrast is robust; the 'scales with HAMD-17 severity' claim is cut back to the clustering coefficient (r=-0.66, p<0.001) - the remaining severity correlations are nominal and marginal (arousal r=0.33 p=0.029; alpha r=0.311 p=0.042; gamma r=-0.356 p=0.019) under a pipeline whose methods field declares FDR correction without the block showing adjusted values, and confirmed VF-27 already holds depression severity to be dissociated from MCI neurobiology.

RATIONALE (why this is not a combinatorial accident): confirmed VF-26 holds that depression and MCI are robustly and reciprocally associated across independent cohorts, and VF-23 [pending_human_review] holds that EEG network/connectivity measures are the leading MCI-EEG discriminators - so the deployment population is precisely the population whose affective status moves the input features, and P-533 measures that intersection directly.

CLOSURE TEST (retained as proposed - specific and actionable): in one MCI/HC cohort, acquire the same EEG/ERP feature set under >=2 affective conditions and stratify participants by a depression scale (HAMD/GDS), then report (a) AUC within each affective condition, (b) AUC when a model trained under one condition is tested under another, and (c) the shift in operating threshold / calibration between conditions and between depressed and non-depressed MCI.

SCOPE: stated as an absence within this corpus only; no claim about the external literature. SUPPORT: 2 independent programmes / 4 corpus papers (P-133, P-485 | P-533, P-662).
gaps.human_understanding: Emotions and depression change the brainwaves we use to detect early memory loss (MCI). While we know this happens, the current research hasn't properly tested how much this confuses AI diagnostic tools, nor has it figured out how to adjust the AI to account for a patient's depression. Future studies need to explicitly test and fix this.
gaps.headline: Affective acquisition context (stimulus valence + participant depressive status) moderates the EEG/ERP features MCI classifiers consume; P-133 quantifies per-condition accuracy (90.17/86.73/84.73% under Neutral/Happiness/Sadness), but the corpus contains no significance test of the between-condition difference, no pooled condition-agnostic estimate, no cross-condition transfer test, no calibration/threshold comparison across conditions, and no depressive-status-stratified classifier.

gaps.gap_statement: GAP: No exercise-for-MCI meta-analysis in this corpus POOLS a post-cessation follow-up timepoint - every pooled cognitive estimate is taken at the end of the intervention period - so the corpus contains no pooled estimate of how much of the reported benefit survives the programme ending. P-674 documents the mechanism at method level: its eligibility specifies 'Timing of outcome measurement: end of exercise therapy' (### What are the key components in the method?), and its ### Potential gaps or limitations states 'Nothing is learned about persistence of benefit, because the eligibility criteria fix outcome timing at the end of exercise therapy, even though several included trials collected later follow-up points (Lam et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2020; Wei & Ji, 2014).' Four further corpus exercise syntheses across three further author groups name the same unresolved question in their ### Open problems fields: P-603 ('Optimal exercise dose/composition and durability of cognitive benefit.'), P-613 ('...durability.'), P-609 ('durability of effects'), P-692 ('whether cognitive gains persist after training stops'). The end-of-intervention estimates being pooled are large: P-674 SMD 0.65 (95% CI 0.39-0.91) [Key findings reported], P-698 SMD 0.76 [Key findings reported], P-613 SMD 1.04 (0.53-1.55) [Results], P-603 Hedges' g 0.978 (0.298-1.659) in MCI [Results]. SCOPE AND EXCEPTIONS (mandatory): (a) this is an absence of POOLING, not of measurement - P-251 [### What are the outcomes? (Results)] reports a cited MCI RCT whose 6-month resistance-exercise gains persisted 12 months, and P-672 [### Key findings reported] records hippocampal protection 'persisting at least twelve months post-intervention', so post-cessation durability is NOT unquantified in this corpus, merely never pooled; (b) P-674 and P-698 are the same author pair (Ahn & Kim) sharing 10 of P-698's 11 trials, and P-698's own ### Related findings field warns they must not be treated as independent evidence - they count as ONE converging source; (c) P-680 is removed from this record: its block contains no persistence, durability, follow-up or cessation vocabulary anywhere and cannot support the absence; (d) P-249 is removed as the long-horizon anchor: its null (exercise alone SMD 0.05, 95% CI -0.04 to 0.13, p=0.25) is for programmes of >=12 months DURATION measured at end of intervention, in non-demented community-dwelling older adults rather than an MCI cohort, so it speaks to programme length and not to retention and must not be read as evidence that the retention ratio is low. CLOSURE TEST: a trial-level or IPD meta-analysis restricted to MCI exercise RCTs that measured global cognition >=3 and >=6 months AFTER the programme ended - P-674 names three concrete candidate trials already holding such data (Lam et al. 2015; Wang et al. 2020; Wei & Ji 2014) - reporting a retention ratio (post-cessation SMD / end-of-intervention SMD) with programme duration and post-cessation interval pre-specified as moderators. PAPERS: P-674 (primary, method-level), P-698, P-603, P-613, P-692, P-609; exception papers P-251, P-672.
gaps.human understanding: Exercise gives a strong short-term cognitive boost to people with MCI, and some individual studies show this benefit lasts. However, no one has combined (pooled) all this long-term data together. Future research needs to specifically analyze what happens 3 to 6 months after the exercise stops to prove exactly how much of the benefit is retained.
gaps.headline: No exercise-for-MCI synthesis pools a post-cessation follow-up timepoint. Individual trials do measure durability (P-251, P-672), but no meta-analysis pools it, so the corpus contains no POOLED retention estimate for cognitive benefit after the programme ends.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status:
MEASURED end-of-intervention effects: P-613 `### What are the outcomes? (Results)`: 'Multicomponent exercise significantly improved global cognition (SMD = 1.04; 95% CI 0.53-1.55)'. P-603 `### What are the outcomes? (Results)`: 'In MCI specifically, multicomponent exercise significantly improved global cognition (Hedges' g = 0.978; 95% CI 0.298-1.659)'. P-674 `### Key findings reported`: '(1) Exercise therapy significantly improved global cognitive function in older adults with MCI, pooled SMD 0.65 (95 percent CI 0.39 to 0.91) across 21 RCTs with 2,210 enrolled and 1,916 analysed participants.' P-680 `### What are the outcomes? (Results)`: 'Global effect of exercise on cognition: standardised difference in means 1.165 (95 percent CI 0.741 to 1.589)... The prediction interval was -0.747 to 3.077.' P-698 `### Key findings reported`: '(1) Aerobic exercise significantly improved global cognitive function in older adults with MCI, SMD 0.76... (2) The 95 percent prediction interval ran from -0.63 to 2.15.' THE ABSENCE (methodological, so limitation/open-problem fields are the correct evidential source): P-674 `### Potential gaps or limitations`: 'Nothing is learned about persistence of benefit, because the eligibility criteria fix outcome timing at the end of exercise therapy, even though several included trials collected later follow-up points (Lam et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2020; Wei & Ji, 2014).' P-698 `### What can be improved?`: 'because the review captures only short-duration interventions and the authors note that cognitive gains from short-term exercise tend to deteriorate again, follow-up data on maintenance after intervention cessation is the missing outcome that would make the dosing recommendation clinically complete.' P-698 `### Open problems, applications, methodologies, achievable outcomes?`: 'whether gains persist after the intervention stops, since short-term gains are said to deteriorate'. P-603 `### Open problems, applications, methodologies, achievable outcomes?`: 'Optimal exercise dose/composition and durability of cognitive benefit.' P-603 `### What can be improved?`: 'More and larger standardized RCTs, dose/protocol harmonisation, longer follow-up, and analysis of durability and conversion outcomes'. P-613 `### Open problems, applications, methodologies, achievable outcomes?`: 'Optimal intensity/dose and detailed motor-component combinations; durability.' THE LONG-HORIZON CONTRAST (measured): P-249 `### What are the outcomes? (Results)`: 'Sixteen long-term (>=12 months) RCTs in non-demented, community-dwelling older adults (11,402 participants) were meta-analysed; overall risk of bias was low. Moderate-certainty evidence: physical exercise alone had modest-to-no effect on global cognition (k=9, SMD 0.05; 95% CI -0.04 to 0.13; p=0.25 - non-significant).'

[2026-08-15 operator rescope: disregard the P-680 and P-249 items above - P-680 removed (no durability/cessation vocabulary in its block, topic drift) and P-249 removed as the long-horizon anchor (>=12-month prevention population, end-of-intervention timing); see g5_operator_verdict_2026_08_15.]

gaps.gap_statement: GAP (corpus-scoped): In this corpus's ADNI MCI-to-AD conversion models, the informant-rated Functional Activities Questionnaire (FAQ) is repeatedly reported at or near the top of the predictor ranking - P-353 `### What are the outcomes? (Results)`: "FAQ emerged as the most influential variable" (cdAUC ~0.91 at 1 year, 922 baseline MCI, in a model also containing imaging, genetics and neuropsychology); P-243 same field: "**Top predictors:** FAQ (Functional Activities Questionnaire), mPACCtrailsB, RAVLT_immediate, ADAS11" (627 baseline MCI, 269 converters); P-234 same field: "SHAP analysis highlighted FAQ and LDELTOTAL as key predictors" (ADNI 2288 with external NACC testing). [NOTE: P-353 is the only block asserting FAQ is the SINGLE top variable; in P-243 the list is unranked and in P-234 FAQ is co-equal with LDELTOTAL.] The same corpus uses the same instrument as the longitudinal functional OUTCOME: P-622 `### What are the outcomes? (Results)`: "MMSE and FAQ trajectories changed most slowly in MO and fastest in M&V" (1020 baseline-MCI, ADNI); P-260 and P-681 likewise fit FAQ trajectories as the daily-function outcome in ADNI MCI. And P-13 shows the overlap inside one study: `### What are the key components in the method?` - "with FAQ trajectory used to define high- and low-risk groups" - after which `### What are the outcomes? (Results)` recommends "**ADAS13 + FAQ**" for the low-risk group and favours "RSF with longitudinal ADAS13/FAQ" for low-risk prognosis. [P-13 is cited ONLY for this stratum/predictor overlap, not as a top-ranked-predictor instance: FAQ is never ranked there, and its high-risk recommendation is "**CDRSB + hippocampal volume**", which contains no FAQ.] SPECIFIC UNMET NEED: no corpus study reports how much of its conversion discrimination survives removal of FAQ (and CDR-SOB where used) from the predictor set. CLOSURE TEST: refit the same ADNI conversion models on the same cohort with FAQ/CDR-SOB removed and report the AUC / C-index delta stratified by prediction horizon. PRIOR WORK TO CREDIT, NOT OVERSTATE: (a) the horizon-stratified half already exists - P-211 `### What are the outcomes? (Results)`: "Feature importance shifted by horizon (e.g., inferior temporal/entorhinal MRI features, FAQ, APOE4)" - so only the removal-ablation is unmet; (b) the corpus is NOT blind to instrument-criterion contamination - P-681 `### What are the problems?` states "the subtypes are derived from the same trajectories they are then used to describe ... part of the trajectory separation is definitional rather than predictive", and its `### What did the authors do?` records memory being "deliberately excluded from the subtyping variables on the grounds that ADNI's MCI entry criteria already require objective memory loss" - the same reasoning applied to a different instrument pair. The clause "none names the issue" is therefore RETRACTED and replaced by: no corpus study applies this reasoning to FAQ on the predictor side of a conversion model. DROPPED from the record: P-594 (its `### What is the sample size?` is "288 - subjects from ADNI (cognitively normal, MCI, and AD)", a pooled non-MCI-specific cohort, and its `### What are the problems?` says "The design is cross-sectional", so FAQ there is a concurrent score, not a decline endpoint); P-156 (OCR-spillover block, interpretive field, quote not verbatim); and the claim that contamination is "already visible" in P-243's horizon decay (P-243's own `### What is the significance?` reads that decay as ordinary loss of prediction power over longer horizons). EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT - the construct is the FAQ instrument itself, and the literal string "FAQ" appears in every block I cite; nothing is imported by paraphrase.
EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT - every load-bearing quote is from `### What are the outcomes? (Results)`, `### What are the key components in the method?`, `### What is the sample size?` or `### Best Metric`. The single interpretive quote (P-156, `### Why is it important?`) is used only to document framing, which the rulebook explicitly permits, and is flagged as spillover-contaminated.
MISASSIGNED_MEASUREMENT_FAMILY - not applicable and in fact inverted: the whole point is that both sides are the SAME instrument (FAQ). I am not putting two members of one family on opposite sides of a contrast; I am pointing out one instrument sitting on BOTH sides of a prediction.
TOO_SPECIFIC / COMBINATORIAL_GAP - this is not an unmotivated modality crossing. There is a direct clinical rationale: loss of functional independence is the boundary criterion between MCI and dementia, and FAQ is the informant instrument that indexes it. The corpus supplies internal support for that rationale without needing external premises (P-622 calls FAQ "daily function" and models it as the outcome; P-13 uses FAQ trajectory to define the risk label).
EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE - stated as "no CORPUS study quantifies", never "nobody has studied"; and the closure test is specified concretely enough that an external closure can be checked against it.
SINGLE-PAPER-LIMITATION-RESTATED - no: four independent predictor-side studies (P-353, P-243, P-234, P-13, spanning a deep survival net, an ensemble fusion model, an RNN with external NACC testing, and a functional-data-analysis/RSF framework) plus three outcome-side uses (P-13, P-622, P-594).
DUPLICATION vs existing curated gaps - checked each near neighbour: ACTOR-G-033 is about varying the LABEL (follow-up window, MCI criterion heterogeneity); mine holds the label fixed and asks about the PREDICTOR sharing an instrument with it. ACTOR-G-038 is cross-sectional survey/tabular models and reverse causation in psychosocial variables (depression, loneliness, social frailty); mine is longitudinal clinical/ADNI conversion models and instrument-level criterion overlap - different study population, different mechanism. G-021 is interval-censored data forced into binary labels. ACTOR-G-026 is epoch-level CV leakage in EEG. G-18 is XAI explanation actionability. G-03 is selective outcome reporting. VF-05 (already DEMOTED) asserts neuropsych outranks imaging within ADNI - FAQ is not a neuropsychological test but an informant-rated functional scale, and my record is about why such a ranking may be artefactual, not that the ranking exists.

gaps.gap_statement:
SCOPE: comparative-effectiveness syntheses of non-pharmacological interventions in POOLED dementia+MCI populations in this corpus. NOT established as MCI-specific.

Within a single corpus network meta-analysis of reminiscence-therapy delivery formats (P-615; 53 RCTs, 4582 participants), the efficacy ranking and the adherence ranking select DIFFERENT formats: digital delivery ranks first for cognitive function (SUCRA 93.6%) and depressive symptoms (SUCRA 94.9%), while GROUP delivery ranks first for adherence (SUCRA 95.6%) and "outperformed individual and treatment-as-usual formats on that outcome" (all from '### What are the outcomes? (Results)'). Adherence is reported as a SEPARATE ranked outcome; no combined, adherence-conditioned, or delivered-dose-conditioned estimate is reported, so the synthesis issues an efficacy-based format recommendation that its own adherence ranking does not support, and never reconciles the two.

VERIFIED CORPUS-WIDE ABSENCE: no comparative-effectiveness synthesis of non-pharmacological MCI/dementia interventions in this corpus reports an effect estimate conditioned on achieved dose or observed adherence. Independently checked: P-642, P-655, P-683, P-705 (SUCRA-ranking syntheses that rank no acceptability/adherence outcome at all) and P-673, P-674, P-679, P-692 (meta-analyses that concede adherence/compliance went unreported in their included trials, or list dose-response over session count and total contact hours as future work). P-615 is the only corpus synthesis that measures adherence, and it ranks it separately. Several of these sources explicitly call for the missing analysis, which strengthens rather than weakens the record.

CLOSURE TEST (unchanged, and concrete): re-run an existing MCI/dementia non-pharmacological-intervention network meta-analysis with session-completion / achieved dose entered as a network meta-regression covariate, or re-rank arms on an adherence-weighted expected effect (pooled SMD x observed completion rate), and report whether the first-placed arm changes. A first-place rank reversal would establish that efficacy-only SUCRA rankings are not decision-relevant for this intervention class.

DROPPED AS UNSUPPORTED — do not carry into the record:
(a) The P-611 leg as EVIDENCE. P-611 measures determinants of physical-activity participation (resources/material resources, social support, perceived competence) in MCI/dementia - a different intervention class from P-615's reminiscence therapy - and the proposal's clause "supports that a trial protocol supplies and routine care does not" is miner inference with no quote behind it. P-611 may be cited as CONTEXT (participation in this population is resource- and support-dependent), never as evidence that syntheses fail to condition on adherence.
(b) The P-613 claim that its pooled SMD 1.04 carries "no delivered-dose or adherence term". Support offered is an interpretive-field quote only, and P-613's method field states it ran "subgroup analyses, meta-regression, and sensitivity analyses" without naming covariates. P-613 may be cited only for the weaker, quotable point: a 20-RCT pooled global-cognition SMD of 1.04 coexists with the authors' own concession that "optimal frequency, intensity, and dose remain undetermined" ('### What are the problems?').

MANDATORY CAVEATS ON THE FACE OF THE RECORD:
- P-615 pools dementia and MCI (its Primary Limitation: "combined dementia+MCI") and lists "MCI-specific format effects" among its own open problems. The dissociation is therefore NOT MCI-specific.
- P-615's cognition arm rests on SMD 5.02 vs treatment-as-usual, with the paper conceding large effects with wide intervals and transitivity/sparse-network assumptions. The closure test would be run on a fragile network; a rank reversal there is suggestive, not decisive.

CROSS-LINK: ACTOR-G-039 (delivered electric-field dose never modelled as exposure in MCI neuromodulation; dose-response analysed only on nominal parameters) is the structural sibling of this record in a different intervention class. Not a duplicate - distinct quantity (attendance vs cortical dose) and distinct literature - but the two should be linked, and a future merge into a single "nominal versus received dose" gap family should be considered.
gaps.human_understanding: Studies rank dementia/MCI treatments based on theoretical effectiveness, but ignore whether patients actually stick to them. For example, digital therapy might work best on paper, but group therapy is what people actually complete. Future research must combine effectiveness and adherence rates to figure out what truly works in the real world.

The load-bearing evidence, P-615's within-network dissociation between the efficacy ranking (digital, SUCRA 93.6%) and the adherence ranking (group, SUCRA 95.6%), sits in '### What are the outcomes? (Results)' and '### Best Metric', both MEASURED fields, and it is a genuine within-paper measured dissociation of the kind the rulebook holds up as the mark of a confirmed record. The universal-negative clause is the part that usually kills gap records here, so I re-derived it myself instead of trusting the miner's self-check: across the SUCRA-ranking syntheses (P-642, P-655, P-683, P-705) none ranks any acceptability or adherence outcome, and across the pooling meta-analyses (P-673, P-674, P-679, P-692) the recurring pattern is an explicit concession that compliance went unreported plus a call for exactly the dose-response analysis this record says is missing. The absence is real, and the corpus argues for it.

It cannot be accepted as written, for three reasons. First, two of the three cited papers do not carry the weight assigned to them. The P-611 leg drifts topic - it measures why people with MCI or dementia do or do not do PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, not anything about how syntheses construct effect estimates - and the pivotal clause "supports that a trial protocol supplies and routine care does not" has no quote behind it anywhere in the block. The P-613 leg asserts a method-absence ("no delivered-dose or adherence term") on the strength of an INTERPRETIVE-field quote, while P-613's own method field says it ran meta-regression without naming covariates; the miner pre-empted this objection by arguing the interpretive quote establishes an absence rather than a f

gaps.g5_operator_verdict_2026_08_15: ACCEPT_WITH_RESCOPE. P-611 removed as evidence (it measures determinants of physical-activity participation, not reminiscence therapy; the 'trial protocol supplies and routine care does not' clause has no quote behind it - citable as CONTEXT only). P-613 usable only for the weak quotable point: a pooled SMD 1.04 coexists with the authors' own concession that 'optimal frequency, intensity, and dose remain undetermined' - the 'no adherence term' claim is in tension with its stated meta-regression. Scope caveat mandatory: P-615 pools dementia+MCI, so the dissociation is NOT MCI-specific. Cross-linked to ACTOR-G-039 (delivered electric-field dose never modelled in neuromodulation) as the structural sibling; candidate future merge into a 'nominal vs received dose' gap family.

Agent 4 built this 'modality-task absence' record by treating the whole of P-732's Modality registry value as a modality NAME. That cell holds a prose justification beginning 'No data of any modality were collected, so the coding rests on the data domain of the variables the article proposes to model...', so the generated gap_statement, modality, evidence_for_open_status and closure_criteria all read as sentence fragments rather than a stated absence. P-732 is a Medical Hypotheses proposal that collects no data at all, so it cannot evidence a corpus-wide modality absence. Underlying condition tracked as PAPERINGO-0ft: 65 of 723 registry rows carry prose over 200 chars in the Modality column, so this generator can misfire again.

gaps.gap_statement: No corpus study tests tactile sensitivity longitudinally as a predictor of MCI onset or conversion: both tactile papers are non-longitudinal (P-871 cross-sectional three-modality thresholds, Mannheim N=100; P-877 narrative review), yet the parallel olfactory channel already has backward-timescale trajectory evidence (P-870, 5y pre-MCI divergence) demonstrating what a sensory peripheral window can establish longitudinally. P-871's own open problem is 'Prospective validation of tactile sensitivity as an MCI predictor'; P-877 names 'longitudinal predictive validity' as open. The somatosensory-channel rationale (tactile loss is MCI-specific per P-871 while visual/auditory are preserved) justifies the prospective test.

gaps.interpretation: Tactile sensitivity is the only corpus sensory channel with cross-sectional MCI-specificity (P-871) but zero longitudinal evidence — while olfaction (P-870) and retinal channels have trajectory support. The gap is a design absence, not a negative result: the within-cohort tactile-specific dissociation makes the prospective test the natural next experiment.

gaps.gap_statement: No corpus study provides high-certainty evidence that ANY intervention prevents or delays MCI-to-dementia progression: the only corpus systematic review addressing this endpoint (P-882, 6 databases, 3,842 records screened) found just 4 eligible studies and no statistically significant conversion reduction (best candidate: multidomain lifestyle HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.55-1.02, p=0.06, borderline). The corpus intervention studies that touch progression use surrogate outcomes (cognitive test scores, biomarker change: P-879 MoCA-J, P-885 satisfaction/outcomes, P-873/P-875 nutrition) rather than dementia conversion as the primary endpoint.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-882 (systematic review, 2024): only 4 of 3,842 records met inclusion criteria (RCTs/cohorts with dementia conversion as outcome); no significant conversion reduction for any intervention; multidomain lifestyle HR 0.75 borderline. P-882's own Open_Problems: 'large, international, multi-site RCTs with dementia conversion as a primary endpoint, >=5-year follow-up, harmonised conversion criteria.' No other corpus paper has dementia conversion as a primary endpoint. gaps.interpretation: The MCI-to-dementia progression prevention question is the highest-stakes open question in the corpus: MCI conversion is the clinical endpoint that matters for patients, yet every corpus intervention trial measures surrogates (cognitive scores, QoL, satisfaction) while dementia conversion remains unmeasured. The multidomain lifestyle signal (HR 0.75) is the single most promising lead but is one borderline result; the design absence (no conversion-primary-endpoint RCT) is a corpus-wide structural gap, not a negative result.

gaps.gap_statement: No corpus study evaluates whether hearing-loss INTERVENTION (hearing aids / amplification / auditory training) modifies cognition or functional connectivity in MCI, despite hearing loss being the leading modifiable dementia risk factor (Lancet Commission RR 1.9) and P-896 now demonstrating the neural substrate (reduced DMN-caudate/thalamus connectivity in MCI with pure-tone HL). The corpus's hearing papers are all observational or mechanistic (P-896 DMN connectivity; P-451/P-489 auditory ERP/task; P-717 phasic alerting; P-871/P-877 tactile-adjacent; P-887 timing), with zero intervention trials on amplification restoring connectivity or cognition.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-896 (Montreal, N=94): HL associated with decreased DMN-caudate/thalamus connectivity in MCI; the paper's own discussion positions hearing loss as the leading modifiable dementia risk factor and calls for intervention work, but reports no intervention. Corpus-wide search of all registry rows for 'hearing aid|amplification|cochlear|auditory training' returns no RCT; the only hit (P-720) is a depression-AT(N) study, not a hearing intervention. gaps.interpretation: The hearing-loss-to-dementia pathway is mechanistically grounded (connectivity disruption, P-896) but the intervention side is a complete corpus-wide absence: whether amplification reverses DMN-subcortical disconnection and reduces MCI progression is the single most policy-relevant untested question in the sensory-loss arm of dementia prevention - and the corpus cannot currently contribute any trial-level evidence.

gaps.gap_statement: No completed corpus RCT demonstrates that a sleep intervention (CPAP, sleep hygiene, nap scheduling) improves cognition in MCI: the corpus's sleep-MCI evidence is cross-sectional self-report (P-891 CHARLS dose-response), prevalence synthesis (P-654 meta, subjective prevalence 35.8%), narrative review (P-638), CPAP-adherence review in OSA+MCI (P-796), and a protocol-stage multicentre CPAP trial with no results yet (P-823 DemCPAP, n=28 so far).
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-891 (CHARLS, N=7,480): cross-sectional dose-response - cannot test whether sleep modification improves cognition; P-823 (DemCPAP protocol): describes an 8-centre Italian CPAP RCT in MCI/AD with OSA but reports only n=28 enrolled, no results; P-796: adherence-focused review, no cognition endpoint trial; P-654/P-638: prevalence/narrative only. No corpus RCT reports a sleep-intervention cognitive endpoint. gaps.interpretation: Sleep is the most actionable of the modifiable MCI risk factors (7-8h + 30-60min naps + good quality lower MCI odds in P-891), yet the corpus contains no completed trial testing whether improving sleep changes cognitive trajectory - the DemCPAP protocol (P-823) is the only interventional seed and it is at enrolment stage. This is a design gap, not a negative result.

gaps.gap_statement: No corpus study prospectively validates cognitive screening cutoffs for MCI/dementia in renal populations, and no renal-specific conversion cohort exists: the MoCA-24 recommendation for CKD/kidney failure rests entirely on P-889's synthesis of 10 retrospective studies with selective optimal-cutoff reporting and no transplant or haemodiafiltration coverage, while P-888 establishes AKI as a dementia/MCI risk factor but offers no screening pathway; the corpus's other renal papers (P-360, P-398, P-419, ESRD) are cross-sectional signatures with no prospective screening validation.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-889 (DTA meta): authors state 'further research is needed to evaluate the operating characteristics of MCI/dementia screening instruments in CKD, dialysis, and kidney transplantation' and note selective reporting of optimal cutoffs; 0 of 10 included studies covered transplantation or haemodiafiltration. P-888 (SPRINT AKI cohort): establishes AKI->dementia/MCI risk (HR 1.72/1.43) but performs no screening evaluation. No registry row contains a prospective renal cognitive-screening validation. gaps.gap_statement: No corpus study validates tele-neuropsychological assessment for MCI detection against an in-person gold-standard comparator: the corpus's only tele-assessment paper (P-906, Mexico, N=47) is an exploratory feasibility study reporting autonomy-cognition correlations (moderate) with no in-person reference battery, no diagnostic accuracy metrics (sensitivity/specificity), and no equivalence testing, so remote MoCA/CDT administration remains unvalidated for screening cutoffs while the COVID-era shift to remote assessment continues.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-906 (tele-neuropsych, N=47): authors present correlations between autonomy and MoCA/CDT and CDT-vs-MoCA indicator divergence but perform no comparison against in-person administration and report no classification performance; the paper itself frames the protocol as 'exploratory'. No other registry row contains a tele-assessment design. gaps.gap_statement: No corpus study tests APOE-stratified cognitive-training response with adequate power and full-report methods: the only APOE x cognitive-training evidence (P-902, Moscow, N=117) is a conference abstract reporting lower MoCA in e4/e4 homozygotes before and after 96h/6-week training and genotype-dependent VEGF/FGF-2 changes, but with small e4/e4 stratum, no trial registration, no effect sizes for training-by-genotype interaction, and abstract-level methods.

Corpus CT trials (P-87 robot vs tablet, P-880 VR, P-895 CPR) do not genotype participants. gaps.gap_statement: No corpus study validates a behavioural central-auditory-processing (CAP) test battery against a neuropsychological MCI gold standard: P-910's systematic review (29 articles) shows CAP deficits are consistent in MCI and tests like Gap Detection Threshold, Dichotic Digit Test, Sentence-in-Noise and Digits Backward distinguish MCI from HC, yet no corpus primary study computes ROC/accuracy of such a battery vs a cognitive reference, and P-910 documents that leading MCI diagnostic guidelines exclude CAP tests entirely.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-910: 23/29 studies show CAP deficit in MCI; four named tests distinguish MCI from HC; six guideline articles audited - none include CAP tests. Corpus census (2026-08-26): P-451 uses auditory ERPs (electrophysiological, not behavioural CAP) and does not validate a CAP battery against a cognitive gold standard; no other corpus study reports CAP-based MCI screening accuracy. gaps.gap_statement: No corpus study tests thyroid function (TSH) as a longitudinal predictor of MCI-to-AD conversion: P-908's ADNI analysis (N=1845) is cross-sectional only, finds a sex-specific TSH-cognition association (male-only, OR 0.80) and itself concludes that longitudinal clinical studies are needed to delineate the chronological onset of thyroid-cognition disorders.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-908: cross-sectional ADNI design; explicit conclusion that longitudinal studies are needed; sex-specific association confined to males. Corpus census: no other corpus paper examines TSH or thyroid function in MCI (only P-248 sleep/endocrine-adjacent and P-740 omega-3 blood biomarkers touch endocrine-adjacent territory, neither testing TSH-conversion prediction). gaps.gap_statement: No corpus RCT tests glucose-lowering medications in MCI with an MCI-without-diabetes control group to isolate neuroprotective from glycemic effects: P-915's scoping review (32 studies) explicitly states that large trials using a control group of individuals with MCI without diabetes are required to exclude glycemic-improvement effects, and that evidence for most agents (metformin, TZDs, DPP-4I, GLP-1 RA) comes from observational or small trials with unresolved mechanisms.

gaps.gap_statement: No corpus study tests a combined GABA-targeted + gamma-entrainment intervention in humans: P-916's review (127 studies) shows GABAergic deficits and gamma dysrhythmia form a bidirectional cascade and explicitly proposes synergistic GABA + gamma strategies, while human 40 Hz trials (tACS/TMS/GENUS) are small (n=4-76), short, and inconsistent on amyloid-PET - no combined-protocol trial exists.

gaps.gap_statement: No corpus study combines longitudinal iADL trajectory monitoring with fluid/imaging biomarkers for dementia-conversion prediction: P-925's conversion model (AUC 0.94 with delayed recall + Stroop + Coding + complex iADL) is clinical-only by design - the authors explicitly state diagnosis was made 'based on clinical criteria and we did not include biomarkers' - while P-919 and P-927 both argue biomarkers materially improve MCI staging and prognosis; the corpus lacks a single model joining complex-iADL change with CSF or imaging predictors.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-925: explicit no-biomarker limitation and simple-clinical-model advantage framing. P-919/P-927: biomarker-stratified staging emphasised as the future standard. gaps.gap_statement: No corpus randomized controlled trial tests immersive virtual reality (IVR) cognitive training against a control condition: P-921 (CVSM IVR, n=31, MCI + mild dementia) is an uncontrolled pretest-posttest pilot - the authors report significant improvements on all cognitive measures (P<.001) with no comparator arm, no blinding, and no follow-up; VF-30 documents the corpus-wide fragility of intervention effect sizes; the consensus guidance (P-927) calls for procedures to implement monitoring/cognitive technologies - the corpus lacks the controlled efficacy evidence such implementation requires.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-921: explicitly a pilot pre-post design; improvements cannot be separated from practice effects; no sham/active control, no randomisation, no follow-up. VF-30: intervention pooled effects large but fragile. Corpus census: 0 sham- or active-controlled IVR cognitive-training RCTs. gaps.gap_statement: No corpus study validates reliable-change (SRB/RCI) equations for non-amnestic MCI or beyond ~2-year horizons: P-922/P-923/P-924 validate SRB equations in amnestic MCI at 1-week (P-923) and 1-year (P-924) retest horizons; P-926 applies RCI across SCD/MCI/AD at ~26 months; none covers non-amnestic MCI, >2-year multi-point monitoring, or conversion endpoints - P-924 explicitly notes its samples are amnestic-only and predominantly White.

gaps.gap_statement: No corpus study operationalises anosognosia/metamemory measures (FOK, patient-informant discrepancy) as a formal screening or prognostic tool for rapid MCI-to-AD conversion: P-936 (Liege, 44 aMCI, 23 converters) shows episodic-FOK overestimation and chance-level prediction accuracy specifically in converters but reports no threshold, no screening protocol, and no biomarker confirmation of AD pathology.

gaps.gap_statement: No corpus study validates ocular functional biomarkers (PVEP P100 amplitude, FERG latencies) longitudinally for MCI-to-AD conversion: P-933 (N=59) links P100/m-RNFL to hippocampal volume cross-sectionally and P-830 pools structural retinal markers, but no corpus study follows ocular-functional change over time or tests conversion prediction with them.

gaps.gap_statement: No corpus study evaluates smoking-cessation (or smoking-stratified management) effects on MCI trajectories: P-934 (ADNI, 870 MCI) shows smoking history accelerates functional and entorhinal-cortex decline, and P-521 shows smoking-related NBM connectivity disruption, but no corpus study tests whether cessation reverses or slows these trajectories.

C-244 (P-955 vs P-1084) is filed as documented_incommensurability with genuine_conflict false: P-955's latent class analysis labels FEWER participants MCI than clinical consensus (41% LCA vs 44% consensus vs 53% actuarial) while P-1084's agnes clustering 'identified more MCI cases than consensus diagnosis', and the pair fails five registry gates (Task_Type T6 vs T2, study_design_type, task_substage, population_specificity, metric type). gaps.gap_statement: The WMH-progression threshold for dementia/MCI risk (P-967: >=1.4 mL over 48 months, OR 2.89) has no external replication and no trial-endpoint validation: P-967 is a single post hoc SPRINT MIND analysis with 33 events and one follow-up MRI.

gaps.gap_statement: Sleep measurement and outcome reporting in MCI/early-dementia studies are methodologically heterogeneous with no core outcome set: P-963 (PRISMA scoping review, 188 studies, 17,139 participants) documents this heterogeneity but no corpus study applies a harmonised sleep protocol to MCI.

gaps.gap_statement: Routine-care dementia risk scores (CIDER, P-973; validated in NACC/PROMPT/ADNI - all high-income specialist settings) have never been validated in low-resource or primary-care settings where diagnostic coverage is 5-10% (P-977 World Alzheimer Report): the settings that most need pragmatic triage are the ones unvalidated.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-973 validates CIDER only in NACC (US ADRCs), PROMPT (Calgary tertiary), ADNI - no LMIC/primary-care cohort; P-977 documents 40-50% HIC vs 5-10% LMIC diagnostic coverage. gaps.gap_statement: Has any non-pharmacological intervention study in MCI (exercise, dance movement, virtual-reality cognitive rehabilitation, or multicomponent) reported a primary outcome battery harmonised across the three most-cited reviews (Liu 2023 exercise NMA, Tao 2023 dance MA, Tortora 2024 VR-CRT PRISMA) to enable direct effect-size pooling across modalities, instead of the current per-study outcome heterogeneity that forced all three reviews to either skip meta-analysis (P-1035) or include only same-outcome RCTs (P-1032, P-1033)?
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-1032 (exercise NMA): high heterogeneity in mind-body and multicomponent nodes; depression scale heterogeneity forced re-grouping. P-1033 (DMI MA): 8 of 29 studies in the meta-analysis subset due to outcome heterogeneity. P-1035 (VR-CRT PRISMA): narrative synthesis only, meta-analysis not feasible. All three reviews independently identified outcome heterogeneity as their primary methodological limitation; no study in the corpus reports a harmonised battery applied across all three intervention families.

gaps.closure_criteria: A multi-modality primary RCT or pragmatic study in MCI patients that applies a single pre-specified primary outcome battery (e.g., MoCA + GDS + a balance measure) across exercise, dance and VR-CRT arms, enabling direct effect-size comparison. Cross-paper convergence from P-1032, P-1033 and P-1035 independently establishing the methodological need for such a study.
gaps.human_evaluation_note: G5 review (delegated evaluator 2026-08-28): cross-paper convergence from 3 independent reviews; not a single-paper limitation; corpus-level methodological gap.

gaps.gap_statement: Has any published study or HTA framework proposed or evaluated a harmonised East-Asian cost-effectiveness threshold or willingness-to-pay benchmark for MCI disease-modifying treatments that integrates national WTP evidence (e.g., Japan-style amyloid-PET WTP from P-1030) with national preference-based utility inputs (e.g., Thailand-style EQ-5D-5L utility across the MCI-dementia continuum from P-1031) into a single regional decision rule, rather than each country using its own ad-hoc threshold?
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-1030 documents a Japan-specific WTP value (23.3% / 41.0% / 500000 JPY) and 4-year DMT cost projection (780B-1.4T JPY). P-1031 documents Thailand-specific EQ-5D-5L utilities across the MCI-dementia severity spectrum (0.91 -> 0.33). Both papers generate country-specific HTA inputs but neither proposes or evaluates a regional harmonised framework. Cross-paper convergence: each paper supplies one half of a regional cost-effectiveness framework but neither is integrated.

gaps.gap_statement: Has any US administrative-claims study built a single integrated cognitive-decline pathway model that quantifies (i) the upstream contribution of atrial fibrillation and anticoagulation exposure to incident cognitive impairment (P-1028 NIS OR 1.48 / 0.79) AND (ii) the downstream 2-year MCI->AD risk gradient (P-1029 MarketScan 9.73-21.6-40.1%) in the same cohort, rather than two separate claims datasets answering two separate questions?
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-1028 uses NIS 2016-2020 and answers the upstream question; P-1029 uses MarketScan 2016-2019 and answers the downstream question. Both are retrospective US claims-based studies, but no single study has integrated the two endpoints. The AF-MCI-AD pathway is implicit in the cognitive-decline literature but no claims-based study has reported it as a single integrated model.

gaps.gap_statement: Clinical trials in MCI/AD rarely correct statistical analysis for short-term practice effects, which mask subtle cognitive decline in the placebo arm and inflate apparent treatment effects (P-1042 1-week retest study; composite z-score of change F(2,163)=181.9, p<0.001, intact > MCI > AD; practice-effect magnitude related to cognition, mood, daily functioning).
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-1042 multivariate study shows practice-effect magnitude is driven by cognitive severity, mood (GDS) and daily functioning (QDRS), and that 1-week retest gain in MCI is non-trivial; standard AD/MCI trial endpoints (ADAS-Cog, MMSE, MoCA) are typically administered at intervals that overlap with practice-effect windows, and prior meta-analyses flag this as inflating placebo-arm scores. gaps.gap_statement: Corpus-wide absence: auditory duration discrimination psychophysics (sub-second 640-1950ms vs supra-second 2440-7440ms); pse, dl, rt; cerad word list linear mixed-effects models (r lme4/lmertest); psychometric function fitting (quickpsy); pearson correlations modality never applied to MCI detection (T1) despite appearing in corpus for other tasks.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Systematic scan: 1 papers use auditory duration discrimination psychophysics (sub-second 640-1950ms vs supra-second 2440-7440ms); pse, dl, rt; cerad word list linear mixed-effects models (r lme4/lmertest); psychometric function fitting (quickpsy); pearson correlations modality but none apply it to T1 task.
