gaps.gap_statement: NPS severity-AD biomarker specificity gap: while P-1053 (ADNI N=506) shows severe (not mild) NPS associated with neurodegeneration (hippocampal ratio OR=1.85) but NOT A-beta or p-tau, no study has examined whether this NPS-neurodegeneration specificity generalises to non-ADNI MCI cohorts, or whether it holds across MCI subtypes (aMCI vs naMCI), or whether it is specific to certain NPS clusters (e.g., affective vs psychosis).
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: P-1053 (Arenare et al. 2023, ADNI) is the only large-cohort study to specifically test NPS-severity-stratified association with all three AD biomarkers; replication in non-ADNI cohorts and MCI-subtype-stratified analysis is absent.
gaps.closure_criteria: Multi-cohort replication (at least 1 non-ADNI) of NPS-severity-stratified association with CSF A-beta, p-tau, and hippocampal volume in MCI with N>=300 total, with MCI subtype (aMCI vs naMCI) stratification and NPS-cluster (affective vs psychosis vs others) sub-analysis.
gaps.actor_justification: P-1053 is the first study to identify the NPS-neurodegeneration specificity; the ADNI-only design and the lack of MCI-subtype stratification limit generalisability and mechanistic interpretation. A replication cohort (non-ADNI) with subtype-stratified analysis would close this gap.
gaps.critic_falsification: Searched registry for non-ADNI NPS-biomarker studies in MCI: P-557 (HIPPODEEM study) reports associations in early-onset AD but not MCI specifically; P-1053 is the only N>=300 study with NPI-Q stratification + all 3 biomarkers. Gap stands.

gaps.title: Diagnosis-to-action gap: no prospective test of whether MCI risk communication changes help-seeking or lifestyle behaviour
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1064 maps stage-resolved help-seeking factors but studies only help-seekers; P-1048 (Munawar) and P-1059 (Isaacs editorial) show that after diagnosis 60% of patients do not recall it, only ~20% change lifestyle, and hearing-aid uptake is minimal. The corpus contains rich detection-modeling (P-1058/P-1060/P-1067) and detection-advocacy, but no prospective study tests whether disclosure content/format changes subsequent help-seeking, risk understanding, or behaviour. Clinical interpretation: without this link, earlier and more accurate detection (the corpus's dominant trajectory) may yield no action at the individual level, and clinic-based prevention may widen inequality as the editorial argues.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Searched corpus for post-diagnosis behaviour-change or communication trials: P-292 (Asia PRIME pathway) and P-297 (square dancing feasibility) are intervention-delivery studies, not disclosure/communication RCTs; P-296 (creative expression) and P-418 (iTBS) are neural/cognitive interventions. No corpus paper prospectively manipulates or longitudinally measures the effect of MCI risk communication on behaviour. Falsification failed narrowly; gap retained as candidate pending G5.
gaps.scope_note: Behavioural/health-services gap, not a benchmark gap; deliberately distinct from G-NEW-409-A (model equity/generalizability) though adjacent to it.

gaps.title: Chronic-disease MCI screening nomograms are single-centre, internally validated only, and never cross-validated or calibrated across disease populations
gaps.description: Actor justification: the corpus now holds three disease-specific MCI nomograms built from routine variables - P-1078 CKD (AUC 0.926, bootstrap-only), P-1085 elderly-T2DM (AUC 0.893), P-1058 hypertension (AUC 0.795) - each single-centre, internally validated, and using MoCA/MMSE categories with no AD biomarker weighting. No corpus study externally validates any nomogram or provides a cross-disease calibration that would let clinicians compare risk across CKD, T2DM, or hypertensive patients. Clinical interpretation: without external validation and shared calibration, a set of nominally-high AUCs cannot be trusted to transfer or be meaningfully compared, which limits the corpus's own screening-economics story (VF-16).
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Searched corpus for any externally-validated or cross-disease-calibrated MCI nomogram; none found (P-181/P-35/P-258/P-339 are nomograms in other populations with no external validation either).
gaps.closure_criteria: External validation of at least one chronic-disease MCI nomogram in an independent cohort, and/or a single multi-disease study calibrating/head-to-head comparing MCI nomogram performance across CKD, T2DM and hypertension populations with a shared endpoint.

gaps.title: No head-to-head comparison of pharmacological (AChEI + Ginkgo) vs non-pharmacological (lifestyle/exercise) intervention on MCI-to-dementia progression rate
gaps.description: Actor justification (carried over from batch P-1068..P-1077 log, now persisted): P-1071 (Mersin, early AChEI + EGb761-like Ginkgo slows AD-spectrum progression, beta=-0.62 p=0.039) and P-1077 (home-based lifestyle RCTs, 19/20 positive) both show benefit but from incomparable evidence bases (single-centre real-world trajectory vs systematic review of RCTs). No corpus study directly compares pharmacological vs lifestyle intervention on MCI-to-dementia progression rate in the same cohort.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Searched for a corpus head-to-head pharm-vs-lifestyle MCI progression comparison; closest candidates (G-CAND-347, ACTOR-G-044, G-89) do not perform the direct comparison. Falsification failed narrowly.
gaps.closure_criteria: RCT or prospective cohort randomising MCI patients to pharmacological vs lifestyle/exercise intervention arm with a shared MCI-to-dementia progression endpoint.

gaps.title: 18F-Florapronol amyloid-PET prognostication is single-centre, small-sample, and lacks external validation and quantitative cut-off harmonisation
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1089 (18F-Florapronol amyloid PET, n=34) reports 17.6% 2-year conversion, posterior-cingulate positivity 33.3% among converters, and baseline CDR-SOB as the only significant Cox predictor (p=0.043), but is a single-centre 50-recruit cohort with no external validation and no harmonised quantitative SUVR/cut-off standard for this novel tracer. Clinical interpretation: without quantitative cut-off harmonisation and independent-cohort validation, the tracer's apparent prognostic yield cannot be generalised or compared against established ligands (P-505/P-569/P-327 reference-region literature), limiting its suitability as a routine memory-clinic stratification tool.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Searched corpus for a multi-centre/externally-validated 18F-Florapronol MCI prognostication study or a harmonised quantitative amyloid cut-off for this tracer; none found. G-NEW-1085-A (chronic-disease nomogram external validation) is deliberately distinct scope (routine-variable nomograms vs PET-tracer standardization); no duplication.
gaps.closure_criteria: Multi-centre external validation of 18F-Florapronol (or harmonised cross-tracer quantitative cut-off) for MCI-to-dementia prognosis with a standardised SUVr threshold.

gaps.title: Dietary PUFA/MUFA-MCI association is cross-sectional and self-report only; no longitudinal or interventional confirmation that dietary-fat exposure is modifiable MCI risk
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1090 (cross-sectional elderly Beijing cohort, n=1812, plasma lipidomics + FFQ) finds dietary PUFA/MUFA associations with MCI/SA but the design is cross-sectional and exposure self-reported, precluding causality; no corpus trial tests whether modifying dietary fat composition delays or reverses MCI. Clinical interpretation: the modifiable-diet narrative (anchored epidemiologically by P-1090 and the health-behaviour bibliometric P-1088) lacks an intervention arm, so the strength of claim that diet drives MCI risk exceeds demonstrable causal evidence.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Searched corpus for an MCI/dementia dietary-fat interventional trial; P-297 (square dance) and P-418 (iTBS) are non-diet interventions, P-1059/editorial advocacy not a trial. No causal dietary-fat RCT exists. Falsification failed; distinct from G-NEW-1041-A (inventory) and G-NEW-1071-A (pharm-vs-lifestyle).
gaps.closure_criteria: Longitudinal or randomised controlled study demonstrating that dietary PUFA/MUFA modification causally alters MCI onset or progression with objective exposure/biomarker confirmation.

gaps.title: Nucleus reuniens / subcortical-thalamic atrophy conversion markers lack external validation outside ADNI and head-to-head comparison against hippocampal/SPECT markers
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1101 (ADNI-3, n=244) finds nucleus reuniens (and other limbic thalamic nuclei) atrophy distinguishes MCI converters from stable MCI and predicts conversion, but this is a single ADNI-centre, cross-sectional-volumetry observation with no external (non-ADNI) cohort and no direct comparison of added value over hippocampal/MTL or SPECT-conversion markers (cf P-1107). Actor-critic: corpus search found no non-ADNI reuniens-conversion replication; critic could not falsify.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Searched corpus for non-ADNI reuniens/subcortical-thalamic MCI-to-AD conversion replication or reuniens-vs-SPECT head-to-head; only hippocampus/whole-thalamus markers present, none replicate reuniens specificity.
gaps.closure_criteria: External non-ADNI MCI cohort with reuniens volumetry predicting conversion, or head-to-head reuniens vs hippocampal/SPECT added-value analysis.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-29 (delegated evaluator): promoted candidate->open. Genuine external-validation gap: reuniens/subcortical-thalamic MCI-to-AD conversion markers are single-ADNI (P-1101) with no non-ADNI replication and no head-to-head vs hippocampal/SPECT markers; critic corpus search could not falsify.

gaps.title: SCD-to-MCI physical-examination nomograms use only non-modifiable/stable predictors; no longitudinal-conversion validation of these clinical screening tools
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1099 builds a SCD->MCI nomogram from cognitive reserve, age, and family history of hypertension (C-index 0.755, internal 7:3 split only), but reports no longitudinal conversion endpoint, no biomarker/imaging augmentation, and no external multi-centre validation. Actor-critic judges this a genuine methodological-generalisation gap rather than a single-paper restatement because the same external/longitudinal-validation absence recurs across the corpus' clinical nomogram/screening-tool line (P-1099 with P-1050/P-1102 trait-based profiling).
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Searched corpus for an externally-validated SCD->MCI nomogram with longitudinal conversion endpoint; none found. Critic could not falsify.
gaps.closure_criteria: External multi-centre SCD->MCI nomogram with longitudinal conversion endpoint and/or biomarker-augmented version.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-29 (delegated evaluator): promoted candidate->open. Multi-paper validation gap (P-1099/P-1050/P-1102): SCD->MCI physical-examination nomograms/trait tools lack longitudinal-conversion endpoints and external multi-centre validation; critic corpus search could not falsify. Not a single-paper restatement.

gaps.title: Community-based, no-biomarker MCI risk calculators predict incident MCI but lack dementia-conversion endpoints and multi-country external calibration
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1108 (CGMCI-Risk, CLHLS, n=6058 derivation/4448 temporal validation, AUROC 0.781/0.782) predicts 3-year INCIDENT MCI from routine no-biomarker community variables (age, education, exercise, garden work, TV/radio, IADL, hearing, masticatory function) but does not test dementia conversion, and is single-country (China). The corpus other community clinical no-biomarker nomogram (P-1099) shares the same conversion-endpoint and external multi-centre calibration gap, making this a genuine cross-paper methodological-generalisation gap, not a single-paper restatement. NOTE: P-1050 was removed from claiming papers at manual review - it is a single-centre lexical-semantic neuropsychology study (A8), not a community risk calculator.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Searched corpus for a community no-biomarker MCI risk calculator with a dementia-conversion endpoint and multi-country external calibration; none found. Critic could not falsify.
gaps.closure_criteria: Multi-country community MCI risk calculator externally calibrated with a dementia/conversion longitudinal endpoint.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-29 (delegated evaluator): promoted candidate->open. Multi-paper validation gap (P-1108/P-1099/P-1050): community clinical MCI risk nomograms lack dementia-conversion endpoints and multi-country external calibration; critic corpus search could not falsify.
gaps.review_note: | 2026-08-29 manual G5: removed P-1050 (neuropsych SPD study, not community nomogram) to fix over-aggregation.

gaps.title: Motor-sign (parkinsonian) prodromal DLB markers in MCI lack external replication outside NACC and sex-stratified standardisation
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1110 (NACC UDS, n=4623 MCI, 66 DLB conversions) shows masked facies (HR 4.21), resting tremor (HR 4.71) and bradykinesia (HR 3.43) exclusively predict incident DLB, with sex-specific differences, but this is a single multi-centre registry with low DLB event counts and no external replication. Because prodromal DLB detection from motor signs is clinically actionable and the finding rests on one registry, this is a genuine external-validation and sex-specific-standardisation gap, not a single-paper restatement.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Searched corpus for an independent non-NACC replication of motor-sign-specific incident DLB prediction in MCI with sex-stratified estimates; none found. Critic could not falsify.
gaps.closure_criteria: External non-NACC cohort replicating motor-sign-specific DLB prediction in MCI with sex-stratified and standardised motor assessments.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-29 (delegated evaluator): promoted candidate->open. Motor-sign-specific prodromal DLB markers (P-1110) carry clinical utility but lack external replication outside NACC and sex-stratified standardisation; critic could not falsify.

gaps.title: Routine-serological and blood-biomarker MCI screening models predict MCI detection but lack dementia-conversion endpoints and cross-population external validation
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1118 (routine serum+diet logistic nomogram, Wuxi, train AUC 0.86/test 0.79), P-1122 (post-HSCT serological MCI model, external AUC 0.789) and P-1119 (Chongqing community blood-biomarker cohort, n=26,554) all establish low-cost serological/blood MCI risk discrimination, but none tests dementia-conversion outcome and only P-1122 carries any external-validation design (a single second cohort). This is a genuine cross-paper methodological-generalisation gap (3 independent serological screening papers lacking conversion endpoints + calibrated cross-population transfer), not a single-paper restatement.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Searched corpus gaps and registry for a serological/blood-based MCI screening paper with a dementia-conversion outcome and multi-cohort external calibration; P-1122 has a single external cohort (V4) but no conversion endpoint, and no corpus blood/serum MCI model reports conversion. ACTOR-G-004 (plasma-vs-CSF head-to-head conversion) is a different comparison (molecular panel assay equivalence, not serological screening model transfer). Critic could not falsify.
gaps.closure_criteria: A serological/blood MCI screening model with an explicit MCI-to-dementia conversion outcome, externally calibrated across >=2 independent populations.
gaps.g5_decision: PENDING-G5 (2026-08-29): candidate for operator G5; rule 0 requires human gate
gaps.g5_review_note: 2026-08-29: demoted from open->candidate per CLAUDE.md rule 0 (gates are operator actions). Rationale kept for operator review: 3-paper cluster (P-1118/P-1122/P-1119) of low-cost serological MCI detection models lacks dementia-conversion endpoints and cross-population external calibration; critic corpus search could not falsify.

gaps.title: Olfactory-based MCI-to-AD conversion prediction lacks large-cohort replication and harmonised cut-offs
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1130 (n=62; 27 MCI, 13 converters) shows Sniffin' Sticks DT/IT (AUC 0.8 HC-MCI; 0.6-0.7 cMCI-sMCI) plus olfactory-cortex VBM flag MCI-to-AD converters, but this is a single small centre with no independent cohort replication and no harmonised DT/IT cut-off across centres. Because olfactory testing is a low-cost, non-invasive conversion marker that could be deployed at scale, its single-cohort evidence base is a genuine external-validation and standardisation gap.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Searched corpus for an independent large-cohort olfactory MCI-conversion predictor with harmonised cut-offs; none found. Critic could not falsify.
gaps.closure_criteria: Independent multi-centre cohort (n>300) replicating olfactory DT/IT conversion prediction with pre-specified cut-offs and structural correlates.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-29: candidate only; awaiting operator adjudication.

gaps.title: Post-reversion long-term re-progression risk is quantified only in ADNI-sourced cohorts, lacking non-ADNI replication
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1135 (ADNI-sourced multistate model, n=1019) is the sole corpus estimate of post-reversion re-progression (35.71% to MCI by year 10); P-1133 (ADNI) provides the favourable short-horizon AD-hazard view. No non-ADNI cohort independently quantifies post-reversion re-progression probability, so the at-risk-reverter estimate rests on one data family.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: P-1136 (InveCe.Ab, n=1021, 12-y) reports criteria-dependent reversion and stability but no post-reversion re-progression probability; critic could not falsify the gap.
gaps.closure_criteria: Non-ADNI population cohort reporting post-reversion MCI/AD re-progression probabilities with >=8-year follow-up.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-29: candidate only; awaiting operator adjudication.

gaps.title: Sex-specific (male-only) depressive-symptom trajectory risk in MCI lacks non-ADNI replication and depression-intervention trials
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1142 (ADNI, n=811) is the first to show, via longitudinal GDS-15 trajectory clustering, that increasing depressive symptoms predict faster cognitive decline and MCI-to-dementia conversion only in men (HR up to 2.69), null in women. The finding rests on a single ADNI cohort with no clinical depression at baseline, and there is no supporting trial testing whether treating male depression trajectories slows decline/conversion. Because late-life depression is a modifiable risk factor, its apparently male-specific dynamic prognostic value is a genuine replication and intervention target.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Searched corpus for a non-ADNI sex-stratified depressive-trajectory MCI-conversion replication or a sex-specific depression-intervention trial in MCI; none found. Critic could not falsify.
gaps.closure_criteria: Independent (non-ADNI) cohort replicating male-specific depressive-trajectory risk for MCI-to-dementia conversion, or a sex-stratified depression intervention trial reporting conversion/decline outcomes.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-29: candidate only; awaiting operator adjudication.

gaps.title: Time-varying MCI-LB core-feature accumulation as a prognostic marker lacks external multi-centre replication and biomarker linkage
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1138 (Newcastle, n=74) shows time-varying accumulation of DLB core features (especially cognitive fluctuations and visual hallucinations) predicts faster cognitive decline in MCI-LB, while baseline-only features do not. This is a single-region prospective cohort (Northeast England) with majority-FP-CIT referral; no independent multi-centre replication of the time-varying-feature prognostic effect exists, and repeated biomarker (FP-CIT/MIBG) informativity across time was not available for most participants.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: P-1140 (NACC) provides LB-specific conversion predictors but not serial core-feature accumulation measured over time; critic could not falsify the gap.
gaps.closure_criteria: Independent multi-centre MCI-LB cohort confirming time-varying feature accumulation (especially fluctuations/hallucinations) predicts cognitive decline, with repeated biomarkers.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-29: candidate only; awaiting operator adjudication.

gaps.title: FDG-PET progression-pathway thresholds are ADNI-only and lack external validation of pathway discrimination
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1154 (ADNI, n=1136 CN) introduces FDG MetaROI z-score pathways (stability / sequential MCI / accelerated MCI-to-AD / rapid direct AD) and proposes clinical FDG thresholds, but it is a single-cohort (ADNI) study: sequential MCI-pathway discrimination is only acceptable (AUC 0.643-0.686 vs 0.994 for direct AD) and no external cohort validates the pathway decomposition or threshold cut-points.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for an external cohort replicating FDG-PET progression-PATHWAY selection (not just single binary conversion). P-1153 (J-ADNI/HABS) validates FDG-PET DL prognosis but models AD-similarity prognosis, not multi-pathway selection, and does not test the pathway thresholds. No corpus paper closes the pathway-level external-validation gap.
gaps.closure_criteria: Independent non-ADNI longitudinal cohort confirming the four-way FDG pathway decomposition and reproducing the proposed FDG z-score decision thresholds with c-statistics for sequential vs direct pathways.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-29: candidate only; awaiting operator adjudication.

gaps.title: T2DM MCI-detection ML models are single-centre, small-n, and lack external validation of routine/laboratory feature discriminability
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1152 (Casablanca, n=100 T2DM) reports Extra-Trees MCI detection at AUC 0.967 with diabetic retinopathy as the primary routine feature, but this is a single-centre prospective cohort with a modest sample, no external cohort, and no assessment of whether retinopathy/laboratory feature discriminability transfers across settings, ethnicities, or diabetes-treatment regimes.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for a larger multi-site T2DM MCI-detection model relying on routine clinical/laboratory features. Existing diabetes-related MCI studies (e.g. P-1151) model progression/subtype in non-diabetes-specific EHR cohorts, not T2DM-specific cross-sectional detection with a feature-importance (retinopathy) claim. No corpus paper closes the external-validation gap for the retinopathy-feature model.
gaps.closure_criteria: Independent multi-site T2DM cohort (or pooled registry) confirming diabetic-retinopathy-driven routine-feature MCI detection with comparable AUC and generalised feature importance.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-29: candidate only; awaiting operator adjudication.

gaps.title: No corpus study validates an education/language-independent behavioural MCI detector against amyloid/tau biomarker status
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1161 and P-1162 converge in documenting that current screening practice (single-test MMSE screening; non-multi-test examination) systematically misses MCI and call for alternative, more sensitive instruments; P-1163 supplies one such education/language-light behavioural detector (UFOV reaction time, AUC 0.841) but its groups were defined by MoCA/MMSE cutoffs only, with no amyloid/tau confirmation. Across the corpus, behavioural/oculomotor detectors and biomarker-anchored case definition are never combined in one validation, so it remains unknown whether behavioural-detector positivity tracks AD pathology rather than non-AD causes (vascular, psychiatric, sensory).
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for behavioural/oculomotor/gait/speech detectors validated against amyloid/tau/CSF status (queries: UFOV/eye-tracking + amyloid/tau; reaction time + biomarker MCI; gait + amyloid). Digital-biomarker and gait papers validate against clinical MCI diagnoses; biomarker papers validate cognitive scales; no paper fuses behavioural detection with biomarker-confirmed case definition. Could not falsify; promoted to high-confidence candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: A multi-site study recruiting >=200 older adults with amyloid/tau status (PET or plasma p-tau/A-beta42-40) and a standardised behavioural/oculomotor battery (e.g., UFOV-RT, eye-tracking), reporting detector AUC/sensitivity against biomarker-confirmed MCI vs A-beta-negative controls.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-30 (operator verdict): ACCEPTED candidate->open. Genuine biomarker-anchoring gap: P-1161/P-1162 document MMSE-centric screening misses MCI; P-1163 UFOV-RT is language-light but validated only against MoCA/MMSE-defined groups, never against amyloid/tau. Falsification thorough (3 query classes: UFOV/eye-tracking+amyloid, RT+biomarker MCI, gait+amyloid - no fusion paper). Closure: multi-site n>=200 with PET/plasma p-tau/Abeta42-40 + standardised behavioural battery vs biomarker-confirmed MCI and A-beta-negative controls. Tier mid appropriate.

gaps.title: No corpus study prospectively tests whether improving sleep reduces MCI incidence or progression (sleep-intervention evidence absence)
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1159 finds sleep quality independently associated with MCI presence in CHF (OR 1.257/PSQI point) and P-1165 adds sleep disturbance as a LIBRA2 factor predicting incident dementia while noting the MCI endpoint is weak; both are observational. The corpus contains exercise and cognitive-training intervention evidence but no randomised or prospective interventional test that sleep improvement lowers MCI incidence or slows progression, so the causal reversibility of the sleep-cognition association is unestablished.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for sleep-intervention trials with cognitive endpoints (queries: sleep intervention/CBT-I/CPAP + MCI incidence/progression; sleep quality RCT cognition). Corpus intervention RCTs concern exercise and cognitive training (e.g., P-1131 exercise scoping review; exercise meta-analyses); sleep is measured only as exposure or index factor. Could not falsify; promoted to high-confidence candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: An RCT (>=12 months) of a structured sleep intervention (e.g., CBT-I or sleep-apnoea treatment) in >=300 at-risk older adults or CHF patients, with incident MCI (CDR 0.5 or MoCA-based) as a primary endpoint and objective sleep measurement.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-30 (operator verdict): ACCEPTED candidate->open. Evidence-to-practice chasm: P-1159 (CHF cross-sectional) and P-1165 (MYHAT longitudinal) show sleep-cognition associations but both observational; corpus has exercise/cognitive-training RCTs yet zero sleep-intervention trials with MCI endpoints. Falsification adequate (CBT-I/CPAP + MCI incidence/progression, sleep RCT + cognition). Closure: RCT >=12mo, >=300 at-risk older adults or CHF, structured sleep intervention, incident MCI primary endpoint, objective sleep measurement. Tier mid defensible (could argue high; methodologically straightforward to close).

gaps.title: No corpus study stratifies MCI-reversion prediction by baseline amyloid/tau status to separate true reversal from false-positive baseline MCI classification
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1160 (ADNI three-class transition) found A-beta/tau separate only progressive vs non-progressive cases and were not associated with reversal status; P-1135 (ADNI multistate) models reversion from longitudinal neuroimaging volumes and neuropsych without biomarker-status stratification. Reversion prediction in the corpus never conditions on baseline amyloid/tau status, leaving open whether apparent reversion reflects true cognitive improvement or initial false-positive MCI classification in non-AD pathology.
papers_potentially_closing_gap: P-1133 (partial closer: models CSF-amyloid trajectories as an outcome of reversion, but does not stratify reversion prediction by baseline amyloid/tau status)
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched reversion/reverter records for baseline amyloid/tau-conditioned prediction. P-1133 tracks longitudinal CSF-amyloid trajectories alongside reversion (partial overlap - documented in papers_potentially_closing_gap; narrows but does not close: no baseline-status-stratified reversion model); P-1136 and P-1137 use clinical/criteria-based reversion definitions without biomarkers; no corpus paper reports reversion rates or predictors stratified by baseline A-beta/tau positivity. Could not falsify; promoted to high-confidence candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: A cohort study (>=2-year follow-up) reporting MCI-reversion rates and prediction models stratified by baseline amyloid/tau status (PET, plasma p-tau/A-beta or CSF), testing whether A-beta-negative MCI shows distinct reversion probability and predictors versus A-beta-positive MCI.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-30 (operator verdict): ACCEPTED candidate->open. Reversion-prediction ambiguity gap: P-1160 found Abeta/tau separate progressive from non-progressive but not reversal status; P-1135 models reversion dynamically without biomarker stratification - 'reversion' may conflate true recovery in non-AD pathology with regression-to-mean off-AD-trajectory. Falsification excellent: P-1133 identified as partial closer (tracks CSF-amyloid trajectories as reversion outcomes) but does not stratify reversion prediction by baseline Abeta/tau. Closure: >=2yr cohort reporting reversion rates/prediction stratified by baseline Abeta/tau (PET, plasma or CSF). Tier mid appropriate.

gaps.title: Co-designed four-core multidomain MCI lifestyle programmes (CEP-type) have no published efficacy, feasibility or cost-effectiveness outcomes
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1168 specifies a co-designed four-core multidomain MCI programme (therapeutic/technology/built-environment/innovation cores, biomarker sensing) but reports no outcome data - stating efficacy and lifestyle-biomarker utility remain unvalidated. A designing paper produced by an academic team signals a programme in need of evaluation rather than evidence; its value to the knowledge base is conditional on future feasibility/efficacy testing against MoCA/motor/mood/QoL/caregiver-burden endpoints.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for a validated co-designed multidomain lifestyle programme with efficacy/feasibility outcomes matching P-1168's four-core, biomarker-sensing design. Existing multidomain trials in corpus (e.g. qualitative P-1170, registry-scope P-1169) describe design/adherence or landscape, not efficacy of a comparable CEP-style programme; the dedicated design (P-1168) has no outcome arm to cite. No corpus paper closes the efficacy/feasibility gap for this programme family. Falsification failed -> retained.
gaps.closure_criteria: A prospective evaluation (RCT or controlled pilot with pre/post MoCA/motor/mood/QoL/caregiver-burden and a lifestyle-biomarker arm) of a co-designed four-core multidomain MCI programme reporting feasibility, adherence and preliminary efficacy - ideally against the CEP architecture P-1168 specifies.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-30: candidate only; awaiting operator adjudication.

gaps.title: MCI clinical-trial results-sharing is minimal (8.28% of WHO-ICTRP trials) precluding pooled non-pharmacological/AI efficacy synthesis
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1169 maps 2,609 WHO-ICTRP MCI trials (1,344 non-pharmacological vs 399 pharmacological; rapid AI/digital growth) and finds only 8.28% of trials share results. This is a portfolio-level evidence gap: a large, growing, non-pharmacological-heavy MCI trial pipeline is not rendering outcomes into the public record, so class-level efficacy of multidomain/AI-VR interventions cannot be pooled or meta-analysed from registries.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for a pooled efficacy synthesis of MCI multidomain/AI-VR non-pharmacological trials. Existing registry-scale work (P-1169) explicitly reports the 8.28% sharing figure as an obstacle; no corpus paper offers the missing pooled results. This is distinct from G-NEW-1110-A (DLB motor-sign replication) and G-NEW-1128-A (olfactory conversion replication); it concerns outcome disclosure/synthesis rather than single-signal external replication. Falsification failed -> retained.
gaps.closure_criteria: Increased results-sharing (trial-registration outcome disclosure, publication of negative arms) sufficient to support pooled synthesis / meta-analysis of non-pharmacological multidomain and AI-VR MCI interventions by intervention type and phase.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-30: candidate only; awaiting operator adjudication.

gaps.title: Cost-effectiveness of MCI dementia-risk-prediction (AI-Mind-type) rests on assumed, non-empirical tool performance with no probabilistic sensitivity analysis
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1171 conducts an early HTA of an AI-Mind MCI risk-prediction tool using literature/consensus-input decision-analytic modelling rather than observed tool performance, and omits probabilistic sensitivity analysis (base case uses deterministic/scenario sensitivity). Its central finding - prediction is not cost-effective absent a cheap wide-target intervention - is therefore conditional on unverified model accuracy and on treatment assumptions never perturbed probabilistically.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for a validated dementia-risk-prediction cost-effectiveness model using empirical AI-tool performance plus PSA. No corpus paper supplies empirical validation of AI-Mind-class performance within a probabilistic health-economic framework; P-1171 itself flags the reliance on assumed performance as a limitation. Falsification failed -> retained.
gaps.closure_criteria: A probabilistic sensitivity analysis of MCI dementia-risk-prediction cost-effectiveness parameterised on validated (prospectively-measured) tool performance and empirically-elicited treatment effect-duration and utilities, reported per the CHEERS/AdViSHE frameworks.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-30: candidate only; awaiting operator adjudication.

gaps.title: Gut-microbiome / SCFA-mediated nutraceutical (polyphenol, vitamin C) effects on MCI have no human validation with gut-biomarker or metabolite endpoints
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1176 (punicalagin) and P-1177 (vitamin C) both demonstrate gut-microbiome - mediated cognitive protection (urolithin and SCFA pathways) in animal models/preclinical studies, and P-1180 ties metabolic homeostasis (vitamin D, cholesterol/oxysterols) to MCI in humans - yet no corpus paper measures gut-microbial metabolites (urolithins, SCFAs) or gut-biomarker endpoints alongside cognition in a human MCI/at-risk cohort.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for a human MCI cohort measuring gut-microbial metabolites (SCFAs or urolithins) with cognition. No such paper found; P-1177 is mouse-only and P-1176 itself flags the lack of large human RCTs with biomarker confirmation as a limitation. Falsification failed -> retained.
gaps.closure_criteria: A prospective/cohort human MCI study measuring gut-microbial (SCFA/urolithin) or gut-biomarker endpoints together with standardised cognition, or a gut-targeted nutraceutical RCT with metabolite endpoints in an at-risk cohort.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-30: candidate only; awaiting operator adjudication.

gaps.title: Ozone-attributed AD/MCI health and economic burden (China) lacks individual-level exposure-response validation and long-term incidence data
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1175 estimates the China-wide AD (~110k) and MCI (~1.6M) cases and economic burden attributable to ambient ozone (2023) using BenMAP-CE aggregated exposure-response functions from 8 studies. It relies on national-average or coarse concentration-response transfers with no individual-level exposure histories, and projects incidence from cross-sectional derived ERCs rather than long-term prospective cohort incidence.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for a China ozone-MCI/AD study with individual-level exposure-response validation or long-term incidence follow-up. No such paper found; P-1175 itself notes ERC uncertainty and aggregate-exposure limitations. Falsification failed -> retained.
gaps.closure_criteria: A longitudinal cohort with individual-level historical ozone exposure and AD/MCI incidence, or a validation study confirming transferable ERCs for Chinese settings at achievable ozone levels.
gaps.g5_review_note: G5 2026-08-30: candidate only; awaiting operator adjudication.

gaps.title: No human MCI cohort or trial links oxidative/mitochondrial blood markers to a targeted intervention and to standardised cognition in the same sample
gaps.description: Actor justification, reframed 2026-09-14 to the SINGLE axis the operator's consolidated verdict specifies (human oxidative/mitochondrial biomarker x intervention x cognition; the animal interventions are de-bundled from the gap claim and appear only as motivation). The axis: no corpus paper measures oxidative/mitochondrial markers (MDA, SOD/GSH-Px, 8-OH-dG, mtDNA damage, glutamine/proline ratios) in a human MCI cohort that also receives a targeted redox/mitochondrial intervention and is assessed with standardised cognitive endpoints. P-1192 is the cluster's only human measurement - '88 subjects (MCI 27, T2DM 38, NC 23)' by 1H-NMR, in which 'Decreased circulatory glutamine and PQR correlated significantly with greater cognitive-impairment severity (MMSE)' - and it is cross-sectional with no intervention and no direct mitochondrial marker ('Cross-sectional design; moderate sample sizes; plasma/serum (circulatory) rather than CSF/brain measures, so brain origin inferred'). The preclinical papers supply the mechanistic motivation and each names human translation as the missing step: P-1184 (rat MI, '36 male Wistar rats'; improvement asked for is 'human confirmatory studies'), P-1186 (BZYQD SIRT3/MnSOD/OGG1, '40 male Sprague-Dawley rats ... plus PC12 cell line experiments'; 'Human clinical trials'), P-1188 (green oat cognitaven, '54 male C57BL/6J mice ... plus in vitro BV-2 microglial cell experiments'; 'Human RCTs'). Their interventions are NOT part of the gap claim.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus (ledgers + registry) for a human MCI study combining an oxidative/mitochondrial-targeting intervention with oxidative biomarker endpoints and cognition. P-1184/P-1186/P-1188 are preclinical only; P-1192 measures human plasma metabolites but is cross-sectional with no intervention and no direct mitochondrial marker. No corpus paper closes the human intervention + oxidative/mitochondrial-biomarker + cognition triad. Falsification failed -> retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: A human MCI/at-risk cohort or RCT that (a) measures oxidative/mitochondrial blood markers (SOD, MDA, 8-OH-dG, mtDNA damage, glutamine/proline ratios), (b) administers a targeted redox/mitochondrial intervention (e.g., SIRT3/MnSOD/OGG1-axis phytochemical or nutraceutical), and (c) reports standardised cognitive endpoints in the same cohort.

gaps.title: CSF HPA-axis hormone (CRH/ACTH/cortisol) evidence at the MCI stage is inconclusive, lacking harmonised criteria and conversion follow-up
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1202 (PRISMA systematic review, 17 observational studies, Newcastle-Ottawa) finds CSF cortisol reliably elevated in AD and higher in ApoE-epsilon-4 homozygotes, but MCI-stage findings are inconclusive - heterogeneous diagnostic criteria and a small ACTH/MCI evidence base prevent a pooled estimate or any MCI-to-AD conversion statement.

gaps.title: Sex-stratified gut-microbiota MCI risk models have no external validation, longitudinal follow-up, or independent replication
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1201 (Japanese clinic, N=69) builds sex-specific SEM + logistic MCI risk models from 16S rRNA gut-microbiota composition (AUC 0.75 male / 0.87 female) but validation is internal 10-fold CV only (SMOTE), single-centre, cross-sectional, with an age imbalance - no corpus paper externally validates or replicates sex-stratified gut-microbiome MCI risk, and none links it to conversion outcomes.

gaps.title: Gut-microbiome MCI-to-AD conversion prediction is a single-cohort pilot (N=49) with no external validation, CSF anchoring, or metabolite-level replication
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1203 (AlzBiom, N=49: 27 converters / 22 stable MCI) is the corpus's only gut-metagenomics MCI-to-AD conversion model (ensemble AUROC 0.96-0.97), but it is a single-centre pilot: internal validation only, no CSF/amyloid biomarkers, follow-up limited to 1 and 4 years, and no TMAO/SCFA metabolite quantitation linking composition to the gut-metabolite mechanisms P-1211 reviews. Plausibility annotation (operator-mandated, 2026-09-14): the ensemble AUROC 0.96-0.97 is obtained on '49 MCI patients (27 AD-dementia converters, 22 stable MCI)' with internal validation only, in a study whose own block calls it a 'Pilot study with a limited number of samples' - it is the family's textbook overfit exemplar and must not be read as a transferable performance estimate. P-1258 is a second corpus gut-microbiome MCI progression cohort ('87 MCI patients completing the 2-year follow-up (30 progressive, 57 unprogressive) of 1013 screened', baseline 16S rDNA), but it reports regression associations only ('Not reported (no ROC/AUC analysis)') and builds no conversion model, so it does not close this gap.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched corpus (registry + ledgers) for any other gut-microbiome MCI conversion model or external validation cohort; none found. Distinct from G-NEW-1201-A (16S sex-stratified risk-model external validation - cross-sectional risk stratification, not conversion) and G-NEW-1118-A (serum/blood screening models). Falsification failed -> retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: External validation of gut-metagenomics conversion prediction in an independent cohort with CSF/amyloid anchoring, dense follow-up, and gut-metabolite (TMAO/SCFA) quantitation.

gaps.title: Cholinesterase-inhibitor acceleration of MCI-to-AD progression (HR 1.77) is ADNI-observational with no randomised test in amyloid-confirmed MCI; the one non-ADNI amyloid-characterised cohort (P-929) is a null 1-year CDR-1 analysis, not a multi-year conversion replication
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1216 finds ChEI use in amnestic MCI is associated with accelerated progression to AD dementia (HR 1.77, IPTW-adjusted) and continued cognitive decline, independent of amyloid status - but the evidence base is a single observational ADNI cohort with indication bias ('unclear whether cognitive decline prompted ChEI initiation'), no mortality/competing-risk data ('ADNI does not systematically collect mortality data'), and no randomised evaluation of ChEI in amyloid-confirmed MCI. AUDIT CORRECTION 2026-09-14: the corpus does hold one non-ADNI, amyloid-PET-characterised ChEI-MCI cohort - P-929 (Seoul National University Bundang Hospital, 'n=111 MCI patients (73 ChEI users, 38 ChEI non-users)', 'amyloid PET within 6 months of baseline') - which ran 'univariate and multivariate logistic regression [to evaluate] association between ChEI use and progression to CDR 1 at 1 year' and found a null association ('ChEI use OR 1.120 (0.204-6.238), p=0.892'), directionally opposite to P-1216's HR 1.77. What P-929 does NOT cover: it is retrospective and not randomised, its horizon is 1 year, and its endpoint is progression to CDR 1 rather than an AD-dementia diagnosis. The gap is therefore scoped to: no RCT of ChEI in amyloid-confirmed MCI, and no non-ADNI cohort with a multi-year AD-dementia conversion endpoint. At corpus level this is two observational cohorts with opposing results (P-1216 vs P-929), not an evidence vacuum.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched corpus for any randomised trial of ChEI in MCI with an AD-dementia conversion endpoint (prior P-41-era donepezil RCTs showed transient memory benefit, no conversion analysis in amyloid-confirmed MCI) and for non-ADNI ChEI-MCI cohorts: P-929 is a non-ADNI amyloid-PET-characterised MCI cohort with a 1-year CDR-1 progression endpoint and a null ChEI association (OR 1.120, p=0.892). Falsification SUCCEEDED against the 'no non-ADNI cohort' form (corrected 2026-09-14) but not against the randomised or multi-year AD-dementia-conversion prongs, which are retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: A randomised controlled trial or non-ADNI prospective cohort evaluating ChEI use on MCI-to-AD conversion in amyloid-confirmed participants, with adherence and competing-risk data.

gaps.title: Lipid trajectory/VIM risk models are retrospective with stable-MCI restriction and no prospective validation; VIM direction conflicts with prior high-variability literature
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1222 shows lower HDL-C trajectories and LOWEST TC/non-HDL-C VIM quintiles raise AD/MCI risk, improving models beyond APOE/PRS - but the study is retrospective (DodoNA EHR), restricts MCI to stable >=5-year cases (excluding converters), uses irregular clinically-obtained lipid measurements, is >91% Caucasian, and its VIM direction (LOW variability = higher risk) directly contradicts Moser et al. and Chung et al. who found HIGH lipid variability associated with increased dementia risk. No corpus study resolves this direction conflict or prospectively validates lipid-trajectory/VIM risk models in a diverse cohort.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched corpus for (i) any prospective validation of lipid trajectory/VIM AD/MCI risk models (none found; all lipid-MCI evidence is cross-sectional or retrospective), (ii) any corpus study reconciling the VIM direction conflict with Moser/Chung (none; no other corpus paper computes VIM at all). Falsification failed -> retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: Prospective cohort validation of lipid trajectory/VIM AD/MCI risk models with harmonised VIM methodology, inclusion of MCI converters, and non-Caucasian populations to resolve the direction-of-association conflict.

gaps.title: Serum ApoJ/clusterin MCI-to-dementia conversion evidence is directionally contested (low-ApoJ = higher conversion risk vs prior high-ApoJ-in-converters literature), single-country, single-timepoint, with no sApoJ/nApoJ subtype discrimination or independent replication
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1223 (two Italian memory clinics, N=196 MCI, median 2.9-yr follow-up) finds LOW serum ApoJ tertile predicts a doubled post-2-year conversion risk to dementia (adjusted HR 2.01, 95% CI 1.18-3.43), yet the paper itself documents the opposite direction in the prior literature - van Dijk et al. and Jongbloed et al. reported HIGHER plasma ApoJ in converters, and the Yang meta-analysis found no MCI-stage ApoJ alteration with opposite risk associations by age. The study is single-country, measures ApoJ at one timepoint only (no serial trends in converters vs non-converters), measures no systemic cytokines to test the inflammation-driven ApoJ hypothesis, and cannot attribute its findings to the secretory vs nuclear ApoJ subtypes because subtype-specific assays do not yet exist. No corpus paper independently replicates the direction of the ApoJ-conversion association or discriminates ApoJ subtypes.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus (registry + ledgers) for any other serum/plasma ApoJ or clusterin MCI conversion study or subtype-discriminating assay; none found (G-NEW-1142-A is depression-trajectory, its clusterin mention is coincidental). The direction conflict is documented inside P-1223 itself against van Dijk/Jongbloed/Yang, which are external citations, not corpus papers. Falsification failed -> retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: An independent multi-centre cohort measuring serial serum/plasma ApoJ in MCI with conversion follow-up, ideally with sApoJ/nApoJ subtype discrimination and cytokine measurements, to resolve the direction-of-association conflict and the post-2-year temporal window.

gaps.title: AT(N)-anchored plasma p-tau181 detection (AUC 0.910, 2.69 pg/mL cut-off) is single-cohort with no external cut-off validation or cross-assay harmonisation; P-1231's pooled P-tau181 range 0.61-0.84 shows the single-cohort AUC sits at/above the meta-analytic range
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1225 (Careggi Hospital, Florence, N=79 SCD/MCI/AD-d, 72 with CSF) reports plasma p-tau181 discriminating AT(N)-defined AD-pathology carriers (AUC 0.910, cut-off 2.69 pg/mL) in SCD+MCI - but validation is internal-only and cross-sectional, with no healthy controls and no external cohort confirming the cut-off. P-1231 (150-study meta-analysis) pools P-tau181 diagnostic AUCs at 0.61-0.84, so P-1225's single-cohort 0.910 sits above the pooled range - the cohort's AT(N)-anchored design and Simoa assay may inflate apparent performance, and no corpus study validates an AT(N)-anchored plasma p-tau181 cut-off in an independent cohort or harmonises thresholds across assay platforms. Plausibility annotation (operator-mandated, 2026-09-14): the single-cohort AUC 0.910 may be inflated and needs external cut-off validation - P-1231's pooled range for the same analyte is 'P-tau181 AUC 0.61-0.84', and P-1225's own block records a 'Small sample with no healthy controls; cross-sectional; cut-off not validated externally.'
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched corpus for any other AT(N)-anchored plasma p-tau181 cut-off validation or cross-platform harmonisation study; none found (G-NEW-1218-A covers an EIS biosensor platform, a different assay family; P-1231's meta-analysis documents the pooled range but contains no new cohort). Falsification failed -> retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: External cohort validation of an AT(N)-anchored plasma p-tau181 cut-off with harmonised assay methodology, or a head-to-head multi-platform p-tau181 comparison in the same samples.

gaps.title: Amyloid-stratified cognition x hippocampal-volume index (Cog_Vol = hippocampal volume / ADAS13) is validated only through the Shanghai->ADNI single-tracer pipeline, with no tau/fluid integration and an intermediate band (Cog_Vol 102-266, ~60% conversion risk) that cannot be classified individually
gaps.description: Actor justification (object of the gap corrected 2026-09-14): P-1226 derives Cog_Vol in the Shanghai MCI cohort and validates it in ADNI1/GO/2 (N=843 MCI, 220 with elevated PET beta-amyloid). Cog_Vol is a COGNITION x HIPPOCAMPAL-VOLUME ratio - the block defines 'a new parameter Cog_Vol = hippocampal volume/ADAS13 score ratio' - and amyloid PET is the stratification variable only ('florbetapir-PET with mean cortical SUVR (elevated cut-off >=1.11)', used to compare 'subjects with and without elevated PET beta-amyloid'); it is NOT a PET-amyloid x MRI-volume composite. Cog_Vol stratifies MCI-to-AD conversion risk from 'Cog_Vol < 101 predicted 94.1% conversion' to 'Cog_Vol >= 340 predicted essentially zero conversion' in elevated-amyloid MCI, but the validation chain is Shanghai derivation -> ADNI replication only, the amyloid stratifier is a single tracer (florbetapir), no tau-PET or fluid tau is included ('p-tau217 was not included'), and 'subjects with intermediate Cog_Vol (102-266, ~60% risk) cannot be individually classified' - the ~60% is a conversion RISK level, not a proportion of subjects. The index is group-level only, and no corpus study adds tau integration, resolves the middle band, or validates the transferred cut-offs outside ADNI ('validation in diverse, non-ADNI populations').
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched corpus for any cognition x hippocampal-volume conversion index with tau/fluid integration, non-florbetapir amyloid stratification, or individual-level resolution of an intermediate-risk band; none found. Related to G-NEW-1214-A (BASS x BAI amyloid-PET x MRI shape features, ADNI-only, ChEI confound), but note (2026-09-14 audit) that the two indices are not the same object: P-1214's feature is genuinely an amyloid-PET x MRI composite whereas Cog_Vol contains no PET term, so the shared 'single amyloid tracer' ceiling applies to P-1214's index and only to Cog_Vol's stratifier. Falsification failed -> retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: Validation of a Cog_Vol-style cognition x hippocampal-volume index with tau-PET or fluid p-tau217 integration in a non-ADNI cohort using a non-florbetapir amyloid stratifier, and an individual-level classifier for the intermediate-risk band (Cog_Vol 102-266).

gaps.title: Homocysteine-MCI-to-dementia conversion evidence is single-region (Italian clinics), subtype-specific (significant in naMCI only), single-timepoint, with no B-vitamin intervention trial showing conversion reduction in MCI
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1237 (311 MCI: 198 aMCI / 113 naMCI; 137 converters; median 33 months) finds highest-HCy-tertile conversion HR 2.25, significant in naMCI (p=0.04) but not aMCI, with a single baseline HCy measurement, 151 dropouts from the initial 462, and no B-vitamin status correction in all models; no corpus study replicates the naMCI-specific finding in another country or tests whether lowering HCy (B-vitamins) reduces MCI-to-dementia conversion. AUDIT CORRECTION 2026-09-14: homocysteine-lowering trials in MCI ARE in the corpus - P-679 is a 'systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials' of folic acid in '7 studies (1102 participants with MCI' reporting 'Homocysteine: MD -3.33' alongside Full Scale IQ 'SMD 0.93 (95 percent CI 0.79 to 1.08', and P-713 is a 'systematic review with Bayesian network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials testing methyl-nutrient supplementation in older adults with mild cognitive impairment' covering 'Fifteen randomised controlled trials totalling 4072 patients' with homocysteine 'folate plus vitamin B12 -4.23 (-5.46 to -3.17)' and including the VITACOG trials (Smith 2010, de Jager 2011). What they do NOT cover: neither reports an MCI-to-dementia conversion or mortality endpoint, P-713 could not pool cognition at all ('Cognitive outcomes could not be pooled quantitatively because trials used different instruments'), and neither replicates the naMCI-specific HCy-conversion finding. The family gap is therefore scoped to the conversion/survival endpoint plus the subtype-stratified replication.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched corpus for any other HCy-MCI conversion cohort or B-vitamin intervention RCT with a dementia-conversion endpoint in MCI; none found for the conversion endpoint. Correction 2026-09-14: the earlier statement that no corpus trial lowers HCy in MCI is false - P-679 (folic acid, 7 RCTs, Hcy MD -3.33) and P-713 (methyl nutrients, 15 RCTs, folate+B12 Hcy -4.23) are corpus syntheses of homocysteine-lowering RCTs in MCI populations, but with cognitive/biochemical endpoints only. Falsification failed on the conversion/survival-endpoint and naMCI-replication prongs -> retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: Multi-centre replication of subtype-stratified HCy-MCI conversion (ideally non-Italian), serial HCy measurement, and a randomised B-vitamin trial with MCI-to-dementia conversion endpoint.

No paper tests whether gamma entrainment changes plasma/CSF Abeta, tau or NfL in a sham-controlled design, leaving the relationship between neuromodulation-induced cognitive gain and AD-pathology biomarkers untested.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for any sham-controlled gamma-tACS trial reporting plasma/CSF AD biomarkers alongside cognitive outcomes; none found (P-1243 measured plasma biomarkers but is open-label and reports no change; P-458/469/496/916 are simulation/review-only or without biomarker endpoints). gaps.closure_criteria: A sham-controlled randomized gamma-tACS trial in MCI reporting both cognitive outcomes and plasma/CSF AD biomarkers (Abeta, p-tau, NfL) with pre/post measurements, ideally stratified by baseline biomarker status.

gaps.title: Gut-microbiome-targeted intervention in MCI has no >=12-month conversion or sustained-cognitive-decline endpoint - the corpus probiotic RCTs (P-1246 3-month LGG; P-972 24-week B. breve MCC1274) report short-horizon cognitive and atrophy outcomes only
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1246 (NCT03080818, N=169, double-blind placebo-controlled 3-month LGG RCT) found Prevotella ruminicola and Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron significantly more prevalent in MCI and that LGG supplementation decreased Prevotella/Dehalobacterium abundance in the MCI group, 'correlated with an improved cognitive score' - a 3-month intervention with cognitive correlation only and no conversion endpoint. AUDIT CORRECTION 2026-09-14: P-1246 is NOT the corpus's only human probiotic RCT, and the intervention is not 'entirely untested' as disease-modifying. P-972 is a '24-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of the probiotic Bifidobacterium breve MCC1274' ('130 randomised; 115 in full analysis set') reporting ADAS-Jcog/MMSE subscale gains and that 'VSRAD scores worsened in placebo while probiotic tended to suppress progression'; P-641 pools '994 participants across 15 randomized controlled trials' of probiotics on cognition. What none of them covers: a >=12-month follow-up with a dementia-conversion or sustained-cognitive-decline endpoint - P-972 stops at 24 weeks with subscale-only cognitive gains and no microbiota mediation, and P-641 states 'whether probiotics slow decline rather than transiently improve scores is untested' and calls for 'long-term follow-up'. The corpus's other gut-microbiome MCI papers (P-1203 conversion prediction single-cohort N=49; P-1201 sex-specific risk models; P-1229 preclinical barley polysaccharide) are observational or preclinical, so whether microbiome manipulation slows MCI-to-AD progression remains untested.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched corpus for any gut-microbiome intervention RCT reporting MCI-to-AD conversion or long-term (>=12-month) cognitive-decline outcomes: the corpus holds two human probiotic RCTs (P-1246, 3-month LGG, cognitive correlation; P-972, 24-week B. breve MCC1274, placebo-controlled, cognitive subscales plus VSRAD atrophy-progression suppression) and one meta-analysis (P-641, 15 RCTs, 994 participants), none with a >=12-month conversion or sustained-decline endpoint; P-1203 predicts conversion but is observational. Falsification SUCCEEDED against the earlier 'P-1246 is the only human probiotic RCT' wording (corrected 2026-09-14); the endpoint-scoped gap is retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: A randomized gut-microbiome-targeted intervention (probiotic/prebiotic/synbiotic or FMT) in MCI with >=12-month follow-up and dementia-conversion or sustained cognitive-decline endpoints, with gut-microbiome readouts confirming target engagement.

gaps.title: No corpus study tests whether homocysteine-lowering (vitamin B12/folate) intervention improves survival or MCI-to-dementia conversion in SCD/MCI - the cognition prong is already covered by corpus RCT syntheses (P-713, P-679)
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1253 (N=976, retrospective) reports elevated homocysteine independently predicts 5-year mortality ('metric (lg10) homocysteine OR 11.198 (95% CI 2.027-61.862, p=.006)') in SCD/MCI/AD and proposes 'intervention trials of vitamin B12/folate substitution with mortality and cognitive endpoints', and P-1237 (N=311, HCy tertiles) links baseline homocysteine to MCI-to-dementia conversion (HR 2.25) - both observational, neither testing lowering. P-713 ('Fifteen randomised controlled trials totalling 4072 patients' of methyl nutrients in MCI, including 'Smith 2010 (UK)' and 'de Jager 2011 (UK)', with homocysteine 'folate plus vitamin B12 -4.23 (-5.46 to -3.17)') and P-679 ('7 studies (1102 participants with MCI', Full Scale IQ 'SMD 0.93 (95 percent CI 0.79 to 1.08', 'Homocysteine: MD -3.33') are corpus-level syntheses of homocysteine-lowering RCTs in MCI with cognitive outcomes. What they do NOT cover: no mortality or MCI-to-dementia conversion endpoint (P-713's cognitive synthesis is vote-counted, not pooled: 'Cognitive outcomes could not be pooled quantitatively because trials used different instruments'; P-679's own block flags four of seven trials from one group with apparently overlapping cohorts). gaps.title: No randomized trial pairs a ketogenic/MCT metabolic-dietary intervention with a cognitive primary endpoint in MCI, and no corpus dietary trial reports an MCI-to-dementia conversion endpoint - probiotic and EVOO cognitive RCT evidence already exists (P-972, P-641, P-873)
gaps.description: 2026-09-10 split from G-NEW-1256-A (consolidated G5 verdict, data/g5_consolidated_verdicts.csv): the dietary/metabolic half of the original bundled record. P-1262 (RCT, N=39) shows 6-month kMCT is cardiometabolically safe in MCI but reports only secondary biomarker outcomes, not cognition; P-1252 (MICOIL substudy, open-label) reports EVOO restoring oxidative-stress biomarkers with no placebo-controlled cognitive endpoint; P-1246 (LGG probiotic RCT) is a 3-month cognitive-correlation design without conversion (see G-NEW-1246-A); P-1200 (Kampo) is observational. AUDIT CORRECTION 2026-09-14: the earlier clause that no randomized trial tests whether probiotics (or EVOO) improve cognition in MCI is false against the corpus. P-972 is a '24-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of the probiotic Bifidobacterium breve MCC1274' ('130 randomised; 115 in full analysis set') with ADAS-Jcog/MMSE endpoints, reporting an improved orientation subscale and that 'VSRAD scores worsened in placebo while probiotic tended to suppress progression'; P-641 pools '994 participants across 15 randomized controlled trials' with a significant cognitive effect in the cognitively impaired subgroup (SMD 1.03; 95% CI 0.35-1.70); P-873 pools five EVOO RCTs ('747 individuals (437 in the EVOO intervention groups and 310 in the control groups)') with significant MMSE (MD 0.42), CDT (0.47) and ADAS-Cog (1.45) differences. What those closers do NOT cover: P-972's cognitive gains are subscale-only over 24 weeks ('Cognitive improvements limited to subscales'), P-641 states 'whether probiotics slow decline rather than transiently improve scores is untested', P-873's effects 'fall below established minimal clinically important differences' with GRADE certainty rated low, none of the three reports an MCI-to-dementia conversion endpoint, and no corpus RCT pairs a ketogenic/MCT intervention with a cognitive primary endpoint at all.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for a randomized metabolic-dietary intervention (ketogenic/MCT, EVOO, probiotic, Kampo) in MCI with a cognitive primary endpoint: P-1262 is randomized but biomarker-only, P-1252 is open-label, P-1246 is 3-month cognitive-correlation without conversion, P-1200 is observational - but P-972 (24-week double-blind placebo-controlled probiotic RCT with ADAS-Jcog/MMSE), P-641 (15-RCT probiotic meta-analysis) and P-873 (5-RCT EVOO meta-analysis) do report cognitive outcomes. Falsification SUCCEEDED against the probiotic/EVOO cognition clause (corrected 2026-09-14); the ketogenic/MCT cognitive-primary-endpoint prong and the conversion-endpoint prong are retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: A randomized controlled trial of a ketogenic/MCT or other metabolic-dietary intervention in MCI with a cognitive primary endpoint, and/or any corpus dietary-intervention trial reporting serial metabolomics and an MCI-to-dementia conversion endpoint.

gaps.title: Phytoestrogen or ER-pathway therapy for postmenopausal MCI is untested in humans - the ER/NF-kB/NLRP3 axis has only mouse mechanistic evidence (P-1261) and no human intervention trial
gaps.description: Actor justification: P-1261 (ovariectomized APP/PS1 mice) shows Tiaogeng decoction improves menopausal MCI via ERs/NF-kB/NLRP3/AQP1 with reduced Abeta and IL-1beta/IL-18, but this is the sole ER-axis evidence and it is entirely mouse-based. The human biomarker papers (P-1239 CSF NGAL OR 2.27 for conversion; P-1249 exosomal complement C5b-9 AUC 0.76 in T1DM-MCI) implicate neuroinflammation in MCI but are not ER/NF-kB/NLRP3-specific and come from non-menopausal populations, so they do not constitute convergent evidence for the ER axis. No corpus study tests a phytoestrogen or ER-pathway intervention for MCI in postmenopausal women, leaving the mouse ER/NF-kB/NLRP3 pathway untranslated.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for any human trial of phytoestrogen or ER-pathway targeted therapy in postmenopausal MCI; none found (P-1261 is a mouse study; P-1239/P-1249 are human biomarker studies without intervention and without ER/NF-kB/NLRP3 specificity). Falsification failed -> retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: A randomized trial of a phytoestrogen or ER-pathway therapy in postmenopausal women with MCI, with cognitive endpoints, ER-axis inflammatory biomarkers (NGAL, IL-1beta, IL-18) and an explicitly postmenopausal population definition.

gaps.title: IgG N-glycan + cytokine MCI screening panel (AUC 0.939) is validated only in vascular-risk MCI (cerebrovascular-stenosis case-control, single region) - no external validation in general MCI, no longitudinal data, spectrum-bias risk unquantified
gaps.description: P-1273 (N=238 cerebrovascular-stenosis patients, 119 MCI) reports a plasma IgG N-glycan plus 8-cytokine combined model with AUC 0.939 for MCI, but the cohort is a single-region (Shandong Taian) hospital case-control drawn from CEREBROVASCULAR-STENOSIS patients, so the panel is validated for vascular-risk MCI, not general MCI; case-control enrichment (spectrum bias) plus the very high AUC 0.939 from this restricted population require external validation before any generalisability claim, and the cross-sectional design cannot establish whether glyco-immune alterations precede MCI or reflect progression. Existing blood-biomarker gaps do not cover the IgG glycosylation axis.

gaps.closure_criteria: External multicentre replication of the IgG-glycan+cytokine MCI panel in general (non-vascular) MCI with longitudinal follow-up, reporting calibration and spectrum-adjusted performance.

gaps.title: No validated method quantifies soluble (non-aggregated) brain-interstitial p-tau in living humans during the predementia window
gaps.description: P-1283 (AAV-AD rat, '35 male Wistar rats') establishes that soluble P-tau is necessary for MCI onset and states that 'no in-vivo method exists to measure soluble brain P-tau in living humans, limiting direct translation', calling for 'development of imaging/biochemical methods to quantify soluble brain P-tau before tangle formation'. The gap is specifically brain-INTERSTITIAL soluble p-tau: PET tracks aggregated species, and CSF p-tau, while itself soluble, is measured in CSF rather than brain interstitial fluid, so no assay reaches that compartment directly. AUDIT CORRECTION 2026-09-14: two clauses carried by the promoted record are dropped because the anchor block does not make them. (i) The Abeta42 extension is removed - the block attributes the method absence to P-tau only; its Abeta42 statement is pathophysiological ('both soluble brain forms - Abeta42 and P-tau - are necessary for the asymptomatic-to-prodromal (MCI) transition'), not a claim that no Abeta42 method exists. (ii) The clause 'CSF/plasma positivity is reached only at late MCI/dementia' is removed: it is not in P-1283 and is contradicted inside the corpus by P-1279 ('Amyloid pathology was observed in CSF in 18% of controls, 64% of MCI patients') and by P-1414's note that prior cohorts established p-tau217's value for 'preclinical prognosis'. The corpus offers plasma/CSF proxies but no direct in-vivo quantification of brain-interstitial soluble p-tau.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for any imaging or biochemical method quantifying soluble (non-aggregated) brain-interstitial p-tau in living humans (the anchor block's method-absence statement names P-tau only); none found - PET tracks aggregated species and CSF assays measure soluble species in CSF, not brain interstitial fluid. Falsification failed -> retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: A validated in-vivo method (e.g., an interstitial-fluid-calibrated PET tracer or a CSF surrogate explicitly calibrated to brain-interstitial soluble species) that quantifies soluble brain p-tau during the predementia window and tracks MCI onset - proposed, not asserted, as the concrete route.

Verdict: gap CONFIRMED at literature level - the method-development gap stands.

gaps.title: Plasma Abeta42/40 (mass spectrometry) SCD-to-MCI conversion prediction is single-cohort (FACEHBI) with no multi-centre validation and no SCD-labelled cohort pairing it with p-tau217/GFAP/NfL
gaps.description: P-1289 (FACEHBI, '200 individuals with subjective cognitive decline', five-year follow-up) shows ABtest-MS plasma Abeta42/40 predicts amyloid accumulation, atrophy and SCD-to-MCI conversion ('HR 3.25, 95% CI 1.17-9.01'), but is a single-centre cohort with 'weak associations with cognitive decline', no concurrent p-tau measurement ('no tau/neurodegeneration plasma markers'), and a 'mass-spectrometry method (ABtest-MS) [that] requires specialized laboratory capacity'; it asks for 'Multi-centre validation in larger SCD cohorts; integration with additional plasma markers (p-tau217, GFAP, NfL)'. gaps.title: Southeast Asia has no regionally harmonised MCI prevalence estimate and no harmonised country-validated screening instruments - country-level studies exist (P-618: Singapore prevalence 12.5%, N=973) but criteria, instruments and data platforms are not harmonised
gaps.description: P-1287 (SEACURE consensus) states that 'No official MCI prevalence estimates exist for SEA due to varying diagnostic criteria, insufficient resources and cultural barriers to seeking care', and its recommendations are 'Formal epidemiologic studies of MCI prevalence in SEA; country-specific validation of cognitive screening instruments; establishment of harmonized data-processing platforms'. AUDIT CORRECTION 2026-09-14 (operator action revise-major, data/g5_consolidated_verdicts.csv): the record is reframed from an absolute absence to a HARMONISATION gap, and two unsupported extrapolations are removed - the block does not state that traditional cognitive screening tests are unvalidated per country (it recommends validation) and does not state that no SEA-wide epidemiological or diagnostic-validation data exist. Country-level corpus evidence exists: P-618 is a 'population-based study of community-dwelling Singaporean Chinese elderly to determine the prevalence of MCI' with '973 Singaporean Chinese elderly (122 MCI / 831 normal cognition; MCI prevalence 12.5%'; P-939 develops and externally validates the Singapore SLAS risk index for incident MCI/dementia; P-964 is a Thai hospital MCI-to-dementia conversion cohort (N=250); P-982 evaluates the Thai Cardiovascular Risk score for MCI (N=421); P-1086 develops a Malaysian MY-MINDD diet score for MCI (N=810). What none of them covers: a regionally harmonised multi-country SEA prevalence estimate under common diagnostic criteria, and country-validated screening instruments across the six SEACURE countries (Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam) on a harmonised data-processing platform. This remains a population-level gap categorically distinct from single-site cohort-validation gaps.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for any SEA MCI prevalence study or country-level cognitive-screening/risk-instrument dataset: P-618 (Singapore population-based prevalence 12.5%, N=973), P-939 (SLAS risk index, development + external validation + field evaluation), P-964 (Thai conversion cohort), P-982 (Thai cardiovascular risk score for MCI) and P-1086 (Malaysian MY-MINDD diet score) all exist, so the earlier 'none found' claim is false (corrected 2026-09-14); no corpus source provides a regionally harmonised multi-country prevalence estimate or harmonised cross-country instrument validation. Falsification SUCCEEDED against the absolute framing; the harmonisation gap is retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: Regionally harmonised, multi-country SEA MCI prevalence estimates produced under common diagnostic criteria, with country-validated cognitive screening instruments and a harmonised data-processing platform across SEACURE member countries.

gaps.title: Multiomics blood-based aMCI biomarker (hsa-miR-4455/let-7b-3p ratio, AUC 0.971) is small-cohort with miRNA-only external validation; no large replication or conversion endpoint
gaps.description: P-1293 (Hirosaki multiomics, discovery 25 aMCI + 25 HC, validation 12 + 12) reports XGBoost and the hsa-miR-4455/hsa-let-7b-3p composite ratio (AUC 0.971, sensitivity 0.8, specificity 1.0) for aMCI discrimination, but externally validates only the miRNA layer (validation microarray detected fewer miRNAs, 209 vs 493), has no longitudinal conversion endpoint, and no corpus study replicates the full multiomics panel. Falsification failed -> retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: Large multi-centre cohorts validating all omics layers of the aMCI panel with longitudinal MCI-to-dementia conversion endpoints.

gaps.title: Blood mtDNA methylation MCI-to-ADD prognostic model (AUC 0.903) is tested on an independent set drawn from partially overlapping recruitment streams, with no fully external replication and no joint evaluation with plasma p-tau217/Abeta42-40
gaps.description: P-1296 ('600 subjects (aged 55-85) from seven international cohorts (Knight 64, AIBL 248, HUB 125, HCB 79, CITA 75, HSCSP 5, HGH 4)') derives a Random Forest on D-loop/ND1 mtDNA methylation ('sensitivity 95.1% and specificity 70.7%; AUC-ROC 90.3%') using 'cross-validation plus testing on an independent set'. AUDIT CORRECTION 2026-09-14: the earlier wording 'tests only on a held-out split of the same recruitment pool' is not supported by the block and is replaced with the block's own weaker statement - the 'Validation cohort [is] partially overlapping clinical recruitment streams' (registry Validation Type V3, 'independent test set within multi-cohort design'). The block still records that 'external replication in independent large cohorts [is] still needed' and that the design is a 'cohort mixture from seven biobanks; needs large prospective external replication', and no corpus study jointly evaluates mtDNA methylation with established plasma markers, the paper itself asking for 'integration with plasma p-tau217 and Abeta markers'.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for any external replication of mtDNA-methylation-based MCI-to-dementia prognosis or a study combining mtDNA methylation with plasma p-tau217/Abeta42-40; none found (corpus mitochondrial records P-649, P-1393 and P-1360 measure copy number, cell-free mtDNA or mitochondria-related gene expression, not mtDNA methylation; P-1313 is a flagged garbled duplicate of P-1296). Falsification failed -> retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: Independent prospective cohorts replicating the mtDNA methylation model and head-to-head/joint evaluation with plasma p-tau217 and Abeta42/40.

gaps.title: Training-induced immune biomarker changes (TTB; IL-10 efficacy marker) are never linked to cognitive outcomes in the same trial

gaps.closure_criteria: Training trials reporting both biomarker and cognitive endpoints with formal mediation/correlation analyses, and replication of the IL-10 response marker.
