gaps.title: NLRP3-gene x occupational-exposure MCI association in aluminum workers is single-factory, cross-sectional, and functionally unvalidated
gaps.description: P-1321 (478 aluminum electrolysis workers, Guangxi) finds high PC2 exposure (alumina dust, magnetic field, fluoride, MnO2) and NLRP3 SNPs (rs10754558 G/C) independently associated with MCI odds (OR 1.56-2.84), with PC2 x rs3806265/rs4612666 interactions, but the design is one factory, cross-sectional, with PCA-composited exposures rather than individual dosimetry: no corpus or external study replicates the gene-environment interaction, and no functional data connect the risk genotypes to NLRP3-inflammasome activation.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for other occupational-exposure/MCI gene-environment studies or NLRP3-inflammasome human data in exposed workers; none found (occupational-exposure search: 0 prior records). Replication and mechanistic validation absent - falsification failed, retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: Replication of the NLRP3 x exposure interaction in another industrial cohort with individual exposure measurement, and/or functional (inflammasome) evidence for the risk genotypes.
gaps.human_evaluation_note: Model-authored candidate; gate G5 is an operator action, NOT self-signed.

gaps.title: Stage-specific multimodal omics-MRI-EEG classifiers (SCD/MCI/AD AUC 0.78-0.98) are single-centre with internal-split validation only
gaps.description: P-1322 (277 participants, genomics/metagenomics/metabolomics/MRI/EEG) reports random-forest AUCs of 0.78 (SCD), 0.84 (MCI) and 0.98 (AD) using an 80/20 stratified internal split with SMOTE/GridSearchCV, but the classifiers have no external cohort validation, the staging is cross-sectional (inferred stages, not longitudinal conversion), and per-modality contribution (notably EEG-only early screening) is not externally tested.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for external-cohort validation of multimodal/staging classifiers or of EEG-based SCD/MCI screening; existing external-validation gaps target other marker families (fluoropyridine PET G-NEW-1089-A, nomograms G-NEW-1085-A, exosomal lncRNA G-NEW-1232-A), none cover this integrated omics-MRI-EEG staging panel - falsification failed, retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: External-cohort validation of the SCD/MCI/AD classifiers (or EEG-only early screening), and/or longitudinal confirmation that the staged groups convert as predicted.
gaps.human_evaluation_note: Model-authored candidate; gate G5 is an operator action, NOT self-signed.

gaps.title: Plasma exosomal miRNA stage signature (miR-210-3p/miR-151-3p AUC>0.9) is a 29-subject single-centre discovery with no external or longitudinal validation
gaps.description: P-1323 (10 AD, 9 MCI, 10 NC, Shanghai 2022-2024) profiles plasma exosomal miRNAs across the NC-MCI-AD continuum and reports ROC AUC >0.9 for miR-210-3p and miR-151-3p, but the cohort is 29 subjects at one centre with ROC evaluation only: no corpus or external study replicates the 10-miRNA panel, and no longitudinal sample tests whether the stage signature predicts conversion rather than merely discriminating cross-sectionally.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for external/large-cohort plasma exosomal miRNA stage panels or longitudinal miRNA conversion data in MCI; existing exosomal-gap records target lncRNA panels (G-NEW-1232-A) and protein NfL/AT(N) markers - none cover this 10-miRNA exosome stage signature - falsification failed, retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: External multi-centre replication of the exosomal miRNA stage panel and/or a longitudinal design showing the signature predicts MCI-to-AD conversion.
gaps.human_evaluation_note: Model-authored candidate; gate G5 is an operator action, NOT self-signed.

gaps.title: Integrated clinical+plasma (Simoa)+DMN-FC+cortical-thickness PD-MCI model (AUC 0.987) is single-centre drug-naive with no external validation
gaps.description: P-1325 (49 early drug-naive PD: 26 PD-MCI / 23 PD-NC + 20 controls) builds a combined model reaching AUC 0.987 for PD-MCI vs PD-NC using backward-selection logistic regression with calibration, but the derivation cohort is single-centre with no external cohort, and backward selection on n=49 risks overfitting: no corpus or external study replicates the integrated plasma+FC+cortical-thickness PD-MCI model.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for externally validated PD-MCI diagnostic models combining plasma markers, DMN FC and cortical thickness; corpus PD-MCI entries are imaging-only, clinical-only or PD-dementia review (P-1328) - no integrated multimodal PD-MCI diagnostic model with external validation - falsification failed, retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: External multi-centre validation of the combined PD-MCI diagnostic model (and ideally a longitudinal PD-MCI-to-PDD endpoint).
gaps.human_evaluation_note: Model-authored candidate; gate G5 is an operator action, NOT self-signed.

gaps.title: Simple 0-3 MCI-to-dementia clinical score (age/MMSE/aMCI, AUC 0.72) is derivation-only without external validation or biomarker augmentation
gaps.description: P-1326 (462 elderly MCI, 33-month follow-up, Ferrara) derives a 0-3 score (age >=78, MMSE <25, aMCI) predicting MCI-to-dementia conversion with ROC AUC 0.72, but the score is derivation-only: no corpus or external study externally validates it or tests whether adding fluid/imaging biomarkers improves its modest discrimination.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for external validation of simple clinical MCI-to-dementia risk scores or of biomarker-augmented versions of such scores; existing conversion-prediction work targets biomarkers (CSF/blood/imaging) rather than validating this three-variable score - falsification failed, retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: External cohort validation of the age/MMSE/aMCI score and/or a biomarker-augmented version reporting net reclassification.
gaps.human_evaluation_note: Model-authored candidate; gate G5 is an operator action, NOT self-signed.

gaps.title: ASL baseline-rCBF MCI-to-AD conversion prediction (93% stepwise; 87% BPCP) lacks FWE-robust, externally replicated endpoints and biomarker comparison
gaps.description: P-1329 (63 CHS-CS participants) reports stepwise logistic models predicting MCI-to-AD conversion with up to 93% accuracy from baseline rCBF, but the individual-region effects and survival predictions do not survive family-wise error correction, the cohort is a single longitudinal sample without external replication, and no amyloid/tau status is integrated: corpus- and corpus-external ASL conversion studies that are FWE-stable and externally validated are absent.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for externally validated ASL-based MCI-to-AD conversion models with FWE-stable primary endpoints or ASL+biomarker comparisons; corpus ASL/perfusion entries are cross-sectional diagnosis, single-cohort prediction or cognitive-reserve moderation (P-1242, P-1329); none provides external FWE-stable replication - falsification failed, retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: External multi-site ASL conversion study with FWE-corrected primary endpoints and/or ASL vs CSF/PET biomarker head-to-head.
gaps.human_evaluation_note: Model-authored candidate; gate G5 is an operator action, NOT self-signed.

gaps.title: 20-metabolite MCI-to-AD conversion panel (5-fold CV 80.3%; 8-metabolite index AUC 0.96) lacks external validation and direct microbiome confirmation
gaps.description: P-1332 (19 P-MCI, 29 S-MCI, Taiwan) builds a 20-metabolite plasma panel with fivefold-CV accuracy 80.3% for P-MCI vs S-MCI and an eight-metabolite index reaching AUC 0.96, with indole-3-propionic acid as a predictor suggestive of gut-microbiota involvement, but the panel is single-centre with internal CV only, and the gut-microbiota link is inferred from one metabolite rather than measured: no corpus or external study validates the panel or confirms the microbiome mediation.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for external validation of MCI-to-AD metabolite panels or direct 16S/metagenomic confirmation of the tryptophan/gut-microbiota pathway in MCI; existing metabolomics gaps target NMR metabolic signatures (G-NEW-1221-A region) and dietary SCFA evidence, none validates this 20-metabolite panel and no gut-microbiome-MCI conversion study exists - falsification failed, retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: External multi-centre validation of the 20-metabolite panel and/or a longitudinal study with direct gut-microbiome measurement confirming indole-3-propionic-acid mediation.
gaps.human_evaluation_note: Model-authored candidate; gate G5 is an operator action, NOT self-signed.

gaps.title: APOE-stratified PRS MCI-to-AD conversion claim (e4 non-carrier HR 1.710) is ADNI-only, European-ancestry, with no external replication
gaps.closure_criteria: External multi-cohort replication of APOE-stratified PRS MCI-to-AD hazard ratios, ideally including a non-European population.
gaps.description: P-1333 (ADNI, 732 MCI: 270 converters / 462 stable) shows a polygenic risk score predicts MCI-to-dementia conversion strongly in APOE e4 non-carriers (PRS+APOE HR 1.710 in non-carriers vs 1.167 in carriers; interaction p=0.0378), but the analysis is ADNI-only, restricted to European ancestry, and no corpus or external study replicates the APOE-stratified PRS conversion signals - the e4-modulated predictability claim rests on a single cohort.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for APOE-stratified PRS MCI-conversion replication or non-European PRS validation studies; P-1335 (40-SNP non-APOE PRS, ADNI+NACC) replicates a non-APOE PRS but does not stratify by APOE genotype as P-1333 does, and no corpus study validates either PRS in a non-European or community MCI cohort, so the falsification attempt failed.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: Genetic-risk signal for MCI conversion is APOE-genotype dependent, so unstratified PRS models average two different effect sizes; enrichment of trial populations by PRS therefore needs APOE-aware calibration that only one single-ancestry cohort currently supports.

gaps.title: Neuron-derived exosomal protein markers C7/ZYX (n=15 discovery) lack independent validation and assay-level confirmation
gaps.closure_criteria: Independent-cohort replication of C7/ZYX expression trends plus quantitative assay (ELISA/Simoa) confirmation.
gaps.description: P-1334 (n=15: 5 AD / 5 MCI / 5 NC, Shenzhen) proposes neuron-derived exosomal proteins C7 and ZYX as markers of normal-to-MCI-to-AD progression from TMT proteomics with fuzzy c-means clustering, but it is a tiny discovery cohort with no independent validation and no assay-level (ELISA/Simoa) confirmation - the proposed markers have not been replicated by any corpus or external study.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for validated neuron-derived exosomal protein markers or larger exosome proteomics cohorts in MCI; P-1323 (plasma exosomal miRNA, n=29) is a similarly small single-centre exosome cohort and offers candidate markers without independent validation, so no study closes the validation gap - the falsification attempt failed.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: Exosome-based markers need the C7/ZYX (and miRNA) candidate sets confirmed in at least one independent cohort with a targeted assay before any downstream diagnostic panel can be built.

gaps.title: Externally replicated non-APOE PRS (ADNI+NACC) untested in non-European/clinical MCI populations and not integrated with blood biomarkers
gaps.closure_criteria: PRS MCI-conversion evaluation in a clinical or non-European cohort, and/or combination of the PRS with fluid biomarkers in one risk model.
gaps.description: P-1335 (40-SNP non-APOE PRS, ADNI 767 MCI + NACC 1373 MCI) predicts MCI-to-AD progression with external replication (NACC beta 0.094, p=0.009) and shows Abeta42 mediation, but both cohorts are research-optimised and predominantly European-ancestry, and no corpus study evaluates the non-APOE PRS in a clinical or non-European population or integrates the PRS with blood biomarkers for bedside conversion risk.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched for non-European or clinical-cohort PRS MCI conversion models in the corpus; P-1342 (Shanghai Aging Study) tests a single PVRL2 SNP x LDL-C interaction, not a PRS, and no corpus study applies a PRS conversion model in a clinical or non-European cohort, so the falsification attempt failed.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: Even an externally replicated PRS has only been validated inside research cohorts; translating PRS-based MCI risk to clinics needs diversity-aware weights and blood-biomarker coupling.

gaps.title: R2SN radiomics MCI subtype split (A-CI 61.5% vs N-CI 21.8% 3-year progression) is ADNI-only with no external validation or biomarker coupling
gaps.closure_criteria: External-cohort validation of the A-CI/N-CI radiomics subtypes and integration with CSF or blood biomarkers in one cohort.
gaps.description: P-1339 (ADNI, 1654: 605 NC / 766 MCI / 283 AD) derives two R2SN radiomics-similarity MCI subtypes (A-CI 61.5% vs N-CI 21.8% 3-year progression) with distinct gene enrichment (potassium-ion transport, synaptic transmission), but subtyping is ADNI-only with no external cohort validation and no integration with CSF/blood biomarkers - the clinically actionable subtype split is not yet externally confirmed.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for external validation of imaging-defined MCI subtypes or R2SN radiomics clusters; P-1330 (AT(N) mismatch MCI subtypes, ADNI-only) is a related biomarker-stratified subtyping validated only within ADNI, and no corpus study validates a radiomics-defined MCI subtype externally or couples it to fluid biomarkers, so the attempt failed.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: Imaging-based MCI subtypes vary with the anchor groups (NC/AD) and cohort composition; without external validation and biomarker coupling, the A-CI/N-CI risk split may not generalise.

gaps.title: PVRL2 rs6859 x LDL-C interaction on MCI-to-AD (HR 2.75; per-mmol/L LDL-C HR 0.52) is single-cohort, Chinese-only, unreplicated
gaps.closure_criteria: Independent-cohort replication of the PVRL2 x LDL-C interaction with larger genotype subgroups and/or functional validation of PVRL2.
gaps.description: P-1342 (Shanghai Aging Study, 316 MCI, 4.5-year follow-up) reports a PVRL2 rs6859 x LDL-C interaction on MCI-to-AD progression (AG/AA HR 2.75 vs GG; in carriers +1 mmol/L LDL-C lowers AD risk 48%), but the finding is single-cohort, Chinese-only, with small genotype subgroups and no independent replication or functional validation of the PVRL2 mechanism.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for replication of lipid x genetic-variant interactions in MCI-to-AD progression; P-1222 (lipid trajectories in ADNI) and P-1333/P-1335 (PRS) test lipid or genetic signals but none tests a PVRL2 x LDL-C interaction or replicates P-1342's interaction in another cohort, so the falsification attempt failed.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: Gene-lipid interactions in MCI progression are fragile to cohort and allele-frequency differences; the PVRL2 x LDL-C direction must be reproduced before genotype-stratified lipid management is actionable.

gaps.title: Plasma p-tau217 + mPACC cognition MCI-to-AD model (AUC 0.87-0.89) derived and validated in one Swedish flutemetamol-trial cohort; no external single-cohort replication in routine memory clinics
gaps.closure_criteria: External validation of the p-tau217 + mPACC composite in at least one independent non-trial memory-clinic cohort with MCI-to-AD outcomes, reporting AUC with CIs.
gaps.description: P-1343 (Flutemetamol PET trial NCT01028053, Lund/Skane, 110 amnestic MCI, 26 progressors) reports AUC 0.87-0.89 for a plasma p-tau217 + mPACC model, but the derivation cohort is a single-centre Swedish PET-trial sample with only 26 conversion events; with no external cohort the 0.87-0.89 range may overfit trial-referral enrichment.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for independent replication of a p-tau217 + cognitive-composite conversion model: P-1346 validates p-tau217 assay equivalence against CSF Abeta42/40 but adds no cognition composite and shares the Swedish region; P-1225/P-1285 use p-tau181/p-tau217 without mPACC in different cohorts. No corpus paper externally replicates the P-1343 model, so the falsification attempt failed.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: Blood p-tau217 plus a short cognition composite is the most implementable progression marker in the batch, but a 26-event single-centre derivation cannot anchor a triage threshold; the model needs a geography-agnostic validation before the AUC claim is portable.

gaps.title: 29-gene plasma random-forest stable-MCI classifier is ADNI-only (n=358) with no external cohort validation; training CV AUC 0.841 falls to 0.775 on held-out test
gaps.closure_criteria: External validation of the 29-gene panel on an independent non-ADNI cohort with stable vs progressive MCI labels, reporting AUC and calibration.
gaps.description: P-1344 builds a 31-probe/29-gene plasma classifier for stable MCI entirely in ADNI (n=358 with 46 unstable / 312 stable); its own CV AUC 0.841 degrades to 0.775 on the held-out ADNI test set, and no external cohort is available to judge whether the 29-gene signature reflects disease biology or site/plate effects.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for non-ADNI validation of plasma gene-expression stable-MCI classifiers: P-1351 and P-1352 validate blood-based panels in Singaporean/Japanese cohorts but use inflammatory DEGs and immune repertoire respectively, not P-1344's 29-gene set, and neither targets the stable-vs-unstable boundary; no closer found.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: A 0.066 AUC drop between CV and held-out test inside the same biobank flags feature instability that only a true external cohort can bound; ADNI-only transcriptomic panels of this vintage routinely fail cross-site exactly at the stable-MCI boundary they claim.

gaps.title: Plasma p-tau217 assay equivalence (Simoa p-tau217+Janssen vs Lilly) established only in two Swedish cohorts; no multi-site/international harmonisation of cut-offs against CSF Abeta42/40
gaps.closure_criteria: Multi-site (non-Swedish) head-to-head p-tau217 assay comparison with harmonised cut-offs against CSF Abeta42/40 and conversion outcomes.
gaps.description: P-1346 compares a novel Simoa p-tau217+Janssen assay with the Lilly assay using CSF Abeta42/40 as the reference, but both cohorts (BioFINDER cohort 1, n=52, and Skane University Hospital Memory Clinic, n=147) are Swedish, so equivalence across laboratories, reagent lots and patient ancestries is unshown and no international cut-off exists.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for multi-site p-tau217 assay harmonisation: P-1343 uses one p-tau217 assay in Sweden only; P-1225/P-1290 use p-tau181 or single-platform p-tau217 without a second platform head-to-head; no corpus record reports cross-site/platform p-tau217 equivalence, so the falsification attempt failed.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: Assay equivalence shown within one country shares pre-analytical and population-specific confounders; the 'same protein, interchangeable vendors' claim holds only when the comparison is reproduced off-Swedish soil.

gaps.title: Progression and reversion predictor clusters (hypertension/bone-joint disease, low WBC; Na up, TSH down) derived in a single Italian multi-centre cohort, with no replication cohort for either direction
gaps.closure_criteria: Replication of the chronic-disease cluster, WBC, Na and TSH associations with MCI progression/reversion in at least one independent community cohort.
gaps.description: P-1348 (Italian multi-centre community cohort, n=459) derives a hypertension/bone-joint cluster and low WBC as progression predictors and Na-up/TSH-down as reversion predictors from a single country's clinic/lab routine data; reversion predictors are rare corpus-wide and none of these associations has been replicated, leaving both directions single-cohort.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for replication of Na/TSH/WBC/comorbidity-cluster effects on cognitive change: G-NEW-1297/P-1297 covers epigenetic-age reversion in US HRS; P-445/P-290 cover reversion rates but not these biochemical predictors; no corpus record replicates P-1348's specific cluster structure, so the falsification attempt failed.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: Somatic comorbidity clusters and electrolyte/TH axis markers are cheap, modifiable and routinely collected, but single-country cluster structures are fragile to healthcare-system coding practices; the reversion direction in particular needs a second population before it informs clinical counselling.

gaps.title: Subthreshold regional florbetaben SUVR conversion thresholds derived in one Korean memory clinic with no independent florbetaben cohort; region-specific cut-offs unvalidated across scanners
gaps.closure_criteria: External replication of the subthreshold regional (e.g. lateral temporal) SUVR conversion thresholds in a non-Korean florbetaben cohort with amyloid-negative aMCI follow-up.
gaps.description: P-1350 (Asan Medical Center, n=103 amyloid-negative aMCI final, + ADNI UC Berkeley replication) proposes subthreshold regional FBB SUVR cut-offs that still predict dementia conversion; the ADNI arm replicates the phenomenon but the region-specific thresholds were derived at one Korean site with one scanner pipeline, so scanner and cohort transferability of the exact cut-offs is untested.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for other subthreshold-amyloid SUVR conversion thresholds: P-60/P-1343 use plasma/CSF tau around amyloid-positivity boundaries; no other corpus study derives or replicates regional subthreshold FBB SUVR cut-offs in amyloid-negatives, so the falsification attempt failed.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: Subthreshold regional SUVR signal is biologically plausible (early sparse plaques can be disease-defining), but scanner- and pipeline-specific threshold derivation without harmonisation makes the exact region cut-offs non-portable across sites.

gaps.title: Immune-repertoire (IGK+TRA) + WDR37 MCI-to-AD model (C-index 0.643) validated only within the single Japanese NCGG biobank; no cross-ethnic replication and no functional validation of WDR37
gaps.closure_criteria: Cross-ethnic external validation of the IGK+TRA repertoire + WDR37 signature on MCI-to-AD follow-up, plus functional evidence for WDR37 in immune-neuronal signalling.
gaps.description: P-1352 (NCGG Biobank Japan, n=145 MCI with follow-up of 856 total RNA-seq) builds a validated C-index 0.643 model from IGK+TRA repertoire features and WDR37 expression; the repertoire is inferred from bulk RNA-seq, the cohort is single-country, and WDR37's role in immune-neuronal signalling is asserted without functional experiments.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for immune-repertoire-based conversion models outside Japan: P-1351 validates inflammatory DEGS in Singapore+ADNI but does not use TCR/BCR clonality; no corpus paper replicates IGK+TRA/WDR37, so the falsification attempt failed.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: Bulk-RNA-derived repertoire features are sensitive to library depth and deconvolution assumptions, and clonality markers are population- and HLA-structured; C-index 0.643 in one biobank does not yet justify a blood test.

gaps.title: Neurotrophin-pathway 6-SNP PRS for 3-year MCI-to-AD conversion (ADNI AUC 0.720 / NACC 0.609) has no non-European replication and no functional validation of 4 of 6 SNPs
gaps.description: P-1353 (ADNI discovery n=767 + NACC replication n=1373, both US, predominantly European ancestry) finds a 6-SNP neurotrophin-pathway PRS improves 3-year MCI-to-AD prediction (0.682->0.720 ADNI, 0.586->0.609 NACC), but the longitudinal cognition/CSF/MRI associations are ADNI-only (NACC lacks those phenotypes), and four of the six SNPs (PIK3R1 rs173703/rs13167294, CALM1 rs8006462, PLCG2 rs4073828) have no significant brain eQTL, leaving their mechanism unanchored.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for pathway-PRS MCI-to-AD replications outside ADNI/NACC or functional progression genetics of TP73/PIK3R1/CALM1/PLCG2: P-1333/P-1335/P-1349 PRSs use different loci (APOE-stratified, non-APOE, EAA), none replicate the neurotrophin six-SNP signature or its eQTL claims; falsification failed.
gaps.closure_criteria: Multi-ancestry (e.g., Asian or South American) replication of the 6-SNP PRS on MCI-to-AD follow-up, plus functional evidence for the non-eQTL SNPs.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: Pathway-restricted PRSs inherit cohort ancestry structure; a PRS that only lifts 3-year AUC by 0.03-0.04 inside one ancestry group is not yet a stratification tool until the same alleles are shown to carry the same sign and size elsewhere.

gaps.title: EGEG gastrointestinal-myoelectrical MCI screening nomogram (validation AUC 0.81) is single-region, with an internal abstract/results AUC discrepancy (0.75 vs 0.81)
gaps.description: P-1354 (western China, 60 communities, n=886; 106 MCI) builds an eight-predictor EGEG nomogram whose validation AUC is reported as 0.75 in the abstract but 0.81 in the results section (95% CI 0.74-0.88), validated only on a same-centre 7:3 split; calibration degrades above 0.4 predicted risk, and no external or cross-device validation exists.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for other gut-signal or peripheral-physiology MCI screeners with external validation: none uses EGEG and none externally validates a similar nomogram; falsification failed.
gaps.closure_criteria: Multi-centre replication with cross-device EGEG parameter standardisation and a resolved, pre-specified primary-outcome AUC.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: A screening signal must generalise beyond the device and region that produced it; an internal abstract/results inconsistency signals that the operating threshold is not yet stable enough to lock into a clinical cut-point.

gaps.title: rTMS-induced plasma MMP/TIMP modulation in MCI (n=20 pilot) has no replication, CSF/imaging correlation, or mechanistic verification
gaps.description: P-1356 (n=20, 10 rTMS/10 sham) reports 6-month reduction of plasma MMP1/9/10 and increase of TIMP1/2 with concurrent visuospatial improvement, but the sample is a single-centre pilot without CSF MMP measures, neuroimaging correlation, or a dementia-outcome arm; the claimed link from neuromodulation to synaptic plasticity via peripheral MMPs is asserted, not demonstrated.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for larger rTMS-biomarker trials or CSF/imaging MMP studies in MCI: corpus NIBS papers (P-418, P-427) report cognitive/connectivity outcomes, not MMP panels; no corpus paper verifies the plasma-MMP to brain-plasticity path; falsification failed.
gaps.closure_criteria: Larger randomised trial with CSF MMP/TIMP, structural/functional imaging, and conversion-relevant follow-up outcomes; replication of the visuospatial effect.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: Fluid biomarker claims from trials with n=10 per arm are unstable; until the MMP/TIMP shift is reproduced with CSF and imaging anchors, it is a pilot signal rather than a response biomarker.

gaps.title: Combined baseline MTL MRI + plasma p-tau181/NfL fast-progressor model (AUC 0.89-0.93 MCI) is ADNI-only with unstable region selection
gaps.description: P-1357 (ADNI GO/2 n=606) shows combined baseline MRI+plasma biomarkers discriminate fast vs slow progressors with AUC 0.89-0.93 in MCI and 0.65-0.73 in CN, but all 15 models are derived and evaluated within ADNI (no external cohort), only p-tau181/NfL plasma analytes are tested, and the most predictive MTL region varies across models (BA35 8x, posterior hippocampus 6x, anterior hippocampus 2x), so the operative feature set is not fixed.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for an externally validated MRI+plasma progressor model in MCI: P-1343 combines plasma p-tau217 with cognition (single cohort), P-1344 29-gene plasma RF (ADNI-only), none externally validates a combined MTL-subregion MRI plus plasma model on decline-rate outcomes; falsification failed.
gaps.closure_criteria: External-cohort validation with pre-specified MTL features (or an event-based composite) and added p-tau217/GFAP plasma measures.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: A progressor-enrichment model whose best predictor changes across outcome models is not yet a deployable screening rule; region selection instability must be resolved (e.g., fixed event-based summary score) before trial use.

gaps.title: Cognitive-only two-step dementia-risk model needs validation in diverse primary-care/referral populations and biomarker add-ons
gaps.description: P-1390 (1004 SCD/MCI: 612 ADNI + 392 BioFINDER-1; Alz & Dementia 2024) replicates a brief-cognitive two-step all-cause dementia model in BioFINDER-1 (AUC 0.86) but the replication PPV dropped from 85.8% (ADNI) to 62.5%, reflecting different referral populations and dementia base rates; no diverse primary-care or non-European validation exists, and biomarker add-ons for the intermediate-risk tier are untested.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for replication of the same two-step 1-year-change cognitive algorithm in primary-care or diverse populations: P-1112 is an all-cause dementia Cox model of drug exposure, and P-608/P-670/P-745/P-857 are umbrella/risk/intervention designs rather than cognitive two-step prediction models; no corpus paper replicates this algorithm outside ADNI and BioFINDER-1; falsification failed.
gaps.closure_criteria: Validation in community/primary-care and non-European referral cohorts, plus evaluation of blood/imaging biomarkers specifically for the intermediate-risk tier.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: The PPV halving on replication shows calibration transfers poorly across base rates; the two-step design's value depends on validated cut-offs and, for the intermediate tier, on orthogonal biomarker stratification.

gaps.title: Early-AD ADAS-Cog-13 decline nomogram is ADNI-only (bootstrap validation) with no external early-AD cohort
gaps.description: P-1391 (421 early symptomatic AD, ADNI-1/GO/2/3; J Alz Dis Reports 2024) builds a biomarker-based nomogram predicting individualized ADAS-Cog-13 decline slopes (overfitting-corrected R2 0.59) but validation is bootstrap-within-ADNI only, the linear-slope assumption is untested against nonlinear trajectories, and trial-enrichment sample-size savings are simulated rather than demonstrated.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for external validation of an early-AD cognitive-decline nomogram: P-768 is a single-centre longitudinal cognitive-decline association study without a nomogram or external validation; P-895 is a primary-care intervention RCT reporting ADAS-Cog Z-scores; P-889 is a CKD cognitive-screening meta-analysis; none validates an early-AD ADAS-Cog-13 slope nomogram outside ADNI; falsification failed.
gaps.closure_criteria: External validation of the nomogram in an independent biomarker-positive early-AD cohort with at least 3 years of repeated ADAS-Cog-13, and testing of nonlinear trajectory assumptions.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: R2 0.59 after optimism correction still leaves substantial decline variance unexplained, and ADNI-only bootstrap validation cannot certify the nomogram for enrichment planning in differently recruited early-AD trials.

gaps.title: Shared T2D-MCI hub genes (COX7C, SNRPG, TOMM7, RPS24) lack functional and longitudinal validation
gaps.description: P-1392 (290 in silico GEO samples + 10 clinical blood samples; Brain Sciences 2024) identifies mitochondrial/translational hub genes shared between T2D and MCI with single-gene AUCs up to 0.916 in the T2D validation set, but the evidence is cross-sectional in silico reanalysis with a tiny clinical set (n=10), no functional (knockdown/overexpression) experiments, no longitudinal T2D-to-cognitive-impairment cohorts, and no correction for multiple testing across analyses.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the corpus for functional or longitudinal validation of COX7C/SNRPG/TOMM7/RPS24 in T2D-MCI: diabetes-related corpus rows (e.g. P-1206 T2DM galectin-3/miRNA) are biomarker or epidemiological studies, none testing these four genes functionally or following T2D patients into cognitive impairment; falsification failed.
gaps.closure_criteria: Functional studies (knockdown/overexpression) of COX7C/SNRPG/TOMM7/RPS24 in neuronal and metabolic models, larger longitudinal T2D cohorts with cognitive follow-up, and plasma protein-level quantification.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: A shared-gene claim built on cross-sectional public microarrays cannot support a causal diabetes-to-cognitive-impairment bridge until the genes' direction and function are tested in longitudinal and experimental settings.

gaps.g5_review_note: Model-authored candidate; gate G5 is an operator action, NOT self-signed.
gaps.title: No corpus study ranks EEG frequency bands as discriminative features, so the alpha-vs-delta/theta MCI-marker question (registered prior KA-09) is unadjudicable from internal evidence
gaps.description: The corpus holds three band-level EEG studies and none performs the evidence class that registered prior KA-09 (Predictor_Surprise: delta/theta beats alpha as MCI discriminator) specifies for its own disproof. P-719 (Beth Israel/Harvard, n=37, amyloid-stratified aMCI) uses the composite SPR (alpha+beta)/(delta+theta), which cannot separate which band carries the signal; P-778 (Newcastle, n=92 MCI, conversion endpoint) uses the theta/alpha ratio whose conversion association (HR 1.84, p=.046) fails both of the paper's own sensitivity analyses; P-890 (Nara Medical University, Japan, n=20 PD-MCI + 10 MCI) reports affirmative alpha-range coherence-cognition correlations (MMSE r=0.761) but in Parkinson-related MCI, no band ranking, and generalisability to non-PD MCI is untested. A targeted scan of all corpus blocks outside the previously mined windows (P-651..P-680, P-681..P-1050, P-1051..P-1392) found no ML feature-importance or graph-metric band-ranking analysis for MCI detection anywhere; alpha-adjacent keyword hits are dominated by non-EEG contexts (Cronbach's alpha, significance alpha, TNF-alpha, GST-alpha, alpha-synuclein, delta-method CIs). The clinical implication KA-09 registers - protocol choice between alpha-suppression metrics and delta/theta connectivity - therefore has no internal evidence basis in either direction.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the full corpus for any EEG band-ranking study (feature importance, graph metric, or explicit between-band comparison for MCI discrimination): modality scan of P-651..P-1392 blocks (the bands not covered by earlier IA-mining sweeps) found EEG-mentioning papers dominated by sleep/PSG (P-769..P-806, P-818..P-827, P-821/P-822 classifiers), rTMS/tDCS protocols, and ERP components (P-658, P-662); the only band-power/coherence papers are P-719, P-778, P-890 (read in full) and P-661 (theta ERS vs alpha ERD in an EMCI/LMCI staging Go/NoGo task - ANOVA on task modulation, not the registered ML/graph ranking class, and a staging contrast rather than MCI-vs-HC discrimination). P-1322 mentions EEG delta/theta slowing only as background prose. No paper closes the gap; falsification failed -> retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: One corpus study reporting band-level feature importance or graph-metric ranking for MCI detection (EEG modality, any cohort) that explicitly compares delta/theta weights against alpha, on an MCI-vs-control or conversion task.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: Band-composite ratios (SPR, theta/alpha) compress the very quantity KA-09 needs decomposed: they cannot attribute discriminative power to a band, so alpha primacy can be neither confirmed nor overturned from composite evidence. P-890's affirmative alpha-coherence finding sits in the PD-MCI population where cholinergic and noradrenergic degeneration differ from typical aMCI, making it the wrong population to settle a general-MCI protocol question. The corpus needs one decomposition study - not more composite-ratio studies - before the KA-09 protocol fork has an evidence basis.

gaps.g5_review_note: Model-authored candidate; gate G5 is an operator action, NOT self-signed.
gaps.title: No corpus study runs a pathologically-incompatible-source transfer arm against a directly-trained baseline, so registered prior KA-10 (transfer works regardless of source-domain pathology) is unadjudicable from internal evidence
gaps.description: KA-10 (Feature_Context_Dependent) registers the belief that transfer learning from any large medical-imaging dataset improves MCI performance regardless of source-domain pathology, disproofable by an incompatible-source arm performing below a directly-trained baseline (or XAI showing transferred attention on anatomically irrelevant regions). The corpus holds a substantial transfer-learning class - P-81 and P-180 (AD/NC source to MCI conversion), P-93 and P-188 (ADNI to small SCD cohorts CLAS/AIBL), P-171/P-174 (disease-state classification source to conversion target, 228 MCI-C/222 MCI-NC), P-199 (Med3D cross-organ initialization to pMCI/sMCI, n=577), P-236 (incomplete-modality transfer), P-356 (ImageNet-pretrained ViT on hippocampal slices), P-358 (Siamese/TL strategies) - and in every reported instance the source is pathology-COMPATIBLE (AD/NC, MCI, or a large 3D medical set whose compatibility is asserted, never tested) and transfer helps: P-93 'transfer learning from ADNI significantly enhanced small-sample SCD model performance'; P-174 'transfer learning from disease-state classification enhances prediction of future MCI conversion' (450 subjects, source 1080). The one study that runs a directly-trained comparator arm, P-3 (CAAT attention transfer 74.61% vs weight-based TL 73.03% vs baseline 3D-CNN 70.84% for MCI-to-AD conversion), uses compatible AD-domain sources only - it falsifies the weaker 'TL always beats baseline' reading but never varies the compatibility parameter KA-10 asserts. No corpus study trains an arm from a pathologically INCOMPATIBLE source (e.g. cardiac, hepatic, musculoskeletal imaging) on an MCI task, so the compatibility premise itself has no internal evidence in either direction.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic scanned all 49 transfer-learning-mentioning blocks for an incompatible-source arm or a directly-trained comparator under incompatible initialization. P-3 runs the baseline-arm design but with compatible AD-domain sources. P-356 (ImageNet ViT) is the only genuinely cross-domain initialization; its block confirms a 3D-ResNet baseline exists but reports no comparative transfer outcome, so it cannot close. P-199's Med3D source is trained across non-brain organs - the corpus's closest incompatible-source instance - but reports no directly-trained same-task arm and its Related-findings frame cross-organ initialization as a strength. P-121 compares architectures (CNN vs ViT) on EEG scalograms, not source domains. No closing paper; falsification failed -> retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: One corpus study training >=2 arms on the same MCI task - one initialized from a pathologically incompatible source domain, one directly trained or initialized from a compatible source - reporting both arms' performance, or XAI evidence that transferred attention localizes to anatomically irrelevant regions on an MCI task.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: Compatibility is an untested free parameter in every corpus architecture: transfer pipelines (Med3D init, ImageNet ViT, ADNI encoders) vary the source but always within the compatible regime, so the corpus can only show that transfer helps where it is expected to help. The KA-10 fork - does source pathology matter - requires a negative-control arm the field has not run; until one exists, architecture selection is justified by compatible-source gains alone, which cannot distinguish 'features transfer across all of medicine' from 'only pathology-compatible features transfer'. The distinction decides whether a small-cohort MCI lab may legally initialize from any large medical checkpoint or must pay for domain-matched pretraining.

gaps.title: No corpus study reports the registered KA-11 evidence class - hippocampal texture vs volumetric features within one model on one cohort - and the corpus's single in-model comparison (P-183, whole-brain T2, conversion task) runs the opposite direction
gaps.description: KA-11 (Feature_Insufficient) registers the belief that hippocampal texture carries independent discriminative information beyond hippocampal volume for MCI detection, disproofable by texture accuracy converging with volumetric accuracy on the same task and dataset. A corpus-wide scan of texture-within-80-chars-of-volume and radiomics-near-hippocampus co-mentions yields exactly three blocks. P-524 (n=714 A+T(N)+ ADNI-adjacent) and P-570 (n=1627, ADNI 1319 + Dalian 308) compare feature families across REGIONS (cerebellar/parietal radiomics vs hippocampal models), confounding region effect with feature effect - neither runs texture-vs-volume within one segmented structure. P-183 (PMID 34442078, n=40, single site) is the only within-model head-to-head: T2-map signal/texture vs volumetric descriptors across 83 brain regions for MCI-to-AD progression, reporting 'signal/texture features improved prediction, while volumetric features were comparatively less influential' (neuropsych-only 0.727 AUC -> 0.824 with texture/signal). Under rule 6 this is not a disproof of KA-11: it is the wrong direction for convergence (texture dominance, not texture-volume equality), the wrong task (progression, not registered detection), and whole-brain rather than hippocampus-local. But it is also the corpus's ONLY within-model texture-vs-volume comparison, so the question KA-11 poses has never been directly run on any corpus cohort.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic re-read all three co-mention blocks plus their hippocampal-radiomics literature lines: P-570's cerebellar-vs-hippocampal comparison varies region while bundling texture+volume inside each region's feature set; P-524's N-biomarker benchmarks region-level radiomics against CSF t-tau, not against volumetry; P-183 is in-model but whole-brain T2 on the conversion task with n=40. No hippocampus-local texture-vs-volume same-cohort comparison exists anywhere in the 1360-row corpus; falsification failed -> retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: One corpus study on a single cohort extracting BOTH texture and volumetric features from the same hippocampal segmentations for MCI-vs-control (or conversion) modelling, reporting either convergent accuracy (KA-11 disproof) or an independent texture contribution (KA-11 support) with both feature families entered in one model.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: The corpus's radiomics literature compares feature families between regions or against clinical benchmarks, never WITHIN a segmented structure, so architectural claims about texture-vs-volume informativeness rest on between-region contrasts that confound region with feature family. P-183's opposite-direction finding (texture dominant, volume weak) on whole-brain T2 makes the missing hippocampus-local experiment more informative, not less: if texture dominance survives restriction to the hippocampus on a detection task, KA-11's premise is not merely unproven but probably inverted - and current hippocampal-volume-first pipelines would be discarding their most acquisition-sensitive signal.

gaps.title: Serum N-glycomics MCI biomarker panels have no external-cohort replication and no longitudinal evidence, so the aMCI-stage glycan discriminators are unactionable until validated
gaps.description: P-1417 (99 serum N-glycans plus 195 isomeric structures by C18 LC-MS/MS with PRM-MS validation, n=64 Michigan ADRC/UM-MAP: 28 controls, 10 naMCI, 14 aMCI, 12 AD) reports the corpus’s first serum N-glycomics panel: six PRM-validated glycans (3511, 5410, 4610, 5521, 6702, 5711) give combined AUC 1.00 for aMCI vs AD (5521 alone 0.99), isomeric profiling gives combined AUC 1.00 for naMCI vs aMCI, sialylation is upregulated and mono/core-fucosylation downregulated in AD, and 5521 correlates with conventional AD markers (tau, pT181, pT217, GFAP). No other glycan-anchored blood-classifier record exists in the 1391-row registry, so none of these effects has a replication cohort, and the design is cross-sectional single-centre: whether the aMCI-stage glycan signal (a) survives an independent cohort, (b) precedes conversion (no longitudinal arm), and (c) adds value beyond the plasma p-tau/NfL/GFAP markers the paper itself correlates with are all untested. Existing blood-biomarker validation gaps do not cover the glycomics axis.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the 1391-row registry for other glycomics/glycan records (Modality/Key_Novelty/Method fields) - P-1417 is the only glycan record in the corpus; no closing paper exists. Cross-checked gaps.json: the only glycan-anchored entry is the IgG N-glycosylation + cytokine case-control gap (P-1273, Shandong Taian) whose axis (IgG Fc glyco-immune) and evidence class this gap extends rather than duplicates - P-1273’s gap covers glyco-immune precedence in MCI, this gap covers serum total-N-glycome panel replication and longitudinal validity. Falsification failed -> retained as candidate.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: Glycan panels are structural-isomer readouts of secretory-pathway and inflammatory state, not protein-abundance readouts: the aMCI-vs-AD discriminating glycans separate stages where protein-level AD markers (the paper’s own pT181/pT217/GFAP correlations) already perform, so the architectural question is whether an isomer-resolved glycan layer carries orthogonal stage information or merely re-expresses the same inflammatory/protein signal in a different molecular alphabet. Without an external cohort and a head-to-head incremental-value design against plasma ATN markers, the glycan layer’s information channel remains unidentified.
gaps.closure_criteria: External-cohort replication of the six-glycan aMCI-vs-AD panel and the naMCI-vs-aMCI isomeric panel in an independent serum glycomics study, plus a longitudinal arm testing whether glycan trajectories precede conversion, plus a head-to-head AUC-increment analysis of glycans beyond plasma p-tau217/NfL/GFAP; a null external replication or zero AUC increment beyond ATN markers would falsify the panel’s clinical claim.

gaps.title: No corpus study measures amyloid status alongside hippocampal microstructure and memory mediation in amyloid-NEGATIVE MCI, so the proposed subthreshold-amyloid hippocampal-risk pathway (WM injury -> hippocampal atrophy -> episodic-memory decline) is single-cohort and unreplicated
gaps.description: P-1425 (BABRI, n=69: 19 amyloid-negative MCI, 18 amyloid-positive MCI, 32 NC; florbetapir PET + 3T T1/DTI) reports that amyloid-negative MCI already shows AD-like multidomain deficits and widespread white-matter compromise, with the amyloid-associated increment localised to the left hippocampal system (greater left cingulum-hippocampus MD and left hippocampal GMV loss), and a mediation model in which hippocampal GMV carries the white-matter-disruption effect onto episodic memory (AVLT-delay; bootstrapped indirect effect -0.333, CI -0.590 to -0.115). The paper itself argues amyloid negativity does not preclude AD progression (citing ~21% 2.5-year conversion). No other corpus record combines amyloid-PET stratification with DTI tract metrics, hippocampal volumetry and a memory-mediation model in the amyloid-negative subgroup: the closest imaging records are amyloid-PET staging studies without DTI mediation (P-578) and DTI studies without amyloid stratification (P-1416), so the pathway's effect sizes, laterality and the mediation direction are all single-cohort estimates awaiting replication.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the 1396-row registry for amyloid-stratified MCI imaging studies combining DTI, hippocampal volumetry and a memory-mediation model: P-578 (dual amyloid+FDG PET, n=145 aMCI) lacks DTI/GMV mediation; P-1416 (DTI-ALPS + hippocampal FA/MD with CSF Abeta42/p-tau, n=60) reports group-level DTI differences without amyloid-status stratification or a mediation model; P-584 (PREVENT-AD MEG+plasma amyloid, n=102) measures amyloid longitudinally but no DTI tract mediation; P-1281 (ADNI hippocampal volumetry + PRS/APOE) lacks DTI and mediation. No closing paper exists; falsification failed -> retained as candidate.
gaps.closure_criteria: An independent amyloid-PET-stratified MCI cohort with DTI, hippocampal volumetry and longitudinal memory follow-up replicating (a) the left-lateralised amyloid-hippocampus increment and (b) the GMV-mediated WM-memory pathway in the amyloid-negative subgroup; ideally with incident-conversion endpoints.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: If white-matter injury precedes and drives hippocampal atrophy via the cingulum-hippocampus pathway even before amyloid positivity, then intervention windows open earlier than amyloid-based staging implies - but until the mediation replicates independently, hippocampal GMV cannot be promoted from a correlational marker to a causal staging node in the amyloid-negative population.

gaps.title: No corpus study jointly profiles the gut-microbial tryptophan-indole axis and circulating or urine host metabolomics on the same participants, so the proposed microbial-to-host-metabolite route into MCI is assembled only from disjoint cohorts
gaps.description: Gut-microbiome MCI studies in the corpus (P-760 shotgun metagenomics, P-856 16S stool in LAPDR, P-1201 16S with sex-specific risk models, P-600 diet/microRNA) establish that microbial composition shifts with MCI, and host-side metabolomics independently nominates indole pathway disruption: P-1402 (untargeted urine LC-MS/MS, MTBLS8662, n=162) reports indole as the key metabolite at the MCI-to-AD transition, and P-1396 (targeted plasma UHPLC-MS/MS, Qingdao rural, n=171) nominates isolithocholic acid - a microbially bile-acid-derived metabolite - in its MCI panel. The mechanistic claim that microbial dysbiosis drives the host indole/bile-acid signal that tracks cognitive stage therefore has both a microbial half and a host half measured in the corpus, but never on the same participants: every microbiome study lacks paired host metabolomics on its own cohort, and both metabolomics studies lack any microbiome measurement. Without a same-participant joint profile the direction of the axis (microbe-to-host vs host-to-microbe) and the mediating metabolites remain unidentifiable.
gaps.critic_falsification_attempt: Critic searched the 1360-row registry for paired designs: all four gut-microbiome blocks (P-600, P-760, P-856, P-1201) were read for host plasma/urine metabolomics co-measurement - P-760 pairs microbiome with serum microRNA (not metabolomics), P-856 pairs with clinical/lifestyle variables only, P-1201 pairs with neuropsych and demographics, P-600 is a diet-quality/microRNA design; none quantifies host metabolites. Reverse search of metabolomics blocks for gut co-measurement found none. The corpus multi-omics row P-1220 (plasma/urine/saliva NMR) has no microbiome arm. Falsification failed -> retained as candidate.
gaps.architectural_interpretation: The two measurement families answer architecturally incompatible questions under the same disease label: microbiome designs identify WHO carries a dysbiotic community, metabolomics designs identify WHICH host metabolic state tracks stage, and the causal handle (microbial tryptophan/bile-acid metabolism feeding the host indole pool) lives in the coupling term that only a same-participant joint design can estimate - disjoint cohorts can agree on marginal associations while leaving the coupling sign and magnitude unidentified.
gaps.closure_criteria: One MCI-staged cohort with 16S or shotgun microbiome sequencing AND targeted or untargeted host metabolomics (plasma and/or urine) on the same participants, reporting microbe-metabolite correlations (e.g., indole- or bile-acid-associated taxa vs P-1402/P-1396 nominated metabolites) and their mediation of the cognition association; a same-participant null correlation would falsify the coupling claim.

gaps.gap_statement: In the frontier speech/language MCI-marker stratum (P-680..P-1262), MCI-SUBTYPE RESOLUTION and DETECTION PERFORMANCE are reported by disjoint sets of papers, so no discrimination figure in this stratum can be read as a property of the marker rather than of the tested cohort's subtype mix. The papers that resolve subtype find the linguistic/gestural signal is subtype-INDEXED rather than severity-graded: P-746 (N=160 Taiwanese memory clinic) finds a DIFFERENT semantic cluster carries the conversion signal in amnestic single-domain MCI (fruits cluster II, 82 per cent, cutoff 0.96, OR 17.5) than in amnestic multiple-domain MCI (vegetables cluster I, 81 per cent, cutoff 0.62, OR 13.5), with all fourteen other cluster comparisons non-significant, and records the non-amnestic multiple-domain group as indistinguishable from controls on all eight clusters despite impairment in two cognitive domains while the amnestic single-domain group, impaired in memory alone, was already abnormal on two - i.e. the marker is blind to the MORE broadly impaired subtype. P-747 (five clinically defined groups: 10 HC / 11 executive MCI / 10 temporo-medial MCI / 11 mild AD / 10 moderate AD) finds no significant correlation between gesture production and MMSE or study group and reads its iconic-gesture pattern as separating temporo-medial from executive MCI rather than tracking severity. NEITHER computes an MCI-versus-control discrimination statistic of any kind. Conversely, the two frontier papers that DO report detection performance treat MCI as one undifferentiated class and report no subtype composition at all: P-884 (mean one-vs-rest AUC 0.81, best OvR AUC 0.95, three-class accuracy 66.7 per cent) ascertains its 77 MCI cases only with MoCA-J, HDS-R and MMSE - screening instruments that cannot yield a domain subtype even in principle - and P-938 (MCI-vs-HC 63 per cent, AD-HC 74 per cent, three-class 82.47-84.17 per cent) administers a full neuropsychological battery to 20 memory-clinic MCI cases but reports no subtype breakdown. P-748 shows the same class is not even internally consistent in ascertainment: its 35 MCI cases are assembled from three sources under Petersen (2004), CERAD and unstated criteria. WHY IT MATTERS: subtype mix is not constant across the settings these tools are proposed for - memory-clinic series are amnestic-enriched, community and remote screening (the deployment case P-884 and P-938 both make) is not - so every published speech/voice-marker AUC in this stratum is a case-mix-weighted average over an unreported composition that no reader can reweight, and confirmed VF-12 (digital/behavioural biomarkers detect MCI across independent cohorts) rests on numbers whose transportability across case-mix has never been quantified. CLOSURE CRITERIA: one speech- or voice-based MCI detection study, N >= 150 MCI, in which MCI subtype is assigned by consensus neuropsychological criteria (amnestic single-domain / amnestic multiple-domain / non-amnestic), reporting (a) MCI-vs-HC AUC with 95 per cent CI separately per subtype on the same model, and (b) the change in pooled AUC when the MCI arm is reweighted from the study's own composition to a stated community subtype distribution.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'a calibration or transfer failure across language, education, device or setting' (the OCT multi-vendor domain-shift gap and the multi-site EEG replication gap), transposed from a hardware/site axis to a clinical case-mix axis - and it is grounded in a printed result rather than an assumed vulnerability: P-746 shows the marker is blind to the subtype with MORE impaired domains, which is the specific fact that makes an unreported composition able to move an AUC in either direction. It is non-obvious because the split is not a shortcoming of any single paper - each half of this literature does its own job competently - and is invisible to any per-paper review; it only appears when the mechanism papers and the performance papers are laid side by side, which is exactly the cross-paper blind spot the lens asks for. It is also actionable with data that already exists: every memory clinic contributing to these studies runs the battery needed to assign a subtype.
gaps.closure_criteria: One speech- or voice-based MCI detection study, N >= 150 MCI, in which MCI subtype is assigned by consensus neuropsychological criteria (amnestic single-domain / amnestic multiple-domain / non-amnestic), reporting (a) MCI-vs-HC AUC with 95 per cent CI separately per subtype on the same model, and (b) the change in pooled AUC when the MCI arm is reweighted from the study's own composition to a stated community subtype distribution.

It is non-obvious because the split is not a shortcoming of any single paper - each half of this literature does its own job competently - and is invisible to any per-paper review; it only appears when the mechanism papers and the performance papers are laid side by side, which is exactly the cross-paper blind spot the lens asks for. It is also actionable with data that already exists: every memory clinic contributing to these studies runs the battery needed to assign a subtype.
gaps.critic_falsification: The absence clause is verified only for the frontier slice I can read (P-680..P-1262). P-938's own card names four pre-frontier corpus speech papers - P-6, P-9, P-352, P-354 - as addressing the same detection task with higher reported accuracies, and P-57 to P-60 and P-612 are further pre-frontier speech entries. I have not opened any of them, so one of them may already report MCI-subtype composition or a subtype-stratified AUC, which would move this record to partially_open. Separately, the external literature does contain amnestic-versus-non-amnestic comparisons of language performance, so a reviewer could argue the subtype-dependence itself is established outside the corpus (EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE); the part I believe is genuinely unmet - and on which the record should stand or fall - is not the subtype-dependence but the reporting practice: a speech-marker AUC published together with its cohort's subtype composition and a reweighting to a different composition.

gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: In the frontier speech/language MCI-marker stratum (P-680..P-1262), MCI-SUBTYPE RESOLUTION and DETECTION PERFORMANCE are reported by disjoint sets of papers, so no discrimination figure in this stratum can be read as a property of the marker rather than of the tested cohort's subtype mix. The papers that resolve subtype find the linguistic/gestural signal is subtype-INDEXED rather than severity-graded: P-746 (N=160 Taiwanese memory clinic) finds a DIFFERENT semantic cluster carries the conversion signal in amnestic single-domain MCI (fruits cluster II, 82 per cent, cutoff 0.96, OR 17.5) than in amnestic multiple-domain MCI (vegetables cluster I, 81 per cent, cutoff 0.62, OR 13.5), with all fourteen other cluster comparisons non-significant, and records the non-amnestic multiple-domain group as indistinguishable from controls on all eight clusters despite impairment in two cognitive domains while the amnestic single-domain group, impaired in memory alone, was already abnormal on two - i.e. the marker is blind to the MORE broadly impaired subtype. P-747 (five clinically defined groups: 10 HC / 11 executive MCI / 10 temporo-medial MCI / 11 mild AD / 10 moderate AD) finds no significant correlation between gesture production and MMSE or study group and reads its iconic-gesture pattern as separating temporo-medial from executive MCI rather than tracking severity. NEITHER computes an MCI-versus-control discrimination statistic of any kind. Conversely, the two frontier papers that DO report detection performance treat MCI as one undifferentiated class and report no subtype composition at all: P-884 (mean one-vs-rest AUC 0.81, best OvR AUC 0.95, three-class accuracy 66.7 per cent) ascertains its 77 MCI cases only with MoCA-J, HDS-R and MMSE - screening instruments that cannot yield a domain subtype even in principle - and P-938 (MCI-vs-HC 63 per cent, AD-HC 74 per cent, three-class 82.47-84.17 per cent) administers a full neuropsychological battery to 20 memory-clinic MCI cases but reports no subtype breakdown. P-748 shows the same class is not even internally consistent in ascertainment: its 35 MCI cases are assembled from three sources under Petersen (2004), CERAD and unstated criteria. WHY IT MATTERS: subtype mix is not constant across the settings these tools are proposed for - memory-clinic series are amnestic-enriched, community and remote screening (the deployment case P-884 and P-938 both make) is not - so every published speech/voice-marker AUC in this stratum is a case-mix-weighted average over an unreported composition that no reader can reweight, and confirmed VF-12 (digital/behavioural biomarkers detect MCI across independent cohorts) rests on numbers whose transportability across case-mix has never been quantified. CLOSURE CRITERIA: one speech- or voice-based MCI detection study, N >= 150 MCI, in which MCI subtype is assigned by consensus neuropsychological criteria (amnestic single-domain / amnestic multiple-domain / non-amnestic), reporting (a) MCI-vs-HC AUC with 95 per cent CI separately per subtype on the same model, and (b) the change in pooled AUC when the MCI arm is reweighted from the study's own composition to a stated community subtype distribution. STATUS: candidate, pending_human_review, gate_verified=false.

gaps.gap_statement: In this corpus's speech/language MCI literature the AUTOMATABLE feature families and the DISCRIMINATING feature family are not the same, and no study measures the automation step that would join them for the hand-coded syntactic and referential variables (P-60 reports ASR-derived lexical features correlating r about 0.92 with manual-transcription features and MCI-vs-CN 87.6 per cent - an automation check on a different, generic feature family) - so the cost-and-scale argument on which speech screening is advanced is evidenced only by the arm of the dissociation that separates MCI from controls least well. P-748 states the dissociation as a within-study head-to-head on the same 105 transcripts: all four generic, machine-computable lexical/syntactic measures were null (utterance count omnibus p .788, MLU .063, type-token ratio .252, formal grammatical errors Fisher pairwise p at 1), while the hand-coded, hypothesis-selected grammatical variables carried the effect, the adjunct clause ratio at MCI d .93 - and P-748's own positioning names that null generic family as the one 'feeding the machine-learning classifiers'. P-747 corroborates the null side on a second manually annotated channel (no significant correlation between gesture production and MMSE or study group). The two frontier papers that DO report a detection figure use a DIFFERENT automatable family - paralinguistic acoustics and speech timing, not lexical/syntactic indices - and reach only weak MCI-relevant performance while making an explicitly at-scale deployment case: P-884's 17 purely acoustic features from two phrases give three-class accuracy 66.7 per cent with the MCI-vs-rest AUC never reported separately, and P-938's automatable speech-timing features give MCI-vs-HC 63 per cent while its improvement path is 'automated extraction from everyday conversation without a caregiver'. Meanwhile the coded side is expensive and its per-variable reliability is unbounded: P-750 quantifies multimodal annotation at about 2 hours of work per 30 seconds of video (about 240 times real time) over 8044 hand-annotated non-verbal markers, and prints no inter-annotator agreement value at all; P-748 double-annotated 20 per cent of each group's samples and reports only a global point-by-point agreement of 92.6 per cent, with no kappa and no per-variable breakdown, which matters because its discriminating variables (referential NP specificity, adjunct embedding) are the harder judgement calls, not the countable ones. WHY IT MATTERS: no study in this stratum reports how much of a hand-coded effect survives fully automatic extraction, nor the coding reliability that upper-bounds what any extractor could reproduce. Until one does, confirmed VF-12 (digital/behavioural biomarkers detect MCI across independent cohorts) is carried by feature families that this corpus's own head-to-head reports as null or weak, and the largest reported linguistic effect in the stratum has no deployable measurement path. CLOSURE CRITERIA: on an existing MCI/HC connected-speech corpus (N >= 100, >= 35 MCI - the SGUL/OPTIMA/Pitt material P-748 used would serve), re-derive the adjunct clause ratio and the definite-versus-indefinite NP distribution from a fully automatic pipeline with no manual correction, and report (a) per-variable agreement between automatic and hand-coded values (ICC or kappa), (b) the hand-coded inter-rater reliability that bounds it, and (c) the group effect size and MCI-vs-HC AUC obtained from the automatic versions against the hand-coded versions on the same transcripts.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern of a clinical-utility / deployability failure - 'discrimination proven, decision impact never tested' - applied one step earlier in the chain: here it is the measurement pipeline, not the clinical decision, that is never tested in the form it would be deployed in. It is non-obvious because both halves look healthy in isolation: the linguistics papers report a large, theoretically motivated effect and the engineering papers report a working classifier, and nothing inside either half reveals that they are standing on different feature families. It rests on a printed within-study head-to-head (P-748, same 105 transcripts) rather than on a comparison the miner assembled across studies, and on the authors' own cost figure for the coded side (P-750). It is actionable on data that already exists, and its closure test produces a number that would be immediately decision-relevant for anyone building a speech screening tool.

gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: there is published work outside this corpus on the effect of automatic speech recognition and automatic parsing errors on dementia speech classification, so a reviewer can fairly say the general question 'does automation degrade the marker' has been asked elsewhere. My defence is narrow and should be judged on it: that external work targets the generic lexical/syntactic and paralinguistic families - precisely the families P-748 reports as null here - whereas the variables that carry the d .93 effect (referential NP specificity, adjunct embedding, and P-746's healthy-control-derived semantic cluster distances) are not standard pipeline outputs and their automatic-versus-manual agreement is, as far as this corpus records, unmeasured. A reviewer who judges that a dependency parser already computes adjunct embedding reliably enough should reject this record. A second, weaker objection: P-748's generic-measure null comes from a pooled three-source sample whose provenance confounds diagnosis, so the null itself could be a power or heterogeneity artefact rather than evidence that automatable measures do not work.

gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: In this corpus's speech/language MCI literature the AUTOMATABLE feature families and the DISCRIMINATING feature family are not the same, and no study measures the automation step that would join them - so the cost-and-scale argument on which speech screening is advanced is evidenced only by the arm of the dissociation that separates MCI from controls least well. P-748 states the dissociation as a within-study head-to-head on the same 105 transcripts: all four generic, machine-computable lexical/syntactic measures were null (utterance count omnibus p .788, MLU .063, type-token ratio .252, formal grammatical errors Fisher pairwise p at 1), while the hand-coded, hypothesis-selected grammatical variables carried the effect, the adjunct clause ratio at MCI d .93 - and P-748's own positioning names that null generic family as the one 'feeding the machine-learning classifiers'. P-747 corroborates the null side on a second manually annotated channel (no significant correlation between gesture production and MMSE or study group). The two frontier papers that DO report a detection figure use a DIFFERENT automatable family - paralinguistic acoustics and speech timing, not lexical/syntactic indices - and reach only weak MCI-relevant performance while making an explicitly at-scale deployment case: P-884's 17 purely acoustic features from two phrases give three-class accuracy 66.7 per cent with the MCI-vs-rest AUC never reported separately, and P-938's automatable speech-timing features give MCI-vs-HC 63 per cent while its improvement path is 'automated extraction from everyday conversation without a caregiver'. Meanwhile the coded side is expensive and its reliability is unbounded: P-750 quantifies multimodal annotation at about 2 hours of work per 30 seconds of video (about 240 times real time) over 8044 hand-annotated non-verbal markers, and prints no inter-annotator agreement value at all; P-748 double-coded 10 per cent of samples with no kappa and no per-variable breakdown, which matters because its discriminating variables (referential NP specificity, adjunct embedding) are the harder judgement calls, not the countable ones. WHY IT MATTERS: no study in this stratum reports how much of a hand-coded effect survives fully automatic extraction, nor the coding reliability that upper-bounds what any extractor could reproduce. Until one does, confirmed VF-12 (digital/behavioural biomarkers detect MCI across independent cohorts) is carried by feature families that this corpus's own head-to-head reports as null or weak, and the largest reported linguistic effect in the stratum has no deployable measurement path. CLOSURE CRITERIA: on an existing MCI/HC connected-speech corpus (N >= 100, >= 35 MCI - the SGUL/OPTIMA/Pitt material P-748 used would serve), re-derive the adjunct clause ratio and the definite-versus-indefinite NP distribution from a fully automatic pipeline with no manual correction, and report (a) per-variable agreement between automatic and hand-coded values (ICC or kappa), (b) the hand-coded inter-rater reliability that bounds it, and (c) the group effect size and MCI-vs-HC AUC obtained from the automatic versions against the hand-coded versions on the same transcripts. STATUS: candidate, pending_human_review, gate_verified=false.

gaps.gap_statement: SYMPTOMATIC CNS MEDICATION STATUS IS A DETERMINANT OF THE RESTING-EEG QUANTITIES THIS CORPUS USES AS MCI MARKERS AND IS SIMULTANEOUSLY A PROXY FOR THE OUTCOME THOSE MARKERS ARE ASKED TO PREDICT, YET NO STUDY QUANTIFIES THE MEDICATION-ATTRIBUTABLE COMPONENT OF AN EEG MARKER'S GROUP DIFFERENCE, DISCRIMINATION OR HAZARD. The corpus's only prospective qEEG prognostic model, P-778 (SUPErB, 92 MCI, 14 incident dementias), prints a baseline table in which cholinesterase-inhibitor (ChEI) exposure rises across exactly the strata in which the marker rises - 'Receiving cholinesterase inhibitors: 0 (0 per cent), 7 (19.4 per cent), 3 (17.6 per cent), 18 (46.2 per cent)' against 'Theta/alpha ratio: 0.336 (0.173), 0.416 (0.164), 0.464 (0.189), 0.506 (0.210)' for controls, MCI-AD, possible MCI-LB and probable MCI-LB - and the primary association (HR 1.84, 95 per cent CI 1.01-3.35) loses nominal significance when ChEI use is entered as a covariate (1.80, 0.97-3.32). P-778 also tests the marker itself by ChEI status within diagnostic groups and finds no significant difference (MCI-AD W = 61, p = .163; MCI-LB W = 277, p = .223), an underpowered null on the pharmacological channel that leaves the marker-outcome decomposition untouched. The stratum carrying 46.2 per cent ChEI exposure is also the stratum that supplied 9 of the 14 events. P-890, the corpus's PD-MCI coherence study, recorded every participant in the medicated ON state, states that 'medications could influence coherence', and names off-medication recording among the changes that would strengthen its associations. THE BIAS IS NOT MERELY UNQUANTIFIED, IT IS UNSIGNABLE FROM THE CORPUS RECORD, because prescription operates on the marker through two channels at once and in unknown relative size: pharmacologically on the oscillatory measure itself (P-890's own concession), and as a record of the treating clinician's suspicion of the very neurodegenerative outcome being predicted (confounding by indication - in P-778 nobody in the control arm and nearly half the highest-risk stratum was treated). The consequence for deployment is concrete: a qEEG screening or prognostic instrument derived in a cohort with one prescribing pattern has no transportable operating characteristics for a clinic with another, and a change in national prescribing guidance would silently move the instrument's threshold. WHAT IS ABSENT IS NOT THE RECORDING OF MEDICATION - P-778 tabulates ChEI status per stratum and P-890 tested levodopa-equivalent daily dose - BUT ANY ESTIMATE OF HOW MUCH OF THE MARKER'S SIGNAL THE TREATMENT CARRIES: no stratified marker-outcome estimate in treated versus untreated participants, no treatment-by-marker interaction, no within-subject on/off or pre/post-initiation shift expressed in the marker's own units so that it can be compared with the marker's diagnostic threshold.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern of NEW-G-21 (handedness-driven asymmetry not modelled or controlled in AI neuroimaging predictors) - a confounding factor that biases the learned quantity and is never entered into the error budget - but is stronger than the handedness case in two respects that the corpus record itself supplies. First, the confounder here is not merely plausible, it is DEMONSTRATED material inside the corpus: P-778 ran the adjustment and the marker's significance did not survive it. Second, the confounder is not exogenous but outcome-linked: cholinesterase inhibitors are prescribed by the clinician who suspects the neurodegenerative process the model is predicting, so the marker can partly be reading the clinician's prior rather than the brain. The non-obvious part is that this cannot be cured by adding treatment as a covariate: with a pharmacological channel acting on the marker and an indication channel acting on the outcome, the adjusted estimate is biased in an unknown direction too, which is why what is needed is a decomposition (on/off shift in marker units plus stratified estimates), not another covariate.
gaps.closure_criteria: In an MCI cohort with a resting-EEG marker and recorded symptomatic CNS medication status: (a) report the marker-outcome association (group difference, discrimination or hazard) stratified by treated versus untreated participants with a treatment-by-marker interaction term; and (b) report a within-subject on/off or pre/post-initiation shift of the marker in its own units, so that the medication-attributable component can be compared against the marker's diagnostic threshold. A covariate adjustment alone, or a within-stratum marker comparison by medication status (as in P-778), does not close it.
