gaps.critic_falsification: The single strongest objection is that P-778's ChEI-adjusted point estimate barely moves (1.84 to 1.80) while only the interval crosses one, so the loss of nominal significance may be the cost of spending a degree of freedom on 14 events rather than evidence of confounding - and the digest itself flags that the paper treats its two sensitivity analyses as equivalent when the visual-hallucination model (1.17) and the ChEI model (1.80) plainly are not. On that reading the corpus evidence for a MATERIAL medication effect reduces to a baseline-table correlation plus one author's concession, which is thinner than the claim's confident framing. A second objection is EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: pharmaco-EEG characterisation of cholinesterase-inhibitor effects on alpha and theta power is a long-standing external literature, so a reviewer may hold that the drug-on-marker channel is already sized and that only its importation into an MCI biomarker's error budget is missing - which is a narrower gap than the one stated here.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no combine-X-with-Y clause. One modality, one cohort; the closure design adds an analysis and a repeat recording, not a second data type.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: the two nearest corpus attempts are recorded here as partial closers rather than ignored - P-890's LEDD correlation (bivariate, among treated patients only, null) and P-818's assertion of freedom from medication effects (no estimate printed). Neither yields a medication-attributable component.

DATA_SCARCITY: the data already exist. P-778 holds per-participant ChEI status and ran the covariate model; the missing stratified estimate, interaction term and attributable proportion require no new cohort. The on/off limb requires one repeat recording, not a scarce population.
RESTATEMENT: see why_new - full grep of the 535 statements returns no medication-as-confounder record; the closest in form (MINE-G-001) concerns affective state on disjoint evidence.

TOO_SPECIFIC: this is not a property of one marker. It applies to the spectral-ratio family (P-778 theta/alpha), the coherence family (P-890 alpha coherence) and to any qEEG marker deployed in a memory-clinic or movement-disorder population where symptomatic prescribing is routine.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: the record is about the internal validity of a biomarker estimate, not about drug efficacy or trial design.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper's own block uses the gap's vocabulary - 'cholinesterase inhibitors', 'medication ON state', 'medications could influence coherence', 'off-medication recordings', 'LEDD', 'medication effects'. No inferential bridge is needed to get from any cited quote to the construct.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: the quantities quoted (46.2 per cent, 0.506, HR 1.80 CI 0.97-3.32, 9 of 14 events) are printed baseline-table and results values, not assertions lifted from significance/novelty/importance fields.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the absence clause was narrowed against the record's own citations before writing. It is NOT 'no study reports medication' (P-778 tabulates ChEI status, P-890 reports LEDD) and NOT 'no study adjusts for medication' (P-778 adjusts). It is 'no study estimates the medication-attributable component of the marker', which neither cited paper does.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked by grep of all 535 statements in existing_gaps.md for medicat|cholinesterase|donepezil|pharmac|levodopa|LEDD|prescri|treatment status|confounding by indication. The only hits are (a) per-paper rejected limitation blurbs that list 'medication uncontrolled' or 'medication confound' as one item among six for a single paper (G-CAND-130/P-485, G-CAND-301/P-552, G-CAND-307/P-558, G-CAND-314/P-565) - none is a gap statement and none proposes an estimate; (b) claims-data modality templates (G-CAND-346, G-CAND-351, G-CAND-355) about prescription records as an INPUT data source, not as a confounder of a signal; (c) ACTOR-G-052, a diabetes-drug RCT design gap. Also checked against the EEG-specific open records: G-22 (multi-site EEG amyloid replication), ACTOR-G-013 (cross-site transfer of network/connectivity biomarkers), ACTOR-G-026 (segment-wise vs subject-wise CV leakage), ACTOR-G-034 (test-retest/ICC of the input feature), ACTOR-G-042 (Lempel-Ziv sign reversal), ACTOR-G-020 (healthy-ageing reference arms), MINE-band-E-G1 (rejected aetiological-composition claim - deliberately not restated: this record makes no claim about aetiology reporting). The closest record in FORM is MINE-G-001, which holds that affective acquisition context is a measured modulator of EEG/ERP feature families that no corpus study prices into a classifier. This record is the same shape applied to a disjoint construct (pharmacological state, not affective state), on disjoint evidence (P-778/P-890/P-818 versus P-133/P-485/P-533/P-662), with a distinct mechanism that G-001 does not have: confounding by indication, where the modulator is assigned by a clinician who is reacting to the outcome.

gaps.gap_statement: THE MCI MARKERS IN THIS PACK ARE ESTIMATED UNDER RESEARCH-GRADE ACQUISITION AND ARGUED FOR ON COST AND ACCESS GROUNDS, BUT NO STUDY RE-DERIVES A MARKER IN ITS OWN COHORT UNDER THE ACQUISITION CONDITIONS OF THE SETTING IT IS PROPOSED FOR AND REPORTS THE PENALTY. The pack's acquisition chains span an order of magnitude in fidelity with nothing bridging them: 128 electrodes on Waveguard research caps for the theta/alpha prognostic ratio (P-778); a 60-channel research rig for the spectral power ratio, itself harmonised across two montages by restriction - 'Only the 52 electrodes shared between the two EEG montages used were retained' (P-719); 16 channels for the frontoparietal alpha-coherence marker (P-890); and a supervised laboratory touchscreen session with an experimenter present for the hand-motor kinematic classifier (P-795). Every one of these is offered as the cheap, scalable alternative to the specialist instruments - P-795's case is stated as a cost argument against 'PET, MRI, clinician-administered batteries, genetic testing', and P-719's improvement section keeps its classifier alive 'because the underlying signal is plausible and the measure is cheap'. P-719's own open problems name the missing study exactly: a 'fully automated reimplementation of the SPR with a quantified performance penalty'. WHY THIS MATTERS IS NOT THAT A CHEAPER DEVICE HAS NOT BEEN TRIED - IT IS THAT THE ECONOMIC ARGUMENT IS THE ENTIRE CLINICAL CASE FOR THESE MARKERS, AND IT IS BEING MADE WITH NUMBERS OBTAINED UNDER CONDITIONS THE DEPLOYED TEST WOULD NOT MEET. The penalty is also marker-specific rather than a single constant: a whole-head band ratio and a regional frontal-to-parietal coherence do not degrade at the same rate as electrodes are removed, so an appeal to the general low-density EEG literature cannot substitute for a paired estimate in the marker's own cohort. The most concrete casualty is threshold portability: P-719 builds the SPR from 'absolute power spectral density from 1 to 40 Hz was estimated and summed within delta, theta, alpha' and publishes an interpretable cutoff at 1.0390, an absolute number that is a property of that montage, reference and cleaning chain, with no estimate of how far it moves under any other. THE ABSENCE CLAUSE IS NARROW AND WAS CHECKED AGAINST THE RECORD'S OWN CITATIONS: it is not that low-channel EEG studies do not exist (P-890 is one, at 16 channels; the corpus also holds P-487 at four channels), but that no study re-derives any of THE FOUR MARKERS NAMED HERE (spectral power ratio, theta/alpha ratio, frontoparietal coherence, touchscreen kinematics) in THE SAME participants under a reduced or automated or unsupervised chain and reports the change in effect size, in discrimination and in the marker's absolute threshold. The paired full-versus-reduced-channel design itself does exist in the corpus for other EEG markers - P-464 (EEG-EGG fusion at all electrodes versus a channel subset in one cohort of 190) and P-117 (NSGA-selected channel subsets; a performance-suspect record) - neither reporting an absolute-threshold shift.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard OCT vendor gap (NEW-G-24): a hardware/domain-shift vulnerability stated as a quantity to be measured in one cohort across two acquisition conditions, not as a missing modality combination. What makes it non-obvious here is the direction of the argument. The obvious version - 'someone should try a cheap EEG' - is uninteresting and half-done in the wider field. The version that bites is that the corpus's markers are justified BY their cheapness (P-719 and P-795 both say so in their own records) while being measured at fidelities no cheap deployment would reach, so the justification and the evidence are about different objects; and that the marker whose economic case is strongest, P-719's SPR, is precisely the one whose decision rule is an absolute number on a summed-absolute-power scale, the least portable form a threshold can take. The closure design also needs no new participants, which separates it from the field's usual answer of 'validate prospectively'.
gaps.closure_criteria: In one cohort already holding the research-grade recording, re-derive the same marker (SPR, theta/alpha ratio, frontoparietal alpha coherence, or the touchscreen kinematic classifier) from a reduced channel set, an automated pipeline, or an unsupervised session, and report the paired change in group effect size, in discrimination and in the marker's absolute decision threshold. A general low-density-EEG result on a different marker (P-464, P-117) is the design precedent but does not close it.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold-standard OCT vendor gap (NEW-G-24): a hardware/domain-shift vulnerability stated as a quantity to be measured in one cohort across two acquisition conditions, not as a missing modality combination. The version that bites is that the corpus's markers are justified BY their cheapness (P-719 and P-795 both say so in their own records) while being measured at fidelities no cheap deployment would reach, so the justification and the evidence are about different objects; and that the marker whose economic case is strongest, P-719's SPR, is precisely the one whose decision rule is an absolute number on a summed-absolute-power scale, the least portable form a threshold can take. The closure design also needs no new participants, which separates it from the field's usual answer of 'validate prospectively'.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: channel-reduction and wearable-montage ablations are routine in the wider EEG machine-learning literature, so the absence may be an artefact of a corpus whose frontier holds only six EEG papers, and the corpus-scoped framing is carrying a lot of the record's weight. A reviewer who applies the ACTOR-G-004/005/008 standard could reject on that basis alone. The second objection is internal: the threshold-portability limb - that P-719's cutoff of 1.0390 will not transport across montage and reference - is my inference from how summed absolute band power behaves, not a corpus finding. P-719 is quoted only for the cutoff and for the fact that the ratio is built from summed absolute power; no paper in the corpus states that the cutoff fails to transport, so if that limb is struck the record reduces to the weaker claim that the deployment penalty is simply unmeasured.

TOO_SPECIFIC: the pattern is demonstrated across three different measurement families in the pack - a spectral band ratio (P-719), a regional coherence measure (P-890, as the unconnected low-fidelity end) and touchscreen kinematics (P-795) - so it is not a property of one marker or one rig.

gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: THE MCI MARKERS IN THIS PACK ARE ESTIMATED UNDER RESEARCH-GRADE ACQUISITION AND ARGUED FOR ON COST AND ACCESS GROUNDS, BUT NO STUDY RE-DERIVES A MARKER IN ITS OWN COHORT UNDER THE ACQUISITION CONDITIONS OF THE SETTING IT IS PROPOSED FOR AND REPORTS THE PENALTY. The pack's acquisition chains span an order of magnitude in fidelity with nothing bridging them: 128 electrodes on Waveguard research caps for the theta/alpha prognostic ratio (P-778); a 60-channel research rig for the spectral power ratio, itself harmonised across two montages by restriction - 'Only the 52 electrodes shared between the two EEG montages used were retained' (P-719); 16 channels for the frontoparietal alpha-coherence marker (P-890); and a supervised laboratory touchscreen session with an experimenter present for the hand-motor kinematic classifier (P-795). Every one of these is offered as the cheap, scalable alternative to the specialist instruments - P-795's case is stated as a cost argument against 'PET, MRI, clinician-administered batteries, genetic testing', and P-719's improvement section keeps its classifier alive 'because the underlying signal is plausible and the measure is cheap'. P-719's own open problems name the missing study exactly: a 'fully automated reimplementation of the SPR with a quantified performance penalty'. WHY THIS MATTERS IS NOT THAT A CHEAPER DEVICE HAS NOT BEEN TRIED - IT IS THAT THE ECONOMIC ARGUMENT IS THE ENTIRE CLINICAL CASE FOR THESE MARKERS, AND IT IS BEING MADE WITH NUMBERS OBTAINED UNDER CONDITIONS THE DEPLOYED TEST WOULD NOT MEET. The penalty is also marker-specific rather than a single constant: a whole-head band ratio and a regional frontal-to-parietal coherence do not degrade at the same rate as electrodes are removed, so an appeal to the general low-density EEG literature cannot substitute for a paired estimate in the marker's own cohort. The most concrete casualty is threshold portability: P-719 builds the SPR from 'absolute power spectral density from 1 to 40 Hz was estimated and summed within delta, theta, alpha' and publishes an interpretable cutoff at 1.0390, an absolute number that is a property of that montage, reference and cleaning chain, with no estimate of how far it moves under any other. THE ABSENCE CLAUSE IS NARROW AND WAS CHECKED AGAINST THE RECORD'S OWN CITATIONS: it is not that low-channel EEG studies do not exist (P-890 is one, at 16 channels; the corpus also holds P-487 at four channels), but that no study re-derives THE SAME marker in THE SAME participants under a reduced or automated or unsupervised chain and reports the change in effect size, in discrimination and in the marker's absolute threshold.

gaps.gap_statement: Ocular and oculomotor MCI markers are scored against a cognitive reference standard (MMSE / MoCA) that is itself administered through the visual channel the marker measures, and no corpus study quantifies how much of the reported marker-to-MCI association is carried by that shared visual demand rather than by cognition. The field explicitly audits its reference standard for education and language contamination - that is the stated rationale for building these markers at all - but only once for visual contamination (P-363, covariate adjustment without an attenuation estimate), even though the markers ARE retinal thinning, visual-evoked potentials, peripheral-field reaction time and gaze behaviour. The corpus contains three mitigation strategies, none of which yields an estimate of the bias: P-363 (choroidal OCT markers, AD/MCI/controls) enters visual acuity as a covariate in generalised estimating equations but reports adjusted estimates only, with no unadjusted-versus-adjusted attenuation; the other two are themselves bias-generating: P-933 excludes participants with eye disease, which removes the very population in which retinal markers are most abnormal, while P-688 swaps the instrument for visually impaired participants (MoCA-B for MoCA), which its own record flags as making the label non-equivalent across levels of one of the tested predictors - and in P-688 that predictor is diabetic retinopathy, reported as an MCI discriminator at AUC 0.678 in the same analysis. Neither strategy yields an estimate of the bias, so every retina-to-cognition effect size in this theme contains an unquantified measurement component with the same sign as the hypothesis.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches two gold patterns at once: the ground-truth-assumption critique (gold: 'Prognostic models treat central nervous system markers as absolute ground truth...') and the calibration/transfer failure 'across language, education, device or setting' - here the untested setting is the patient's vision. It is non-obvious because it inverts the field's own selling point: markers marketed as escaping the education and language bias of the screen are validated by that same screen along the one axis (vision) where marker and screen are structurally coupled. The evidence is not the miner's inference - P-688's record states the non-equivalence in its own words, and P-933 shows the opposite mitigation with the same missing estimate.
gaps.closure_criteria: One ocular MCI cohort (N >= 200, MCI prevalence documented, recruited without ocular exclusion) in which best-corrected visual acuity and contrast sensitivity are measured on every participant, and the ocular-marker-to-MCI association is estimated TWICE against the same participants: once with the visually administered screen label (MMSE or MoCA) and once with a vision-independent reference standard (informant-based CDR, a verbally administered battery, or biomarker / adjudicated-conversion status). The study must report (a) the change in marker AUC or effect size between the two labels, (b) a formal mediation estimate of the proportion of the association carried by acuity and contrast sensitivity, and (c) marker AUC stratified by acuity tertile. A study that instead re-runs an existing cohort's analysis with acuity entered as a covariate and reports the attenuation would partially close it.

Eight of the ten pack digests say nothing about how vision was handled, so some of these studies may well screen acuity in a methods paragraph the extract never reached - and the mainstream ophthalmic-AD literature does routinely apply acuity thresholds, which a reviewer may judge to be adequate control by design. The claim therefore has to be read as the absence of a QUANTIFIED bias estimate in the corpus record, not as proof that no ocular MCI study ever measured acuity; if a reviewer finds an external study reporting acuity-stratified marker accuracy against a vision-independent label, the record collapses to EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE.

gaps.gap_statement: In the corpus's ocular and oculomotor MCI literature the brief cognitive screen occupies two incompatible roles at once: it defines the case label AND it is the incumbent the new marker claims to replace or beat. Consequently no study has estimated the marker's accuracy, or its increment over the screen, on ground the screen did not create. The two halves of the required design exist in the corpus but never together: P-1006 runs the comparator arm and the marker LOSES (demographics plus eye movements AUROC 0.752 against demographics plus MMSE 0.767), with the headline 0.840 obtained only by placing MMSE inside the model, so the reported increment is by construction a function of the incumbent; P-988, the only prospective study, has a screen-independent 40-month adjudicated conversion label but runs no screen comparator and reports no AUC at all. Around them, P-1163 asserts favourable benchmarking against conventional screeners while grouping participants by MoCA-J/MMSE-J cutoffs and reporting no screener accuracy of its own, P-966 makes a screening-tool claim with no discrimination figure of any kind, P-952 makes one from cross-validated cross-sectional classification, and P-830, pooling 126 retinal studies, cannot deliver a pooled diagnostic accuracy. The whole economic argument for these markers is that they are cheaper than or better than a five-minute screen, and that comparison has never been made against a label the screen did not produce.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'No longitudinal follow-up data exists for MCI patients after computational diagnosis; the clinical utility of AI flagging ... has never been demonstrated' - the same discrimination-versus-value structure, one link earlier in the chain, and like that gold case the apparent closers dissolve on inspection. It is non-obvious because the theme reads as having strong accuracy evidence (AUC 0.87 in P-952, 0.841 in P-1163, 0.840 in P-1006) while the single occasion on which the incumbent screen was placed in the same sample, the marker came second - and that result is invisible unless the three AUCs are read as a comparison rather than as a headline.
gaps.closure_criteria: A diagnostic-accuracy study (N >= 300, consecutively or population-sampled rather than case-control-selected) in which MCI status is fixed by a reference standard the brief screen did not produce - amyloid/tau or CSF adjudication, or >= 24 months of clinically adjudicated conversion - and in which the ocular or oculomotor marker AND the incumbent screen (MMSE or MoCA) are BOTH scored blind to that standard. Required outputs: each test's AUC with 95 percent CI; the DeLong (or bootstrap) test of the difference between them; and the net benefit or net reclassification of adding the marker to the screen at a stated decision threshold. A study reporting only the marker's AUC, or only the marker-plus-screen model, does not close it.

gaps.gap_statement: In the corpus's ocular and oculomotor MCI evidence the positive results carry effect sizes and confidence intervals while the negative results carry none, so 'no difference' cannot be distinguished from 'not enough participants'. This asymmetry is consequential rather than cosmetic, because the negatives are precisely the results that would bound the field's screening claims. P-686's nine-parameter amnestic-MCI null is the corpus's only hard constraint on free-viewing eye-movement MCI screening, and its Statistical Analysis section confines Cohen's d to the effect sizes of statistically significant outcomes, so every aMCI-versus-control cell is left without an effect size, an interval or a post hoc power figure - while the same paper applies a Bonferroni correction multiplying significant p values by 54. P-1163 reports no central-field group difference and non-significant gaze-error measures with no equivalence margin, alongside a fully specified positive arm; P-966 reports a correction-latency trend and no discrimination figure of any kind; and P-1006's shortfall against MMSE (0.752 against 0.767) is reported as two separate AUROCs with no test of their difference. No corpus study in this theme reports an equivalence test, a smallest effect size of interest, an effect size for a null contrast, or a paired test of an AUC difference, and the one a priori power calculation in the theme (P-1163) sizes the primary contrast only. The result is that the theme's disconfirming evidence is uninterpretable while its confirming evidence is fully quantified.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern of a methodological validation weakness spanning several papers ('EEG-based screening for amyloid-positive MCI has only been demonstrated in single-site settings ... without any multi-site replication'), and it identifies a directional bias with a named mechanism rather than a generic complaint: because confirming results are quantified and disconfirming ones are not, any downstream synthesis of this theme - including this corpus's own verified-finding and conflict ledgers - reads quantified positives against dashes. It is non-obvious because each paper looks statistically careful in isolation: P-686 corrects for 54 comparisons, P-1163 runs an a priori power calculation, and the omission only becomes visible when the theme's four negative results are read side by side.
gaps.closure_criteria: A re-analysis of an existing free-viewing or saccadic eye-movement MCI dataset (>= 30 per group, as in P-686) or a new study, that pre-specifies a smallest effect size of interest for MCI-versus-control discrimination and reports, for EVERY marker-by-group contrast including the non-significant ones, the effect size with its 90 percent confidence interval and a two-one-sided-tests equivalence verdict (equivalent / different / inconclusive). Where an index test is compared with a cognitive screen, the AUC difference must be reported with a DeLong or bootstrap confidence interval rather than two independent AUCs. P-686's own record notes the effect sizes are already computed for the significant contrasts, so the closing analysis is a re-run of existing data, not a new cohort.

gaps.gap_statement: The MCI peripheral-biomarker literature in this corpus has a promotion mechanism but no retirement mechanism. Negative marker results are published - in P-734's case in the title itself - without any of the apparatus that converts a failure to reject into evidence of absence: no pre-specified smallest effect of interest, no equivalence or non-inferiority margin, no minimum detectable effect at stated power, and no interpretation of the printed interval against any threshold of clinical irrelevance. Where an interval is printed at all (P-861 OR 1.05, 0.89-1.24; P-837 SMD 0.46, -0.37 to 1.29) it is read only as 'not significant'; where it is not printed at all (P-734, ADAM10 MCI-vs-frail-MCI) the null still carries the paper's title. The consequence is structural, not cosmetic: every null in this strand is filed by its own authors as 'sample size not sufficient' (P-740), 'may be attributable to insufficient statistical power' (P-861) or 'the number of studies and sample size is relatively small' (P-837), so the candidate analyte is never retired, the same markers keep re-entering the literature as 'promising', and syntheses such as P-837 pool nulls that were never designed to be informative and produce a further uninformative null. CLOSURE TEST: a re-analysis of an existing MCI cohort with banked plasma (N >= 200 with >= 60 incident converters or >= 60 MCI cases) that pre-specifies a smallest effect of interest for the candidate analyte - stated either as an SMD (e.g. 0.20) or as a delta-AUC over a fixed clinical base model (e.g. 0.05) - and reports a two-one-sided-tests equivalence result, or the minimum detectable effect at 80 per cent power, alongside the point estimate and interval, so that the negative conclusion is issued as an equivalence conclusion rather than as a failure to reject. SCOPE: absence asserted for how these corpus papers report their own nulls, which is checkable in their own text; no claim is made that equivalence methodology is unknown to the wider field.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches two gold patterns at once: the objective-function framing bias ('progression modelled, reversion not' - here, promotion instrumented, retirement not) and the clinical-utility pattern ('discrimination proven, decision impact never tested' - here, the number that would let a marker be dropped is never computed). It is non-obvious because paper-by-paper the behaviour looks like honest reporting: three of the four claiming papers concede their power problem candidly and one puts the null in its title, which reads as integrity. The defect only becomes visible when the set is read together with P-837, where those same nulls are pooled and the synthesis is still unable to retire the analyte - the pattern reproduces itself one level up. It is also actionable with data already collected, which P-734's own digest states.
gaps.closure_criteria: A re-analysis of an existing MCI cohort with banked plasma (N >= 200, with >= 60 incident converters or >= 60 MCI cases) that (a) pre-specifies a smallest effect of interest for the candidate peripheral analyte, expressed either as an SMD (e.g. 0.20) or as a delta-AUC over a fixed clinical base model of age, sex, education and MMSE/MoCA (e.g. 0.05); (b) reports a two-one-sided-tests equivalence result against that margin, or the minimum detectable effect at 80 per cent power, alongside the point estimate and its interval; and (c) states the negative conclusion as an equivalence conclusion. A paper that merely reports another non-significant p value with a 'larger samples needed' sentence does NOT close this gap.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches two gold patterns at once: the objective-function framing bias ('progression modelled, reversion not' - here, promotion instrumented, retirement not) and the clinical-utility pattern ('discrimination proven, decision impact never tested' - here, the number that would let a marker be dropped is never computed). It is non-obvious because paper-by-paper the behaviour looks like honest reporting: three of the four claiming papers concede their power problem candidly and one puts the null in its title, which reads as integrity. The defect only becomes visible when the set is read together with P-837, where those same nulls are pooled and the synthesis is still unable to retire the analyte - the pattern reproduces itself one level up. It is also actionable with data already collected, which P-734's own digest states.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is that equivalence testing is a general statistical convention rather than a domain research question, so a reviewer could rule this NOT_IN_SCOPE as a reporting-standards complaint that belongs in a methods editorial, not in a gaps ledger - and could add that early-phase biomarker discovery is not expected to power for equivalence, since discovery studies are meant to screen candidates cheaply and let meta-analysis settle them later. The counter is that P-837 is exactly that meta-analysis and it settles nothing, but a reviewer who does not accept that step would downgrade this record to a soft-flagged single-paper limitation aggregated four times.
fp_codes_cleared: FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: no pack paper reports an equivalence margin, TOST result or minimum detectable effect. P-861 is the nearest and is listed as a partial closer rather than ignored; its own text stops at a power disclaimer. P-734's digest states outright that no equivalence or non-inferiority test was run.

TOO_SPECIFIC: the record spans four analyte classes (ADAM10, p-tau181, EPA/DHA, LCN2), four designs (cross-sectional, prospective cohort, RCT, meta-analysis) and four countries, so it is not one narrow instance that would trivially generalise.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: biomarker study design and reporting for MCI is core corpus scope; this is not trial regulation or drug development.

The claim is about a reporting standard not being applied here, not about a method not existing.

DATA_SCARCITY: the opposite - every element of the closure test is computable from data already collected. P-734's digest names the fix and says it needs no new data; P-728's digest makes the same point about its own index.
COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no combination of modalities or methods is proposed anywhere in the record.

P-861 and P-837 DO print confidence intervals, so the claim is NOT 'no interval is reported' but 'no interval is interpreted against a pre-specified margin', and the record prints both intervals on its face. P-861 DOES run formal interaction tests, splines and negative controls, which is why it is filed as a partial closer and not as a claiming paper. P-788 does report an interval on its null AUC (0.39-0.74) and the record quotes it.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: every quote is tagged with the digest field it came from. The one quote that sits in an interpretive field (P-837, 'What is the significance?') is explicitly marked as the digest analyst's appraisal and carries no numeric weight in the record; all load-bearing quotes come from problems / limitations / open-problems fields or from the authors' own limitation sentences.

gaps.gap_statement: The stratified claims that carry MCI biomarker papers - 'the marker works differently in MCI than in cognitively healthy people', 'only in amyloid-PET-negative patients', 'only in APOE e4 carriers', 'only in women' - are, in this corpus, read off which stratum crosses a significance threshold rather than estimated from the product term the claim requires. P-730's central conclusion (CSF Abeta42 informs diagnostic stage only in amyloid-negative ADNI patients) and P-720's central conclusion (the depression-to-AT(N) association is amplified in MCI) are both stratum-versus-reference arguments with no interaction coefficient anywhere; P-807's stated objective IS an interaction and no estimate for it is printed. The one pack paper that does run the tests, P-861, finds all four non-significant (0.3555, 0.7321, 0.1458, 0.3708) and still leads its abstract and conclusion with the subgroups. This matters beyond individual papers because these stratum-specific statements are the ones that propagate: they are what a stratified-medicine reading of the biomarker literature is built from, they are what determines which subgroup a marker is later marketed for, and inside this corpus's own machinery two papers reporting opposite stratum-specific results are indistinguishable from a genuine disagreement. Nothing in the corpus establishes that any of these stratum-specific peripheral-biomarker effects survives a formal interaction test, let alone replicates. CLOSURE TEST: a pre-registered analysis in an independent MCI cohort (N >= 500, index stratum >= 100) that estimates one of these specific stratified biomarker claims with an explicit exposure-by-stratum product term, reports the interaction coefficient with its confidence interval and p value, and states whether the stratum-specific claim survives - reported whether or not the interaction is significant. SCOPE: absence asserted for this corpus.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard pattern of a temporal-or-ground-truth assumption critique and of the MISASSIGNED_MEASUREMENT_FAMILY lesson recorded in this repo's own audit history: before asserting that an effect differs between two arms, verify that the difference was measured rather than inferred from two separate significance verdicts. It is non-obvious because the defect is invisible in the abstract - each paper's stratified sentence reads as a finding - and because two of the four papers (P-730, P-720) are otherwise carefully executed on large cohorts. Its value to this corpus is concrete rather than editorial: stratum-specific statements are exactly the material that downstream conflict detection compares across papers, so an untested interaction in one paper and an untested interaction of the opposite sign in another will present as a genuine disagreement when neither claim has statistical warrant.
gaps.closure_criteria: A pre-registered analysis in an MCI cohort independent of the originating study (N >= 500, with the index stratum >= 100) that takes one named stratified biomarker claim from this literature - depression-to-p-tau181/NfL amplified in MCI (P-720); CSF Abeta42 related to diagnostic stage only in the amyloid-PET-negative stratum (P-730); circulating C8:0 protective only in APOE e4 heterozygotes or only in women (P-861) - fits the exposure-by-stratum product term explicitly, and reports the interaction coefficient with its confidence interval and p value together with the stratum-specific estimates, publishing the result whether or not the interaction reaches significance. A further paper that reports only stratum-specific estimates does NOT close this gap.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold-standard pattern of a temporal-or-ground-truth assumption critique and of the MISASSIGNED_MEASUREMENT_FAMILY lesson recorded in this repo's own audit history: before asserting that an effect differs between two arms, verify that the difference was measured rather than inferred from two separate significance verdicts. It is non-obvious because the defect is invisible in the abstract - each paper's stratified sentence reads as a finding - and because two of the four papers (P-730, P-720) are otherwise carefully executed on large cohorts. Its value to this corpus is concrete rather than editorial: stratum-specific statements are exactly the material that downstream conflict detection compares across papers, so an untested interaction in one paper and an untested interaction of the opposite sign in another will present as a genuine disagreement when neither claim has statistical warrant.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is that a formal interaction test is chronically underpowered in exactly these designs - P-861's four null interaction tests may be the rule rather than the exception - so requiring one could suppress genuine effect modification rather than discipline spurious claims, and a reviewer could argue the real problem is not the missing test but the framing of the abstract, which is a writing complaint rather than a research gap. A second objection: P-807's exposures are questionnaire composites rather than blood analytes, so it is a same-shape corroborating instance rather than a fourth biomarker leg, and stripping it would leave three claiming papers.
fp_codes_cleared: FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: the two papers that could close it are named on the face of the record. P-861 runs the tests but on its own exposure only and does not change its reporting; P-888's exposure is a clinical event, not a peripheral analyte. Neither replicates another paper's stratified claim.

TOO_SPECIFIC: four papers, four exposure classes (CSF amyloid, plasma AT(N), composite SES/lifestyle, pooled LCN2) and four stratifiers (amyloid status, MCI status, biofluid/age, lifestyle) - broad enough that closing one instance would not trivially close the rest, which is why the closure test names three specific claims.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: MCI biomarker analysis design, core corpus scope.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: the record does not claim that interaction testing is unknown to the field - it cites two corpus papers that do it. It claims that the specific stratified MCI-biomarker findings in this corpus have not been estimated with a product term or replicated, which is a statement about these findings, not about the availability of the method.

DATA_SCARCITY: no - P-730's digest specifies the exact single model (multinomial on all 558 participants with an amyloid-status-by-Abeta42 product term) that would settle its own claim on data already collected.
COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no combination of modalities or methods is proposed.

P-861 DOES report four interaction tests and P-888 DOES report interaction analyses, so the record never says 'no corpus study tests interactions'; both are cited as partial closers with their tests quoted, and the absence clause is narrowed to (a) the four claiming papers' own stratified claims and (b) the absence of any replication of a stratum-specific peripheral-biomarker effect with a pre-specified product term.

gaps.gap_statement: Composite peripheral-burden indices - allostatic load, cumulative infection burden, and their relatives - are the main route by which multi-marker blood biology enters MCI epidemiology, and in this corpus the composition rule that defines the index is treated as a fact about the participant rather than as an analytic choice that has to be defended. Neither of the two pack papers that build one reports a sensitivity family over the construction rule, and both show what that costs. P-741 prints the two indices side by side on the same 475 people: the pre-specifiable count over all eleven pathogens is null after adjustment (OR 1.65, 0.79 to 3.48), while the index built by deleting the two organisms that had shown significant negative associations in that same dataset gives OR 3.32 (1.26 to 8.77) - and the abstract, discussion and conclusion all rest on the second. P-728's allostatic-load index is not even the same measurement across participants: it is high-risk values divided by AVAILABLE values, availability runs from 51 of 57 for blood pressure down to 26 for fibrinogen, and a person scored over eleven markers sits on the same 0-to-100 scale as a person scored over three, with no minimum-component sensitivity analysis. Why it matters: if index composition and index denominator are free parameters, then a 'cumulative burden' effect estimate is not comparable across studies, cannot be pooled, and cannot be falsified - and P-741 demonstrates that the free parameter is enough to move a burden estimate from null to a doubled odds ratio without touching a single measurement. CLOSURE TEST: an MCI cohort study (N >= 400) that pre-registers its index composition and denominator before outcome analysis and publishes the full leave-one-out family - the all-component index plus one estimate per component dropped in turn - together with a minimum-component-availability sensitivity analysis, so the reader can see the range of effect estimates the construction rule spans. SCOPE: absence asserted for this corpus.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard data-structure pattern ('ML architectures force continuous, interval-censored multi-visit data into artificial discrete binary labels') by naming a specific way the analysis pipeline mangles the exposure rather than the outcome. It is non-obvious because the two failures look unrelated on the surface - one is post-hoc index selection in a Singaporean serology cohort, the other is a missing-data denominator in a Brazilian memory clinic - and only converge once you ask what the burden index is a measurement OF. Its strongest feature is that the cost is not argued but measured: P-741 prints both estimates, so the record does not have to speculate about how much the construction rule matters. It is actionable with data already collected, which P-728's digest states explicitly.
gaps.closure_criteria: An MCI cohort study or re-analysis (N >= 400, with the outcome ascertained after the exposure) that (a) states its composite-index composition and denominator rule before outcome analysis, ideally in a registered protocol; (b) publishes the complete leave-one-out family - the all-component index plus one effect estimate per component dropped in turn, each with its confidence interval; and (c) reports a minimum-component-availability sensitivity analysis, restricting the primary model to participants scored on at least a stated number of components or imputing under a stated missingness model on a fixed denominator. A paper that reports one index and one estimate, however carefully adjusted, does NOT close this gap.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold-standard data-structure pattern ('ML architectures force continuous, interval-censored multi-visit data into artificial discrete binary labels') by naming a specific way the analysis pipeline mangles the exposure rather than the outcome. It is non-obvious because the two failures look unrelated on the surface - one is post-hoc index selection in a Singaporean serology cohort, the other is a missing-data denominator in a Brazilian memory clinic - and only converge once you ask what the burden index is a measurement OF. Its strongest feature is that the cost is not argued but measured: P-741 prints both estimates, so the record does not have to speculate about how much the construction rule matters. It is actionable with data already collected, which P-728's digest states explicitly.
gaps.critic_falsification: The record rests on two claiming papers, and they are not doing the same thing: P-741's defect is outcome-dependent variable selection (a general inferential sin that happens to appear in an index) while P-728's is missing-data handling (a general measurement sin that happens to appear in an index). A reviewer could reasonably say the composite index is incidental to both and that the record manufactures a class from two unrelated errors - the same move that got ACTOR-G-042 flagged for MISASSIGNED_MEASUREMENT_FAMILY. The defence is that the closure test (leave-one-out family plus minimum-component denominator) repairs both and is specific to composite exposures, but if a reviewer rejects the class, only P-741 survives and it becomes a single-paper limitation.
fp_codes_cleared: FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: neither claiming paper reports any sensitivity family over its construction rule, and both digests say so directly; P-807 is named as the nearest same-shape paper and it does not report component-level contributions either.

TOO_SPECIFIC: the record covers two structurally distinct construction failures (outcome-selected composition; participant-varying denominator) across two exposure families (eleven-pathogen serology; eleven-marker allostatic load) in two countries, and its closure test is written to cover the class rather than one index.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: exposure measurement in MCI observational epidemiology, core corpus scope.
RESTATEMENT: see why_new; checked against ACTOR-G-009, G-017, G-029, G-033 and the theme's 37-statement gap file, and against both sibling candidates from this pack.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: the record does not claim that specification-curve or leave-one-out reporting is unknown to epidemiology - it claims these corpus burden-index papers do not do it, which is checkable in their own text, and that the corpus therefore contains no MCI burden estimate whose construction sensitivity is visible.

DATA_SCARCITY: the opposite - both fixes are computable on data already collected; P-728's digest states that neither of its two proposed routes requires new data, and P-741 already holds both indices.

COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no combination of modalities or methods is proposed. The record is about how a single multi-component exposure is scored, not about pairing X with Y - this is the distinction on which ACTOR-G-009 was rejected and this record deliberately avoids it.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: checked. The record does not say 'no paper reports more than one index' - P-741 reports two, and the record's central evidence IS that pair. The absence clause is narrowed to the leave-one-out family and the minimum-component denominator analysis, neither of which appears in P-741, P-728 or P-807.
EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: both claiming papers' own text uses the construct - index composition, availability denominator, sensitivity analysis - so no bridge is built from an unrelated finding.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: every quote is tagged with its digest field; all load-bearing quotes come from problems / improvement / reporting-inventory fields, and both numeric quotes (1.65 and 3.32; 51 of 57 and 26) are printed table values reproduced in the digest, not author assertions from a significance or novelty field.

gaps.gap_statement: MCI risk-prediction models are chosen, and their operating points fixed, on discrimination alone (AUC / C-index, Youden-style cut-offs, decision curves plotted against a hypothetical threshold-probability range). That prices a correct high-risk flag and a correct low-risk flag as equal goods. The corpus's own empirical valuation of what a prediction does to the person who receives it prices them very unequally: a high predicted risk costs -0.18 utility while a low predicted risk gains +0.06, roughly a threefold asymmetry against flagging (P-1075), and the corpus's own health-economic model shows that asymmetry is large enough that risk prediction is DOMINATED by doing nothing even at 95 percent sensitivity and specificity (P-1171). No corpus MCI model reports the expected utility of deploying at its own operating point under those measured weights. The nearest attempts stop short in a specific way: P-1108 reports net benefit over a 4-57 percent threshold-probability range and P-1118 reports a decision-analysis curve, but neither anchors any threshold to a measured disclosure utility, and both score model-versus-treat-all/treat-none rather than predicting-versus-not-predicting, which is the comparison P-1171 shows the prediction strategy loses. The consequence is that a model can be reported as a success on AUC while, on the corpus's own numbers, deployment at its published cut-off is not demonstrably better than issuing no prediction at all - and at the delivery end the same blind spot repeats, because the only corpus study that put a real blood-biomarker risk-disclosure product in front of MCI patients (P-1156) measured self-rated understandability and usefulness and no comprehension or psychological outcome at all.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'objective-function framing bias' (the reversion gold gap) and 'clinical-utility failure - discrimination proven, decision impact never tested', but goes past the second of those: it does not merely say utility is untested, it identifies the specific missing number, shows that the corpus already contains both the measured weight and a demonstration that the weight flips the sign of the decision, and names the exact computation nobody performs. It is non-obvious because the field looks as if it has already handled this - decision curve analysis IS reported (P-1108, P-1118) - and the record has to survive that objection rather than ignore it: DCA sweeps a hypothetical harm-to-benefit exchange rate and benchmarks against treat-all/treat-none, whereas the measured weights fix the exchange rate and the relevant comparator is issuing no prediction. It also carries its own scope limit: the utility weights are Dutch, general-population and stated-preference, which is the honest reason this is an unperformed analysis rather than a proven harm.
gaps.closure_criteria: A study that takes at least one already-published MCI risk model with a stated operating point (for example P-1060's CN Model 3 at sensitivity 0.67 / specificity 0.81 / PPV 0.46, P-1108's CGMCI-Risk, or P-1118's nomogram at cutoff 0.595), applies empirically measured risk-disclosure utility weights (P-1075's -0.18 for a high predicted risk and +0.06 for a low one, or a replication of them in an MCI patient sample), and reports (a) expected net utility per person screened at the published cut-off, (b) the threshold probability implied by the measured weights - note that -0.18 against +0.06 implies a harm-to-benefit exchange rate near 0.75, which the closing study should compute and compare against the 4-57 percent range over which P-1108 currently claims net benefit - and (c) the cut-off, if any, at which predicting beats not predicting, with prediction-versus-no-prediction as the explicit comparator rather than treat-all/treat-none. Reported on a held-out or external cohort with N >= 200 and a stated outcome prevalence, with a sensitivity analysis over the utility weights.
gaps.modality: C5 Clinical/Population (risk-prediction models, blood-biomarker disclosure, health-economic evaluation)
gaps.task_type: T2 / T6 (MCI-to-dementia risk prediction and its evaluation)
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern 'objective-function framing bias' (the reversion gold gap) and 'clinical-utility failure - discrimination proven, decision impact never tested', but goes past the second of those: it does not merely say utility is untested, it identifies the specific missing number, shows that the corpus already contains both the measured weight and a demonstration that the weight flips the sign of the decision, and names the exact computation nobody performs. It is non-obvious because the field looks as if it has already handled this - decision curve analysis IS reported (P-1108, P-1118) - and the record has to survive that objection rather than ignore it: DCA sweeps a hypothetical harm-to-benefit exchange rate and benchmarks against treat-all/treat-none, whereas the measured weights fix the exchange rate and the relevant comparator is issuing no prediction. It also carries its own scope limit: the utility weights are Dutch, general-population and stated-preference, which is the honest reason this is an unperformed analysis rather than a proven harm.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE at the methodological level: utility-weighted threshold selection is not a new idea outside this corpus (Pauker-Kassirer threshold reasoning, and Vickers' decision-curve framework explicitly interprets the threshold probability as a harm-to-benefit exchange rate), so a reviewer can say the method exists and only its application is missing here. Two things limit that objection but do not remove it. First, the missing object is not the method but the anchoring: DCA's exchange rate is elicited from nobody, and the corpus now contains a measured one that no model uses. Second, the empirical anchor itself is thin and non-independent - P-1075 and P-1171 share four authors (Vermeulen, Olde Rikkert, Rovers, Govers), so the entire evidential basis for the asymmetry is one Dutch group's stated-preference study plus that same group's model consuming it, in a general-population sample imagining a prognosis rather than MCI patients receiving one. If those weights do not replicate in patients, the arithmetic this gap demands would change its answer, though not its necessity.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no combination of modalities or methods is proposed; the missing object is an evaluation quantity (expected utility at the operating point), computable on a single existing model.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: the two nearest closers are named in the record itself and their residual is stated - P-1171 does the utility arithmetic but for a hypothetical tool at assumed 95/80 percent accuracy rather than any real model at its published cut-off, and P-1108/P-1118 report decision curves whose threshold probability is never anchored to a measured disclosure utility. P-1031's EQ-5D-5L values are health-state utilities, not information utilities.

DATA_SCARCITY: nothing scarce is required. The models exist (P-1060, P-1108, P-1118), the utility weights exist (P-1075), and the arithmetic is a spreadsheet operation on already-published sensitivity, specificity and prevalence.

TOO_SPECIFIC: the absence spans the whole reporting convention of the batch - a held-out ADNI conversion model, a temporally validated community score, a memory-clinic serology nomogram and a disclosure-materials study - not one paper's limitation.
RESTATEMENT: differentiated above by id from G-07, G-09, G-17, G-350, NEW-G-23, NEW-G-27 and ACTOR-G-078; no existing gap references P-1075 or P-1171.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the 'no model reports expected utility at its operating point' clause was checked against every paper cited here. P-1171 is excluded from the clause by construction (it evaluates a hypothetical tool, not a model's operating point) and P-1108/P-1118 are admitted as partial, with the exact respect in which they fall short stated rather than suppressed.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: each paper is cited only for vocabulary present in its own block - P-1075 for utility/disclosure cost, P-1171 for disutility, P-1060 for PPV, P-1108 for DCA/net benefit, P-1118 for DAC and cutoff, P-1156 for psychological impact. No paper is cited for a construct its digest does not contain.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: the threefold asymmetry is quoted from P-1075's own results field, not from a significance or novelty field. The further arithmetic (that the measured weights imply a threshold probability near 0.75, outside P-1108's 4-57 percent net-benefit range) is deliberately NOT asserted as a finding; it is placed in the closure criteria as the computation the closing study should perform.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked against every gap in existing_gaps.md that touches value, cost, thresholds or clinical impact. G-07 asks whether cost-effectiveness (QALY/ICER) of biomarker TRIAGE has been quantified - a costing question about test strategies, and P-1171 partially answers it; this record is about the utility weight inside such a calculation and its absence from model reporting. G-09 / NEW-G-27 ask for a prospective trial in which acting on an AI or XAI flag changes patient or clinician outcomes - an experimental design that does not exist; this gap is a retrospective, computable analysis on models that already exist. G-350 asks for a harmonised East-Asian WTP threshold using state utilities (P-1030, P-1031); P-1031 measures the utility of BEING in an MCI health state (0.91 self-report), which is a different quantity from the utility change caused by receiving a prognosis, and confusing the two is precisely the substitution this record objects to. G-17 is the reversion objective-function gap - same family (objective-function framing bias) but a different objective. ACTOR-G-078 pairs care-outcome with conversion prognostication - an endpoint-choice gap, not a loss-function gap. NEW-G-23 asks for calibration (ECE, reliability diagrams); calibration is a necessary input to this computation but is not the computation. IA-17 (confirmed) is about generalisation of high in-study performance, and IA-06 (merged into IA-17) framed AUC-sufficiency as a belief; neither states or tests the asymmetric-utility claim, and neither is a gap record. No existing gap cites P-1075 or P-1171 at all.

gaps.gap_statement: Prognostic studies of dementia risk factors inside prevalent-MCI cohorts condition on an index event - being in the MCI stratum at enrolment - that the studied exposure itself helped cause. Conditioning on a common effect of the exposure and of every unmeasured cause of MCI induces an association between them inside the stratum, which drives exposure-progression estimates toward the null or reverses their sign. The corpus's within-MCI prognostic literature returns exactly that pattern - smoking null on 7 of 9 outcomes in 870 ADNI MCI (P-934), incidental Lewy pathology null on MMSE decline in 206 autopsy-confirmed MCI-due-to-AD (P-1076), the sex-by-APOE-e4 conversion difference near-zero (24 percent vs 25 percent) in unstratified ADNI MCI (P-984), gender not predicting progression in 210 clinic-selected SCD despite a large female cognitive-reserve deficit (P-1146) - and each null is read substantively: as mechanism (smoking acts through a vascular rather than amyloid pathway), as staging (Lewy-AD synergy begins only after dementia onset), or as a warrant for subtyping. No corpus study estimates, bounds or corrects the selection-induced component of any of these estimates, although the correction is directly computable in the same datasets: ADNI and NACC both enrol the cognitively normal arm from which the probability of entering the MCI stratum given exposure can be fitted, and the corpus already uses the necessary weighting machinery for other purposes (P-1216 and P-1158 apply inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting inside prevalent aMCI; P-961 fits a marginal structural Cox model with inverse probability weighting in the cognitively healthy NACC arm; P-791 uses IPTW only against missing-data selection). Propensity weighting is therefore applied everywhere in this corpus except to cohort entry itself. It matters because these nulls are being converted into mechanistic claims about which pathway a risk factor acts through and into therapeutic-timing claims about when mixed pathology starts to count, and a selection artefact is a sufficient alternative explanation for every one of them.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern that challenges a fundamental assumption and ground-truth standard (the peripheral-versus-central prodromal record; the interval-censored-data-structure record): the untested assumption here is that a prevalent-MCI cohort is an unbiased sampling frame for studying the exposures that caused MCI. It is non-obvious because the field's nulls look like substantive discoveries and are published as such - a pathway claim in P-934, a staging claim in P-1076 - so the defect is invisible from inside any one paper and only appears when within-stratum analyses drawn from three independent sources - ADNI (P-934 and P-984, an overlapping participant pool counted once), the NACC autopsy series (P-1076) and an Italian memory clinic (P-1146) - are seen to produce the same attenuation. It is actionable rather than aspirational: the corpus already contains the estimator (P-961), the weighting practice (P-1216, P-1158), and the cognitively normal arm from which the selection model is identifiable, so the closing analysis needs no new data collection.
gaps.closure_criteria: A study using a cohort that contains both a cognitively normal arm and a prevalent-MCI arm (ADNI or NACC, N >= 500 prevalent MCI) that, for at least one exposure with an established association with INCIDENT MCI (smoking, APOE e4, type 2 diabetes, hearing impairment): (a) fits a selection model for MCI-stratum membership on that exposure using the cognitively normal arm; (b) re-estimates the within-MCI exposure-to-progression association with inverse-probability-of-selection weighting, or reports a quantitative bias analysis / bounding argument for the conditioning-induced component; and (c) reports the corrected estimate side by side with the naive within-MCI estimate, stating whether the naive null survives. Closure would be partial rather than complete if the analysis is run for a single exposure in a single cohort.
gaps.modality: C5 Clinical/Population, with C2 structural MRI and C3 CSF outcomes in the cited analyses
gaps.task_type: T4 / T2 (risk-factor association and progression prediction within prevalent MCI)
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern that challenges a fundamental assumption and ground-truth standard (the peripheral-versus-central prodromal record; the interval-censored-data-structure record): the untested assumption here is that a prevalent-MCI cohort is an unbiased sampling frame for studying the exposures that caused MCI. It is non-obvious because the field's nulls look like substantive discoveries and are published as such - a pathway claim in P-934, a staging claim in P-1076 - so the defect is invisible from inside any one paper and only appears when within-stratum analyses drawn from three independent sources - ADNI (P-934 and P-984, an overlapping participant pool counted once), the NACC autopsy series (P-1076) and an Italian memory clinic (P-1146) - are seen to produce the same attenuation. It is actionable rather than aspirational: the corpus already contains the estimator (P-961), the weighting practice (P-1216, P-1158), and the cognitively normal arm from which the selection model is identifiable, so the closing analysis needs no new data collection.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: index-event / collider bias in prognostic research is a described methodological problem outside this corpus (it is the standard explanation offered for paradoxes such as the obesity and smoking survival paradoxes in diseased cohorts), so a reviewer may hold that the field has addressed it and the corpus sample merely misses the papers that did - the exact reason ACTOR-G-004, -005 and -008 were rejected. The record survives only if applying that correction to prevalent-MCI prognostic cohorts is genuinely unperformed, and I cannot verify that outside the corpus. A second, weaker objection is that each cited null has a mundane competing explanation the papers themselves offer - P-934's CSF and FDG arms were underpowered with heavy attrition, P-1076's cohort was autopsy-selected with attrition by the second visit, P-984's cells are small - so an evaluator could hold that ordinary power loss, not conditioning, explains the pattern, which would make the gap real but far less consequential than stated.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no combination of modalities or methods is proposed; the missing object is a bias analysis on existing estimates.

DATA_SCARCITY: explicitly not - ADNI and NACC both contain the cognitively normal arm needed to fit the selection model, and the same corpus already fits marginal structural and IPTW models on those data.

TOO_SPECIFIC: the absence spans four within-stratum analyses over three data sources (ADNI, NACC autopsy, Careggi Florence), four different exposures (smoking, Lewy pathology, sex-by-APOE-e4, gender/cognitive reserve) and three designs (longitudinal cohort, autopsy-anchored mixed model, clustering plus survival). NON-INDEPENDENCE DECLARED: P-934 and P-984 both draw prevalent-MCI participants from ADNI-1/2/GO and their samples almost certainly overlap, so they are ONE data source, not two; P-1216 and P-1158 are likewise ADNI. The independent sources supporting the pattern are therefore three (ADNI, NACC, Careggi), not four papers.
RESTATEMENT: differentiated above by id from ACTOR-G-017, G-030, G-033, G-034, G-038, G-075 and G-078, with the mechanism distinction stated in each case rather than asserted.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: the nearest closers are named and their residual stated - P-1076 names survival bias but performs no correction and asks for one; P-1216 and P-1158 weight for treatment assignment within the stratum; P-961 weights in the pre-MCI arm and so does not condition at all; P-791 weights for missing-data exclusion.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the 'no corpus study estimates or corrects the selection component' clause was checked against every propensity/IPW paper the corpus digests contain (found by grepping for inverse probability, IPTW, IPCW, IPW, E-value and bias analysis) and each of the four hits is admitted into the record with the exact respect in which it falls short. The clause is stated for cohort-entry selection only.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: each paper is cited only for what its own block says. P-1076 alone is cited for the selection-bias construct, because it is the only cited paper whose text contains that vocabulary; P-934, P-984 and P-1146 are cited strictly for their reported nulls, their baseline imbalance and their own substantive interpretations, all of which are verbatim in their blocks. The collider mechanism is labelled in the claim as the record's synthesis, not attributed to any paper.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: every quoted number comes from a results, methods or problems field, not from a significance or novelty field. The record does not claim that any specific null IS a selection artefact - only that the artefact is a sufficient untested alternative and is never bounded.
gaps.dedup_note: Grepped existing_gaps.md and existing_records_core.md for collider, index event, index-event, survivor bias, survival bias, selection bias, left-truncation and immortal time: the only hits are three rejected single-paper G-CAND limitation stubs (G-CAND-195, G-CAND-242, G-CAND-317), none of which states this as a gap. Differentiated by id from the nearest live records. ACTOR-G-038 is the closest and is genuinely different: it concerns cross-sectional survey/tabular models whose top SHAP predictors are reverse-caused BY MCI - the bias there is outcome-causes-predictor in a cross-sectional design, whereas this is conditioning-induced non-exchangeability in longitudinal within-stratum prognostic models, and the two have different corrections. ACTOR-G-017 and ACTOR-G-033 concern how the MCI label and the conversion endpoint are DEFINED (ascertainment rules, follow-up windows); this record takes the definition as given and concerns who ends up inside it. ACTOR-G-030 asks for demographics-only baselines against digital classifiers - a confounding-control question in diagnostic models, not a selection question in prognostic ones. ACTOR-G-034 and ACTOR-G-075 concern measurement reliability and practice effects. ACTOR-G-078 concerns endpoint choice. No existing gap cites P-934, P-984, P-1076, P-1146, P-1216, P-961 or P-791.

gaps.gap_statement: CORPUS-SCOPED GAP. Every stand-alone fluid-analyte MCI diagnostic study in this pack reports its operating characteristics at a disease prevalence its own sampling design imposed - 1:1 matched case-control (P-1232: '155 MCI patients and 155 age/sex-matched healthy controls'), balanced 20/20/20 groups (P-1218), 50% pathology-positive by construction (P-1225: '36 of 72 (50%) classified as AP+ carriers'), 53.6% MCI among recruited diabetic inpatients (P-1212) - and then advances the marker for population or memory-clinic SCREENING. None reports a positive predictive value, or a false-positives-per-true-case count, at any prevalence resembling the population it proposes to screen. The absence is decision-critical rather than cosmetic because sensitivity and specificity are prevalence-invariant while PPV is not, and these markers' specificities are low (P-1232 60.7%, P-1219 53.9%, P-1218 70%): at a realistic community MCI prevalence a 60% specificity generates several false positives per true case, so the 'non-invasive early diagnostic tool' claim is unsupported by anything these papers measured. The corpus's clinical-risk-score arm has already done this calculation and shown the result - P-939's SLAS index at its optimal cut-off gives 'PPV 0.169 at 10.2% cumulative incidence', and P-1060's cognitively-normal model reports PPV 0.46 - so the method and the demonstration both exist in this corpus; they have simply never been applied to the analyte arm that makes the screening claims. Related failure in the same family: P-1227 reports '84% accuracy across the entire cohort' on a sample where '90 converted' out of '648 ADNI participants' (13.9%), i.e. a figure below the 86.1% obtainable by predicting non-conversion for everyone [DERIVED by the miner from the two quoted numbers, 558/648; the paper reports no AUC, sensitivity or specificity], and reads it as evidence that CSF status still adds value.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard clinical-utility pattern - the XAI gold gap ('descriptive feature attribution without proving it improves clinician decision-making') and NEW-G-23 in shape but not content: it moves past 'these markers are weak' to name the specific quantity a deployment decision turns on and show it has never been computed for this marker class. Non-obvious in three ways. (1) The absence is invisible to the usual audit because the papers DO report sensitivity, specificity and AUC, and one (P-1225) even reports PPV - so a checklist scan sees complete reporting; the defect is the prevalence at which the PPV was computed, not its absence. (2) The corpus itself supplies the counterfactual: P-939 does the calculation in a community field evaluation and PPV falls to 0.169 at 10.2% incidence, at a SPECIFICITY (0.672) that is better than P-1232's 60.7% and P-1219's 53.9% - so the analyte papers' screening claims are being made from a worse operating point than the one already shown to fail. (3) It is closable with existing data, so it is a methodological gap rather than a data limitation.
gaps.closure_criteria: Take one published stand-alone fluid-analyte MCI diagnostic study's 2x2 table (or re-run its model) and report, alongside the existing AUC/sensitivity/specificity: (a) PPV and NPV recomputed at two externally sourced MCI prevalences bracketing the proposed deployment setting (e.g. ~5-8% community aged 65+ and ~30-40% memory clinic), and (b) the number of false positives per true case detected at the proposed operating point. Minimum acceptable form: N>=200 with a pre-specified operating threshold fixed before the recomputation, prevalence sources cited, and the resulting PPV compared against the paper's own deployment claim. A study reporting only ECE and a reliability diagram does NOT close this gap; a study reporting only decision-curve net benefit at its own sampled prevalence does not close it either.

gaps.task_type: T1 (MCI detection / diagnostic classification), with T2 spillover in P-1227

gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE. Prevalence-conditioned PPV for a blood MCI/AD marker is not an unexplored idea in the wider field - primary-care evaluations of plasma p-tau217 have reported predictive values at realistic primary-care prevalence - so this is a corpus-scoped absence for the marker classes actually represented here (exosomal lncRNA, serum RBP, BVR-A, an impedance-biosensor p-tau181), not a field-wide one, and the statement must carry that scope or it will be closed on external search the way ACTOR-G-004/005/008 were. A second, weaker objection: the P-1227 no-information-rate figure is arithmetic I performed on two quoted numbers rather than a number the paper printed, and it is flagged as DERIVED in the claim; if the operator rejects miner-derived arithmetic, that leg drops without damaging the other five papers.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: does not name any modality or method pair; it names a quantity (prevalence-conditioned predictive value) that a single existing dataset can produce.
DATA_SCARCITY: the required data already exist inside the cited papers - a 2x2 table and an external prevalence estimate are sufficient; nothing scarce is needed.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: the two papers that DO address it are named as closers rather than omitted (P-939, P-1060), and P-1212's decision-curve analysis is credited as the nearest attempt inside the analyte arm. The gap is scoped to what remains: no stand-alone fluid-analyte MCI diagnostic study reports predictive value at a prevalence other than its own sampled one.
RESTATEMENT: distinguished by id from NEW-G-23, G-07, G-09, NEW-G-27, ACTOR-G-017, ACTOR-G-029 and VF-29 in why_new; each differs in the measured quantity and in the closure test.

TOO_SPECIFIC: spans six papers across four independent cohorts (Guangzhou, Florence, Incheon, Jinan, Xuzhou, ADNI) and four marker classes (exosomal lncRNA, p-tau181 by two different platforms, serum RBP, BVR-A/HOMA-IR); it is a class-level property, not one study's design flaw.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the negative clause was checked against every paper the record cites. P-939 and P-1060 DO report prevalence-realistic PPV and are therefore listed as closers in a different arm, not as claiming papers; P-1225 DOES report PPV and the clause is narrowed to the prevalence at which it was computed; P-1212 DOES run decision-curve analysis and is credited. The surviving clause names only the stand-alone analyte diagnostic arm.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: the quantity is diagnostic-test performance in MCI, squarely inside the corpus scope; no trial-design or drug-development content.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked against every gap in T04_blood_omics_existing_gaps.md and against grep of all 534 statements in existing_gaps.md for 'prevalence', 'PPV', 'NPV', 'predictive value', 'spectrum bias', 'case-control', 'no-information', 'balanced', 'external validation'. NOT NEW-G-23 (calibration): that gap's closure criteria are Platt/isotonic/temperature scaling with Expected Calibration Error and a reliability diagram - a different quantity (agreement of predicted probabilities with observed frequencies within a cohort) from prevalence transportability of PPV across settings; a perfectly calibrated model in a 50%-prevalence sample is still miscalibrated for a 15%-prevalence one, and vice versa. NOT G-09 / NEW-G-27 / G-07: those require a prospective clinician-facing trial, an AI-vs-standard-of-care RCT, or a health-economic model - none of which this needs; this gap is closable by recomputation from data the papers already hold, which is why it is worth surfacing separately. NOT ACTOR-G-029 (analytical-platform domain shift): that concerns the loss when a threshold trained on one assay platform is applied to another; this concerns the loss when a threshold validated at one disease prevalence is applied at another, and holds even with a single platform. NOT ACTOR-G-017 (MCI case ascertainment rules moving prevalence ESTIMATES): that gap is about how the case definition changes the reported prevalence of the disease; this is about how the sampled prevalence changes the reported usefulness of a test. NOT VF-29 (ascertainment dominates estimates) for the same reason. The many G-CAND-* 'no external validation' rejections concern generalisation of discrimination, not the prevalence-dependence of predictive value. No existing gap cites P-939's PPV 0.169 or P-1060's PPV 0.46.
