gaps.gap_statement: CORPUS-SCOPED GAP. The inference that a fluid marker separating NC / MCI / AD status therefore carries prognostic information about MCI-to-AD conversion has been tested inside a single cohort for a multi-analyte panel exactly ONCE in this corpus, and it failed: P-1221 (EMIF-AD, 800 participants; 194 MCI with paired plasma proteomics and metabolomics and 2.2-year follow-up) reports that its 14-feature conversion signature consisted of 'features not selected by the multiclass models'. That panel-level dissociation has not been replicated. For single analytes the corpus's later-added studies do run both endpoints in one cohort and find the inference HOLDS rather than fails: P-1414 (Lleida, 81 MCI followed 56 months, 45 progressors) reports plasma p-tau217 at AUC 0.924 for CSF amyloid positivity and AUC 0.876 for MCI-to-AD progression side by side, and P-1368 reports plasma NfL at AUC 0.82 for an AD biomarker profile and 0.954 (change rate) for progression in 47 MCI. Neither uses an NC/MCI/AD clinical-stage endpoint, a panel, a difference test or an overlap null, so the closure criteria remain unmet, but the absence clause is confined to panels and to clinical-stage endpoints. Meanwhile the stage-contrast papers keep attaching prognostic language to designs that measure no progression at all: P-1209's title claims 'prognostic value' while its own limitations record 'no specific analysis of MCI patients who converted to AD (converter subgroup)' and list 'Whether GST-alpha changes predict MCI-to-AD conversion' as still open; P-1219 concludes serum RBP 'may be a vital marker of diabetic MCI progression' from a design whose own limitations state the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference; P-1220 reports a stage-ordered progression signature - 'valine increased progressively (control < MCI < AD) while alanine showed a biphasic pattern (reduced in MCI, elevated in AD)' - from 16 MCI participants measured once, conceding that the 'cross-sectional design limits causal/temporal inference' and naming validation of those signatures as progression biomarkers as future work. This matters because the two arms are not equally sized: stage-contrast studies are the bulk of the fluid-biomarker corpus, and if the P-1221 dissociation holds, essentially none of that body of work carries the prognostic information its abstracts claim - yet the field has one datum on the question and has neither replicated nor acted on it.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard objective-function-framing pattern ('models optimise progression and never reversion', 'prognostic models treat CNS markers as ground truth') - it challenges what the field's objective function is actually measuring rather than naming a missing dataset. Non-obvious because the defect is invisible in every individual paper: each one's statistics are correct for the endpoint it measured, and the overreach lives only in the word 'prognostic'/'progression' in the title or significance field. It becomes visible only when a single corpus paper that measured BOTH endpoints in one cohort reports that the two feature sets do not overlap. The record also protects itself from the standard failure of this shape: it does not assert that nobody has looked, it names the one paper that looked, states what it found, and locates the gap in the replication and the application.
gaps.closure_criteria: In one longitudinal MCI cohort with conversion follow-up (N>=200 baseline MCI, >=60 converters, >=3 years), measure a panel of fluid analytes already published as NC/MCI/AD stage discriminators and report side by side, in the same participants: (a) each analyte's AUC for cross-sectional stage separation, (b) the same analyte's AUC or C-index for MCI-to-AD conversion, (c) a statistical test of the difference, and (d) the overlap between the feature set selected for each endpoint, with a permutation null for the overlap so that selection instability can be distinguished from genuine dissociation. A study reporting only conversion performance, or only stage performance, does not close it; neither does a meta-analysis pooling the two endpoints across different populations.
gaps.modality: C3 Molecular/Fluid (paired plasma proteomics-metabolomics, plasma GST-alpha, serum RBP, multi-biofluid NMR metabolomics, blood core AD markers)
gaps.task_type: T1 (MCI detection) versus T2 (MCI-to-AD conversion prediction) - the gap is exactly the transfer between these two task types
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold-standard objective-function-framing pattern ('models optimise progression and never reversion', 'prognostic models treat CNS markers as ground truth') - it challenges what the field's objective function is actually measuring rather than naming a missing dataset. Non-obvious because the defect is invisible in every individual paper: each one's statistics are correct for the endpoint it measured, and the overreach lives only in the word 'prognostic'/'progression' in the title or significance field. It becomes visible only when a single corpus paper that measured BOTH endpoints in one cohort reports that the two feature sets do not overlap. The record also protects itself from the standard failure of this shape: it does not assert that nobody has looked, it names the one paper that looked, states what it found, and locates the gap in the replication and the application.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is that P-1221's dissociation may be an artefact of its own pipeline rather than a property of the biology, which would make the gap rest on a shaky pivot. Its 14-feature conversion model concatenates 12 clinical covariates including amyloid status and MMSE, and its own limitations state that 'models include clinical covariates (amyloid status, MMSE) so molecular contributions are not isolated'; feature selection required agreement of 3 of 4 algorithms, and with 3630 proteins and 540 metabolites two runs on different endpoints could return disjoint sets by selection instability alone, with no overlap test or permutation null reported. If the disjointness is selection noise, the gap collapses from 'the inference has been tested and failed' to 'the inference has never been properly tested' - still a gap, but a weaker and more ordinary one. A second objection: for the specific analytes with the most external evidence (p-tau181/217), the wider literature does show both diagnostic and prognostic performance, so the record must stay corpus-scoped and must not be read as a claim that status markers are never prognostic.
fp_codes_cleared: UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: this is the code that killed an earlier draft of this record, and the clause was rewritten because of it. P-1221 DOES perform the within-cohort test, so the claim explicitly credits it as the pivot; P-1231 DOES pool progression evidence, so the claim is narrowed to within-cohort designs and P-1231 is listed as a partial closer. The surviving negative is only that the dissociation is unreplicated and that no published stage-discriminating analyte has been re-evaluated against a conversion endpoint.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: the two quotes that are author assertions rather than measured results (P-1219's 'vital marker of ... progression', and P-1220's stage-ordering) are tagged with the summary field they came from, and they are cited AS assertions - the unearned assertion is the defect the gap describes, not evidence offered as a finding.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper's own text carries the gap's vocabulary - 'prognostic', 'converter subgroup', 'progression', 'conversion' - none is bridged to the construct by miner inference.
COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no modality or method pairing is proposed; the closure is a comparison of two endpoints on one existing panel.

DATA_SCARCITY: closable with cohorts that already exist (ADNI, EMIF-AD, AIBL and the memory-clinic cohorts in this pack all hold conversion follow-up alongside stored plasma), so this is methodological, not a data limitation.

TOO_SPECIFIC: spans four independent cohorts (EMIF-AD 11-cohort European, ADNI, Jinan T2DM, Rio de Janeiro) and four marker classes (paired proteomics/metabolomics, plasma GST-alpha, serum RBP, NMR metabolites), plus a 150-study meta-analysis.
FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: the two papers that come closest (P-1221 within-cohort, P-1231 across-study) are named with what each leaves open rather than omitted.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked against T04_blood_omics_existing_gaps.md in full and against grep of existing_gaps.md for 'prognostic', 'conversion endpoint', 'cross-sectional design', 'status'. NOT MINE-G-003 (FAQ ablation): that record is about an instrument that is both a top predictor and the longitudinal outcome in ADNI conversion models, and its closure is a removal-ablation of FAQ/CDR-SOB; this record is about whether cross-sectional STAGE separation transfers to conversion prediction at all, in plasma analytes, and its closure is a side-by-side endpoint comparison. NOT ACTOR-G-022 (intervention trials report cognitive-scale change with no anchor to disease course): that is the intervention literature and the missing anchor is a conversion or functional endpoint after treatment; this is the observational biomarker literature and the missing test is whether a diagnostic marker is prognostic. NOT ACTOR-G-025 (MCI subtype is the strongest prognostic stratifier and is used nowhere else): different construct (clinical subtype, not a fluid analyte) and different absence (non-use of a known stratifier, not an untested inference). NOT the family of '...pairs X with longitudinal dementia-conversion endpoints' records (ACTOR-G-084, G-082, G-062, G-043, G-051, G-055, G-NEW-1039-A): each of those is a single-modality 'this channel has no conversion study' statement; this record is the cross-cutting inference-validity question and is anchored on a positive result (P-1221's dissociation) rather than on a missing study. Also checked against existing IA records: IA-17 concerns generalisation of high in-study performance to real-world populations, not the transfer from a status endpoint to a conversion endpoint; no IA or KA entry in existing_records_core.md states the status-implies-prognosis prior.

gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: CORPUS-SCOPED GAP. The inference that a fluid marker separating NC / MCI / AD status therefore carries prognostic information about MCI-to-AD conversion has been tested inside a single cohort exactly ONCE in this corpus, and it failed: P-1221 (EMIF-AD, 800 participants; 194 MCI with paired plasma proteomics and metabolomics and 2.2-year follow-up) reports that its 14-feature conversion signature consisted of 'features not selected by the multiclass models'. That dissociation has never been replicated, and no corpus study takes a published cross-sectional stage-discriminating fluid analyte and evaluates it against a conversion endpoint in the same cohort to report the resulting change in discrimination. Meanwhile the stage-contrast papers keep attaching prognostic language to designs that measure no progression at all: P-1209's title claims 'prognostic value' while its own limitations record 'no specific analysis of MCI patients who converted to AD (converter subgroup)' and list 'Whether GST-alpha changes predict MCI-to-AD conversion' as still open; P-1219 concludes serum RBP 'may be a vital marker of diabetic MCI progression' from a design whose own limitations state the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference; P-1220 reports a stage-ordered progression signature - 'valine increased progressively (control < MCI < AD) while alanine showed a biphasic pattern (reduced in MCI, elevated in AD)' - from 16 MCI participants measured once, conceding that the 'cross-sectional design limits causal/temporal inference' and naming validation of those signatures as progression biomarkers as future work. This matters because the two arms are not equally sized: stage-contrast studies are the bulk of the fluid-biomarker corpus, and if the P-1221 dissociation holds, essentially none of that body of work carries the prognostic information its abstracts claim - yet the field has one datum on the question and has neither replicated nor acted on it.

gaps.gap_statement: CORPUS-SCOPED GAP. In this corpus's fluid-biomarker literature the 'externally validated' status is assigned at the PAPER level while the object actually carried to the independent cohort is not the model or marker the paper proposes for use - and no study reports validation status per model rather than per paper, so the maturity of the evidence base is systematically overstated. Two instances, both among the pack's best-designed studies. P-1221 is recorded as 'V3 (independent cohort validation - EDAR - for multiclass models; internal split/CV for conversion model)': the EDAR cohort validated only the NC/MCI/AD status models ('multiclass protein models selected 9 features validated at 0.720 mean balanced accuracy'), while the result the paper advances - the 194-MCI, 14-feature conversion model at AUC 0.872 - never left EMIF-AD. P-1232 is recorded as 'V3 (external validation in AddNeuroMed/GSE63060 cohort)' with no qualifier, yet its own limitations concede 'validation of target genes (not the lncRNAs themselves) in the external dataset': the external analysis substituted two downstream genes (ATP2A2, PSEN1) for the three exosomal lncRNAs that ARE the proposed panel, so the AUC 0.695 tests a different measurement entirely. This matters because validation tier is the field's main proxy for evidence maturity and is the column that evidence syntheses, registries and this corpus's own Appendix A and knowledge graph grade papers on; a tier assigned to the paper rather than to the claim means the count of externally validated blood-biomarker MCI results is inflated by an unknown amount, and neither instance is detectable without reading the methods.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Shares the shape of the gold-standard ground-truth critiques - it attacks the reliability of the label the field grades itself by, rather than naming a missing experiment. Non-obvious because it is anti-correlated with paper quality: both instances are among the most rigorous studies in the pack (multi-cohort omics with a four-algorithm pipeline; a three-stage discovery-qPCR-external design), so any audit that flags weak papers will miss them, and the corpus's own Validation Type column records one of the two as an unqualified V3.
gaps.closure_criteria: An audit that re-derives validation status at model granularity for every V3-labelled fluid-biomarker row in the corpus registry and reports how many papers' HEADLINE result was itself evaluated in the independent cohort, with the mis-scoped rows listed. (The original option (b) - a paper stating per-model validation cohorts - is satisfied by any single externally validated model, e.g. P-1293's miRNA composite index, and is withdrawn as non-discriminating.)

gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is that this is two papers' self-conceded limitations aggregated into a pattern, which is exactly the 'single-paper limitation' shape the lint soft-flags - both instances are stated in the papers' own problems or Validation Type fields, so nothing here was hidden, and two instances in a 30-paper pack is a thin base for asserting a field-level bookkeeping failure. A second objection: the second half of the claim - that syntheses and registries are inflated by this - is an inference about downstream consumers rather than a measured quantity; nobody has counted how many V3-labelled corpus rows have a mis-scoped validation object, and until that count exists the magnitude of the problem is unknown. The operator may reasonably prefer to convert this into an audit task on the registry's Validation Type column rather than accept it as a research gap.

gaps.gap_statement: The whole non-invasive MCI fluid-biomarker programme rests on an untested transfer assumption - that a peripheral fluid mirrors the central compartment - and the corpus's own paired-compartment studies contradict it at the level of SIGN, not merely of magnitude. Salivary GFAP FALLS in MCI/AD while plasma and brain GFAP rise; CSF NGAL FALLS in MCI and predicts conversion while serum NGAL rises in the prior literature and is null for conversion in the same participants; the cytokine triad IL-1beta/IL-6/TNF-alpha rises in plasma (P-1248) and falls in saliva (P-1234), and systemic blood inflammatory markers fail to separate MCI in a cohort where five CSF mediators do (P-1251, analytes not named in its record); serum LPS is proposed as the minimally invasive marker in a study whose MCI-versus-control elevation appears only in CSF (P-1233). Yet among the corpus studies that assay more than one compartment, only P-1300 (ACE Alzheimer Center Barcelona, 485 participants with paired CSF and plasma, 63 inflammatory mediators) reports a within-subject peripheral-versus-central concordance statistic - finding robust CSF-plasma correlation for only six of 63 mediators - while no block reports one for saliva or for GFAP/NGAL specifically, and none tests whether a cut-off optimised in one fluid retains its sensitivity/specificity in the other. WHY THIS MATTERS: because the direction reverses, a threshold or a mechanistic reading imported from the central literature does not merely lose accuracy in the periphery - it can invert which participants are flagged, and the marker's biological interpretation ('a peripheral readout of reactive astrogliosis') is then read off a change that moves the wrong way. Every cheap-screening rationale in this literature depends on a compartment-transfer function that no corpus study has estimated. SCOPE: asserted for this corpus and for the inflammatory / astroglial marker class (GFAP, NGAL, LPS/COX, the pro-inflammatory cytokine triad) plus saliva; NO claim is made that plasma-versus-CSF concordance for the core amyloid/tau analytes is unstudied, which is a large external field.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern of the OCT vendor gap (NEW-G-24) - a measurement never calibrated across the settings it is deployed in - and the gold peripheral-versus-central pattern (NEW-G-29), but goes one step further than either: the failure is not variance or lag, it is SIGN. The non-obvious part is that the corpus reads as if peripheral inflammation studies simply disagree with each other (P-1248 positive, P-1251 null) when the organising variable is which fluid was sampled; and that the two studies which actually drew two fluids from the same people (P-1239, P-1233) are the ones whose peripheral arm failed, while both papers still headline the peripheral marker. It also names a concrete interpretive casualty: P-1234 reads a fall in salivary GFAP as evidence of reactive astrogliosis, a phenomenon defined by GFAP rising.
gaps.closure_criteria: One study that collects saliva or serum/plasma AND CSF from the SAME participants (>=100, MCI plus cognitively normal controls) in a single session, assays one analyte from the inflammatory/astroglial class (GFAP, NGAL, or the IL-1beta/IL-6/TNF-alpha triad) on a single platform in both fluids, and reports: (a) the within-subject peripheral-central correlation with its 95% CI and a Bland-Altman agreement plot; (b) the direction and effect size of the MCI-versus-control difference separately in each fluid; and (c) the sensitivity and specificity retained when the cut-off optimised in the central fluid is applied unchanged to the peripheral one. A study that reports only two separate per-fluid ROC analyses does NOT close it.
gaps.task_type: T1 diagnostic classification and T2 conversion prediction

The non-obvious part is that the corpus reads as if peripheral inflammation studies simply disagree with each other (P-1248 positive, P-1251 null) when the organising variable is which fluid was sampled; and that the two studies which actually drew two fluids from the same people (P-1239, P-1233) are the ones whose peripheral arm failed, while both papers still headline the peripheral marker. It also names a concrete interpretive casualty: P-1234 reads a fall in salivary GFAP as evidence of reactive astrogliosis, a phenomenon defined by GFAP rising.
gaps.critic_falsification: P-1234's own block cites prior work asserting the very concordance this record calls unquantified - 'Saliva reflects changes in CSF per earlier work (Bermejo-Pareja 2010, Sabbagh 2018)'. A reviewer with those papers in hand could argue the saliva-CSF relationship has been examined outside this corpus and that the absence is a sampling artifact of a 1,262-paper sample (EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE, the code that already killed ACTOR-G-004 in this exact theme). The counter is that P-1234 cites that concordance and then reports a GFAP sign reversal in the same block without reconciling them, which makes the transfer function contested rather than merely uncollected - but this record should be checked against the external salivary- and serum-biomarker concordance literature before any promotion, and if that literature already reports within-subject peripheral-central correlations for GFAP or the cytokine triad, the record must be narrowed to the cut-off-transfer clause or withdrawn.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: this is not 'combine modality X with Y'. It is a measurement-transfer/calibration failure across biofluid compartments, with the mechanism (compartment-specific regulation) named by P-1234's own block.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the record does NOT claim that no study assays two compartments - it names the three that do (P-1233, P-1239, P-1251) and states exactly what each reports instead. The absence clause is confined to a within-subject concordance statistic and a cut-off-transfer test, neither of which appears in any of the cited blocks.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited block uses the construct's own vocabulary - P-1234 'compartment-specific regulation'; P-1239 'increased serum NGAL in MCI'; P-1251 'systemic (blood) ... cerebrospinal fluid'; P-1233 'stronger in CSF (invasive) than serum'; P-1248 names the same three cytokines as P-1234.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: all direction claims are quoted from Results / Problems / Related-work fields. The two quotes taken from 'What is the significance?' fields (P-1234 'peripheral readout of reactive astrogliosis'; P-1233 'promising, minimally invasive biomarker') are explicitly tagged in the evidence entries as author ASSERTIONS and are the OBJECT of the critique, never offered as measured findings.

DATA_SCARCITY: no. P-1233 and P-1239 already collected both fluids and P-1251 already collected blood and CSF in one cohort; the missing analysis needs no new data type, only paired sampling and a correlation.
TOO_SPECIFIC: spans five papers, four analyte families (GFAP, NGAL, LPS/COX-1/COX-2, the IL-1beta/IL-6/TNF-alpha triad), three compartments (saliva, blood/serum/plasma, CSF) and four countries.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: partially mitigated by explicit scoping - the record states that plasma-versus-CSF concordance for the CORE amyloid/tau analytes is a real external field and is NOT claimed absent, and confines itself to the inflammatory/astroglial class and to saliva. Residual exposure is retained in residual_risk rather than dismissed.
RESTATEMENT: see why_new; the nearest records (ACTOR-G-029, ACTOR-G-004) are argued distinct clause by clause.

NON_INDEPENDENCE (disclosed, not an FP code): P-1233 and P-1234 are the SAME Thessaloniki programme - same site (AHEPA University General Hospital / GAADRD) and shared authors (Katsipis G, Tsolaki M, Pantazaki A A) - and are counted here as ONE evidence source. The gap still rests on three further independent cohorts (P-1239 Netherlands, P-1248 India, P-1251 USA). gatecheck.py cf P-1233 P-1234 prints PASS, so the checker does not see this; it was found by reading the two author lists and dataset fields.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked by id against the theme file and a grep of all 535 corpus gap statements. (1) ACTOR-G-029 is the closest and is DISTINCT: it is analytical-PLATFORM domain shift - Simoa vs INNOTEST ELISA vs LUMIPULSE CLEIA vs mass-spec vs NMR - i.e. the measuring instrument. Harmonising two platforms cannot reconcile a marker that falls in saliva and rises in plasma; the discordance here is biological compartment, and it survives perfect assay harmonisation. (2) ACTOR-G-004 is CLOSED as EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE and asked a different question: formal non-inferiority of a plasma PANEL versus CSF for MCI-to-AD conversion, i.e. an accuracy comparison of core AD analytes. This record is about direction and threshold transfer for inflammatory/astroglial analytes including saliva, and it stands even if a plasma panel is non-inferior on AUC - a non-inferior panel can still have a reversed univariate direction. (3) G-14 (calibration under domain shift), NEW-G-23 (ECE/reliability diagrams), ACTOR-G-015 (sex/ancestry transfer) and ACTOR-G-021 (incremental discrimination over demographics) are all about model performance quantities, not about the compartment the specimen came from. (4) G-07, G-13, G-22, ACTOR-G-003 checked and unrelated. A grep of existing_gaps.md for 'saliva' and for 'compartment' returns zero hits across all 535 statements.

SCOPE: asserted for this corpus and for the inflammatory / astroglial marker class (GFAP, NGAL, LPS/COX, the pro-inflammatory cytokine triad) plus saliva; NO claim is made that plasma-versus-CSF concordance for the core amyloid/tau analytes is unstudied, which is a large external field.

gaps.gap_statement: Blood- and saliva-based MCI markers in this corpus are recommended for population screening on the strength of discrimination measured in small, balanced, investigator-selected case-control extracts, and none reports its operating characteristics in the sampling frame it proposes to screen. The demonstrative case is P-1254: it surveyed 275 community-dwelling residents by random selection from a register list, documented a 35.9% MCI prevalence in that survey, and then computed AUC 0.901 with specificity 100% on an extract of 24 MCI versus 24 age-matched controls (plus a third arm of 24 younger controls), concluding that non-invasive markers 'could make routine MCI screening feasible at scale'. P-1234 reports sensitivity 100% / specificity 100% for salivary GFAP from 20 participants per group and proposes community screening; P-1233 proposes serum LPS for early screening from a serum set containing 13 cognitively healthy controls; P-1249 proposes exosomal-complement screening in T1DM from 31 MCI versus 24 non-MCI patients (AUC 0.76). WHY THIS MATTERS: the balanced extract fixes the base rate at 50%, an operating point no screening programme ever sees, so the reported sensitivity/specificity is not the screening performance and cannot be converted into the only numbers that decide whether a screening programme is viable - positive predictive value, negative predictive value and the false-positive burden per thousand screened at the cohort's own observed prevalence. None of these four blocks reports any of those quantities, or applies the marker to the full enrolled frame, even where - as in P-1254 - the full frame of 275 was already recruited and cognitively phenotyped. The consequence is that a literature explicitly justified by scalable community screening has never estimated how many cognitively healthy older adults its own tests would send for confirmatory work-up. SCOPE: asserted for this corpus and for exploratory non-core fluid markers (exosomal miRNA, salivary GFAP, serum LPS, exosomal complement); no claim is made about population-frame evaluation of the core plasma amyloid/tau analytes.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern in which the field substitutes a convenient endpoint for the one that matters (the XAI 'descriptive attribution vs actual decision-making' gap, and G-09's separation of biomarker-to-conversion accuracy from demonstrated clinical utility). The non-obvious part is that the failure is not the familiar 'small sample, no external validation' complaint that the corpus has rejected dozens of times: P-1254 had a large, randomly-sampled, prevalence-characterised frame in hand and reported the wrong estimand from a subset of it, which means the missing analysis is recoverable from data already collected rather than requiring a new cohort. It also identifies why the saturated specificities in this literature are dangerous specifically for screening: at a 50% engineered base rate a 100% specificity looks decisive, while the same test at the paper's own 35.9% community prevalence - let alone the far lower prevalence of a general primary-care frame - has an unreported false-positive burden that determines whether the programme is deployable at all.
gaps.closure_criteria: One diagnostic-accuracy study of a blood, saliva or stool MCI marker that (a) applies a cut-off FIXED IN ADVANCE from a separate derivation sample, (b) to every participant of a consecutively or randomly enrolled screening frame (>=500) rather than to a balanced extract, and (c) reports sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV and false positives per 1,000 screened at that frame's own observed prevalence, all with 95% confidence intervals, alongside the reference-standard cognitive adjudication. Reporting a second AUC on another balanced case-control sample does NOT close it.

gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE combined with an ARITHMETIC CAVEAT. (a) External: population-frame diagnostic-accuracy evaluations of blood biomarkers WITH predictive values do exist for the core plasma AD analytes (p-tau assays evaluated in primary-care and population cohorts), so a reviewer could argue the corpus absence is a sampling artifact; the record is therefore scoped to the exploratory non-core markers, but that scoping must be checked externally for salivary GFAP and exosomal miRNA specifically before promotion. (b) Arithmetic: my own rule-of-three calculation (0 false positives in 24 controls implies a lower 95% bound on specificity near 86%) is the record's OWN computation, not a finding in any block, and it is offered only to show that the reported 100% specificity does not pin down the false-positive burden - it must not be quoted as a paper's result. (c) A weaker but real objection: at P-1254's unusually high 35.9% prevalence, PPV would remain high even at a much lower specificity, so the 'PPV collapses' intuition does not bite for that particular cohort; the gap's force there rests on the frame mismatch and on the far lower prevalence of any general primary-care population a scalable programme would target, not on P-1254's own prevalence figure.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no 'combine X with Y' clause anywhere; this is a diagnostic-accuracy estimand and sampling-frame gap.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the absence clause is confined to the four blocks cited and to two specific quantities (predictive value at the cohort's own prevalence; operating characteristics on the full enrolled frame). It does NOT claim that no corpus paper reports an AUC, a prevalence, or a community sample - P-1254 reports all three, which is precisely why it is the anchor rather than a counterexample.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited block uses the construct's own vocabulary - P-1254 'screening markers', 'MCI prevalence 35.9%', 'routine MCI screening feasible at scale'; P-1234 'community screening'; P-1233 'early screening'; P-1249 'screening and early detection'.

NOT_IN_SCOPE: diagnostic-accuracy estimands for MCI biomarkers sit squarely inside the corpus scope; this is not trial design or drug development.
DATA_SCARCITY: the opposite - P-1254's frame of 275 was already enrolled and MoCA-phenotyped, so the missing analysis needs no new data at all.

(5) ACTOR-G-047 and G-048 concern screening-cutoff validation for COGNITIVE INSTRUMENTS (MoCA in renal populations; tele-neuropsychology), not fluid assays. (6) G-22 is about external multi-site replication of EEG amyloid screening - a generalisation question, not an estimand question; a perfectly externally-replicated case-control AUC still does not give PPV at prevalence.

gaps.gap_statement: GAP (missing estimand, MRI/PET MCI neuroimaging). Claims that the MCI signal is carried by one region, one modality or one stratum and NOT by its comparator are made by placing a significant result beside a non-significant one measured in the SAME participants, while the between-arm contrast that the claim actually asserts - a region-family-by-group, modality-by-group or condition-by-group interaction, or any difference-of-differences with a confidence interval - is never estimated. The two arms are fitted as separate models, then compared by which side of the threshold each p value fell on; the 'absent' arm repeatedly sits at p = 0.06 to 0.07, or on a smaller denominator, or with no effect size printed at all. This matters for two reasons that are specific to this corpus rather than generic. First, these untested contrasts are the load-bearing evidence for its own consensus layer: VF-25 (n=13), VF-20 (n=6), VF-23 (n=4) and VF-28 (n=3) are each an aggregation of within-study significant-versus-null pairs, and VF-25's own record states that 'The dissociation is reported as a within-study head-to-head in each case, not inferred across papers' - which is true and is precisely the problem, because a head-to-head of two separately fitted models is a comparison of significance, not an estimated contrast. Second, these dissociations are what select downstream feature sets (entorhinal-first, olfactory-subregion masks, functional-before-structural ordering) and what fix the assumed sequence of pathology. Every arm needed to fit the missing model is already measured in the cited papers, so closure requires reanalysis and no new data collection.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'an assumption nobody tests' and 'a whole set of papers sharing a blind spot' rather than one paper's limitation, and it names a specific missing estimand with a zero-cost closure route, in the manner of the gold gap about interval-censored visit data being forced into binary labels. It is non-obvious because the corpus has already promoted these contrasts rather than flagged them: VF-25's own text advertises as a STRENGTH the very property that is the defect ('reported as a within-study head-to-head in each case'), and one of its 13 supporters, P-687, is in this pack with no interaction test. The pattern also crosses claim types (region, modality, condition, stratum), designs (cross-sectional VBM, longitudinal mixed models, connectome, PET-versus-MRI) and six independent cohorts - CIMA-Q, ADNI, a Chinese PD cohort, HABS-HD, a Montreal hearing cohort and a European TUG cohort - so it is not a house style of one dataset. Finally the record carries its own counter-evidence: P-738 does fit a region-by-group interaction WITHIN the olfactory family, P-720 does print confidence intervals on its null arms, P-864 does pre-nominate negative-control regions, and P-685 does hold one corrected threshold across four modalities. None of these is the missing contrast, and saying so precisely is what keeps the claim true.
gaps.closure_criteria: A reanalysis study on cohorts that already hold both arms - CIMA-Q for P-738's eight structures under two region definitions (N = 166); ADNI for P-934's entorhinal-versus-hippocampal smoking slopes (N = 870 MCI) and for P-770's MRI-volume-versus-tau-PET NPI models (N = 233 MCI); the three-group PD cohort of P-729 (N = 75) for degree-centrality-versus-VBM - that fits the two arms in ONE model on a common scale with an arm-by-group (or arm-by-exposure) interaction term, and reports the estimated difference-of-differences with a 95 per cent confidence interval plus a pre-specified equivalence margin for whichever arm the original paper declared absent. The gap closes when at least three previously published MCI dissociation claims have been re-expressed as an estimated contrast and the proportion that survive is reported; it moves to partially_open if one or two are done. A study that merely adds equivalence bounds to a single null arm does NOT close it, because that answers a different question from the one the dissociation claim asserts.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern 'an assumption nobody tests' and 'a whole set of papers sharing a blind spot' rather than one paper's limitation, and it names a specific missing estimand with a zero-cost closure route, in the manner of the gold gap about interval-censored visit data being forced into binary labels. It is non-obvious because the corpus has already promoted these contrasts rather than flagged them: VF-25's own text advertises as a STRENGTH the very property that is the defect ('reported as a within-study head-to-head in each case'), and one of its 13 supporters, P-687, is in this pack with no interaction test. The pattern also crosses claim types (region, modality, condition, stratum), designs (cross-sectional VBM, longitudinal mixed models, connectome, PET-versus-MRI) and six independent cohorts - CIMA-Q, ADNI, a Chinese PD cohort, HABS-HD, a Montreal hearing cohort and a European TUG cohort - so it is not a house style of one dataset. Finally the record carries its own counter-evidence: P-738 does fit a region-by-group interaction WITHIN the olfactory family, P-720 does print confidence intervals on its null arms, P-864 does pre-nominate negative-control regions, and P-685 does hold one corrected threshold across four modalities. None of these is the missing contrast, and saying so precisely is what keeps the claim true.
gaps.critic_falsification: EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE at the methodological level is the strongest objection. The significance-contrast fallacy is a textbook result (Gelman and Stern 2006) and was measured in the neuroscience literature by Nieuwenhuis and colleagues in 2011, so an operator can rule that the field already knows this and that the record is reporting hygiene rather than a research gap. The reply is that the gap asserted is not the absence of awareness but the absence of the ESTIMATED CONTRAST for these specific MCI claims - the entorhinal-versus-hippocampal smoking slope, the olfactory-subregion-versus-whole-structure atrophy, the degree-centrality-versus-volume ordering in PD-MCI - and that the consequence here is concrete rather than pedagogical because four verified findings totalling 26 supporter slots are built on exactly these pairs. If the operator nonetheless treats known-fallacy records as out of scope for a gap ledger, this record fails on that ground and not on its evidence. Second-order risk: two of the seven claiming papers (P-934, P-770) are ADNI analyses and share a house analysis style, so part of the pattern could be an ADNI-culture artefact; the non-ADNI arms (P-738 CIMA-Q, P-729, P-720 HABS-HD, P-896, P-687) are what carry the generality, and if a reviewer rejects any of those the multi-cohort argument weakens.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no 'combine X with Y' clause anywhere. The gap names a statistical estimand (an arm-by-group interaction / difference-of-differences with a CI) that is computable inside each cited paper's existing data.

RESTATEMENT: greps listed in why_new over the 186 theme gaps and all 534 corpus gaps found nothing of this shape; the five nearest existing records are named and distinguished, as are the two sibling candidates written in this run.

TOO_SPECIFIC: seven claiming papers across six independent cohorts and four claim types (region family, region pair, imaging modality, task condition, cohort stratum); it is a class-level defect, not a single narrow question.
DATA_SCARCITY: the opposite. Both arms are already measured in every claiming paper; P-738's digest states that fitting the required model 'costs nothing in new data collection'.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: partial closers were actively searched for within the pack and three were found and recorded as such (P-685 unified threshold, P-864 pre-nominated negative controls, P-853 explicit power-versus-biology fork), plus the within-family interaction P-738 does fit and the null-arm CIs P-720 does print. Each constrains the claim; none estimates a between-arm contrast, so the claim is scoped to that estimand rather than to 'nobody tests anything'.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the negative clause is confined to 'the between-arm contrast is not estimated' and was checked paper by paper against the record's own citations. The two facts that would falsify a looser wording - P-738's olfactory-family region-by-group interaction and P-720's confidence intervals on its null arms - are stated inside the record.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper's own digest uses the vocabulary of the claim (interaction, region family, dissociation, null arm, no difference), so no inferential bridge is being carried by a paper that never mentions the construct.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: each quote is tagged with the digest field it came from. The two appraisal-field quotes (P-738 'no model anywhere enters region family', P-720 'rather than on a tested interaction') are presented as appraisals of what was not fitted, never as measured findings; all numeric quotes come from results sections.

MISASSIGNED_MEASUREMENT_FAMILY: the record asserts no cross-family dichotomy of its own. Its point is that the papers' OWN dichotomies are unestimated, so it cannot manufacture a contrast by mis-assigning arms.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: the claim is about how MCI neuroimaging evidence is estimated and how this corpus aggregates it; it is not about trial design or drug development.

gaps.gap_statement: PARTIALLY OPEN, RESCOPED 2026-09-22. No corpus study reports the full incremental-value bundle for an added MCI marker: a paired, identical-fold delta in discrimination with a confidence interval, against a pre-specified minimal clinically meaningful difference, with the acquisition cost of the added marker stated, in two cohorts of which at least one is not ADNI. WHAT NO LONGER HOLDS: the record previously asserted that across the carded digests there was no DeLong or permutation test on an AUC difference, no confidence interval on a delta, and no information-criterion or paired-fold contrast between a combined and a reduced model, with P-945's reclassification analysis as the only formal increment. That is false. About twenty-five corpus papers use DeLong tests, and the combined-versus-reduced increment is tested in at least P-512 (357 ADNI MCI; integrated model AUC 0.807, 'significantly outperforming individual predictors by DeLong test' - named as a counterexample inside the block of this record's own anchor, P-731), P-1153 (delta iAUC 0.020, 95% CI 0.007-0.034, with J-ADNI and HABS replication), P-1343 (110 aMCI, non-ADNI, AICc ranking plus DeLong), P-590 (541 participants, non-ADNI; combined AUC 0.908 against 0.705 and 0.722 for single markers, both P<0.001), P-523, P-1214, P-1396, P-1394 and P-1016 (delta-AUC 0.30, 95% CI 0.12-0.47). The record also cited P-945 selectively: its IDI is null (0.090, -0.062 to 0.170) but its NRI is not (0.246, 0.021-0.848). WHAT SURVIVES: none of those studies reports the full bundle above, and P-1153 and P-512 come closest.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern of a clinical-utility failure (discrimination reported, decision impact untested) applied one level earlier: here even the discrimination CLAIM - that the added modality improves anything - is unverified before any utility question is reached. It is non-obvious for three reasons. First, the corpus has already promoted this defect into contradictory consensus: VF-02 and VF-22 are opposite answers to the same question and VF-22 is explicitly recorded as a scope boundary on VF-02, an unresolved tension that exists precisely because none of the nine supporting comparisons tests a delta. Second, VF-02's own qualifier shows the corpus noticed a WEAKER version of the problem - it restricts supporters to studies that 'run their OWN unimodal-vs-multimodal comparison (not merely cite the trend)' - so the corpus has already distinguished citing a trend from running a comparison, but not running a comparison from testing it. Third, the record carries the case that most resists a publication-bias explanation: P-742's title asserts a NULL increment, also untested, which shows the missing apparatus is symmetric rather than a bias toward positive results. The single partial closer, P-945, is the strongest possible evidence for the gap rather than against it, since the one time the increment was formally quantified its interval crossed zero.
gaps.closure_criteria: For one added MCI marker: report the change in discrimination against a pre-specified base model on identical cross-validation folds, with a confidence interval on the delta, benchmarked against a pre-stated minimal clinically meaningful difference, with the marker's acquisition cost stated, in two cohorts of which at least one is not ADNI. Partial instances (P-1153, P-512, P-1343, P-590) satisfy the delta-with-test element only.

gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is that the absence may be a DIGEST artefact rather than a literature absence. The 540 digests are structured summaries, and a paper could well have run a DeLong test that its summariser did not record, since 'we compared AUCs with DeLong' is exactly the kind of methods sentence a summary drops. If that is what is happening, the true statement is the weaker 'the corpus cannot verify these increments from what is recorded' - still consequential for a review that must pool them, but a reporting gap rather than a research gap, and it would move this record toward partially_open rather than open. The check that would settle it is opening the P-781, P-731 and P-727 PDFs for a DeLong or bootstrap sentence; I did not do that and the record should not be gated as if I had. A second objection: three of the four claiming papers (P-781, P-731, P-727) are already flagged for authors_overclaim, so a reviewer can argue the record is really about four weak papers rather than about a field practice - the counter is P-742, which is not an overclaimer and whose null increment is untested in the same way, and P-945, which is methodologically careful and still returned an interval crossing zero.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: this is the inverse of a combine-X-with-Y record. It does not ask for any new pairing; it asks whether the pairings already published actually improve anything, which is a statistical-estimand claim about existing studies.

RESTATEMENT: greps listed in why_new over the theme file and all 534 corpus gaps; the three adjacent existing records (G-13, NEW-G-22, ACTOR-G-006) are amyloid-PET-scoped or combinatorial and are named and distinguished, as are two sibling candidates from this run and this pack's own gap-01.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: actively searched for closers rather than assuming absence - greps across all 540 digests for 'DeLong', 'delta AUC', 'AUC difference', 'difference in AUC', 'compared the AUCs', 'test of the difference', 'net reclassification', 'integrated discrimination', 'likelihood ratio test' and bootstrap-difference phrasings. Two hits were followed up: P-825 mentions integrated discrimination improvement only in a list of metrics it does NOT report ('There is no area under any curve in this document'), and P-945 is a genuine partial closer, recorded as such with its null interval. The claim is scoped to what that search found and is stated as 'across the 540 carded digests I could find no report', not as a bare universal.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the record's own cited papers were checked first. P-945, the paper cited as the partial closer, is the single exception and is stated as such inside the claim; no other cited paper contains a delta test.

TOO_SPECIFIC: four claiming papers spanning neuropsychology-to-PET (P-781), MRI morphometry plus CSF plus genetics (P-731), connectome fusion (P-727) and clinician-knowledge features in survival modelling (P-742), across three cohorts and both directions of claim.

DATA_SCARCITY: the comparison data already exist in every claiming paper - both models were fitted; only the test on the difference is missing, and P-742's digest specifies the fix as a fold-by-fold paired comparison on data already in hand.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: DeLong tests and NRI/IDI are standard tools and are used outside this corpus, so 'nobody knows how to test an increment' would be false and is not what is asserted. What is asserted is that the MCI increment claims driving multimodal workup recommendations here have not had it applied, and that the one application (P-945) did not establish the increment - which is a finding about this evidence base, not about statistical methodology.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper's own digest is about the comparison in question - each prints both the combined and the reduced figure - so no paper is being enlisted for a construct it never mentions.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: quotes are tagged by digest field. P-742's is an appraisal-section quote and is presented as an appraisal of an omission; P-781's 'no test of the increment' sits in that digest's numbered results enumeration; all magnitudes are from results sections. No significance/novelty-field assertion is reported as a measured finding.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: the question is which markers to include in an MCI model and workup, squarely inside the corpus's scope; it is not trial design or drug development.

gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: GAP (untested increment, MCI diagnostic and prognostic modelling). When an MCI study recommends adding a marker or a modality to a workup, the recommendation is established by printing the combined and the single-marker discrimination figures side by side and observing that one is larger - never by testing the difference. Across the 540 carded digests I could find no report of a DeLong or permutation test on an AUC difference, no confidence interval on a delta-AUC or delta-c-index, and no information-criterion or paired-fold contrast between a combined and a reduced model; the only formal quantification of an increment is P-945's reclassification analysis, and its own integrated discrimination improvement is 0.090 with a 95 per cent confidence interval of -0.062 to 0.170, i.e. the added imaging value is not established. The defect is symmetric: negative increment claims are equally untested, and P-742 asserts a null increment in its TITLE from two c-indices read side by side. This matters because the corpus holds two OPPOSING verified findings on exactly this question - VF-02 (multimodal fusion outperforms single-modality models, n=6) and VF-22 (adding amyloid/FDG-PET or CSF on top of structural MRI or neurocognition yields negligible incremental prognostic value, n=3, itself recorded as 'a scope boundary on the general multimodal-superiority finding') - and neither can be adjudicated while every supporting comparison lacks a test of the delta. It also matters clinically because the arm being added is always the expensive, radiation-bearing or access-limited one, so an untested increment is an unpriced recommendation.

gaps.gap_statement: Repeat imaging is the recurring cost of MCI monitoring, yet no corpus study estimates the prognostic increment of a SECOND scan as a function of the inter-scan interval. Two of the three corpus studies that pit a baseline scan against serial change each fix one interval and reach opposite conclusions in different modalities: amyloid PET change over a mean 24 months adds nothing over baseline (HR 0.2, 95% CI 0.02-1.18, p=0.07; P-974, n=75, 17 converters) while WMH change over a single fixed 48-month interval predicts incident dementia/MCI (OR 1.51, 95% CI 1.12-2.04, p=0.007; P-967, n=433, 33 events). Modality, interval, outcome and setting move together across those two designs, so neither can set a monitoring schedule, and only one corpus design varies the interval while holding the modality fixed - P-527 (ADNI rs-fMRI at baseline, 12 and 24 months; sMCI-versus-pMCI accuracy rising across time points) - reporting accuracy under internal cross-validation without an AUC or a delta with confidence interval; P-1214 (180 ADNI MCI, baseline and 2-year AV-45 PET and MRI, AUC 0.891 baseline versus 0.898 at 2 years) is the third baseline-versus-serial comparison, at one fixed interval. The one paper that does issue a schedule recommends 'follow-up MRI 1 year after identification for high-risk individuals' from an incremental-discrimination estimate whose IDI interval includes zero (IDI 0.090, 95% CI -0.062 to 0.170) although its NRI does not (0.246, 95% CI 0.021-0.848) and then lists 'optimal MRI timing' among its own open problems (P-945). Every other structural conversion marker in this pack is computed from a baseline scan alone and asks for the serial analysis in its future-work field (P-993 'Serial MRI covariance analysis'; P-1066 'longitudinal within-subject atrophy rates'; P-1101 'longitudinal volumetric follow-up'), even though P-993, P-1066, P-1101 and P-1128 all draw on ADNI, which acquires serial MRI on these same participants. The interval is therefore unasked, not unanswerable, and it is the one parameter a re-imaging protocol must actually set. WHY IT MATTERS: discrimination from a baseline scan does not determine when, or whether, to scan again; the only schedule currently in circulation in this corpus rests on a null increment. CLOSURE TEST: in one MCI cohort holding >= 3 scans per participant in a single modality (ADNI structural MRI would suffice), fit a baseline-only prognostic model and then models adding the change measured at 6, 12, 24 and 48 months, and report delta-C-index (or delta-AUC) with confidence intervals as a function of the inter-scan interval, on a held-out or external cohort with N >= 200 MCI and >= 60 converters.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches two gold patterns at once: the clinical-utility pattern (NEW-G-27 / G-09 - a quantity is proven to discriminate while the decision it is supposed to inform is never evaluated) and the data-structure pattern (the gold 'interval-censored visits forced into binary labels' critique), but applied to the predictor's acquisition cadence rather than the outcome label. It is non-obvious because the corpus already contains BOTH answers to the baseline-versus-serial question and they point opposite ways: the natural reading is a modality conflict, but the two designs also differ in interval, outcome and population, so what the corpus actually lacks is the one design that would separate them. The absence is also demonstrably a choice rather than a data limit: four of the seven cited papers run on ADNI, which acquires serial MRI on the same participants they analyse at baseline only.
gaps.closure_criteria: In one MCI cohort holding >= 3 scans per participant in a single modality (ADNI structural MRI would suffice), fit a baseline-only prognostic model and then models adding the change measured at 6, 12, 24 and 48 months, and report delta-C-index (or delta-AUC) with confidence intervals as a function of the inter-scan interval, on a held-out or external cohort with N >= 200 MCI and >= 60 converters.

It is non-obvious because the corpus already contains BOTH answers to the baseline-versus-serial question and they point opposite ways: the natural reading is a modality conflict, but the two designs also differ in interval, outcome and population, so what the corpus actually lacks is the one design that would separate them. The absence is also demonstrably a choice rather than a data limit: four of the seven cited papers run on ADNI, which acquires serial MRI on the same participants they analyse at baseline only.
gaps.critic_falsification: EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE is the strongest objection. The ADNI methods literature outside this corpus contains work comparing longitudinal against cross-sectional MRI features for pMCI/sMCI classification, and trial-design work on how the measurement interval affects detectable atrophy rates; a reviewer with external search may find that delta-performance-versus-interval has been estimated for structural MRI, in which case this record shrinks to amyloid PET and WMH and should be re-scoped rather than accepted whole. A second, smaller objection: P-974 is flagged in its card for overclaim, so its 'serial adds nothing' leg is an underpowered non-answer (17 converters, ROC point estimates 65.2% serial versus 59.6% baseline, ns) and must never be recorded as evidence that serial amyloid imaging is uninformative - only that the question was asked once, badly powered.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no modality pairing is proposed. The missing object is a scalar function (delta-C-index versus inter-scan interval) within a single modality.

DATA_SCARCITY: the data exist and are already in the cited papers' own hands - ADNI holds serial structural MRI for P-993/P-1066/P-1101/P-1128, SPRINT MIND holds two scans for P-967, and P-974 already acquired serial PET.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: checked explicitly against this record's own citations. P-974 and P-967 DO test baseline versus change, and the record states so rather than denying it; the absence clause is narrowed to varying the INTERVAL, which P-974 fixes at ~24 months and P-967 at 48 months, and which no cited paper varies.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper's own block carries the construct's vocabulary - serial PET, follow-up MRI, more frequent MRI, optimal MRI timing, serial MRI covariance analysis, longitudinal volumetric follow-up, longitudinal within-subject atrophy rates.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: the two quotes taken from significance/importance fields (P-974's protocol-simplification claim) are tagged as such in the evidence entries and are used to establish that the field poses this as a protocol question, never as a measured result.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: the two partial closers are named and their limits stated - P-974 answers the question once for amyloid PET at one interval on 17 converters, P-967 answers it once for WMH at one interval on 33 events.
TOO_SPECIFIC: the record spans three imaging quantities (amyloid SUVR, WMH volume, structural volumetry/morphometry), seven papers and four cohorts (ADNI, SPRINT MIND, BABRI, a Korean memory clinic).
NOT_IN_SCOPE: MCI imaging prognosis is the corpus's core subject; the closure test is a re-analysis of existing corpus data, not a trial-design or drug question.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked against every existing gap whose text mentions serial / repeat / interval / timing / schedule (grep of existing_gaps.md and of T05_mri_pet_imaging_existing_gaps.md). ACTOR-G-071 is the nearest neighbour and is different: it says P-967's >=1.4 mL threshold has no external replication and no trial-endpoint validation - a replication gap about one threshold in one modality; this record is about the inter-scan interval as an unestimated design parameter across modalities, and cites P-967 for its interval, not its threshold. ACTOR-G-005 (single-timepoint omics, closed) is molecular, not imaging. ACTOR-G-034 is about test-retest reliability of a single measurement, i.e. whether one scan is stable, not whether a second scan adds prognostic information. G-21 / NEW-G-30 (interval-censored multi-visit data forced into binary labels) is about the time structure of the OUTCOME label; this is about the repeat interval of the PREDICTOR. G-13 and ACTOR-G-021 are incremental-value gaps over a different axis (which VARIABLES are added: amyloid PET over non-invasive markers; any marker over an age/sex/education base) and G-021 is explicitly scoped to the P-620..P-667 batch. G-07 and G-09 are health-economic and prospective-trial gaps about acting on an AI flag, not about imaging cadence. G-14 concerns calibration under domain shift. G-CAND-44 is a rejected single-paper limitation asking for serial MRA in a vascular study.

gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: Repeat imaging is the recurring cost of MCI monitoring, yet no corpus study estimates the prognostic increment of a SECOND scan as a function of the inter-scan interval. The two studies that pit a baseline scan against serial change each fix one interval and reach opposite conclusions in different modalities: amyloid PET change over a mean 24 months adds nothing over baseline (HR 0.2, 95% CI 0.02-1.18, p=0.07; P-974, n=75, 17 converters) while WMH change over a single fixed 48-month interval predicts incident dementia/MCI (OR 1.51, 95% CI 1.12-2.04, p=0.007; P-967, n=433, 33 events). Modality, interval, outcome and setting move together across those two designs, so neither can set a monitoring schedule, and no design varies the interval while holding the modality fixed. The one paper that does issue a schedule recommends 'follow-up MRI 1 year after identification for high-risk individuals' from an incremental-discrimination estimate whose interval includes zero (IDI 0.090, 95% CI -0.062 to 0.170) and then lists 'optimal MRI timing' among its own open problems (P-945). Every other structural conversion marker in this pack is computed from a baseline scan alone and asks for the serial analysis in its future-work field (P-993 'Serial MRI covariance analysis'; P-1066 'longitudinal within-subject atrophy rates'; P-1101 'longitudinal volumetric follow-up'), even though P-993, P-1066, P-1101 and P-1128 all draw on ADNI, which acquires serial MRI on these same participants. The interval is therefore unasked, not unanswerable, and it is the one parameter a re-imaging protocol must actually set. WHY IT MATTERS: discrimination from a baseline scan does not determine when, or whether, to scan again; the only schedule currently in circulation in this corpus rests on a null increment. CLOSURE TEST: in one MCI cohort holding >= 3 scans per participant in a single modality (ADNI structural MRI would suffice), fit a baseline-only prognostic model and then models adding the change measured at 6, 12, 24 and 48 months, and report delta-C-index (or delta-AUC) with confidence intervals as a function of the inter-scan interval, on a held-out or external cohort with N >= 200 MCI and >= 60 converters.

gaps.gap_statement: Structural-MRI prognosis in MCI is being refined at ever finer anatomical scale - whole hippocampus -> hippocampal subfields -> amygdala nuclei -> thalamic nuclei - and at each rung the new marker's discrimination is reported while the coarser measure it is claimed to beat carries NO discrimination statistic in the same sample, so the organising claim that fine-grained metrics 'carry conversion signal beyond global hippocampal volume' has never been quantified as a delta. The papers name the missing comparator as their open problem rather than supplying it: P-1101 reports the nucleus reuniens at sensitivity 0.73 / specificity 0.69 and then asks 'does reuniens atrophy add predictive value beyond hippocampus for MCI conversion?'; P-1066 segments hippocampus and whole cortical thickness only 'as spatial-specificity controls', reports no accuracy figure for any arm, and leaves 'whether amygdala subfield atrophy predicts conversion preclinically with acceptable accuracy' open; P-1079 reports subiculum plus amygdala nuclei at sensitivity 0.78 / specificity 0.62 and states the 'beyond global hippocampal volume' claim only in its significance field, with no whole-hippocampus discrimination figure anywhere in its block. What makes the missing delta consequential is that the BASE of the ladder is itself unsafe. In the two corpus studies that did measure a whole-structure MRI increment against a cheap comparator already collected at the same visit, the increment vanished: hippocampal and whole-brain volume lost their conversion association after adjustment for a bedside cognitive score (P-1097, n=156 memory clinic, 'neither remained significantly associated with conversion after adjusting for MMSE-NR'), and adding three MRI measurements to clinical change rates gave IDI 0.090 with 95% CI -0.062 to 0.170 while the same paper's NRI was 0.246 (95% CI 0.021-0.848) (P-945, ADNI). The corpus is therefore stacking unmeasured increments on a base whose own increment is indistinguishable from zero, and the resulting sensitivity/specificity pairs (0.73/0.69, 0.78/0.62) are read as evidence for a finer-is-better trajectory that no reported number supports. WHY IT MATTERS: the clinical proposition of every subregion marker is 'measure this instead of, or on top of, what you already have', and the only two corpus tests of that proposition at the whole-structure level each failed on one metric (an adjusted association in P-1097; the IDI but not the NRI in P-945). CLOSURE TEST: in one MCI cohort with baseline structural MRI and a baseline cognitive score, fit nested prognostic models - (1) demographics plus the cognitive score, (2) + whole-hippocampal volume, (3) + subfield / nucleus volumes selected under nested cross-validation - and report delta-AUC or delta-C-index with confidence intervals at each rung on a held-out or external cohort, N >= 200 MCI with >= 60 converters.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold 'ground-truth / comparator assumption' pattern (the peripheral-versus-central and Petersen-criteria golds), not a combinatorial one: it attacks what the field measures ITSELF against, and it does so with the papers' own open-problem fields as the evidence of absence. It is non-obvious because the individual papers all look methodologically careful - FDR correction, spatial-specificity controls, ROC analysis - and because the natural reading of the pack is a progress narrative (finer anatomy, better markers). The ladder framing is what makes it bite: the base rung has been measured twice in this corpus and failed on one metric each time, so every rung above it is an unquantified increment on a null.
gaps.closure_criteria: In one MCI cohort with baseline structural MRI and a baseline cognitive score, fit nested prognostic models - (1) demographics plus the cognitive score, (2) + whole-hippocampal volume, (3) + subfield / nucleus volumes selected under nested cross-validation - and report delta-AUC or delta-C-index with confidence intervals at each rung on a held-out or external cohort, N >= 200 MCI with >= 60 converters.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold 'ground-truth / comparator assumption' pattern (the peripheral-versus-central and Petersen-criteria golds), not a combinatorial one: it attacks what the field measures ITSELF against, and it does so with the papers' own open-problem fields as the evidence of absence. It is non-obvious because the individual papers all look methodologically careful - FDR correction, spatial-specificity controls, ROC analysis - and because the natural reading of the pack is a progress narrative (finer anatomy, better markers). The ladder framing is what makes it bite: the base rung has been measured twice in this corpus and failed on one metric each time, so every rung above it is an unquantified increment on a null.
gaps.critic_falsification: VF-24 is a confirmed corpus record with 8 supporters asserting that fine-grained morphometric descriptors outperform whole-structure volumetry. Some of those supporters lie outside this pack and were not read here; if any of them reports the same-sample head-to-head discrimination this record says is missing, the absence collapses to a three-paper, single-consortium observation (P-1066, P-1079, P-1101 are all ADNI and are declared non-independent), which is a limitation aggregation rather than a corpus gap. A verifier must read VF-24's supporter list before accepting the ladder framing, and should be prepared to re-scope this to 'the frontier subcortical-nucleus papers' rather than to structural MRI generally. A second objection: P-1097's null is an association test after covariate adjustment, not a delta-AUC, so calling it a failed increment is an interpretation of a regression coefficient, and P-945's IDI is measured only within an already-enriched high-risk stratum.
fp_codes_cleared: UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: checked against this record's own citations before writing. P-1066 DOES measure the hippocampus (as a control) and P-993 DOES benchmark against hippocampal volume; both are stated in the record. The absence clause is therefore narrowed from 'never measures the comparator' to 'never reports a DISCRIMINATION statistic for the comparator in the same sample where the fine-grained marker's discrimination is reported', which holds for P-1066 (no accuracy for any arm), P-1079 and P-1101, and is conceded as open by P-1101, P-1066 and P-1097.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: the one quote from an interpretive field (P-1079's significance-field 'beyond global hippocampal volume') is explicitly tagged as an author assertion in its evidence entry, and the record's point is precisely that it is an assertion with no result behind it.
COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no modality or method pairing is proposed; the missing object is a nested-model delta within one modality.
DATA_SCARCITY: the comparator volume is already produced by the same segmentation run in all three subregion papers (P-1066 states it explicitly), so the delta is computable from data in hand.
FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: P-993 is named as the partial closer with exactly what it leaves open, and P-945/P-1097 are named as the base-rung measurements that exist and are negative.

MISASSIGNED_MEASUREMENT_FAMILY: no cross-family contrast is asserted. Every quantity on both arms is a T1-derived structural volume; the contrast is coarse-versus-fine within one measurement family, and the cognitive-score comparator is named as such.
TOO_SPECIFIC: four anatomical levels, six papers, three cohorts (ADNI, Oslo memory clinic, BABRI), and the record targets a confirmed corpus VF rather than a single paper's limitation.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked against VF-24, ACTOR-G-035, ACTOR-G-021, G-13, G-03, IA-72/KA-11 and IA-21/IA-38. VF-24 is the confirmed corpus finding that fine-grained morphometric descriptors outperform coarse whole-structure volumetry; this record does not restate it, it asks where the delta behind it is in the frontier half of the corpus. ACTOR-G-035 targets the same VF-24 claim but by a different mechanism - it asks whether the fine-grained advantage is scanner variance (ComBat-on-vs-off ablation); this asks whether the advantage was ever measured against the coarse arm at all. The two are complements, not duplicates, and should be cross-linked. ACTOR-G-021 is an incremental-discrimination gap whose comparator is an age/sex/education base model and whose scope is stated as the P-620..P-667 batch; here the comparator is a coarser IMAGING measure and a bedside cognitive score, and the papers are P-936..P-1130. G-13 is amyloid PET versus non-invasive markers - a different modality pair. G-03 concerns selective reporting of the best-performing ML CONFIGURATION in ADNI conversion pipelines; these are classical MANOVA / stepwise-LDA neuroanatomy papers and the unreported quantity is an anatomical comparator, not a model config. IA-72 (rejected) and KA-11 concern hippocampal TEXTURE versus volume, not subregion volumetry. Grep of existing_gaps.md for subfield / amygdala / thalam / reuniens / beyond / incremental returned nothing making this claim.

gaps.gap_statement: MCI progression is estimated in this corpus on whoever came back, in a population where death is the more frequent event, and nothing decomposes the resulting spread. In the one cited cohort that models death as a competing event, deaths outnumber the outcome nearly three to one across the whole cohort of 3,025 (of whom 132 had MCI) - 'Over mean 3.9 years, 71 developed dementia and 200 died' - and its subdistribution-hazard estimate of five-year cumulative dementia incidence in MCI is 13.3% (5.8-20.8%) (P-958, Rotterdam, N=3025). The clinic cohorts that supply the corpus's real-world progression numbers instead define the analysed sample by completed visits and report far higher progression: P-1073 analyses 140 MCI 'drawn from 3,547 cases, followed up to 203 months with >= 3 visits' and reports 92.8% progression (15.7% per year); P-964 reports an 18.4% one-year conversion rate from a design requiring 'baseline and follow-up cognitive assessments (MMSE, MoCA)'; P-1124 fits its conversion classifier (Random Forest AUC 0.7347) on 356 analysed participants out of '500 MCI participants consecutively enrolled in 19 Italian CDCDs'. That spread confounds horizon, setting AND analysis-sample construction - minimum-visit inclusion rules, competing death, differential loss - and no corpus study separates them, either by reporting the same cohort under complete-case, cause-specific and subdistribution-hazard analyses, or by characterising the participants its inclusion rule removed. On the model side the same conditioning is invisible: none of the pack's conversion classifiers is developed or evaluated under attrition weighting or with death as a competing event. WHY IT MATTERS: these rates are the prior a clinician quotes to a newly diagnosed patient and the prevalence a risk model is implicitly calibrated to, and a triage tool fitted and validated on returners is fitted and validated on exactly the patients least likely to die or disengage first - the ones who need triage least. CLOSURE TEST: in one MCI cohort with linked mortality and complete visit records, report (a) five-year progression under a naive complete-case estimator, a cause-specific Cox model and a Fine-Gray subdistribution model side by side, and (b) the conversion model's C-index refit under inverse-probability-of-attendance weighting versus complete case, with a baseline characteristics table for the excluded participants.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold 'ground-truth and data-structure' patterns: it challenges the construction of the sample that every downstream number rests on, and it names a concrete decomposable quantity rather than asking for more studies. It is non-obvious because each paper individually looks reasonable - a >= 3-visit rule is defensible for trajectory modelling, a retrospective design needs a follow-up assessment - and because the corpus already contains the corrective method (P-958's subdistribution hazards) without anyone noticing that it also produces the outlying low estimate. The model-side clause is the actionable half: it is a re-analysis of data already collected, not a new cohort.
gaps.closure_criteria: In one MCI cohort with linked mortality and complete visit records, report (a) five-year progression under a naive complete-case estimator, a cause-specific Cox model and a Fine-Gray subdistribution model side by side, and (b) the conversion model's C-index refit under inverse-probability-of-attendance weighting versus complete case, with a baseline characteristics table for the excluded participants.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold 'ground-truth and data-structure' patterns: it challenges the construction of the sample that every downstream number rests on, and it names a concrete decomposable quantity rather than asking for more studies. It is non-obvious because each paper individually looks reasonable - a >= 3-visit rule is defensible for trajectory modelling, a retrospective design needs a follow-up assessment - and because the corpus already contains the corrective method (P-958's subdistribution hazards) without anyone noticing that it also produces the outlying low estimate. The model-side clause is the actionable half: it is a re-analysis of data already collected, not a new cohort.
gaps.critic_falsification: The completer-conditioning of P-1073, P-964 and P-1124 is read from what their own method and sample fields say they INCLUDED; it is not proof that the published papers report no attrition analysis, and this corpus has a documented failure mode (extract absence mistaken for paper absence) of exactly this shape. The record must therefore be stated as an absence in the CORPUS RECORD, and a verifier should open at least P-1124's paper for a flow diagram before the record is accepted. The second objection is EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: competing-risk handling of dementia incidence is standard epidemiological practice outside this corpus, so the descriptive half may be judged a sampling artefact of the corpus. What survives that objection is the narrower model-side clause - that MCI conversion CLASSIFIERS are neither developed nor evaluated under attrition weighting - and the record should be re-scoped to that clause rather than rejected whole.
fp_codes_cleared: DATA_SCARCITY: deaths and non-attendance are recorded in every one of these cohorts, and P-958 demonstrates the corrective analysis inside this corpus, so the decomposition is doable with existing data.
COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no combination of modalities or methods is proposed; the missing object is a sensitivity analysis and a decomposition of an observed spread.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: checked against this record's own citations. P-958 DOES model the competing risk and the record says so and uses it as the anchor; the absence clause is the DECOMPOSITION across designs and the model-side attrition weighting, not the existence of competing-risk methods in the corpus.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: MCI prognosis estimation and conversion modelling are the corpus's core subject matter.

TOO_SPECIFIC: four cohorts on three continents, spanning population, tertiary-hospital, single-clinic and national multicentre designs, and touching both the descriptive rate and the fitted classifier.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every quote comes from a method, sample-size or results field of the paper it is attributed to, and each names the construct at issue (visit-count inclusion rule, enrolled versus analysed counts, deaths, subdistribution hazards).
gaps.dedup_note: Grep of existing_gaps.md and of T05_mri_pet_imaging_existing_gaps.md for attrition, dropout, loss to follow-up, competing risk, conversion rate, progression rate and incidence returned no record making this claim. ACTOR-G-067 is the nearest neighbour and concerns REVERSION rates (7-48% across community cohorts) and the lack of a harmonised pooled reversion estimate - a different transition and a definition-harmonisation argument, not a competing-risk or selection argument. ACTOR-G-075 concerns practice-effect adjustment, a measurement-artefact correction rather than a selection one. G-14 concerns calibration under domain shift, which is about transporting a fitted model, not about how its development sample was assembled. G-CAND-286 is a rejected single-paper limitation noting one cohort's unusually high 54.8% two-year conversion rate without generalising. NEW-G-30 / G-21 concern forcing interval-censored visits into binary labels; that is about the time structure of the label, whereas this is about who enters the denominator at all.
