gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: MCI progression is estimated in this corpus on whoever came back, in a population where death is the more frequent event, and nothing decomposes the resulting spread. In the one cited cohort that models death as a competing event, deaths outnumber the outcome nearly three to one - 'Over mean 3.9 years, 71 developed dementia and 200 died' - and its subdistribution-hazard estimate of five-year cumulative dementia incidence in MCI is 13.3% (5.8-20.8%) (P-958, Rotterdam, N=3025). The clinic cohorts that supply the corpus's real-world progression numbers instead define the analysed sample by completed visits and report far higher progression: P-1073 analyses 140 MCI 'drawn from 3,547 cases, followed up to 203 months with >= 3 visits' and reports 92.8% progression (15.7% per year); P-964 reports an 18.4% one-year conversion rate from a design requiring 'baseline and follow-up cognitive assessments (MMSE, MoCA)'; P-1124 fits its conversion classifier (Random Forest AUC 0.7347) on 356 analysed participants out of '500 MCI participants consecutively enrolled in 19 Italian CDCDs'. That spread confounds horizon, setting AND analysis-sample construction - minimum-visit inclusion rules, competing death, differential loss - and no corpus study separates them, either by reporting the same cohort under complete-case, cause-specific and subdistribution-hazard analyses, or by characterising the participants its inclusion rule removed. On the model side the same conditioning is invisible: none of the pack's conversion classifiers is developed or evaluated under attrition weighting or with death as a competing event. WHY IT MATTERS: these rates are the prior a clinician quotes to a newly diagnosed patient and the prevalence a risk model is implicitly calibrated to, and a triage tool fitted and validated on returners is fitted and validated on exactly the patients least likely to die or disengage first - the ones who need triage least. CLOSURE TEST: in one MCI cohort with linked mortality and complete visit records, report (a) five-year progression under a naive complete-case estimator, a cause-specific Cox model and a Fine-Gray subdistribution model side by side, and (b) the conversion model's C-index refit under inverse-probability-of-attendance weighting versus complete case, with a baseline characteristics table for the excluded participants.

gaps.gap_statement: GAP (outcome-label validity, MRI/PET MCI prognosis). Every MCI-to-AD prognostic model in this pack is scored against an endpoint that names an aetiology it never verifies, and the resulting misclassification is DIRECTIONAL rather than random. The endpoint is assigned on clinical severity alone - P-1214 defines it as 'conversion defined as first CDR > 1' - while the corpus's own papers record that Lewy-type co-pathology is present in 30-50% of AD patients (P-1210) and that a CSF Lewy-type aggregate marker independently predicts that same conversion endpoint (Syn1, HR 2.890) inside ADNI, and that at the MCI stage cognitive scoring cannot separate the DLB-bound from the AD-bound trajectory while PRESERVED hippocampal volume marks DLB rather than AD risk (P-1181). The leading risk indices carry hippocampal volume with the OPPOSITE sign - P-1226's index is literally 'a new parameter Cog_Vol = hippocampal volume/ADAS13 score ratio' - so a DLB-bound converter is routed by construction into the low-risk stratum, which is exactly where P-1226 records converters it cannot explain ('conversions in low-risk Cog_Vol >= 340 subjects with negative PET amyloid may represent misdiagnosis'; limitation field: 'unknown pathology of low-risk converters'). No study in this pack reports stratum risks or discrimination separately for aetiologically adjudicated converters, so the published false-negative rate of hippocampus-weighted MCI risk indices cannot be separated from a second disease travelling in the opposite direction on the index's own dominant feature; and the blind spot propagates into the value case, since P-1171's health-economic evaluation of exactly this tool class concedes 'no distinction between dementia aetiologies' and lists 'aetiology-stratified dementia modelling' as future work. CRITICAL SCOPE NOTE: adding amyloid/tau confirmation - the adjudication asked for by existing gaps ACTOR-G-079, ACTOR-G-082 and G-NEW-1047-A - does NOT close this gap, because Lewy co-pathology coexists with AD pathology (P-1210's 30-50% figure is for AD patients), so an amyloid-positive converter may still be on the DLB trajectory. What is absent is adjudication of the ALTERNATIVE aetiology at the outcome. Absence asserted for this pack; no claim is made about the external literature.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'Prognostic models treat central nervous system markers as absolute ground truth' and 'no consensus on whether current MCI diagnostic criteria are compatible with computational biomarker-driven models': it attacks the ground-truth standard rather than adding a missing modality. Non-obvious because the contamination is not a random labelling error but is anti-correlated with the model's own feature - the patients the index calls SAFEST are the ones most likely to be on the other trajectory - which means the usual remedy (bigger N, external cohort, amyloid confirmation) cannot fix it. All three legs are separately verifiable in the pack's own digests and one of them (P-1210's alphaS-SAA in ADNI) shows the adjudication data partly already exist.
gaps.closure_criteria: In a cohort with aetiological adjudication AT THE OUTCOME - CSF or skin alpha-synuclein seed amplification, DAT-SPECT/MIBG, or autopsy - of >=300 MCI patients followed >=4 years, apply one published hippocampus-weighted MCI risk index (e.g. Cog_Vol, or ADAS13 >= 24 with left hippocampal volume < 2715) and report: (a) stratum-specific conversion rates and discrimination computed separately for AD-track and Lewy-track converters; (b) the proportion of the LOW-risk stratum's converters that are Lewy-track; and (c) the change in the index's sensitivity when Lewy-track converters are removed from the positive class. ADNI already holds alphaS-SAA/PMCA data on a subset (used by P-1210), so a first pass is doable on existing data.
gaps.modality: MRI/PET (structural MRI hippocampal volumetry + amyloid PET) with CSF adjudication
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern 'Prognostic models treat central nervous system markers as absolute ground truth' and 'no consensus on whether current MCI diagnostic criteria are compatible with computational biomarker-driven models': it attacks the ground-truth standard rather than adding a missing modality. Non-obvious because the contamination is not a random labelling error but is anti-correlated with the model's own feature - the patients the index calls SAFEST are the ones most likely to be on the other trajectory - which means the usual remedy (bigger N, external cohort, amyloid confirmation) cannot fix it. All three legs are separately verifiable in the pack's own digests and one of them (P-1210's alphaS-SAA in ADNI) shows the adjudication data partly already exist.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: clinicopathological series (NACC/autopsy) already quantify the accuracy of clinical AD diagnosis, and the prognostic effect of Lewy co-pathology in AD is an active external field, so a reviewer could rule that the corpus absence is a sampling artefact. My defence is that the record's specific unmet analysis is narrower than 'is clinical AD diagnosis accurate' - it is the attribution of a PUBLISHED MCI risk index's stratum risks and false negatives to alternative-aetiology misclassification, using that index's own hippocampal term as the mechanism - but I have not verified that no such re-analysis exists outside the corpus, and that verification would decide the record. A second, independent weakness: the directional half of the mechanism rests entirely on P-1181, a 2021 conference-abstract narrative review of 17 articles whose own limitation field says 'differentiation accuracy not established as a test metric' and which reports no effect size for the preserved-hippocampus-to-DLB association; if that association is weak or confined to non-amnestic MCI (as P-1181 itself hints), the contamination of the low-risk stratum could be numerically trivial. Third: three of the five papers (P-1210, P-1214, P-1226) are ADNI, so 'every model in this pack' is substantially one cohort.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no 'combine X with Y' clause. The record is a validity claim about the outcome label with a stated directional mechanism; the closure test is a re-analysis of an existing index, not a new modality pairing.

RESTATEMENT: five neighbouring records checked by id above; each is either baseline-ascertainment, follow-up-window, or amyloid/tau confirmation. None concerns alternative-aetiology adjudication of the converter class or the hippocampal sign inversion.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: the two pack papers that touch the question are credited in papers_potentially_closing_gap and both leave the quantitative half open (P-1181 has no metric; P-1210 stratifies exposure, not outcome).
TOO_SPECIFIC: not narrow - it applies to every hippocampus-weighted MCI risk index and to the health-economic case built on them.
DATA_SCARCITY: no - alphaS-SAA/PMCA data already exist in ADNI (P-1210 used them) and DAT-SPECT/MIBG are routine, so the closure study is doable with existing infrastructure.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: within corpus scope (MCI prognostic modelling and its endpoint).

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper's OWN vocabulary carries the construct - P-1210 says alpha-synuclein and conversion to AD, P-1181 says DLB and hippocampal volume, P-1226 says misdiagnosis and unknown pathology, P-1171 says dementia aetiologies. No inferential bridge is needed to connect any paper to the gap's construct.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: the source field is tagged on every quote. P-1210's '30-50%' sits in a background/motivation field and P-1181's two quotes sit in the Results field of a NARRATIVE review with no effect size - all three are labelled as synthesis/background claims in the evidence entries and are not presented as measured head-to-head findings. The only measured statistics cited are P-1210's HR 2.890 (p=0.040) and P-1214's endpoint definition.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the absence clause ('no study reports stratum risks or discrimination separately for aetiologically adjudicated converters') was checked against the record's own five papers. P-1210 is the only near miss and it stratifies the exposure while keeping the unadjudicated clinical endpoint - stated explicitly in papers_potentially_closing_gap rather than left for a reviewer to find.
MISASSIGNED_MEASUREMENT_FAMILY: no cross-family contrast is asserted. The single measurement quantity in the mechanism is hippocampal volume, read by both arms of the argument.

gaps.gap_statement: GAP (operating-point transportability, MRI/PET MCI risk stratification). The quantity these papers hand to a memory clinic is an ABSOLUTE conversion risk read off a numeric cut-point - 'Cog_Vol < 101 predicted 94.1% conversion to AD within the first two years in subjects with elevated PET beta-amyloid', 'Cog_Vol >= 340 predicted essentially zero conversion (0/42 elevated-amyloid; 3.2% in all MCI)' (P-1226) - and in every case in this pack the cut-point was selected by optimisation on the same sample in which its risk is then reported: P-1226 uses 'quartile-based cut-offs' derived in ADNI while describing itself as a validation ('this study adjusted cut-offs and validated the approach in ADNI'), P-1214 uses 'ROC with Youden's J optimal cut-offs' in its own 180 patients, P-1210 uses 'ROC-determined cutoffs (Youden's index) for alpha-syn and alpha-syn/tau ratios' in its own 250, and P-1154 emits 'proposed FDG z-score thresholds for a pathway-specific decision framework' that it concedes are 'pathway thresholds not yet externally validated'. Absolute risk is the LEAST transportable output a model can produce - it moves with both the optimisation optimism in the cut-point and the base rate of the cohort, and P-1226's base rate is a research-cohort one ('273 (32.3%) progressed to AD over a mean 2.76 years') - yet no study in this pack ever freezes a published cut-point and reports the risk it actually delivers in a cohort not used to choose it. The papers that DO validate externally validate a different quantity: P-1153's three-cohort design reports discrimination deltas, not a rule ('improved prediction significantly in ADNI-MCI (iAUC 0.768 to 0.787, Delta 0.020 [0.007-0.034]) and nominally in J-ADNI-MCI (0.020) and HABS-NC (0.059)'). Why this is not a reporting nicety: P-1171's health-economic model of exactly this tool class finds current practice dominates risk prediction, 'driven by the disutility of receiving a high-risk prediction', and that 'With a restricted 8%-eligible lecanemab scenario or 80% prediction accuracy, prediction was generally not cost-effective' - so the unmeasured optimism between an in-sample-tuned operating point and a real one is the difference between a deployable tool and a net-harmful one. Absence asserted for this pack; no claim is made about the external literature.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern of a calibration/transfer failure that separates a proven statistic from the number actually used in the clinic - the same shape as the gold 'discrimination proven, decision impact never tested' gap, but one step earlier: here even the discrimination-to-decision translation is unmeasured. Non-obvious because four of these papers are otherwise methodologically careful (competing-risks modelling, bootstrap, FDR correction, an external cohort) and the failure is invisible to every check they do run - AUC is threshold-free, so an externally validated AUC certifies nothing about the cut-point printed in the abstract. The link to P-1171 is what makes it consequential rather than pedantic: the same pack contains a formal demonstration that the value of the whole tool class inverts on exactly this operating characteristic.
gaps.closure_criteria: Take one published MCI risk-stratification rule with its cut-points frozen exactly as printed (e.g. Cog_Vol < 101 / >= 340, or 'ADAS13 >= 24 and left hippocampal volume < 2715'), apply it unchanged to a consecutive memory-clinic cohort of >=300 MCI patients with >=3 years follow-up and a documented cohort conversion rate, and report (a) the observed conversion proportion with 95% CI in each stratum next to the derivation-cohort figure, and (b) the same numbers after re-optimising the cut-points in the new cohort - so the optimism component and the base-rate component are separated rather than confounded. Registering the hippocampal-volume cut-point together with the segmentation software version is required for (a) to be reproducible.
gaps.gap_type: operating_point_transportability (in-sample cut-point optimism + base-rate dependence of absolute risk)
gaps.modality: MRI/PET (hippocampal volumetry, amyloid PET, FDG-PET) and CSF
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern of a calibration/transfer failure that separates a proven statistic from the number actually used in the clinic - the same shape as the gold 'discrimination proven, decision impact never tested' gap, but one step earlier: here even the discrimination-to-decision translation is unmeasured. Non-obvious because four of these papers are otherwise methodologically careful (competing-risks modelling, bootstrap, FDR correction, an external cohort) and the failure is invisible to every check they do run - AUC is threshold-free, so an externally validated AUC certifies nothing about the cut-point printed in the abstract. The link to P-1171 is what makes it consequential rather than pedantic: the same pack contains a formal demonstration that the value of the whole tool class inverts on exactly this operating characteristic.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is that a reviewer merges this into G-14 as one 'thresholds and calibration do not transport' family - the two records share the diagnosis (everything reported is in-distribution) and differ only in which statistic is missing, and the operator may reasonably decide the corpus does not need both. A second real objection is EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE in a strong form: optimism correction of selected cut-points and locked-rule external validation are standard prediction-model methodology (TRIPOD requires the latter), so frozen-threshold validations of MCI risk rules may well exist outside this 1,262-paper sample, and I have not checked. Third, the record is partly an argument about reporting practice rather than an unanswered scientific question: a critic could say the fix is a journal checklist, not a study - my answer is that the closure test produces a number nobody currently has (the shrinkage of 94.1% in a real clinic), but that answer is contestable. Fourth, P-1210's Youden cut-offs are ancillary to its main Cox analysis rather than its headline deliverable, so it is the weakest of the four instances.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no 'combine X with Y' clause anywhere; the closure test re-uses an existing published rule.

RESTATEMENT: six neighbouring records checked by id in why_new, each separated on the quantity being validated (predicted-probability calibration, ECE, assay platform, discrimination spectrum, incremental discrimination, population template) versus this record's frozen-rule absolute stratum risk.
TOO_SPECIFIC: covers four threshold-publishing papers across three modalities (structural MRI + amyloid PET, CSF, FDG-PET) and a whole class of clinical rule, not one paper's limitation.
DATA_SCARCITY: no - consecutive memory-clinic MCI cohorts with 3-year follow-up are routine; the closure study needs no new measurement technology.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: within corpus scope (MCI prediction-model methodology). P-1171 is used only as the cost-of-error argument, not to import health-economics as the gap's subject.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the absence clause was checked against the record's own six papers before being written and was narrowed as a result - P-1154's bootstrap/Monte Carlo internal validation and P-1153's genuine two-cohort external validation are both stated in papers_potentially_closing_gap, and the clause is restricted to a FROZEN cut-point evaluated in data not used to select it, which none of the six does.
EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every quote comes from a paper whose own text names the construct - cut-offs, thresholds, Youden's index, conversion rate, prediction accuracy. No inferential bridge.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: source field is tagged on every quote, and P-1171's two quotes are explicitly marked model-derived (a decision-analytic simulation with, per its own limitation field, no probabilistic sensitivity analysis) rather than measured.
MISASSIGNED_MEASUREMENT_FAMILY: no cross-family contrast is asserted; all four instances are the same operation - choosing a cut-point by optimisation on the evaluation sample.

gaps.gap_statement: Every fall-risk operating point published for a mobility or balance measure in MCI in this corpus is calibrated against a SUBSTITUTE endpoint rather than against an observed fall. P-709's Four Square Step Test cut-off of 15.11 s (AUC 0.825) is fitted to falls the participant RECALLED over the preceding 12 months; P-1013's wearable postural-sway system, titled and framed as fall PREDICTION, is scored against Berg Balance Scale and Timed Up and Go performance rather than against any fall that occurred. The one study in the stratum that ascertained falls prospectively (P-695, monthly fall calendars with telephone prompting) built no classifier and ran no ROC analysis at all, and its null is under-powered by its own reported diagnostics. The absence matters for two reasons that are specific to MCI rather than generic. First, recall-based fall ascertainment is misclassified BY the memory deficit that defines the population, and the error is one-directional (under-reporting), so a cut-point fitted to recalled falls is displaced by an unquantified amount in a direction that cannot even be signed - the deriving paper's own appraisal says exactly this. Second, scoring a balance sensor against a balance test is circular: it establishes concurrent agreement with an existing clinical scale, not prediction of the event. Falls are the proximal harm that motivates mobility screening in cognitively impaired older adults, and thresholds from this literature are already being recommended for triage, yet no threshold here has been tested against a fall anyone observed, and no study has measured how far a recall-derived cut-point moves when the same cohort's falls are recorded prospectively.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'an endpoint everyone substitutes for the one that matters' and the gold ground-truth pattern (the peripheral-vs-central prodromal gap, which challenges what is treated as ground truth rather than naming a missing modality). It is non-obvious precisely because this stratum LOOKS validated: both P-709 and P-1013 print ROC-family statistics, so a reader scanning the registry sees fall-risk discrimination in MCI as an answered question. The defect is in the label, not the model, and it interacts with the disease under study - the outcome is ascertained by asking a memory-impaired person to remember. It also produces a closure test (compare recalled against prospectively recorded falls in the same cohort and report the cut-point displacement) that is cheap, specific, and has never been run.
gaps.closure_criteria: A prospective cohort of at least 200 community-dwelling adults with criterion-diagnosed (not screen-threshold) MCI, in which a mobility or balance measure (FSST, TUG, instrumented postural sway or gait) is captured at baseline and falls are ascertained by monthly calendars with telephone prompting over at least 12 months, reporting (a) AUC with 95 percent CI and a cut-point with sensitivity/specificity for at least one incident fall, derived and evaluated with internal-optimism correction, and (b) the SAME cohort's 12-month retrospectively recalled fall history analysed identically, so that the displacement between the recall-derived and the prospectively-derived cut-point is reported as a number. Part (b) is the clause that no study anywhere has supplied and is the part that is doable with data any such cohort will already hold.
gaps.modality: Behavioural/Digital (clinical balance and mobility tests; wearable inertial postural sway)
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern 'an endpoint everyone substitutes for the one that matters' and the gold ground-truth pattern (the peripheral-vs-central prodromal gap, which challenges what is treated as ground truth rather than naming a missing modality). It is non-obvious precisely because this stratum LOOKS validated: both P-709 and P-1013 print ROC-family statistics, so a reader scanning the registry sees fall-risk discrimination in MCI as an answered question. The defect is in the label, not the model, and it interacts with the disease under study - the outcome is ascertained by asking a memory-impaired person to remember. It also produces a closure test (compare recalled against prospectively recorded falls in the same cohort and report the cut-point displacement) that is cheap, specific, and has never been run.
gaps.critic_falsification: Prospective fall-prediction studies with fall-calendar ascertainment and ROC analysis exist in the wider geriatric-falls literature, including in cognitively impaired samples, so a reviewer could code the headline absence EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE and treat it as a sampling artefact of this 1,262-paper corpus. If that objection lands, the record should NOT be published as a corpus-wide absence; what survives it is the narrower clause, which I believe is unaddressed anywhere: no study in this literature has compared retrospectively recalled with prospectively recorded falls in the SAME MCI cohort to quantify how far the recall bias displaces the derived cut-point. The record should be downgraded to that clause rather than kept at full width if the external check finds prospective MCI falls-ROC work.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: this is not a combine-X-with-Y statement. It concerns the reference standard against which an existing measure is scored, not a missing pairing of modalities.

RESTATEMENT: zero of the 534 existing gap statements match 'fall'; the five nearest open records (G-030, G-017, G-033, G-040, G-09) were each checked and concern a different label or a different failure.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: P-695 is named in the record itself as the paper that partly addresses it (prospective calendars) and is stated to leave the discrimination estimate missing, so the record cannot be falsified by its own citations.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the absence clause is deliberately narrowed to the CO-OCCURRENCE of prospective ascertainment with a reported operating point, because P-695 (cited here) supplies the former and P-709/P-1013 (cited here) supply the latter.
TOO_SPECIFIC: four independent papers, three measurement families (stopwatch balance test, wearable inertial sway, optical motion capture), four countries.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: fall-risk discrimination within MCI is a registry task type (T4) already populated by these rows; this is inside corpus scope.

DATA_SCARCITY: the required data are not scarce - P-695 already ran monthly fall calendars with telephone prompting in exactly this population, so the closure study is a design choice, not a data limitation.
EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper's own text uses the construct vocabulary (falls, fallers, fall risk, fall prediction); no inferential bridge is made from a paper that does not discuss falls.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: each quote is tagged with the summary field it came from; the appraisal-field quotes are presented as concessions/absences, and the only results-field quote (P-1013's sensitivity range) is used only to establish that operating points exist, not as a measured finding supporting the gap.

MISASSIGNED_MEASUREMENT_FAMILY: no cross-family dichotomy is asserted; the contrast is between outcome ascertainment methods (recall vs clinical-scale surrogate vs prospective calendar), and each paper is assigned to the method its own text names.

gaps.gap_statement: Every motor or behavioural MCI marker in this frontier stratum that carries a discrimination figure or a proposed threshold was measured under OBSERVED, single-occasion, best-effort testing - six continuous laps of a pressure walkway (P-761), a 10 m straight and curve walk in front of a depth camera (P-1082), supervised Berg Balance Scale and Timed Up and Go trials (P-1013), a tablet task with an experimenter present (P-795) - while the deployment each paper proposes is unobserved capture at home or in the community. No study in the stratum measures the same marker in the same people under both conditions, so the shift in the marker's distribution, in its discrimination and in its operating threshold between the supervised protocol and free-living capture is unquantified. The one free-living study in the stratum cannot supply it: P-1100 monitored a consumer fitness tracker in daily life but on 20 people with AUC 1.0, which its own record grades as not credible without validation. This matters because the supervised protocol standardises away precisely what free-living capture would contain - self-selected pace, turns, obstacles, fatigue, competing task demands - and because being watched raises effort, so the clinic measurement and the home measurement are not the same quantity even when they carry the same parameter name. The entire cost argument for these markers is low-burden at-home screening, and there is no evidence that a clinic-derived cut-point survives the move to the setting it is intended for.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold hardware/vendor domain-shift pattern (NEW-G-24, OCT across vendors) and the brief's named category 'a calibration or transfer failure across language, education, device or setting', with setting as the axis. It is non-obvious because the papers do not read as laboratory studies: P-1013 is titled 'Ecological', P-1082 sells a low-cost camera as home-ready, P-795 sells a one-minute self-administrable test - the marketing language of each paper is free-living while its measurement is supervised, and the discrepancy only appears when the protocol section is read against the application section. The closure test is concrete and produces a single decision-relevant number: the sensitivity/specificity obtained when the clinic cut-point is applied unchanged to home data.
gaps.closure_criteria: One study measuring the same gait/motor marker set in the same MCI and cognitively-characterised control participants under both (a) the supervised in-clinic protocol and (b) at least 7 days of unsupervised free-living wear or in-home capture, with N of at least 100 per arm, reporting per parameter: the between-setting bias and limits of agreement; the AUC in each setting; and, decisively, the sensitivity and specificity obtained when the clinic-derived cut-point is applied unchanged to the free-living data, alongside the free-living-optimal cut-point, so the threshold displacement is reported as a number.
gaps.modality: Behavioural/Digital (instrumented gait, depth-camera gait, wearable inertial sensing, touchscreen motor task, consumer fitness tracker)
gaps.task_type: T1 (MCI detection) and T4 (within-MCI risk discrimination)
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold hardware/vendor domain-shift pattern (NEW-G-24, OCT across vendors) and the brief's named category 'a calibration or transfer failure across language, education, device or setting', with setting as the axis. It is non-obvious because the papers do not read as laboratory studies: P-1013 is titled 'Ecological', P-1082 sells a low-cost camera as home-ready, P-795 sells a one-minute self-administrable test - the marketing language of each paper is free-living while its measurement is supervised, and the discrepancy only appears when the protocol section is read against the application section. The closure test is concrete and produces a single decision-relevant number: the sensitivity/specificity obtained when the clinic cut-point is applied unchanged to home data.
gaps.critic_falsification: The laboratory-versus-real-world gait comparison is an established methodological literature outside this corpus - real-world walking speed is known to differ systematically from lab-measured speed - so a reviewer could code this EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE and argue that the transfer consequence is already predictable without a new study. The clause that survives that objection is narrower and is the one the record should be reduced to if the external check lands: no study has reported the MCI-DISCRIMINATION consequence of the setting change, i.e. the AUC and the sensitivity/specificity obtained when a clinic-derived MCI cut-point is applied unchanged to free-living capture. A second, weaker objection is that this stratum has so few papers reporting any cut-point at all that the gap could be recoded as an instance of the broader digital-marker deployment-evidence gap rather than standing alone.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no combine-X-with-Y clause; this concerns transferring one existing measure between two acquisition settings.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the record names P-1100 as the free-living study that exists inside the stratum and states why it cannot supply the estimate, and names P-1013 as the paper that moved the setting but kept supervision - so the absence clause is the co-occurrence of both settings in the same participants, not the non-existence of free-living data.

RESTATEMENT: checked against G-048, G-080, G-029, G-034, G-030, G-070 and the theme file; each concerns a different axis (administration mode, intervention endpoint, assay platform, repeatability, demographics, geography).
TOO_SPECIFIC: five papers, five countries, five instrument families.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: all five are in-corpus registry rows in T1/T4 with behavioural/digital modality.
DATA_SCARCITY: not a data limitation - wearable and camera capture in the home is cheap and P-1100 already did a month of it; the missing element is running both conditions in one cohort.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every quote comes from a paper that itself names either the supervised measurement condition or the home/community deployment target; no bridge is built from a paper silent on setting.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: quotes are tagged by field and are drawn from methods, limitations, improvement and application fields; no significance- or novelty-field assertion is presented as a measured result, and P-1100's AUC 1.0 is cited only as an uninterpretable number, never as a finding.
gaps.dedup_note: Grepped existing_gaps.md for free-living, home-based, ecological, laboratory, real-world, unsupervised, remote, in-clinic and naturalistic. The only live records returned are ACTOR-G-048 (no corpus study validates TELE-NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL assessment against an in-person gold standard - a remotely administered cognitive test, a different construct from passive free-living sensing) and ACTOR-G-080 (home-based digital cognitive-training practice-effect adjustment - an intervention endpoint). Also checked and distinguished: ACTOR-G-029 (analytical-PLATFORM domain shift for fluid-biomarker classifiers - same shape, different modality and a hardware/assay rather than a setting axis, and the corpus evidently accepts modality-specific instances of the domain-shift pattern, cf. gold NEW-G-24 for OCT vendors); ACTOR-G-034 (test-retest reliability of ML input features never reported - about repeatability within one setting, not transfer between settings); ACTOR-G-030 (demographic-confound control); ACTOR-G-070 (MCRS in low-resource settings - a population/geography axis); this theme's G-CAND-339/341 (auto-generated instrument recitations).

gaps.gap_statement: No pooled MCI cognitive-intervention or MCI-outcome estimate in this corpus has ever been shown to be expected to hold in a new setting. The syntheses report and conclude from the confidence interval, which describes only how precisely a mean has been located; the prediction interval, which is the statistic that says what a NEW trial or a NEW cohort should expect, is computed in only two corpus cognitive-outcome syntheses (a third, P-838, computes prediction intervals for exercise effects on depression in MCI, all crossing zero) and in BOTH of them it crosses zero into a substantial negative range while the same paper reports a large or moderate positive pooled effect. P-680 pools exercise versus control on global cognition at SMD 1.165 (95% CI 0.741 to 1.589) with a prediction interval of -0.747 to 3.077, and the authors 'compute the interval, and note its assumptions, but do not carry it into their conclusion'. P-698 pools aerobic exercise at SMD 0.76 with a prediction interval of -0.63 to 2.15. Where dispersion is most extreme the statistic is simply absent: P-711 pools MCI-to-normal-cognition reversion at 31 per cent over 48 studies with I2 = 98.9 per cent and study-level rates from 4.6 to 62.8 per cent, reports no prediction interval, and its 26-to-35-per-cent interval therefore 'describes the precision with which that mean has been located, not the range in which a new study's rate would fall'. This matters because these pooled means are exactly the quantities the field carries forward as established effects and as the base rate for three-state (convert / stay / revert) MCI models, and because the corpus's moderator meta-regressions on these pools (P-698 on session frequency; P-674 on delivery setting) report coefficients but no configuration-specific prediction interval, so no corpus study has asked which configurations land a new trial on the negative side of these intervals. A field that plans, powers and recommends from the confidence interval while its only two transportability estimates include harm is making a replication claim it has not tested.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'a calibration or transfer failure across ... setting' and the clinical-utility family (discrimination proven, transportability never tested), and it is the safest gap class the brief names: a methodological, within-paper gap doable with data already published (tau-squared and k are printed). Its non-obvious content is not that a statistic is missing but that where it exists it is NEGATIVE: two independent syntheses, both concluding a positive effect, both carry a prediction interval that includes harm. That inverts the corpus's reading of the exercise-in-MCI evidence from 'replicated positive effect' to 'a mean whose expected value in a new setting has never been shown to be positive'. It also identifies the exact statistic a downstream verified-finding record should be required to carry before an intervention effect is promoted.
gaps.closure_criteria: A synthesis or re-analysis of MCI cognitive-intervention trials (k >= 10, any modality) that reports, for its primary pooled cognitive estimate, tau-squared and the 95 per cent prediction interval alongside the confidence interval, AND a pre-specified meta-regression on study-level moderators (comparator class, diagnosis mix, session dose, blinding status, baseline severity) reporting the coefficient and interval for each, with the explicit statement of which moderator configurations predict a negative effect. It closes only if the prediction interval for at least one defined intervention-and-population configuration excludes the null. Separately for the reversion base rate: a re-pooling of the 48 studies in P-711 reporting a prediction interval for the reversion proportion and a meta-regression on the moderators already extracted (follow-up duration, number of assessment waves, diagnostic criterion, recruitment setting, baseline MMSE).
gaps.modality: Neuropsychological/Behavioural (global cognitive scales: MMSE, MoCA, composite cognitive scores) in intervention and outcome-prevalence syntheses

Its non-obvious content is not that a statistic is missing but that where it exists it is NEGATIVE: two independent syntheses, both concluding a positive effect, both carry a prediction interval that includes harm. That inverts the corpus's reading of the exercise-in-MCI evidence from 'replicated positive effect' to 'a mean whose expected value in a new setting has never been shown to be positive'. gaps.critic_falsification: P-680 and P-698 are not independent evidence at the level that matters here: both are meta-analyses of exercise interventions in MCI published within a year of each other and almost certainly pool an overlapping set of primary trials, so their two prediction intervals may be two views of the same dispersion rather than two replications of the finding. Neither digest declares the overlap and neither names the other, so the extent is unquantified. If the overlap is near-total, the record's strongest empirical clause reduces to a single underlying evidence base whose prediction interval crosses zero - still a real and unmined fact, but one supporting paper wide rather than two. A verifier should also weigh the softer objection that a prediction interval is conservative by construction when k is small (k = 20 contributing effect sizes in P-680, 11 trials in P-698), so an interval crossing zero is partly a small-k artefact; the answer is that this is precisely the quantity a reader needs and its width is the finding, but the objection is legitimate and the record should not be read as evidence that exercise does not work.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: checked clause by clause against the three cited papers. P-680 and P-698 DO compute prediction intervals - the record states this rather than denying it. P-698 DOES run moderator contrasts - the record does not claim no synthesis runs any moderator analysis; it claims none identifies the features that place a new trial on the negative side of its own prediction interval, which is true of both P-680 (no meta-regression at all) and P-698 (two pre-chosen dichotomies, both null, neither framed against the interval).
TOO_SPECIFIC: the statement spans three syntheses, two distinct estimand families (intervention effect size and outcome prevalence) and three intervention modalities.
DATA_SCARCITY: the opposite - all inputs are already published; the closure test is a re-analysis.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: the METHOD is standard and not claimed as novel; what is asserted absent is a transportability estimate for these MCI quantities, and the absence is documented by the papers' own text (P-711) rather than inferred from corpus sampling. The record does not claim nobody anywhere computes prediction intervals.
EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: each cited paper's own block uses the construct's vocabulary - 'prediction interval' occurs verbatim in all three digests.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: the quoted numbers (-0.747 to 3.077; -0.63 to 2.15; I2 98.9 per cent; 4.6 to 62.8 per cent) are results, not significance or novelty assertions; the two appraisal-field quotes are flagged with their field and are used only for the claim that the statistic was not carried into a conclusion, which is a statement about the paper's text.

gaps.gap_statement: Every comparative recommendation this corpus carries out of the MCI intervention and MCI-outcome synthesis literature - which exercise modality is best, whether longer stimulation is better, which recruitment setting reverts more - is read off separately pooled estimates inspected side by side, and the three named here have not been tested. P-680 concludes aerobic and resistance exercise beat multimodal from three separate pools whose intervals overlap heavily, with 'no formal between-subgroup test (a Q-between statistic, meta-regression or any direct comparison) ... reported anywhere in the paper'. P-705 attributes its residual 89-to-92-per-cent heterogeneity to differing stimulation frequency, site and duration and prints three duration-band estimates, but 'the explanation is asserted and never tested - no meta-regression is run'. P-711 reports community-based reversion at 36 per cent against hospital-based at 20 per cent, yet 'every comparative claim in the discussion, including the community-versus-hospital contrast on which the practical reading depends, rests on inspection of confidence intervals rather than on a tested effect'. Where between-group tests HAVE been run on these pools the record is mixed and does not reach the three claims above: P-698 ran three (intervention type p = 0.09, session time p = 0.24, weekly frequency Q(2) = 7.67, p = 0.02, the last correctly claimed) and P-674 tested facility-based against community-based delivery (Q(1) = 7.33, p < 0.01; meta-regression p = 0.007); P-698's aerobic-with-versus-without-cognitive-loading comparison gave Q(1) = 2.91, p = 0.09 and was claimed anyway. The absence matters for two reasons that a per-paper limitation note does not capture. First, an untested ranking read off overlapping intervals is not weaker evidence for a comparative claim, it is no evidence for one, so the corpus's head-to-head layer for this literature is populated with statements about how two author teams read intervals rather than about the world. Second, when two such rankings disagree - P-680 ranking aerobic and resistance above multimodal against P-684 finding multicomponent exercise strongest - the disagreement is manufactured by the missing test and must not be minted as a conflict about exercise.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: It is a within-paper, recomputable methodological gap of the class the brief prefers, and it carries a positive empirical payload rather than only a missing method: one tested contrast in this corpus failed (Q(1) = 2.91, p = 0.09) and was asserted anyway, while the tested contrasts that succeed (P-698 frequency; P-674 setting) are not the ones the three named claims rest on. Non-obvious because the affected claims do not look untested - they are printed as conclusions, highlights and clinical recommendations with confidence intervals attached, and each individual interval is genuinely significant against control; what is missing is the comparison, and the intervals overlap. It also has direct consequences for the corpus's own relational products: it identifies a class of apparent CONFLICT (P-680 versus P-684 on exercise modality) that is an artefact of the missing test rather than a disagreement about evidence, which is exactly the kind of record a gate is supposed to catch.
gaps.closure_criteria: A re-analysis of the already-published pools that reports, for each comparative claim currently in circulation in the MCI intervention and reversion literature (exercise modality; tDCS duration and stimulation site; recruitment setting and diagnostic criterion for reversion), a Q-between statistic or a meta-regression coefficient with its confidence interval, corrected for the number of contrasts tested, and states explicitly which of those claims survive. Alternatively, for exercise modality specifically, a single randomised trial with aerobic, resistance and multimodal arms in one protocol, powered for the between-arm contrast rather than for each arm against control, reporting the between-arm difference with its interval.
gaps.modality: Neuropsychological/Behavioural (MMSE, MoCA, composite cognitive scores) and outcome-prevalence proportions, in intervention and prognosis syntheses
gaps.actor_justification: It is a within-paper, recomputable methodological gap of the class the brief prefers, and it carries a positive empirical payload rather than only a missing method: the one time the contrast was tested in this corpus it failed (Q(1) = 2.91, p = 0.09) and was asserted anyway. Non-obvious because the affected claims do not look untested - they are printed as conclusions, highlights and clinical recommendations with confidence intervals attached, and each individual interval is genuinely significant against control; what is missing is the comparison, and the intervals overlap. It also has direct consequences for the corpus's own relational products: it identifies a class of apparent CONFLICT (P-680 versus P-684 on exercise modality) that is an artefact of the missing test rather than a disagreement about evidence, which is exactly the kind of record a gate is supposed to catch.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest argument against is that this is a general and long-established criticism of subgroup reporting in meta-analysis rather than an MCI research gap, and that a reviewer could reasonably code it NOT_IN_SCOPE or as a reporting-standards complaint that belongs in a critical appraisal rather than in a gap ledger: the fix is not a new study but a correction to how existing reviews are written, and journals already have guidance requiring it. The defence is that the record's closure criterion is a concrete re-analysis with a stated output, and that the comparative claims in question are actively circulating as clinical recommendations and as this corpus's head-to-head records - but the objection is real and a reviewer who wants a substantive rather than a procedural gap should reject it. A second, narrower risk: P-680 and P-698 are both exercise-in-MCI syntheses with probably overlapping primary trials, so two of the four instances may not be independent, though the untested-comparison pattern is carried by P-705 and P-711 in unrelated domains.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no combine-X-with-Y clause anywhere; the record concerns a missing statistical test on existing pooled data.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: checked clause by clause against the record's own citations. The record does NOT claim that no corpus synthesis runs a subgroup analysis (P-705 and P-711 both report subgroups) nor that none runs a between-group test (P-698 does, and is cited for exactly that). The asserted absence is confined to a test of difference for the comparative claims the papers themselves make, and each instance rests on that paper's own affirmative statement.

RESTATEMENT: not a restatement of a single paper's limitation - it spans four papers, three intervention or outcome domains and two claim types (effect ranking and heterogeneity attribution). Nearest existing gaps are distinguished by id in why_new; no existing gap names a between-subgroup test.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: the paper that partially addresses it (P-698) is named as a partial closer and its result is used as evidence, not ignored; P-680's own recommended correction is quoted as the closure criterion.
TOO_SPECIFIC: four papers, three domains, and the gap generalises to any comparative claim the corpus mines from a synthesis.
DATA_SCARCITY: the opposite - the pooled estimates, k and heterogeneity statistics are already published; the closure test is arithmetic on existing data.

NOT_IN_SCOPE: the object is how this corpus's own evidence syntheses license comparative claims, not trial design or drug development; the trial-based closure route is offered as an alternative, not as the record's substance.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper's own block uses the construct's vocabulary - 'between-subgroup test', 'meta-regression', 'between-group test' occur verbatim in P-680, P-705, P-711 and P-698 respectively.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: the numeric quotes (duration bands, setting proportions, Q(1) = 2.91) are results-field quantities; the three absence quotes are appraisal-field statements and are labelled as such, and they are used only for the claim that a test is not reported, which is a statement about the paper's text rather than a measured finding.

'Q-between' and 'between-subgroup test' occur nowhere; 'meta-regression' occurs once, in G-CAND-268, a one-line per-paper limitation stub about MRS studies ('high unexplained heterogeneity with no moderator analysis') that names no comparative claim and proposes no test. Distinguished by id from: (a) T07_neuropsych_instruments_p1-gap-01, this pack's companion record - that record is about the prediction interval, i.e. whether the pooled MEAN transports to a new setting, and its payload is that the interval includes harm; this record is about whether a claimed DIFFERENCE between two pooled means exists at all, and its payload is that the difference was never tested and failed the one time it was. They share P-680 and P-711 as sources but assert different absences with different closure tests, and either could close without the other; (b) ACTOR-G-032, which is about building a multivariable responder-prediction model, an individual-level task, not about testing a study-level contrast in an existing synthesis; (c) MINE-G-002 (durability of exercise benefit) and ACTOR-G-022 (scale change unanchored to disease course), both of which concern the OUTCOME rather than the comparison; (d) the pack lead proposing 'no adequately powered within-protocol head-to-head of exercise modalities exists' - that lead is one modality-specific instance and is here subsumed as one alternative closure route, while the record's scope is the untested-comparison pattern across intervention effect, heterogeneity attribution and outcome prevalence.

gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: Every comparative recommendation this corpus carries out of the MCI intervention and MCI-outcome synthesis literature - which exercise modality is best, whether longer stimulation is better, which recruitment setting reverts more - is read off separately pooled estimates inspected side by side, and none of them has been tested. P-680 concludes aerobic and resistance exercise beat multimodal from three separate pools whose intervals overlap heavily, with 'no formal between-subgroup test (a Q-between statistic, meta-regression or any direct comparison) ... reported anywhere in the paper'. P-705 attributes its residual 89-to-92-per-cent heterogeneity to differing stimulation frequency, site and duration and prints three duration-band estimates, but 'the explanation is asserted and never tested - no meta-regression is run'. P-711 reports community-based reversion at 36 per cent against hospital-based at 20 per cent, yet 'every comparative claim in the discussion, including the community-versus-hospital contrast on which the practical reading depends, rests on inspection of confidence intervals rather than on a tested effect'. The one instance in the corpus where the contrast WAS tested is negative and was claimed anyway: P-698's aerobic-with-versus-without-cognitive-loading comparison gave Q(1) = 2.91, p = 0.09. The absence matters for two reasons that a per-paper limitation note does not capture. First, an untested ranking read off overlapping intervals is not weaker evidence for a comparative claim, it is no evidence for one, so the corpus's head-to-head layer for this literature is populated with statements about how two author teams read intervals rather than about the world. Second, when two such rankings disagree - P-680 ranking aerobic and resistance above multimodal against P-684 finding multicomponent exercise strongest - the disagreement is manufactured by the missing test and must not be minted as a conflict about exercise.

gaps.gap_statement: The four longitudinal MCI estimates examined here (P-737, P-681, P-723, P-751) are computed on the subset of a cohort that stayed alive and kept attending, the loss is acknowledged to be non-random with respect to the outcome, and none bounds it, models it, or reports which way its own estimate moves under correction. Elsewhere in the corpus P-646 (HRS: Fine-Gray with death competing plus multiple imputation), P-791 (CHARLS: inverse-probability weighting) and P-1154 (ADNI: Fine-Gray over four pathways) do apply a correction, but none reports the corrected and uncorrected specifications side by side with the difference. The pattern is visible in four different estimand families. INCIDENCE: P-737's authors concede that 'the condition of dropouts is not reflected in the data and many robust participants were included, so those who developed MCI or dementia may have been unable to complete clinical visits and dropped out, resulting in underreporting of new-onset MCI', and then report oral frailty at HR 1.54 for incident MCI with no 'competing-risks treatment of death, missing-data procedure or sensitivity analysis ... described in the extract', and with 'interval-censored ascertainment across unevenly spaced waves treated as exact event times'. SUBTYPE COMPOSITION: P-681 restricts ADNI MCI participants to 'those with at least three follow-up visits across all three cognitive domains, leaving 813' of 1038, then reports '287 (35.2 percent) in the "No cognitive decline group"' converting at 17.4 per cent - a subtype share partly manufactured by a visit requirement that removes the people least able to return. CHANGE-SCORE CONTRASTS: P-723 loses 61 per cent of its baseline cohort to 'death, illness preventing continuation and the appearance of new exclusion criteria, all of which select against the participants whose mobility deteriorated most', and 'do not attempt any quantification, comparison of completers with non-completers, or sensitivity analysis'. NON-FATAL HAZARDS: P-751 analyses unplanned heart-failure rehospitalisation with 'standard Cox and Kaplan-Meier methods with no competing-risk treatment (no Fine-Gray model, no cumulative incidence function)' against 161 deaths in 274 patients. The absence matters because the direction of the bias is not the same across these four quantities - it deflates incidence, inflates the non-progressive subtype share, attenuates a decline contrast, and leaves a non-fatal hazard unadjusted for a competing event that occurred in 59 per cent of the sample - so a reader cannot even apply a uniform mental correction, and the corrections are all available in data already collected.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard data-structure pattern directly - the gold gap 'Machine learning architectures force continuous, interval-censored multi-visit clinical trial data into artificial, discrete cross-sectional binary labels' is the same class of critique applied to the modelling side; this record applies it to the sampling and censoring side, and P-737 supplies the interval-censoring instance verbatim. It is non-obvious because none of these four papers looks like a selection-bias paper: each reports a clean headline number with confidence intervals, and three of the four have limitation sections that mention the loss without touching the estimate. It spans four different estimand families across three countries and two data types, and it explains a substantive puzzle in the corpus - why a 'No cognitive decline' group makes up 35.2 per cent of an ADNI MCI sample - with a mechanism other than diagnostic false positives or practice effects. Finally, it is the class the brief prefers: methodological, actionable on existing data, with a closure test that is a re-analysis rather than a new cohort.
gaps.closure_criteria: A re-analysis of at least one multi-wave MCI cohort (N >= 1000, >= 3 assessment waves, documented deaths and dropouts) that reports its primary incidence or hazard estimate under three specifications side by side: (a) complete-case as currently published; (b) inverse-probability-of-attrition weighting, accompanied by a table comparing baseline characteristics of retained versus lost participants; (c) an interval-censored event model for wave-based ascertainment and, where a non-fatal endpoint is analysed, a Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard or cumulative-incidence function treating death as a competing event - with the numerical difference between specifications reported and interpreted. For the trajectory-subtype family specifically: the subtype solution and the resulting subtype shares recomputed without the minimum-follow-up-visit restriction (or with the restriction varied), reporting how much the 'no decline' share moves.
gaps.modality: Clinical/population longitudinal cohorts with neuropsychological ascertainment (MMSE, MoCA, CDT/AFT/TMT-B trajectories) and instrumented motor measures
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold-standard data-structure pattern directly - the gold gap 'Machine learning architectures force continuous, interval-censored multi-visit clinical trial data into artificial, discrete cross-sectional binary labels' is the same class of critique applied to the modelling side; this record applies it to the sampling and censoring side, and P-737 supplies the interval-censoring instance verbatim. It is non-obvious because none of these four papers looks like a selection-bias paper: each reports a clean headline number with confidence intervals, and three of the four have limitation sections that mention the loss without touching the estimate. It spans four different estimand families across three countries and two data types, and it explains a substantive puzzle in the corpus - why a 'No cognitive decline' group makes up 35.2 per cent of an ADNI MCI sample - with a mechanism other than diagnostic false positives or practice effects. Finally, it is the class the brief prefers: methodological, actionable on existing data, with a closure test that is a re-analysis rather than a new cohort.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest argument against is that the four instances may not be one gap. P-751's competing-risk problem is a well-defined estimand error with a single named fix (Fine-Gray) and would exist even with zero dropout; P-681's minimum-visit rule is a deliberate, disclosed inclusion criterion required by the estimator (the block states GBMTM 'becomes unstable with high levels of' missing data), not an uncontrolled loss; P-723's 61 per cent loss is a small-sample calamity that most readers would file under power rather than under censoring. Bundling them under 'informative selection' may therefore be the miner's abstraction rather than a property the papers share, and a reviewer could split the record or reject it as three unrelated single-paper limitations plus one methodological error. The defence is that all four have the same operational consequence - an estimate conditioned on remaining in the study, with the conditioning never quantified - and the same closure test, but the unifying construct is supplied by this record and not by any of the four papers, and that is a legitimate objection. A second risk: the direction of the bias is asserted only where a paper or its block states it (P-737 underreporting, P-723 selection against decliners); for P-681 and P-751 the record claims only that the direction is unreported, and a reviewer may find the P-681 clause the weakest link since a subtype share can move either way under a different visit rule.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: contains no combine-X-with-Y clause; it names an analytic procedure not applied to data already held.

RESTATEMENT: not a single paper's limitation - four papers, four estimand families, three countries; the nearest existing gaps (ACTOR-G-033, G-017, G-057, G-075, G-080, G-NEW-1042-A) are distinguished by id and by mechanism in why_new, and none of the corpus's 534 gap statements uses the vocabulary of attrition, censoring or competing risk.
TOO_SPECIFIC: the opposite risk applies - the statement is deliberately bounded to four documented instances rather than asserted corpus-wide.

DATA_SCARCITY: explicitly not - the participants were enrolled, the deaths and dropouts are counted, and every correction named is computable from the collected data. This is an analysis gap, not a data limitation.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: inverse-probability weighting, interval-censored models and Fine-Gray are standard methods and the record does not claim otherwise or claim methodological novelty. What is asserted absent is any application of them to these MCI estimates, and the absence is documented by each paper's own text rather than inferred from corpus sampling; the closure criterion is correspondingly a re-analysis, which is the form the brief accepts for a methodological gap.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: the paper that comes closest, P-737, is named as a partial closer with the specific thing it does (a case-versus-non-case baseline table) and the specific thing it does not (a retained-versus-lost comparison or any re-estimation).

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: checked against the record's own citations. The record does not claim no corpus paper ever compares subgroups at baseline - P-737 does, and is credited for it. It does not claim P-681 ran no sensitivity analysis, only that none is reported in its block. Each absence clause is tied to the specific paper whose block states that specific procedure was not performed.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: each cited paper's own block carries the construct's vocabulary - 'dropouts', 'attrition', 'competing risks', 'censored', 'follow-up visits' occur verbatim in P-737, P-723, P-751 and P-681 respectively.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: the quantitative quotes (HR 1.54, 287 / 35.2 per cent, 161 deaths in 274, 61 per cent, 813 of 1038) are results and methods quantities; the appraisal-field quotes are labelled by field and are used only for statements about what procedure a paper did not perform.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: the object is the analysis of MCI cohort data inside this corpus, not trial design or drug development.
gaps.dedup_note: Grepped all 534 statements in existing_gaps.md for attrition, competing risk, Fine-Gray, informative censoring, inverse probability, dropout, drop-out, loss to follow-up and selective loss: zero relevant matches. Distinguished by id from the nearest neighbours: (a) ACTOR-G-033, which is about the OUTCOME LABEL being operationalised non-comparably across inconsistent minimum-follow-up windows, contaminating the stable negative class with right-censored future converters - that is about how long you follow people and what you call the outcome; this record is about WHO remains in the analytic sample and how their loss is handled, which bites even when the window and the label are held fixed; (b) ACTOR-G-017, about incompatible MCI case definitions across studies - a between-study definitional issue, not a within-study selection issue; (c) ACTOR-G-057, G-075, G-080 and G-NEW-1042-A, all of which concern practice and retest effects on the SCORE of a retained participant - a measurement-error mechanism that operates on the people who came back, whereas this record concerns the people who did not; the two mechanisms are additive and neither substitutes for the other; (d) ACTOR-G-022 and MINE-G-002, both about intervention outcomes rather than cohort selection. Also checked all 36 entries of the T07 theme gap file: none mentions attrition, censoring or competing risk.

gaps.gap_statement: In this corpus the diagnostic accuracy reported for a bedside cognitive or behavioural instrument in MCI is measured against a reference standard that the instrument itself helped to produce, so every such figure is an UPPER BOUND whose inflation has never been quantified for any instrument. P-855 concedes the mechanism in its own limitations - the Shape Trail Test was one of the tests used to assign executive-domain impairment, giving 'a potential overestimation in the classification accuracy' - and its only remedy, a memory/language-subtype re-analysis, reduces but does not eliminate the contamination, leaving the instrument's true value 'bounded above by the reported 0.758-0.785'. P-822 carries the same structure UNACKNOWLEDGED: its psychomotor-vigilance exposure shares at least four of the twelve MoCA-J tasks that constitute the MoCA-J-defined MCI outcome, and its AUC 0.71 (0.68-0.74) belongs to a model of mean reaction time plus covariates including sleep measures (against 0.70 for the covariates alone), reported without any acknowledgement of the shared measurement content. WHY THE ABSENCE MATTERS: the corpus converts numbers of exactly this kind into instrument-CHOICE recommendations (P-842's abstract: the MoCA 'emerged as superior to the Mini-Mental State Ex-amination (MMSE) in early MCI detection') and into deployment proposals for resource-limited settings, and the bias plausibly scales with how deeply an instrument is already embedded in routine diagnostic batteries - so the ranking rewards incumbency rather than signal, and the direction of the error is systematic rather than random. SPECIFIC UNMET NEED: no corpus study re-estimates an instrument's MCI discrimination against a reference standard from which that instrument has been REMOVED, and reports the resulting change in AUC or in sensitivity/specificity at a fixed operating point. This is an ablation on data the cited cohorts already hold - both administered a full battery - not a new data-collection problem.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern of the XAI record ('moves beyond X is missing to critique what the reported quantity actually establishes') and of the OCT vendor-variance record (a systematic, directional, quantifiable bias in the measurement, not a missing modality). It is non-obvious in three ways: the bias direction is the same across all instruments so it is invisible in cross-study comparisons; the bias magnitude plausibly scales with an instrument's incumbency in routine batteries, which makes head-to-head instrument rankings self-reinforcing rather than merely noisy; and the corpus already contains the design that removes the bias (P-781's independent biological criterion) applied to a different question, which shows the fix is feasible and simply has not been pointed at MCI detection.
gaps.closure_criteria: A diagnostic-accuracy study in >= 200 community or memory-clinic participants that adjudicates MCI status TWICE on the same cohort - once with the index instrument inside the neuropsychological battery and once with it removed (or with the label set by an index-test-independent criterion: clinical consensus without the test, or amyloid/tau status) - and reports the PAIRED difference in AUC and in sensitivity/specificity at a pre-fixed operating point, with a confidence interval on the difference. A single instrument (MoCA, TMT/STT, or a comparable bedside test) is sufficient; the deliverable is the magnitude of the inflation, not a new instrument.
gaps.modality: Neuropsychological / behavioural instruments (paper-and-pencil and computerised bedside tests)
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern of the XAI record ('moves beyond X is missing to critique what the reported quantity actually establishes') and of the OCT vendor-variance record (a systematic, directional, quantifiable bias in the measurement, not a missing modality). It is non-obvious in three ways: the bias direction is the same across all instruments so it is invisible in cross-study comparisons; the bias magnitude plausibly scales with an instrument's incumbency in routine batteries, which makes head-to-head instrument rankings self-reinforcing rather than merely noisy; and the corpus already contains the design that removes the bias (P-781's independent biological criterion) applied to a different question, which shows the fix is feasible and simply has not been pointed at MCI detection.
gaps.critic_falsification: Incorporation bias is a named QUADAS-2 domain and neuropsychology already has an actuarial-criteria literature - P-855 itself applies 'the Bondi rule' - showing MCI rates move when the diagnostic algorithm changes. A verifier searching outside the corpus may find a published study that already quantifies index-test removal for the MoCA or TMT, which would downgrade this to EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE (corpus-absence only). The second-strongest objection is internal: P-822 is an association study, not a diagnostic-accuracy study, and never presents the PVT as an index test; calling its AUC 0.71 an index-test figure is the miner's framing rather than the paper's. If a gate drops that leg, the record's claiming evidence rests substantially on one paper (P-855), which the lint soft-flags as a single-paper limitation.
fp_codes_cleared: FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: the two in-corpus mitigations are named INSIDE the record and their limits stated - P-855's subtype re-analysis (residual contamination conceded, residual AUCs 0.69/0.72) and P-781's independent amyloid-PET criterion (different question, no operating point). Neither reports an accuracy CHANGE from removing the index test.
RESTATEMENT: distinguished by id from MINE-G-003, ACTOR-G-033, ACTOR-G-017, NEW-G-23, G-04, G-047/048/054/063 in why_new - different task stage, different mechanism, different closure test.

TOO_SPECIFIC: spans two instrument families (paper-and-pencil trail-making variant; computerised reaction-time task), two independent cohorts (Hong Kong community; Toon Health Study, Japan), and a downstream consequence limb (instrument-choice recommendation).
COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no 'combine X with Y' clause anywhere; the ask is an ablation within one instrument's own evaluation.
DATA_SCARCITY: not a data limitation - both claiming cohorts administered a full neuropsychological battery, so the re-adjudication is a re-analysis of data already collected.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: diagnostic-accuracy evaluation of MCI screening instruments is core corpus scope (C5, T1).

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper's own vocabulary carries the construct - P-855 'tautological problem' and 'STT was used as one of the tests for defining impairment'; P-822's own printed MoCA-J task list; P-842's own instrument-ranking sentence. P-781 is cited only for its criterion type and its own 'clinic cannot act on 0.833' line.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: the P-842 quote is explicitly flagged in roles and evidence as an abstract-level ASSERTION carrying third-party numbers, used only to show a recommendation is being made. The two P-855 lines that are digest APPRAISAL rather than author claims are marked as such in their 'supports' fields.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the absence clause is narrowed to 'no study reports the CHANGE in accuracy when the index test is removed from the reference standard'. Both partial addressers (P-855's subtype analysis, P-781's independent criterion) are named inside the record, so neither falsifies the clause.

MISASSIGNED_MEASUREMENT_FAMILY: no cross-family contrast is asserted; P-855 (paper-and-pencil) and P-822 (computerised RT) are placed on the SAME arm as two instances of one defect, not on opposite arms.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked against every existing record that touches label/criterion overlap. (1) MINE-G-003 is the closest: it is criterion-instrument contamination on the PREDICTOR side of longitudinal ADNI MCI-to-AD CONVERSION models (T2), for one informant instrument (FAQ/CDR-SOB), with a removal-ablation closure test. This record is the REFERENCE-STANDARD side of cross-sectional T1 diagnostic accuracy for bedside cognitive tests, in non-ADNI single-site cohorts - a different task, a different mechanism (the label contains the index test, rather than a predictor duplicating an outcome), and a different closure (re-adjudicate the label, not drop a predictor). (2) ACTOR-G-033 asks for one cohort held fixed while the LABEL DEFINITION is varied (MoCA<25 vs MMSE vs Petersen vs ICD) to partition labelling artefact from model quality; that is between-definition incomparability. The circularity here survives even if every study used an identical definition, because the index test is an input to that definition. (3) ACTOR-G-017 is about four incompatible operationalisations never applied to the same cohort - about ascertainment rules, not about the index test's membership of the rule. Note P-812 in this same pack applies MDS Level I and Level II at 1 SD and 2 SD in one cohort and should be examined as a partial closer for G-017; that is a separate matter from this record. (4) NEW-G-23 (calibration/ECE), ACTOR-G-048 (tele-neuropsychology unvalidated), G-054 (digital self-administered MMSE), G-063 (LASSI-L cut-points unanchored to biomarkers) and G-047 (renal screening cutoffs) are all instrument-or-setting-specific validation absences; none concerns the reference standard's composition. (5) G-04 (Petersen criteria vs computational biomarkers) is a criteria-design question, not a bias-magnitude question.
