gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: In this corpus the diagnostic accuracy reported for a bedside cognitive or behavioural instrument in MCI is measured against a reference standard that the instrument itself helped to produce, so every such figure is an UPPER BOUND whose inflation has never been quantified for any instrument. P-855 concedes the mechanism in its own limitations - the Shape Trail Test was one of the tests used to assign executive-domain impairment, giving 'a potential overestimation in the classification accuracy' - and its only remedy, a memory/language-subtype re-analysis, reduces but does not eliminate the contamination, leaving the instrument's true value 'bounded above by the reported 0.758-0.785'. P-822 carries the same structure UNACKNOWLEDGED: its psychomotor-vigilance exposure shares at least four of the twelve MoCA-J tasks that constitute the MoCA-J-defined MCI outcome, yet its AUC 0.71 (0.68-0.74) is reported as a property of the PVT. WHY THE ABSENCE MATTERS: the corpus converts numbers of exactly this kind into instrument-CHOICE recommendations (P-842's abstract: the MoCA 'emerged as superior to the Mini-Mental State Ex-amination (MMSE) in early MCI detection') and into deployment proposals for resource-limited settings, and the bias plausibly scales with how deeply an instrument is already embedded in routine diagnostic batteries - so the ranking rewards incumbency rather than signal, and the direction of the error is systematic rather than random. SPECIFIC UNMET NEED: no corpus study re-estimates an instrument's MCI discrimination against a reference standard from which that instrument has been REMOVED, and reports the resulting change in AUC or in sensitivity/specificity at a fixed operating point. This is an ablation on data the cited cohorts already hold - both administered a full battery - not a new data-collection problem.

gaps.gap_statement: In the MCI non-pharmacological intervention literature the INDEPENDENCE of the units being pooled and compared is never audited, at either level, so both the precision of each pooled effect and the apparent replication across syntheses are inflated by an unmeasured amount. WITHIN a synthesis, record-level de-duplication is routine while trial-level de-duplication is not: P-834 removed 1,112 duplicate RECORDS at screening ('Records identified 3,433; duplicates removed 1,112; full texts assessed 218; included 24.') and then pooled two reports of one Hong Kong tai chi trial and two-to-three reports of one Canadian resistance/walking trial as separate studies, with 'no duplicate-publication check, no rule for selecting one report per trial, and no mention of the issue in the limitations'; correcting it would leave roughly 21 independent trials in place of 24 articles and remove about 389 double-counted participants, inside pools as small as n = 1,205 for its headline delayed-recall estimate. The correct handling exists in the same literature and the same year - P-833 states 'A total of 8 articles and 7 studies were included in this review.' BETWEEN syntheses, agreement with prior meta-analyses is asserted with no trial-overlap accounting: P-839 reads its executive-function null as 'consistent with a previous meta-analysis (Liu et al., 2021)' while simultaneously claiming 'In the initial search, no scoping review and meta-analysis focusing on DMI in older adults with AD, MCI, and dementia was found', and P-845's entire contribution is to explain the disagreement among four prior meta-analyses rather than to re-pool them. WHY THE ABSENCE MATTERS: inverse-variance pooling assumes independent studies, so a repeated cohort both moves the point estimate and narrows its interval; and the poolable base here is tiny (P-833: 7 RCTs / 188 participants; P-839's entire meta-analytic pool is '600 participants with MCI'), so one duplicated or shared trial is a large fraction of the evidence. Downstream, a reader - or an evidence-mapping pipeline that counts syntheses as supporters - reads several reviews of substantially the same trials as several confirmations. SPECIFIC UNMET NEED: no MCI intervention synthesis in this pack reports a sensitivity analysis contrasting article-level with trial-level pooling, and none reports its own primary-trial overlap with the syntheses it cites as consistent.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern of the interval-censoring record - a critique of how the data STRUCTURE is handled in the pipeline, with a stated consequence for the numbers that come out - rather than a missing-study complaint. It is non-obvious because the defect is invisible at exactly the level where readers look: the PRISMA flow shows a large, competent de-duplication step (1,112 records) that has nothing to do with the failure, and the pooled forest plot shows study names that look distinct. It is also the one gap in this pack whose consequence lands on the corpus's own machinery: syntheses are counted as evidence, and this record is the reason several of them may be one piece of evidence. Finally it is closable now, on printed data, and its target magnitude is already estimated (~389 participants, 24 articles -> ~21 trials).
gaps.closure_criteria: Assemble the trial-level (not article-level) inventory of the MCI non-pharmacological intervention RCTs pooled by the corpus's syntheses, and report two numbers: (a) for at least one synthesis with a known multiply-reported cohort, the pooled effect and I-squared re-computed after selecting one report per underlying trial, with the delta-SMD, delta-CI width and the number of participants removed (P-834 supplies the target: ~24 articles -> ~21 trials, ~389 participants); and (b) a corrected-covered-area / overlap matrix across the syntheses that claim consistency with one another, so that agreement between reviews can be read as independent replication or as the same participants counted again.

(1) MINE-G-002 concerns the TIMING of pooled outcomes (no post-cessation follow-up is ever pooled) and mentions review overlap only inside a scope caveat about one same-author pair; it does not claim, or ask for, a unit-of-analysis audit. gaps.gap_statement: Clinician-facing exercise DOSE prescriptions for MCI are being published in this corpus with no dose-response function on a common intensity/volume axis behind them - the two syntheses that fit a function do so on weekly session frequency alone (P-674: b = 0.244 per session, R2 41.85 per cent; P-698: 0.264 per session, 52.70 per cent of between-study variance), a positive slope the randomised volume contrast did not reproduce - and the monotone more-is-better premise those prescriptions embody has been directly tested once inside a trial and came back null. The exposure has no common metric: P-839 charts intensity across its 29 included studies in four mutually incommensurable units, 'so intensity cannot be harmonised across the corpus even in principle', and P-834's own limitations concede that its prescription strata could not be evaluated at all - 'some exercise prescriptions (i.e., type: RT; intensity; session time; exercise frequency: high; duration: long) didn't match the criteria for subgroup studies because the available studies were too small' - concluding 'It's therefore less persuasive to determine a distinct relationship between specific exercise parameters and ameliorations on subdomains of EF.' The one trial in this pack that randomised dose directly - P-846, N = 224, 90 vs 240 min/wk of high-intensity functional training - reports 'a null between doses: 90 min/wk performed as well as 240 min/wk on 19 of the 20 outcomes, and better on the twentieth', its authors noting 'the lower-dose group performed equally -or in some domains, even better -than the high-dose group'. Reviews nevertheless issue specific prescriptions: P-806's central artefact is a clinician prescription table, and 'However, optimal training modality and dosage for achieving better cognitive health remain unclear' is 'stated flatly, immediately after Table 1'; P-845 recommends 52 weeks, 1-2 hour sessions, 2-3 times a week while stating 'the dose-response to aerobic exercise intervention has not been adequately established.' WHY THE ABSENCE MATTERS: dose is the one parameter a clinician has to choose, so the specificity of the published guidance is manufactured rather than estimated, and the direction of the only randomised evidence is that a two-and-a-half-fold reduction in weekly volume costs nothing measurable - which, if it holds, changes the feasibility case for exercise in MCI far more than any further demonstration that exercise works. SPECIFIC UNMET NEED: no corpus synthesis re-expresses the printed FITT parameters of MCI exercise trials on a single intensity/volume axis and fits a dose-response, and within this pack P-846 is the only randomised dose contrast, so the null has no replication.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern of the reversion-objective-function record (a framing bias in what the field chooses to estimate) combined with 'an assumption nobody tests': the whole non-pharmacological MCI literature prescribes a dose while the quantity that would justify the prescription is unmeasurable from the way the exposure is recorded. It is non-obvious because the guidance documents and the admission that dose is unresolved are in the SAME paragraphs of the SAME papers, and because the one direct test points away from the assumption rather than merely failing to support it. The closure is achievable on existing published data.
gaps.closure_criteria: A trial-level meta-regression over MCI exercise RCTs in which each trial's prescribed intensity and weekly volume are converted from the printed FITT parameters onto ONE axis (e.g. MET-minutes per week, or per cent heart-rate reserve), reporting the dose-response slope with a confidence interval AND the number of trials whose printed parameters cannot be converted at all - the latter being the quantity P-839's four-unit finding predicts will be large. Alternatively, a second dose-randomised MCI trial (two prescribed weekly volumes, one modality held fixed) powered for EQUIVALENCE with a pre-specified non-inferiority margin on a named cognitive endpoint, which would test the P-846 null rather than merely repeat it.
gaps.modality: Structured exercise / physical activity as exposure, with neuropsychological test batteries as the outcome
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern of the reversion-objective-function record (a framing bias in what the field chooses to estimate) combined with 'an assumption nobody tests': the whole non-pharmacological MCI literature prescribes a dose while the quantity that would justify the prescription is unmeasurable from the way the exposure is recorded. It is non-obvious because the guidance documents and the admission that dose is unresolved are in the SAME paragraphs of the SAME papers, and because the one direct test points away from the assumption rather than merely failing to support it. The closure is achievable on existing published data.
gaps.critic_falsification: MINE-G-004 explicitly proposes 'a future merge into a single nominal versus received dose gap family', so an operator may reasonably fold this in as an amendment to that family rather than accept it as a new gap - that is the single most likely rejection route. Substantively, the strongest objection is that P-846's null is weak evidence against a dose-response: it is one 12-week trial of one modality in one population, the comparability claim rests on the absence of significance with no equivalence test and no non-inferiority margin (its own digest says so), and a difference between 90 and 240 min/wk that this trial could not detect is not the same as dose not mattering. If the P-846 leg is discounted, what remains is closer to the already-rejected 'optimal dose undetermined' statement.

COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no combine-X-with-Y clause; the ask is a common exposure metric and a dose-response slope.
DATA_SCARCITY: not a data limitation - the FITT parameters are printed in the included trials; the missing step is conversion and regression.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: MCI intervention trials and syntheses are corpus rows (C5, T6) whose outcomes are neuropsychological instruments.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper's own vocabulary carries the dose construct - P-834 'exercise prescriptions ... intensity; session time; exercise frequency', P-845 'dose-response', P-806 'dosage', P-846 the 90 vs 240 min/wk randomisation, P-839 the intensity-unit chart.

MISASSIGNED_MEASUREMENT_FAMILY: no cross-family contrast is asserted; the four incommensurable intensity units are named as four units of ONE construct (intensity), which is the point rather than a manufactured dichotomy.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked against the corpus's whole dose family. (1) ACTOR-G-039 is about DELIVERED electric-field dose in neuromodulation being unmeasured while nominal parameters are analysed - a received-versus-nominal gap in a different intervention class. (2) MINE-G-004 is about effect estimates never being conditioned on ACHIEVED dose or observed adherence, and explicitly proposes merging with G-039 into a 'nominal versus received dose' family. This record is about the NOMINAL side that both of those take as given: the prescribed dose is not on a common axis at all, so there is no dose-response function to condition on, and it adds the one thing neither record contains - a randomised head-to-head test of the dose premise. (3) MINE-G-002 is about outcome TIMING (no post-cessation follow-up is ever pooled), not about the exposure. (4) G-349 is about harmonising the OUTCOME battery across reviews; this is the exposure side. (5) G-CAND-322 was rejected as a per-paper limitation dump whose text includes 'undetermined optimal dose/intensity'; this record is not that statement - it names the measurement mechanism that makes the estimate unobtainable, names the guidance being issued anyway, and cites the direct randomised test that contradicts the premise. (6) ACTOR-G-044 concerns the conversion endpoint, not dose.

gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: Clinician-facing exercise DOSE prescriptions for MCI are being published in this corpus with no dose-response function behind them, and the monotone more-is-better premise those prescriptions embody has been directly tested once and came back null. The exposure has no common metric: P-839 charts intensity across its 29 included studies in four mutually incommensurable units, 'so intensity cannot be harmonised across the corpus even in principle', and P-834's own limitations concede that its prescription strata could not be evaluated at all - 'some exercise prescriptions (i.e., type: RT; intensity; session time; exercise frequency: high; duration: long) didn't match the criteria for subgroup studies because the available studies were too small' - concluding 'It's therefore less persuasive to determine a distinct relationship between specific exercise parameters and ameliorations on subdomains of EF.' The one trial in this pack that randomised dose directly - P-846, N = 224, 90 vs 240 min/wk of high-intensity functional training - reports 'a null between doses: 90 min/wk performed as well as 240 min/wk on 19 of the 20 outcomes, and better on the twentieth', its authors noting 'the lower-dose group performed equally -or in some domains, even better -than the high-dose group'. Reviews nevertheless issue specific prescriptions: P-806's central artefact is a clinician prescription table, and 'However, optimal training modality and dosage for achieving better cognitive health remain unclear' is 'stated flatly, immediately after Table 1'; P-845 recommends 52 weeks, 1-2 hour sessions, 2-3 times a week while stating 'the dose-response to aerobic exercise intervention has not been adequately established.' WHY THE ABSENCE MATTERS: dose is the one parameter a clinician has to choose, so the specificity of the published guidance is manufactured rather than estimated, and the direction of the only randomised evidence is that a two-and-a-half-fold reduction in weekly volume costs nothing measurable - which, if it holds, changes the feasibility case for exercise in MCI far more than any further demonstration that exercise works. SPECIFIC UNMET NEED: no corpus synthesis re-expresses the printed FITT parameters of MCI exercise trials on a single intensity/volume axis and fits a dose-response, and within this pack P-846 is the only randomised dose contrast, so the null has no replication.

gaps.gap_statement: Outcome-instrument selection in MCI change research is governed by availability and convention, and studies do not report whether the instrument they use to measure change was shown responsive or reliable in the population they apply it to. The corpus contains one study that ran exactly that check prospectively - P-865 gated every anchor-based estimate on a prespecified responsiveness correlation of at least 0.30 in 769 amnestic MCI trial participants - and the field's default instrument failed it: the MMSE met the 0.30 criterion at no time point before Month 36, had a test-retest intraclass correlation of 0.48 (against 0.68 CDR-SB, 0.66 ADAS-Cog 11, 0.76 ADAS-Cog 13) and a ceiling rising from 12.2% to 15.2%. That verdict is never carried into the studies that depend on the instrument: P-873 pools its headline global-cognition effect on MMSE (MD 0.42, 95% CI 0.15-0.68) after selecting the instrument from a fixed prioritisation hierarchy that ranks MMSE first, and P-937's five-dataset progression harmonisation rests on MMSE because it is one of only two instruments common to all five cohorts. The absence matters because the pooled effect being interpreted, 0.42 MMSE points, is roughly a fifth of P-865's own minimal within-patient deterioration threshold of 2-3 MMSE points on the same instrument in the same disease stage, so the quantity is benchmarked (in P-873's own text) against a dementia-population MCID rather than against any MCI-specific responsiveness or reliability evidence, and the scale has not been shown to register change of that size above its own measurement error in MCI. GAP SCOPE: asserted for this corpus.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard pattern 'a measurement never calibrated across settings' and the ACTOR-G-030 family of data-structure critiques: it challenges the measurement assumption underneath a large body of reported effects rather than naming a missing modality pair. It is non-obvious because the corpus already contains the verdict - P-865 published the MMSE's failure of an explicit adequacy criterion in 769 MCI patients - and the corpus nonetheless continues to pool and harmonise on that instrument; the defect is a transfer failure inside the corpus, not ignorance. It is also quantitatively sharp: the pooled effect (0.42) and the instrument's own minimal within-patient threshold (2-3) are both published numbers on the same scale in the same disease stage, so the size of the problem is calculable rather than rhetorical.
gaps.closure_criteria: A head-to-head responsiveness and reliability comparison in one MCI cohort (N >= 300, at least two follow-up visits) that reports, for MMSE, MoCA, ADAS-Cog and CDR-SB simultaneously: test-retest ICC in a clinically stable subgroup, ceiling/floor proportions, and the correlation between change on each instrument and change on an independent clinician- or informant-rated global change anchor, with a prespecified adequacy threshold declared in advance; plus a re-pooling of an existing MCI intervention meta-analysis restricted to instruments that pass that threshold, reporting whether the pooled estimate and its sign survive.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold-standard pattern 'a measurement never calibrated across settings' and the ACTOR-G-030 family of data-structure critiques: it challenges the measurement assumption underneath a large body of reported effects rather than naming a missing modality pair. It is non-obvious because the corpus already contains the verdict - P-865 published the MMSE's failure of an explicit adequacy criterion in 769 MCI patients - and the corpus nonetheless continues to pool and harmonise on that instrument; the defect is a transfer failure inside the corpus, not ignorance. It is also quantitatively sharp: the pooled effect (0.42) and the instrument's own minimal within-patient threshold (2-3) are both published numbers on the same scale in the same disease stage, so the size of the problem is calculable rather than rhetorical.
gaps.critic_falsification: P-865's authors attribute both the MMSE ceiling and the poor reliability to the trial's own entry criterion requiring an MMSE of 24 or above, which restricts range and mechanically depresses ICC. If that attribution is right, the unfitness verdict may be an artefact of a trial-enriched sample and may not transfer to the community and clinic populations that P-873 and P-937 pool - in which case the pooled 0.42-point MMSE effect is not necessarily sitting on a noise floor of that size, and the record weakens from 'the scale cannot register the change being reported' to the softer and more familiar 'nobody checks whether it can'. A reviewer could also argue the MMSE's ceiling in MCI is common knowledge in the wider literature, so the absence to defend is strictly the reporting practice, not the fact.

TOO_SPECIFIC: spans three papers, three designs (secondary psychometric analysis of a phase III RCT N=769; five-RCT meta-analysis N=747; five-dataset IPD harmonisation N=7838) and concerns the single most widely used cognitive instrument in the corpus.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: instrument measurement properties in MCI are core corpus scope; no drug-development or trial-regulatory question is raised.

DATA_SCARCITY: the closure study needs no new data type. ADC-008, the five harmonised progression datasets and any serial-testing memory-clinic cohort already hold repeat administrations plus clinician global ratings.
FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: P-865 addresses it for four instruments in one trial cohort and is listed as a partial closer with what it leaves open, rather than being ignored.

gaps.gap_statement: The reproducibility of the human judgement that creates an MCI case is almost never measured in this corpus, and where it has been measured it is poor. P-866 is the one corpus study that computed it: across 648 adjudicated dossiers in a phase 3 prevention trial, the site investigator who examined the patient and the blinded adjudication committee working from the same dossier agreed on MCI due to AD at Cohen's kappa 0.327 with 71.0% overall agreement, agreement fell to 40.5% on cases the investigator had diagnosed as MCI at two consecutive visits, and 41 of 410 cases (10%) declared events against a non-supporting investigator diagnosis made up 42.7% of all endpoint events in the trial. The other two papers in this pack whose primary output rests on clinician judgement concede they did not measure it: P-865, whose entire threshold derivation is calibrated against clinician-rated change anchors, states that interrater variability could not be evaluated because rater information was limited; P-913, which adjudicates incident MCI in a 560-person cohort and diagnoses 12% of cases from a single information source, lists formal inter-rater reliability for chart review among its improvements and diagnostic accuracy of each modality combination versus a gold standard among its open problems. No corpus study propagates a measured label-reliability estimate into the quantity it then reports - an incident-MCI rate, a conversion rate, a threshold, or a discrimination metric. This matters because a criterion whose reproducibility is fair puts a ceiling on the agreement any model can achieve with it: incident-MCI rates and classifier AUCs are quoted to two or three decimal places against a label whose own reproducibility has been measured once and was 0.327, and single-source ascertainment - the design almost every cohort in this corpus uses - has a measured false-negative rate of 42.7% in the only setting where anyone checked. GAP SCOPE: asserted for this corpus. STATUS: candidate, pending_human_review, gate_verified false.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard pattern that challenges the ground-truth standard used in current modelling ('prognostic models treat central nervous system markers as absolute ground truth'), transposed to the clinical label rather than a biomarker. It is non-obvious because the corpus does contain the number - the field's own measurement of its label reliability, kappa 0.327, sits in a methods report from a terminated prevention trial - and it has never been used as a bound on anything. The 42.7% ascertainment false-negative figure is the sharp edge: it says that in the one setting where a wide net was cast, nearly half of all true endpoint events were invisible to the examining clinician, which is the ascertainment design essentially every cohort in this corpus uses.
gaps.closure_criteria: A cohort or trial in which at least 100 incident-MCI ascertainments are independently adjudicated twice - two blinded panels, or a panel against a site clinician who records an explicit endpoint opinion rather than one inferred from a diagnosis code - reporting Cohen's kappa with a confidence interval, the resulting spread in the incident-MCI rate between the two adjudications, and, where a prediction model is fitted on that cohort, the model's AUC or C-index re-estimated against each adjudication separately, so that the label-reliability component of reported discrimination is separated from model quality.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold-standard pattern that challenges the ground-truth standard used in current modelling ('prognostic models treat central nervous system markers as absolute ground truth'), transposed to the clinical label rather than a biomarker. It is non-obvious because the corpus does contain the number - the field's own measurement of its label reliability, kappa 0.327, sits in a methods report from a terminated prevention trial - and it has never been used as a bound on anything. The 42.7% ascertainment false-negative figure is the sharp edge: it says that in the one setting where a wide net was cast, nearly half of all true endpoint events were invisible to the examining clinician, which is the ascertainment design essentially every cohort in this corpus uses.
gaps.critic_falsification: P-866's kappa is itself a constructed comparison. Its own '### What are the problems?' records that investigators never offered endpoint opinions, so the paper compares committee decisions against what investigator diagnoses were taken to support - an inference the authors built - and the kappa inherits that construction. A reviewer can therefore argue 0.327 understates genuine clinician agreement and is an artefact of the comparison, which would blunt the record's central number. Separately, TOMMORROW's construct is MCI due to AD in a genotype-enriched, biomarker-free prevention trial, plausibly the hardest label in the field; the ordinary all-cause MCI label used by most corpus classifiers may be substantially more reproducible, so a single trial's kappa should not be treated as a bound on the whole corpus without replication.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no modality pairing is proposed; the missing operation is a duplicate adjudication and the propagation of its result.

RESTATEMENT: distinguished by id against ACTOR-G-017, G-033, G-21 and G-079 in why_new - definition variation and data-structure label noise are different mechanisms from rater irreproducibility, and their closure designs differ.

TOO_SPECIFIC: three papers, three settings (phase 3 prevention trial N=3494 randomised; ADCS trial secondary psychometrics N=769; surgical-aging cohort N=560), and the construct - the MCI label - is the dependent variable of essentially the whole corpus.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: endpoint ascertainment and diagnostic reliability are measurement questions inside the corpus's scope, not trial-regulatory or drug-development questions.
DATA_SCARCITY: no scarce data is required. Duplicate adjudication of existing dossiers in NACC-style or trial cohorts is a re-reading exercise on records that already exist.
FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: P-866 partially addresses it and is credited as the corpus's only measurement, with an explicit statement of what it leaves open, rather than being missed.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: all three papers' own blocks carry the construct's vocabulary - P-866 kappa/agreement/adjudication, P-865 interrater variability, P-913 inter-rater reliability and gold standard. No leg is a miner's inferential bridge from an unrelated finding.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: quotes are tagged by field; the reliability numbers come from '### Key findings reported' and '### What are the outcomes? (Results)', the concessions from '### Potential gaps or limitations', '### What can be improved?' and '### Open problems'. Nothing measured is quoted from a significance or novelty field.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the clause 'no corpus study propagates a measured label-reliability estimate into the quantity it reports' was checked against this record's own citations first. P-866 measures reliability but reports its event count of 96 without any uncertainty derived from kappa; P-865 states it could not measure it; P-913 states it did not. The claim that reliability has been measured is explicitly attributed to P-866 in the claim text rather than denied.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked against the 36 theme gaps and grepped all 535 statements in existing_gaps.md for 'kappa|inter-rater|interrater|rater|adjudicat|label noise'; the only hits are unrelated. (a) ACTOR-G-017 concerns four incompatible OPERATIONALISATIONS of MCI (ICD code, screening threshold, composite score, consensus criteria) and its closure is to apply two or more definitions to one cohort. (b) ACTOR-G-033 concerns non-comparable outcome-label definitions and follow-up windows, with closure by holding a cohort fixed and varying the label rule. Both are about WHICH RULE is used; this record is about the reproducibility of ONE rule applied by different clinicians, and its closure is a duplicate adjudication, not a duplicate definition. (c) G-21 concerns label noise created by forcing interval-censored multi-visit data into binary labels - a data-structure mechanism, not a rater mechanism. (d) ACTOR-G-079 concerns adjudicating REVERTERS against amyloid/tau, i.e. accuracy against biology for one transition; this record concerns agreement between human raters on the incident diagnosis itself, which is measurable without any biomarker. (e) IA-02, IA-31, IA-88 and KA-16 in existing_records_core.md concern whether cognitive tests are sufficient for screening, not whether their consensus interpretation is reproducible.

gaps.gap_statement: This literature converts statistically indeterminate comparisons directly into recommendations about what to administer to patients, and reports no equivalence margin, minimum detectable difference or power calculation that would license the inference. Four papers in this pack do it in four different directions of protocol change. P-935 recommends reconsidering the conventional preference for delayed recall over learning, and proposes shorter equally predictive protocols, on the basis that free recall and delayed free recall entered jointly in one Cox model had 'similar effect sizes' of around a 20% hazard reduction per SD - in a block that contains no confidence interval for either hazard ratio. P-874 concludes that a three-odorant panel suffices because extending the panel raised healthy-versus-MCI AUC only from 0.766 to 0.777, with no test of that difference. P-929 argues against routine off-label cholinesterase-inhibitor prescribing in MCI from a null whose amyloid-PET odds ratio is 3.925 with a 95% CI of 0.676 to 34.315. P-945 recommends a follow-up MRI one year after high-risk identification on an incremental-value estimate of IDI 0.090 whose 95% CI runs from -0.062 to 0.170 and therefore includes no effect. The absence matters because these are the recommendations that reach practice by subtraction and addition - drop a subtest, shorten a panel, stop a drug, schedule a scan - and in each case the interval or the untested difference is wide enough to contain a change of clinically relevant size in the opposite direction to the recommendation. Nothing about these four studies makes the missing analysis hard: an equivalence or non-inferiority framing with a prespecified margin can be applied to the data already collected. GAP SCOPE: asserted for this corpus. STATUS: candidate, pending_human_review, gate_verified false.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard pattern of an objective-function or inference framing bias rather than a missing dataset: the field's default is to read a wide interval as a decision. It is non-obvious because each individual paper looks defensible in isolation - a null result, a marginal AUC gain, a shared point estimate - and the defect only becomes visible when the four are laid side by side and it is noticed that every one of them ends in a concrete instruction about clinical practice. It is also actionable at zero data cost: all four re-analyses run on data already collected, and the record specifies them individually rather than gesturing at 'more rigour'.
gaps.closure_criteria: For any MCI assessment-protocol recommendation that rests on a no-difference or negligible-difference finding, a re-analysis of the same data with a prespecified equivalence margin: for P-935, a two-one-sided-test on the difference between the FR and DFR log hazard ratios in the joint Cox model with a margin declared in advance (for example a hazard-ratio ratio within 0.90-1.11) and both intervals reported; for P-874, a DeLong or bootstrap test of the paired AUC difference between the 3-item and full panels with a prespecified non-inferiority margin on AUC; for P-929, the minimum detectable odds ratio at the achieved N of 111 (and 50 matched) reported alongside the null, so the reader can see what the study could and could not have detected. A recommendation to change a protocol should be reported only where equivalence or superiority is established at the declared margin.
gaps.modality: Neuropsychological / behavioural instruments and assessment protocols
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold-standard pattern of an objective-function or inference framing bias rather than a missing dataset: the field's default is to read a wide interval as a decision. gaps.critic_falsification: The four legs are not equally defective and bundling them risks treating a probably-correct equivalence claim as the same failure as an uninformative null. P-935's joint Cox model has 1422 participants and 187 incident events, so a properly specified equivalence test on the FR-versus-DFR difference might well pass at a reasonable margin - meaning its recommendation could be right even though its reported evidence does not establish it. P-929, by contrast, is simply underpowered at N=111 with a 50-person matched subsample. A reviewer could reasonably split this record in two, or reject the P-935 leg on the grounds that the criticism is about reporting rather than about a false conclusion. A second objection: it is possible the underlying papers do report intervals that the digests omit, in which case the count-based clause about P-935's missing confidence intervals is a property of the digest rather than of the publication, and that leg would need checking against the PDF before the record is gated.

gaps.gap_statement: Every head-to-head comparison of competing MCI case definitions in this corpus scores the candidate rules against a progression endpoint that the same clinical apparatus produces - consensus dementia diagnosis made at the same centre, by the same clinicians, largely from the same neuropsychological battery that generated the classification. A rule that flags biologically real cases the consensus panel would call normal is therefore counted as a false positive, so these comparisons can only return 'the incumbent wins' (P-955) or 'the definitions are equivalent' (P-986, P-1136), and cannot detect a rule with better biological validity. The corpus already contains the design that breaks the circle - P-971 adjudicates two competing classification schemes by measuring CSF amyloid/tau positivity among exactly the people the schemes classify differently, and finds 72.2% of the disputed cases biomarker-positive - but no criterion-comparison study applies it to the case definitions themselves. The consequence is that the field's operative best-practice claim, that multi-test neuropsychological criteria have 'superior validity regarding neuropathology' (P-1162), rests on an unquantified assertion in a single-author narrative appraisal that no corpus primary study has ever tested, while criterion choice is simultaneously moving hard numbers: reversion 43.4% vs 48.3% (P-986), MCI rate 44/53/41% (P-955), and a 3.7-fold difference in dementia incidence (P-1094).
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'Prognostic models treat central nervous system markers as absolute ground truth' and 'There is no consensus on whether current MCI diagnostic criteria (e.g., Petersen rules) are compatible with or optimal for computational biomarker-driven models' - it is a ground-truth/reference-standard critique, not a missing-modality one. Non-obvious in three ways. (1) The naive reading of these five papers is that the criterion question has been well studied; the point is that the study design cannot answer it. (2) The corpus supplies its own counterfactual: P-971 runs the biomarker-anchored adjudication on a neighbouring question, so the gap is not a capability limit but an unmade connection - and P-971 and P-1084 share authors (Bondi, Edmonds, Thomas), so the group holding the method is the group that published the criterion comparison without it. (3) It exposes that the corpus's best-practice recommendation (P-1162) asserts a neuropathological-validity advantage that no corpus study has measured and that the studies which could have measured it were designed so that they could not.
gaps.closure_criteria: In a cohort with both multi-domain neuropsychological data and a non-clinical reference (NACC autopsy-linked MCI participants, n>=200, or an amyloid/tau-characterised memory-clinic or ADNI sample, n>=400): classify every participant under at least three operationalisations applied blind to each other (Petersen/Winblad one-test, Jak/Bondi two-test actuarial, and a data-driven or latent-class rule), then rank the rules against the non-clinical reference rather than against consensus dementia diagnosis - reporting, for the discordant cases only (those one rule calls impaired and another calls normal), the proportion neuropathologically or biomarker-positive, plus net reclassification improvement against the reference and the same reclassification broken out by race and by education stratum. The gap closes when such a study reports which criterion the discordant cases side with biologically, and whether that answer differs by subgroup.
gaps.modality: Clinical/Population - neuropsychological criteria and consensus diagnosis (C5)
gaps.task_type: T6 diagnostic-criteria comparison, with T2/T5 endpoints (MCI->dementia progression, reversion)
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern 'Prognostic models treat central nervous system markers as absolute ground truth' and 'There is no consensus on whether current MCI diagnostic criteria (e.g., Petersen rules) are compatible with or optimal for computational biomarker-driven models' - it is a ground-truth/reference-standard critique, not a missing-modality one. Non-obvious in three ways. (1) The naive reading of these five papers is that the criterion question has been well studied; the point is that the study design cannot answer it. (2) The corpus supplies its own counterfactual: P-971 runs the biomarker-anchored adjudication on a neighbouring question, so the gap is not a capability limit but an unmade connection - and P-971 and P-1084 share authors (Bondi, Edmonds, Thomas), so the group holding the method is the group that published the criterion comparison without it. (3) It exposes that the corpus's best-practice recommendation (P-1162) asserts a neuropathological-validity advantage that no corpus study has measured and that the studies which could have measured it were designed so that they could not.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE. The Jak/Bondi actuarial criteria were introduced partly on ADNI CSF-biomarker evidence, and published work outside this corpus (Bondi/Edmonds-line ADNI analyses) does compare conventional against actuarial criteria using CSF amyloid and tau positivity rates. If a reviewer counts that as the adjudication this record calls absent, the gap collapses to a corpus-sampling artefact. Two things partly survive that objection and should be checked before the record is accepted: (a) the external comparisons report biomarker POSITIVITY RATES per criterion, not a ranking of criteria against a neuropathological or biomarker-defined ENDPOINT with reclassification statistics, and none of them reports the race/education-stratified reclassification that P-955's method-by-race finding makes urgent; (b) the corpus's own best-practice statement (P-1162, 2025) still lists the head-to-head comparison as open, which is weak evidence that the field does not regard the question as settled. A second, smaller risk: P-955's Penn Memory Center cohort contributes to NACC, so P-955 and P-1084 may share participants; they are not treated here as independent replications, only as separate instances of the same design flaw.

RESTATEMENT: checked by id against G-017, G-033, G-04, G-067, MINE-G-003, G-048/G-050/G-054 - see why_new. This record additionally reports that G-017's absence clause is falsified by four corpus papers.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the absence clause was checked against every paper cited here. P-971 is the only cited paper that performs a biomarker-anchored adjudication of two classification schemes, and it is named in the record as a partial closer, not as a supporter of the absence. P-1076 (also NACC, autopsy-anchored) uses autopsy as an EXPOSURE inside one fixed MCI definition, not to referee competing definitions. No cited paper compares MCI case definitions against a non-clinical reference.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: searched the digest corpus for papers mentioning actuarial/Jak-Bondi/Petersen criteria comparison (27 hits) and for autopsy/neuropathology papers that also mention criteria; the closest are P-1092 (MCI-LB criteria stability, some autopsy-confirmed, but a single aetiological criterion set, not a head-to-head of general-MCI definitions) and P-1162 (assertion only, no data). Both are named in the record.

TOO_SPECIFIC: the gap spans five independent cohorts on three continents (Penn ADRC, Swedish GAS/SNAC, Essex Memory Clinic, InveCe.Ab Italy, NACC) and governs which people are called impaired, so it is not trivially true at this specificity.

DATA_SCARCITY: the data exist. NACC holds autopsy-linked MCI cohorts (P-1076 assembles 206 such participants) and ADNI holds CSF on MCI participants classified under multiple schemes (P-971 uses exactly that), so the closing study needs no new data collection.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper's own text uses the vocabulary of the gap - 'criteria', 'consensus diagnosis', 'biomarker adjudication/confirmation', 'neuropathology'. No paper is cited for a construct it does not discuss.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: the P-1162 quote is explicitly flagged in the evidence block as an assertion sitting in a narrative review's results field, and is used as the statement of a standing belief, never as a measured finding. The quantitative claims (43.4/48.3%, 44/53/41%, IRR 3.7, 72.2%) are all taken from results fields of primary analyses.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked against ACTOR-G-017, whose absence clause is 'no study applies two or more definitions to the SAME cohort to quantify how much of an effect estimate is attributable to the ascertainment rule'. That clause is FALSIFIED by P-955, P-986, P-1094 and P-1136, all of which do exactly that; G-017 should be revisited for partial closure. This record is the next-order absence: the multi-definition design exists, but it has no reference standard outside the classification apparatus. Also checked ACTOR-G-033 (label operationalised over inconsistent follow-up windows and different prevalent-MCI rules; no cohort held fixed while varying only the label) - same falsification applies and, more importantly, G-033 is about partitioning AUC/SHAP variance in ML models, not about the reference standard for adjudicating between criteria. Checked G-04 (no international consensus workshop output proposing a revised MCI case definition with quantitative biomarker thresholds) - that is a governance/consensus-process gap, this is a study-design gap about how competing criteria are scored. Checked ACTOR-G-002 and G-011 (reversion modality gaps), ACTOR-G-067 (reversion rates vary 7-48% with no harmonised pooled meta-analysis) - G-067 asks for harmonisation of rates, not for an independent adjudication standard. Checked MINE-G-003 (FAQ used as both predictor and outcome in ADNI conversion models) - same circularity FAMILY but a different mechanism (one instrument on both sides of one model) and a different closure test (ablate FAQ and report delta-AUC); here the circularity is between the classification rule and the endpoint used to referee competing rules. gaps.gap_statement: MCI screening instruments and models in this corpus are characterised only by prevalence-invariant statistics - AUC, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy - estimated in samples whose case fraction is set by the recruitment site, and, within the pack examined here, none reports what its predictive values or false-positive burden would be at the prevalence of the setting it is recommended for. Elsewhere in the corpus three studies do report a predictive value at a measured population prevalence - P-939 (SLAS risk index: PPV 0.169 at 10.2 per cent cumulative incidence, field-deployed as a community questionnaire), P-325 (CHARLS classifier: PPV 0.2228 at the 13.7 per cent wave prevalence, proposed for community screening) and P-757 (pooled rapid-screen PPV 56.2 per cent at 24.6 per cent prevalence with explicit false-positive-burden reasoning, though not at the preoperative target prevalence) - none of them propagating a prevalence interval, printing per-1,000 counts or reporting the threshold shift needed to hold PPV, so the closure criteria remain unmet. The pattern is systematic: P-998 proposes a receded near point of convergence as a low-cost triage signal for the general geriatric population and reports AUC 0.764 with sensitivity 70.9% and specificity 69.5% in a sample containing 299 MCI among 1,190 (a 25% case fraction); P-1016 proposes a routine-variable model as a high-specificity second-opinion screening layer from a set of 2,156 AD versus 2,684 MCI in which both classes are patients; P-991 benchmarks three brief screens on 622 memory-clinic attendees of whom only 33 are healthy controls; P-979's national panel recommends MoCA, ACE-III or MMSE with clock drawing to general practitioners. The one predictive value reported anywhere in the pack is P-1060's PPV 0.46, and it is obtained in an ADNI cognitively-normal sample in which 139 of 487 progressed - so even at that enriched event fraction most people the model flags do not convert. The deployment base rate is measured in the same corpus and is far lower: P-1062 finds community MCI prevalence 9.3% (95% CI 6.7-12.7) in an urban Delhi cohort it had powered for 26%. The absent quantity is the only one that decides whether a screening pathway is implementable - the fraction of flagged people who have the condition, and the false positives generated per thousand screened, at a stated deployment prevalence.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern that separates discrimination from decision consequence - 'No longitudinal follow-up data exists for MCI patients after computational diagnosis; the clinical utility of AI flagging ... has never been demonstrated' - but one step earlier and far cheaper to close: before asking whether acting on a flag helps, the corpus cannot say what fraction of its flags are correct where the flagging would happen. Non-obvious in three ways. (1) Every paper here reports its numbers correctly and completely by convention; the defect is in what the convention omits, so no individual paper reads as deficient. (2) The two halves of the missing calculation both sit in this corpus - a measured community prevalence (P-1062) and screening operating points (P-998, P-991, P-1016) - and have never been put together, so the gap is an unmade connection rather than a missing capability. (3) It explains a pattern the corpus otherwise treats as coincidence: proposals keep arriving at sensitivity/specificity near 0.70 and being described as promising triage signals, a level whose acceptability is undecidable without the base rate.
gaps.closure_criteria: For one instrument or model already in the corpus (for example P-998's NPC threshold or a MoCA/MMSE cut-off from P-979's recommended set), and for a named deployment population with a measured prevalence and its confidence interval (for example the 9.3%, 95% CI 6.7-12.7 of P-1062, or an Australian general-practice denominator matching P-979's pathway): report, at a pre-specified operating threshold, PPV, NPV and the expected number of true positives, false positives and missed cases per 1,000 people screened, with the interval propagated from the prevalence CI; then report how far the threshold must move to hold PPV at a stated acceptable level and what that costs in sensitivity. The gap closes when at least one MCI screening proposal states the fraction of the people it would flag who actually have MCI in the setting where it is recommended. ILLUSTRATION, NOT A PAPER'S CLAIM (this is the miner's arithmetic from two quoted figures, and no cited paper performs it): P-998's 70.9% sensitivity and 69.5% specificity applied at P-1062's 9.3% prevalence gives PPV about 0.19, i.e. roughly four in five flagged people would not have MCI. Both inputs are verbatim corpus quantities; the multiplication is the miner's and is offered only to show that the missing number is decision-relevant, not as evidence from either paper.

gaps.task_type: T1 MCI detection / MCI_vs_NC, with T2 conversion prediction for P-1060

gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE. The prevalence-dependence of predictive values is textbook diagnostic epidemiology, and published work outside this corpus does compute PPV for MMSE and MoCA at community prevalence; a reviewer may reasonably hold that the field is not blind to this and that only this 1,262-paper sample is. Two defences, both partial: the record is scoped to corpus practice and to a specific closable computation attached to named corpus instruments and a named corpus prevalence, rather than to a claim about the world literature; and the corpus's own behaviour is the evidence that the practice is not routine - P-1060 records PPV 0.46 as a limitation and does not act on it, and P-998 asks for external threshold validation while never asking what the threshold does at a screening base rate. A second, smaller objection: P-1060's PPV is for 5-year incident prodromal AD in cognitively normal people, not for prevalent MCI detection, so it is used here only as evidence that predictive values are reportable and are near-absent, never as a comparator to P-1062's prevalent-MCI figure.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the absence clause was checked against the record's own citations. P-1060 DOES report PPV and NPV, so it is listed as a partial closer and the clause is narrowed accordingly: the absence is of predictive values computed at a stated DEPLOYMENT prevalence, not of predictive values altogether. No other cited paper reports a predictive value.
DATA_SCARCITY: nothing new needs collecting. The computation requires only a published sensitivity/specificity pair and a published prevalence, both of which the corpus already holds.

TOO_SPECIFIC: the gap spans an oculomotor population screen, a routine-variable ML model, a brief-instrument head-to-head, a multimodal ADNI risk model and a national primary-care guideline, so it is not a single-instrument nicety.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: screening-pathway performance for MCI detection is core corpus scope; the record proposes no drug development or trial design.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper's own text uses the vocabulary of the gap - screening, triage, sensitivity, specificity, predictive value, prevalence. P-979 is cited only for the deployment pathway it actually recommends, and P-1062 only for the prevalence it actually measured.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: all quoted numbers come from results, sample-size or limitations fields of primary analyses. The only derived number in the record - PPV about 0.19 - is explicitly labelled as the miner's arithmetic and is confined to the closure_criteria field, never presented as a finding of P-998 or P-1062.
gaps.dedup_note: Grepped all 534 gap statements for 'PPV', 'positive predictive value', 'pre-test probability', 'base rate', 'prevalence-adjust' and 'number needed' - zero hits; the same grep over existing_records_core.md returns zero. Checked NEW-G-23 (no MCI model applies Platt/isotonic/temperature scaling or reports Expected Calibration Error and a reliability diagram) - distinct: calibration is agreement between predicted and observed risk WITHIN a validation cohort, whereas this is the transfer of operating characteristics to a different base rate; a perfectly calibrated model in ADNI still misstates PPV in general practice. Checked ACTOR-G-040 (the clinically decisive adjacent-stage contrast is under-evaluated relative to easy extreme contrasts and reviews propagate easy-contrast performance) - adjacent but different: G-040 is about WHICH CONTRAST is evaluated, this is about the BASE RATE at which any contrast's numbers are used, and the two are independent (a study can evaluate the hard SCD-vs-MCI contrast and still never state a PPV). Checked G-09 and NEW-G-27 (no prospective AI-vs-standard-of-care or XAI-augmented decision trial) - those ask whether acting on a flag changes outcomes; this asks what fraction of flags are correct, which is prior to and cheaper than an impact trial. Checked line-378 gap (no batch paper reports incremental discrimination over an age/sex/education base model) - that concerns marker value-added, not base-rate transfer. Checked the theme file's ACTOR-G-047/G-048/G-054 (renal cutoffs, tele-neuropsychology, digital MMSE) - each asks for sensitivity/specificity against a gold standard, i.e. they request exactly the prevalence-invariant statistics this record says are insufficient.

gaps.gap_statement: The corpus prices disease modification in MCI per MMSE point, and has never checked that price against money actually spent - not even inside the cohort that produced the coefficient. P-1093 converts 36-month MMSE change in GERAS-US into +$8,504 of societal cost for MCI and a $2,638 per-person saving from slowing progression 30%, figures offered to inform value assessments of amyloid-targeting therapy. The earlier report of the same cohort, P-1000, found that over those same 36 months total societal costs did not rise while cognition worsened: approximately $2,430 down to $2,007 per month in MCI. The two are not arithmetically incompatible - one is a conditional coefficient, the other a marginal trajectory - but that is exactly the point: the conditional coefficient has never been shown to reproduce any observed expenditure path, and no corpus record reconciles the pair. The unmet study is a validation of a cost-of-progression coefficient against realised, individually linked expenditure, which matters because these coefficients are used as if they were measurements to justify screening programmes and reimbursement decisions.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern of a clinical-utility failure transposed to the economic arm - a quantity is estimated and acted on, but the thing it predicts is never measured against it - and the gold health-economics precedent G-07 shows this class is in scope. Non-obvious in three ways. (1) The evidence is strongest precisely where it is least expected: the contradiction-shaped material comes from two analyses of one cohort by one author group, so no cross-study heterogeneity argument explains it away and no reader comparing different cohorts would notice it. (2) It targets the number that leaves the literature and enters policy - a per-person dollar saving from slowing progression - rather than an internal methodological nicety. (3) It identifies a validation that is cheap and immediately doable with existing linked claims data, unlike the treatment-effect linkage P-1093 itself proposes, which must wait for trial outcomes.
gaps.closure_criteria: In a cohort with individually linked administrative expenditure (Medicare claims, a national health-insurance database, or an integrated delivery-system ledger) and at least three repeated cognitive assessments over >=24 months in MCI or early AD, n>=500: fit the same MMSE-change-to-cost model used in P-1093, then compare each participant's model-predicted cost increment against their realised expenditure over the identical window, reporting calibration of predicted versus observed cost (slope, intercept, mean absolute error, and the proportion of participants whose realised cost moved in the predicted direction), with the comparison repeated in the tertile whose cognition declined most and in a period without pandemic disruption. The gap closes when a published cost-of-progression coefficient for MCI has been shown to reproduce, or has been shown to fail to reproduce, an observed expenditure path.
gaps.modality: Clinical/Population - health economics anchored on MMSE-measured progression (C5)
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern of a clinical-utility failure transposed to the economic arm - a quantity is estimated and acted on, but the thing it predicts is never measured against it - and the gold health-economics precedent G-07 shows this class is in scope. Non-obvious in three ways. (1) The evidence is strongest precisely where it is least expected: the contradiction-shaped material comes from two analyses of one cohort by one author group, so no cross-study heterogeneity argument explains it away and no reader comparing different cohorts would notice it. (2) It targets the number that leaves the literature and enters policy - a per-person dollar saving from slowing progression - rather than an internal methodological nicety. (3) It identifies a validation that is cheap and immediately doable with existing linked claims data, unlike the treatment-effect linkage P-1093 itself proposes, which must wait for trial outcomes.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is that the record manufactures a tension between two quantities that were never meant to agree. P-1093 estimates cost conditional on cognitive decline, holding other drivers fixed; P-1000 reports the unconditional cost path, which can fall for reasons the model deliberately conditions away - pandemic service reduction, differential dropout of the most expensive participants, or a baseline diagnostic workup that front-loads cost. If a reviewer accepts that as sufficient, the pair is simply two correct answers to two questions and no gap exists. The record is written to survive that reading - it asserts only that no reconciliation or realised-expenditure validation exists, not that the two numbers contradict - but the objection would still weaken it to a reporting request rather than a research gap. A second risk is scope: P-1000 and P-1093 are the same GERAS-US cohort with a shared first author, so this rests on one cohort plus one policy report, and P-977's model-based costs are a 2016 global synthesis rather than a comparable estimate. A third is EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: cost-of-illness models for dementia have been compared against claims data outside this corpus, though the corpus itself carries no such comparison for an MCI-stage progression coefficient.

P-1000 reports realised costs but fits no progression coefficient; P-1093 fits the coefficient but reports no realised-cost comparison. No cited paper performs the validation the record says is absent.

DATA_SCARCITY: the closing study needs linked administrative expenditure plus repeated cognitive testing, both of which exist at scale (P-1000's own improvement list asks for exactly such linked administrative datasets), so this is a methodological gap, not a data limitation.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: health economics of MCI detection is established corpus scope (G-07 is a confirmed health-economics gap); the record proposes no drug development or trial design.
EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper's own text uses the vocabulary of the gap - societal cost, progression, MMSE, modelled versus observed. No paper is cited for a construct it does not discuss.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: no quote is drawn from a significance or novelty field and presented as a result. The two load-bearing numbers (+$8,504 with the $2,638 saving, and $2,430 to $2,007 per month) both come from '### What are the outcomes? (Results)'. The record explicitly states the two are not arithmetically incompatible rather than asserting a contradiction.

MISASSIGNED_MEASUREMENT_FAMILY: the record does not place the two figures on opposite arms of a manufactured dichotomy; it names them as a conditional coefficient and a marginal trajectory respectively and asks only for a reconciliation.

gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: The corpus prices disease modification in MCI per MMSE point, and has never checked that price against money actually spent - not even inside the cohort that produced the coefficient. P-1093 converts 36-month MMSE change in GERAS-US into +$8,504 of societal cost for MCI and a $2,638 per-person saving from slowing progression 30%, figures offered to inform value assessments of amyloid-targeting therapy. The earlier report of the same cohort, P-1000, found that over those same 36 months total societal costs did not rise while cognition worsened: approximately $2,430 down to $2,007 per month in MCI. The two are not arithmetically incompatible - one is a conditional coefficient, the other a marginal trajectory - but that is exactly the point: the conditional coefficient has never been shown to reproduce any observed expenditure path, and no corpus record reconciles the pair. The wider economic case that motivates MCI early detection rests on the same footing: P-977, the corpus's canonical burden reference, states its own cost estimates are model-based. The unmet study is a validation of a cost-of-progression coefficient against realised, individually linked expenditure, which matters because these coefficients are used as if they were measurements to justify screening programmes and reimbursement decisions.

gaps.gap_statement: In longitudinal MCI cohorts the patient's cognitive state is observed only at scheduled visits, and the schedules behind the corpus's transition quantities differ by up to sixfold (annual CDR staging in P-1157; approximately annual ADNI visits behind P-1135's transition curves; a 3-year assessment interval in P-1108; 4-6-year intervals in P-950). Several of these papers name their own schedule as a threat to their own headline quantity - P-1136 records that 'reversion/consistency metrics depend on visit cadence', P-1135 that its 'MCI definition [is] dependent on visit-driven diagnosis' with 'reversion inferred from state changes which may include measurement noise', P-1157 that it 'relies on annual CDR which may lag true dementia onset', and P-1113 that there is 'potential misclassification of NC-AD transitions' behind its 208 apparently-direct normal-cognition-to-AD converters. Yet no study in this evidence set re-estimates its OWN transition probabilities, conversion hazards or trajectory taxonomy after systematically thinning its OWN visit series to a longer interval - an analysis its existing data already support at zero additional cost. The absence matters because the schedule is the sampling rate of the outcome, not a nuisance covariate: it determines whether a state a patient passed through is seen at all, so a claimed biological phenotype (P-1113's 'direct' NC-to-AD route, 208 of 542) and quantitative transition curves (P-1135's reversion probability rising 2% -> 8% and post-reversion re-progression 8% -> 35.71% by year 10) cannot be separated from what each study's calendar could resolve, while progression and reversion rates from differently-scheduled cohorts are pooled and compared as if the calendar were neutral.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern that a gap should challenge a temporal or ground-truth assumption and expose a data-structure violation ('ML architectures force continuous, interval-censored multi-visit clinical trial data into artificial, discrete cross-sectional binary labels' and 'prognostic models treat CNS markers as absolute ground truth, failing to map the temporal lag'). It is non-obvious because the corpus's most methodologically sophisticated papers are the ones it indicts: P-1135 and P-1140 are exactly the trajectory-aware, interval-censored analyses the field prescribes as the remedy, and both still treat the calendar as given. It is also actionable with data already in hand - thinning an existing visit series is a re-analysis, not a new cohort - and it has a falsifiable target: if P-1113's 208 'direct' NC-to-AD converters largely disappear when a matched cohort is analysed at a finer interval, a published disease phenotype dissolves into a sampling artefact.
gaps.closure_criteria: In one cohort with at least annual visits and >=1,000 baseline MCI participants (NACC or an ADNI-scale research cohort), estimate the same multistate model on (a) the full visit series and (b) series systematically thinned to 2-year and 4-year intervals, and report for each schedule: the MCI-to-normal reversion probability curve, the MCI-to-dementia transition intensity, and the proportion of normal-cognition-to-AD converters classified as 'direct' (no observed intermediate MCI visit), each with a confidence interval for the between-schedule difference. The gap is closed when at least one study reports those three deltas; it is closed as a null if the deltas are shown to be small relative to their confidence intervals.

gaps.gap_statement: The headline conclusion of the neuropsychological-prognosis papers in this pack is almost always a CONTRAST - between sexes, between two predictors, between two outcome definitions, between two raters, between two diagnostic criteria - and in each case the paper reports the two stratum-specific estimates but never the difference between them, so the quantity the conclusion actually asserts is absent from the record. P-1142 concludes depressive-symptom trajectories predict decline and conversion 'only in men with MCI' from 'linear mixed-effects models (separately by sex)' with HR 2.69 in men against 1.37 and 1.25 non-significant in women, and reports no sex-by-trajectory interaction estimate. P-1126 concludes 'motor variability (not mean) carried the cognitive signal' because 'variability (but not mean performance) predicted MMSE change', with no test of the mean-versus-variability difference. P-1097 reports 'Hippocampus volume, but not WBV, was associated with conversion' with no hippocampus-versus-whole-brain contrast. P-1109 concludes 'SP-ECog-12 gave higher prognostic value than self/PT ratings' from paired ratings of the same instrument by the same participants (HR 3.34 vs 9.61, 1.44 vs 2.82, 0.93 vs 1.82) with no paired comparison. P-1095 finds a predictor significant on a continuous outcome and null on the dichotomous one and files the divergence as an unresolved problem. P-1136 runs the mirror-image error, concluding two MCI criteria 'showed comparable risk of dementia over time' from an absence of difference with no hazard ratio, confidence interval or equivalence margin. Even P-1150, the one paper here fitting an explicit interaction model, reports only the subgroup hazards (7.6 for e4/4, 2.3 for e3/4) and not the interaction contrast. The absence matters because differential claims are the corpus's route from association to stratified clinical action - sex-specific depression screening, choosing motor variability over mean, treating the two MCI criteria as interchangeable, preferring informant to self-report - and none of these can enter a meta-analysis, a guideline or a downstream synthesis as an effect, because no effect for the difference was ever estimated.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern in which the deep defect is how a result is framed rather than which result was obtained ('ML architectures force continuous, interval-censored multi-visit clinical trial data into artificial, discrete cross-sectional binary labels'; 'XAI relies on descriptive feature attribution without proving it improves clinician decision-making'). It is non-obvious in three ways. First, it unifies six papers whose surface topics are unrelated - depression trajectories, upper-limb motor variability, MRI volumetry, informant ratings, dispersion indices, diagnostic criteria - under one missing quantity. Second, it captures both directions of the error in the same record: the difference-in-significance conclusion (P-1142, P-1126, P-1097, P-1109) and its mirror, equivalence inferred from a null (P-1136). Third, it is self-limiting in the right way - P-1150 shows the interaction model is routinely fitted in this literature, which makes this a recoverable reporting omission rather than a methodological impossibility, and every listed quantity can be produced by refitting existing data.
gaps.closure_criteria: For each contrast type, one study reporting the difference itself with an interval: (a) a pooled model on an ADNI-scale MCI cohort (N>=800) reporting the sex-by-depressive-trajectory interaction hazard ratio with 95% CI, rather than two sex-stratified hazard ratios; (b) a within-participant paired comparison of informant-rated versus self-rated function on the same instrument (N>=500), reporting the difference in hazard ratio or in C-index with a confidence interval; (c) a criteria comparison in a population cohort (N>=1,000, follow-up >=10 years) with a pre-specified equivalence margin (e.g. hazard-ratio ratio within 0.80-1.25) formally tested rather than equivalence inferred from a non-significant difference. The gap is closed when studies of this design exist for the contrasts the corpus already asserts.

gaps.gap_statement: MMSE and MoCA are used across the MCI literature as interchangeable readouts of global cognition - swapped freely as the OUTCOME of an intervention synthesis and as the cognitive COVARIATE of a conversion model - but the exchange has never been costed. In the two corpus studies that run the same analysis twice, once per instrument, the answer changes. An MCI-only Bayesian network meta-analysis of 46 acupuncture/moxibustion RCTs ranks a different regimen first on MMSE than on MoCA and finds 13 of 19 regimens beating control on MMSE against only 7 of 21 on MoCA (P-1235); a 250-patient Thai conversion cohort finds vitamin D deficiency a significant predictor of 1-year MCI-to-dementia conversion (OR 3.13, 95% CI 1.04-9.44) in the model adjusted for baseline MMSE, and not significant when baseline MoCA is substituted as the only changed term (P-964). Neither paper reports its own divergence as a result: P-1235's stated limitations name heterogeneity, publication bias and inconsistency, and P-964's significance line carries the vitamin D association forward unqualified. SPECIFIC UNMET NEED (asserted for THIS CORPUS): no corpus study reports a concordance statistic between its instrument-specific results, a between-instrument test of the difference, or any estimate of the instrument-attributable component of an MCI treatment ranking or risk-factor effect. WHY IT MATTERS: instrument choice is not random - it tracks trial vintage, country of the trial base and the ceiling behaviour of MMSE at the MCI stage - so the instrument term is a systematic, directional, unmeasured component of the effect estimates and treatment hierarchies that this literature publishes as clinical guidance, and neither of the two routes the corpus actually takes measures it: analysing the scales separately (P-1235, P-705) leaves two unreconciled answers, and pooling them into a unit-free standardised mean difference (P-692) assumes exactly the exchangeability that P-1235 and P-964 fail to display.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches two gold patterns at once: 'a measurement never calibrated across settings' (the gold OCT vendor-shift and EEG multi-site gaps) and 'an assumption nobody tests' (the gold handedness-confound gap NEW-G-21, where a known modulator is simply never modelled). It is non-obvious for three reasons. First, both demonstrating papers publish BOTH arms openly - the discordance is sitting in print and is treated as two results rather than as one result about the instruments, which is why keyword mining misses it. Second, the obvious remedy is itself the untested assumption: pooling MMSE and MoCA into a standardised mean difference (P-692, and the practice VF-30 flags) does not remove the instrument term, it standardises it away unexamined. Third, it inverts the usual reading of P-964: the paper is catalogued in this corpus as a conversion-rate benchmark with a 'novel vitamin D deficiency association', and the finding that actually generalises is the fragility of that association to a covariate swap.
gaps.closure_criteria: TWO-PART, both runnable on data that already exists. (a) SYNTHESIS ARM: restrict an MCI-only intervention network to the PAIRED subset of trials that report BOTH MMSE and MoCA (P-1235 records 42 of 46 trials contributing MMSE and 37 contributing MoCA, so a paired subset exists), re-run the network meta-analysis twice on that FIXED trial set, once per instrument, and report (i) the rank correlation between the two SUCRA orderings with a credible interval, (ii) whether the first-placed regimen is the same, and (iii) the per-regimen difference in mean difference after equating the two scales. A first-place change on the paired subset would establish that the instrument, not the evidence base, moves the hierarchy. (b) COHORT ARM: in one MCI conversion cohort with both instruments administered at baseline (P-964's design: N >= 250, 1-year or longer conversion endpoint), refit an identical risk-factor model with MMSE and with MoCA as the cognitive covariate and report a formal test of the difference between the two exposure coefficients (e.g. bootstrap or seemingly-unrelated-estimation difference-of-coefficients test with a CI), not two separately reported models. The gap closes when either arm reports the instrument-attributable component with an interval.

gaps.actor_justification: Matches two gold patterns at once: 'a measurement never calibrated across settings' (the gold OCT vendor-shift and EEG multi-site gaps) and 'an assumption nobody tests' (the gold handedness-confound gap NEW-G-21, where a known modulator is simply never modelled). It is non-obvious for three reasons. First, both demonstrating papers publish BOTH arms openly - the discordance is sitting in print and is treated as two results rather than as one result about the instruments, which is why keyword mining misses it. Second, the obvious remedy is itself the untested assumption: pooling MMSE and MoCA into a standardised mean difference (P-692, and the practice VF-30 flags) does not remove the instrument term, it standardises it away unexamined.
