gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest demonstration is confounded in the direction that weakens it. P-1235's MMSE network (42 studies, 19 regimens) and MoCA network (37 studies, 21 regimens) are not the same trials, so the change of first-placed regimen may be entirely a change of evidence base - ACP+CT+EARA may simply have no MoCA data and be absent from the second network - rather than a property of the instruments. On the cohort side, P-964's two models differ only in the covariate, but MMSE and MoCA also differ in ceiling behaviour at the MCI stage, so the disappearance of the vitamin D effect under MoCA adjustment may reflect better confounding control by the more sensitive instrument, which would be an argument for preferring MoCA rather than evidence of an unmeasured instrument term. Both readings are consistent with the record's absence clause - nobody has partitioned them - but a reviewer could fairly hold that the field's implicit answer (use the more sensitive instrument at the MCI stage) already settles the practical question, leaving this a reporting deficiency rather than a research gap. The closure test is designed to break exactly this tie by fixing the trial set before varying the instrument.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: not a 'no study combines X with Y' claim. Nothing is being asked to be combined; the record names a specific exchangeability assumption and the specific statistic (rank concordance / difference-of-coefficients) that would test it.

RESTATEMENT: distinguished by id from ACTOR-G-022, G-023, G-016, G-017, G-033, G-349, G-009, G-14, G-029, VF-30 and MINE-G-004 in the why_new field, with the discriminating clause stated for each. The nearest, MINE-G-004, differs in quantity (adherence vs instrument), literature and MCI-specificity, and its own record explicitly endorses same-shape siblings on distinct quantities as non-duplicates.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: no corpus paper performs MMSE-MoCA equating, agreement or interchangeability analysis (grep over all 540 digests for crosswalk / equating / equipercentile / conversion table / interchangeab / Bland-Altman). The four corpus papers that analyse both instruments report the arms and never the comparison.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the absence clause was deliberately narrowed after checking the record's own citations. It does NOT say 'no corpus study analyses two scales' - P-1235, P-705, P-692 and P-964 all do, and all four are cited here. It says no study reports a concordance statistic, a between-instrument test, or an instrument-attributable estimate, which each cited paper's own record confirms rather than contradicts.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: MMSE-MoCA score crosswalks and equating tables do exist outside this corpus, and this record does not deny them - they map score LEVELS between instruments within one sample and say nothing about whether a treatment hierarchy or a risk-factor coefficient survives the swap, which is the quantity named here. Absence is asserted for THIS CORPUS only, following the MINE-G-003 convention.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: every quote is tagged with the summary field it came from. The two quotes drawn from '### What is the significance?' (P-1235's recommendation, P-964's framing) are used only to characterise what those papers ASSERT or RECOMMEND - which is precisely the object of the critique - and never as measured findings. All quantitative legs come from '### What are the outcomes? (Results)', '### Key findings reported' or '### What is the sample size?'.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every evidence paper's own block contains MMSE and MoCA and the analysis being characterised; no inferential bridge is required from any cited paper's finding to the gap's construct. P-1180, which does NOT carry the construct, is explicitly marked context-only and supplies no evidence leg.

MISASSIGNED_MEASUREMENT_FAMILY: MMSE and MoCA are the same measurement family - brief clinician-administered global cognitive screeners - and that is the point of the record, not a manufactured contrast. A tempting extra leg (P-1180's 25(OH)D correlating with MoCA at r=0.185 and SDMT at r=0.11) was DROPPED precisely because MoCA and SDMT are different families (global screener vs processing-speed test), so a difference between them is expected and proves nothing.

TOO_SPECIFIC: the record spans four papers, two literatures (evidence synthesis and observational cohorts), two roles for the instrument (outcome and covariate) and two continents' trial bases; the closure test is a general procedure, not a single-study repair.
DATA_SCARCITY: no new data collection is required. Both closure arms are re-analyses of datasets that already exist (P-1235's paired trial subset; P-964's cohort with both instruments at baseline).

NOT_IN_SCOPE: measurement of the instruments that define and track MCI is squarely in scope; the corpus already carries accepted records on label operationalisation (G-017, G-033), assay-platform transport (G-029) and calibration transport (G-14).
gaps.dedup_note: Checked by id against every adjacent record. ACTOR-G-022 (intervention results reported as cognitive-scale change with no anchor to disease course) is about what a scale point MEANS for the disease; this record is about which of two scales you read changing WHICH TREATMENT WINS - G-022 would be equally true if only one scale existed. VF-30 (pooled MCI intervention estimates fragile, in part because 'non-interchangeable outcome scales pooled as unit-free SMDs') asserts non-interchangeability as a FINDING and a reason for fragility; it does not name the missing measurement, and P-1235 shows the problem survives when the scales are NOT pooled, which VF-30 does not cover. ACTOR-G-023 (no closed loop, transitivity assumed, hierarchies unfalsifiable) is about network geometry - P-1235 actually runs node-splitting, and its two rankings would diverge even in a perfectly connected network. MINE-G-004 is the structural SIBLING and should be cross-linked, not merged: same shape (one synthesis, two rankings, no reconciliation) but a different quantity (achieved dose/adherence vs outcome instrument), a different literature (reminiscence therapy) and - importantly - G-004 carries a mandatory caveat that it is NOT MCI-specific because P-615 pools dementia+MCI, whereas P-1235 is MCI-only, so this record supplies the MCI-specific instance that G-004 could not. ACTOR-G-017 and ACTOR-G-033 both concern the diagnostic/outcome LABEL (ascertainment rule, conversion window, prevalent-MCI criteria) and their closure tests vary the LABEL; this record varies the OUTCOME MEASURE and the COVARIATE while holding the label fixed - in P-964 the case definition, the cohort and the conversion endpoint are all identical between Model 1 and Model 2. ACTOR-G-016 concerns measurement SOURCE (self vs informant vs objective); both MMSE and MoCA are clinician-administered objective instruments, so G-016's dichotomy does not reach this. G-349 asks for a harmonised outcome battery across three named reviews to ENABLE pooling; this record asks for the discordance to be QUANTIFIED, which is the prior question and is answerable without any new trial. ACTOR-G-009 (undefined 'multi-ingredient' arm makes a nutritional NMA ranking uninterpretable) is about arm definition, not outcome measurement. G-14 (calibration under domain shift) and ACTOR-G-029 (assay-platform domain shift for fluid classifiers) are the same family one level away - transport across measurement platforms - but neither touches administered cognitive instruments.

gaps.gap_statement: THE COMPARATOR ARM OF AN MCI INTERVENTION TRIAL IS TREATED AS A FIXED ZERO POINT, YET ITS OBSERVED PRE-POST TRAJECTORY VARIES IN SIGN AND IN A MAGNITUDE THAT RIVALS THE TREATMENT EFFECT ITSELF - AND NO CORPUS SYNTHESIS EXTRACTS, REPORTS OR MODELS THAT TRAJECTORY. A between-group standardised mean difference is the difference of two trajectories, but only one of them is ever inspected. In this pack the comparator arms move in both directions at rates that cannot both be natural history: P-694's blank control LOST 0.57 MMSE points in 30 days (22.40 -> 21.83) while its intervention arm gained 1.26, so the whole ANCOVA contrast (partial eta-squared 0.325) is driven jointly by one arm rising and the other falling; P-700's control declined significantly on four separate instruments over roughly four months (IADL 4.85 -> 4.25, WCST categories 1.75 -> 1.10, Symbol Span 16.45 -> 14.35, Digit Span forward 5.70 -> 5.10), which is what produces its between-group d values of 1.51 to 1.96; and at the opposite extreme P-714's active comparator GAINED 3.4 MoCA points in 12 weeks (22.8 -> 26.2, p = 0.004) against an intervention gain of 2.7, giving a between-group p of exactly 1.000. THE CONSEQUENCE IS A SCALE FAILURE, NOT A SINGLE-TRIAL FLAW: an identical intervention gain of about three points yields d ~ 1.5 against a deteriorating comparator and p = 1.000 against an improving one, so the effect sizes that MCI intervention meta-analyses pool are not measured against a common reference. The syntheses that pool them describe the resulting dispersion but never test this source of it. P-705 pools 18 RCTs at I-squared 92 per cent (MMSE) and 89 per cent (MoCA), attributes the dispersion to stimulation parameters, and concedes in its own appraisal that 'no meta-regression is run'; P-692 publishes a memory pool of SMD 2.54 at I-squared 93 per cent with no leave-one-out or outlier check; P-759 pools trials whose control arms are donepezil (3), nimodipine (6), sham acupuncture (2), sham acupoint (2), rTMS (1) and wait-list (1) into a single MMSE MD of 1.09 with no comparator-stratified estimate printed. Comparator identity and comparator trajectory are both recorded in the primary trials and both discarded at the synthesis step. WHAT IS ABSENT IS NOT A NEW TRIAL BUT A RE-ANALYSIS OF DATA ALREADY IN THE CORPUS. CLOSURE TEST: take an existing MCI-intervention meta-analysis (P-692, 10 RCTs / 1,017 participants, or P-705, 18 poolable RCTs / 1,074 participants), extract for each included trial the CONTROL-arm baseline-to-endpoint change on the pooled instrument together with its comparator class (blank/no-treatment, waitlist, education-only, active dose-matched), then (a) meta-regress the pooled effect on control-arm change and report the proportion of tau-squared explained, and (b) re-report the pooled effect within comparator class. The gap closes when at least one MCI intervention synthesis prints both. SCOPE (mandatory): this is an absence of EXTRACTION AND MODELLING, not of measurement - every primary trial cited here prints its control-arm values, and P-690 additionally verified comparator-arm exercise dose by heart-rate bracelet, so the covariate is recoverable from published tables. The claim is stated for the 30 intervention papers examined in this pack and for the three syntheses named; it is not asserted for corpus syntheses outside that set.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'a calibration or transfer failure' and 'a temporal or ground-truth assumption': the field treats the comparator arm as an assumed-stable reference in exactly the way the gold OCT gap treats a single vendor as an assumed-stable device, and the consequence is the same - published effect sizes are not on one scale. It is non-obvious in three ways. First, the two failure directions are usually discussed separately (practice effects inflate placebo arms; control decline inflates contrasts) and are here shown to coexist inside one 30-paper intervention set, which is what makes the pooled scale incoherent rather than merely biased. Second, it names a covariate that is already printed in the primary papers and therefore closes without new data collection, which distinguishes it from a DATA_SCARCITY complaint. Third, it supplies a candidate explanation for the one quantity these syntheses report and cannot explain - I-squared of 89 to 93 per cent - so the closure test is falsifiable in a strong sense: if control-arm change explains no tau-squared, the record is refuted.
gaps.closure_criteria: Take an existing MCI-intervention meta-analysis (P-692, 10 RCTs / 1,017 participants, or P-705, 18 poolable RCTs / 1,074 participants), extract for each included trial the CONTROL-arm baseline-to-endpoint change on the pooled instrument together with its comparator class (blank/no-treatment, waitlist, education-only, active dose-matched), then (a) meta-regress the pooled effect on control-arm change and report the proportion of tau-squared explained, and (b) re-report the pooled effect within comparator class. The gap closes when at least one MCI intervention synthesis prints both.

It is non-obvious in three ways. First, the two failure directions are usually discussed separately (practice effects inflate placebo arms; control decline inflates contrasts) and are here shown to coexist inside one 30-paper intervention set, which is what makes the pooled scale incoherent rather than merely biased. Second, it names a covariate that is already printed in the primary papers and therefore closes without new data collection, which distinguishes it from a DATA_SCARCITY complaint. gaps.critic_falsification: The three comparator conditions are not the same kind of object - P-694's is a blank no-treatment control, P-700's is never specified in the paper at all, and P-714's is an active motor-cognitive training arm - so part of the sign reversal is explained trivially by comparator class rather than by any unmodelled instability, and a reviewer could argue the fix is simply to report comparator class (which P-759 already prints) rather than to model a trajectory. The record survives that objection only because the two DECLINING comparators are the ones whose digests call the decline implausible on its own terms, but the strength of the record would be higher if a corpus trial existed in which two same-class comparators moved in opposite directions.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no modality or method pairing is proposed; the missing object is a covariate in an existing analysis, not a combination of X with Y.

RESTATEMENT: distinguished by id from G-NEW-1042-A, MINE-G-004, MINE-G-002, ACTOR-G-022, ACTOR-G-023 and G-349 in why_new; the closest (G-NEW-1042-A) is contradicted in direction by this record's central evidence.

TOO_SPECIFIC: the claim spans three primary trials in three countries with three different interventions and three independent syntheses covering tDCS, traditional Chinese exercise and acupuncture; it is not one paper's limitation.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: the three syntheses named are the corpus's own quantitative pools for their intervention classes, and the absence is quoted from their appraisals ('no meta-regression is run'); no corpus synthesis in this pack prints a comparator-stratified or comparator-change-adjusted estimate.
DATA_SCARCITY: the required data are already published - every trial cited prints its control-arm baseline and endpoint values, so this is a modelling absence, not a data limitation.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: control-arm response is a standard meta-regression covariate in other fields (for example placebo-response modelling in depression trials), which is precisely why its absence from the MCI intervention syntheses is a defect in THIS literature rather than an unexplored idea; the record claims the absence for the named corpus syntheses only, not for science at large.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: the object is the analysis of MCI intervention trial data already in the corpus, not trial design policy or drug development.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the only universal clause ('no comparator-stratified or comparator-change-adjusted estimate') was checked against each cited paper - P-705's appraisal states no meta-regression was run, P-692 reports no sensitivity or leave-one-out analysis, and P-759 prints comparator composition in its characteristics table without a comparator-stratified estimate in the digest; none of the six cited papers performs the analysis the record says is missing.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper's own text uses the vocabulary of the gap - control/comparator arm values, heterogeneity, meta-regression - and no leg rests on an inferential bridge from an unrelated finding.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked against every T08 theme gap and against the corpus gap list by keyword (control arm / comparator / attention-matched / practice effect / regression to the mean / heterogeneity / meta-regression / moderator). (1) G-NEW-1042-A is the nearest and is NOT this: it asserts that trials fail to correct for short-term PRACTICE EFFECTS, which act in one direction (upward) inside a placebo arm; this record's core observation is the opposite and is what G-1042-A cannot accommodate - two of the three comparator arms here move DOWNWARD at rates the digests call implausible, and P-694's own appraisal states explicitly that the decline 'cannot be explained by practice effects, which would push scores up'. The gap is the absence of any modelled comparator trajectory, of either sign, at synthesis level. (2) MINE-G-004 covers syntheses failing to condition on ACHIEVED DOSE OR OBSERVED ADHERENCE of the intervention; the covariate here is the comparator's change score and comparator class, a different quantity on a different arm, and G-004's own checked list (P-642, P-655, P-683, P-705, P-673, P-674, P-679, P-692, P-615) was interrogated for adherence, not for control-arm trajectory. (3) ACTOR-G-022 says intervention results are never anchored to disease course (no conversion or biomarker endpoint) - an endpoint-choice gap, not a comparability-of-scale gap. (5) MINE-G-002 (no pooled post-cessation timepoint) is about WHEN the outcome is measured, not about what the comparator did between measurements. (6) G-349 concerns outcome-instrument harmonisation across reviews, not comparator behaviour.

gaps.gap_statement: NUTRITIONAL AND WHOLE-FOOD TRIALS IN MCI REPORT NULLS WITHOUT EVER ESTABLISHING THAT THE RANDOMISED EXPOSURE CONTRAST WAS ACHIEVED, SO THE FIELD'S ACCUMULATED NUTRITION NULL CANNOT BE SIGNED - IT IS EQUALLY CONSISTENT WITH 'THE NUTRIENT DOES NOT WORK' AND WITH 'THE NUTRIENT WAS NEVER DIFFERENTIALLY DELIVERED'. Assignment is being read as exposure. Where the corpus does measure exposure, assignment and exposure come apart, and in both directions. P-740 randomised 163 institutionalised patients (93 amnestic MCI, 70 mild-to-moderate AD) to pure EPA, pure DHA, EPA+DHA or placebo for 24 months, returned a flat null on every prespecified endpoint (adjusted p: ADAS-cog 0.42, MMSE 0.11, QOL 0.54, ADCS-ADL 0.44, GDS 0.57) - and its own exposure biomarker went the WRONG WAY: erythrocyte n-3 FELL in the supplemented arms, with no adherence figure, no pill count, no interim biomarker and no per-protocol or achieved-exposure analysis anywhere in the report; its single significant baseline imbalance also falls on that same exposure variable (RBC EPA 1.23, 0.83, 1.32, 0.87 per cent of total fatty acids, p = 0.03). P-756 measured habitual intake and found the randomised dose contrast partly dissolved before the trial began: group mean usual anthocyanin intake was 13.9 mg (control), 68.1 mg (low-dose) and 73.3 mg (high-dose), so the low-dose arm's habitual intake (68 mg) already exceeded the 47-48 mg/day it was assigned, and its null on every outcome is uninterpretable as a dose effect. P-724, the third whole-food trial, reports a clean primary null (no TIME by TREATMENT interaction on any of seven cognitive, three mood or eight blood-pressure outcomes) and its appraisal directs the reader to 'Treat as unmeasured: bioavailability, adherence, blinding success, batch effects and pandemic-wave effects.' WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE THREE TRIALS: these unsigned nulls are already being counted as evidence at field level. P-684's umbrella map of 57 systematic reviews records nutrition as its negative cell - 'no evidence for improving cognition' - a conclusion about nutrient efficacy assembled from trials that never demonstrated nutrient delivery. THE DESIGN THAT WOULD SETTLE IT EXISTS IN THE CORPUS BUT HAS NEVER BEEN PAIRED WITH A COGNITIVE ENDPOINT: P-713's network meta-analysis shows biochemical verification is routine in the methyl-nutrient arm of the same literature, with all three regimens credibly lowering serum homocysteine against control (folate+B12 -4.23, -5.46 to -3.17), proving delivery - yet P-713 could produce no pooled cognitive estimate at all because the constituent trials used heterogeneous scales. So the corpus contains verified delivery without a poolable cognitive endpoint, and cognitive endpoints without verified delivery, and no nutritional MCI trial reports a cognitive or clinical effect estimated as a function of ACHIEVED exposure. CLOSURE TEST: re-analyse an existing corpus dataset in which the exposure biomarker was already collected at baseline and endpoint - P-740 (163 randomised, 24 months, erythrocyte fatty acids by gas chromatography) is the ready case and its own appraisal names this as the untried analysis - estimating the ADAS-cog and MMSE effect per unit of ACHIEVED change in the biomarker using randomised assignment as an instrument (complier-average causal effect / instrumental-variable estimation, not a naive per-protocol split), and print that estimate beside the intention-to-treat estimate. Prospectively, an MCI nutritional RCT closes this gap by pre-specifying an exposure biomarker with a delivery pass/fail criterion, reporting habitual intake by arm at baseline, and reporting both ITT and achieved-exposure estimates. SCOPE (mandatory): stated for the nutritional and whole-food supplement trials in this 30-paper pack (P-740, P-756, P-724) and for the two syntheses that read or could have read them (P-684, P-713). It is NOT asserted for behavioural or device interventions, where the analogous quantity is session attendance rather than a biomarker.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'a temporal or ground-truth assumption' most directly - the field's ground truth for exposure is the randomisation list rather than the measured biology - and secondarily the 'clinical-utility' pattern in which an accumulated conclusion (nutrition does not help cognition in MCI) outruns what the underlying trials establish. It is non-obvious because the corpus reads the same trials as informative nulls, and because the disconfirming detail in each paper is buried in a place a synthesis never looks: an erythrocyte fatty-acid table whose supplemented arms went DOWN, and a baseline habitual-intake row whose low-dose mean exceeds the assigned dose. It also carries its own internal control: P-713 shows the verification design already exists one nutrient class over, which converts the record from 'trials are imperfect' into a specific, cheap, already-affordable design change. Finally, the closure test is a re-analysis of data already collected, so the gap is actionable rather than aspirational.
gaps.closure_criteria: Re-analyse an existing corpus dataset in which the exposure biomarker was already collected at baseline and endpoint - P-740 (163 randomised, 24 months, erythrocyte fatty acids by gas chromatography) is the ready case - estimating the ADAS-cog and MMSE effect per unit of ACHIEVED change in the biomarker using randomised assignment as an instrument (complier-average causal effect / instrumental-variable estimation, not a naive per-protocol split), and print that estimate beside the intention-to-treat estimate. Prospectively, an MCI nutritional RCT closes this gap by pre-specifying an exposure biomarker with a delivery pass/fail criterion, reporting habitual intake by arm at baseline, and reporting both ITT and achieved-exposure estimates.

It also carries its own internal control: P-713 shows the verification design already exists one nutrient class over, which converts the record from 'trials are imperfect' into a specific, cheap, already-affordable design change. Finally, the closure test is a re-analysis of data already collected, so the gap is actionable rather than aspirational.
gaps.critic_falsification: Conditioning on achieved exposure is conditioning on a post-randomisation variable, so the analysis this record asks for is not itself randomised evidence: participants whose erythrocyte n-3 rose may differ systematically (absorption, diet, adherence-correlated health behaviour) from those whose fell, and an instrumental-variable estimate rescues this only under exclusion-restriction and monotonicity assumptions that a four-arm supplement trial with 20 per cent attrition may not satisfy. A reviewer could therefore argue that the honest reading of P-740 is simply 'an ITT null with a delivery caveat attached' - which is what its own digest recommends - and that no additional estimate is licensed. The record's answer is that even an uninterpretable achieved-exposure estimate would bound the delivery explanation, and that the reporting half of the closure test (habitual intake by arm, a pre-specified delivery criterion) carries no such assumption; but the causal half is genuinely contestable.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no X-with-Y pairing is proposed; the missing object is an exposure-conditioned estimate within a single existing trial.
RESTATEMENT: distinguished by id from MINE-G-004 (attendance covariate in behavioural syntheses), ACTOR-G-009, ACTOR-G-052 and the ACTOR-G-044..074 absent-trial family in why_new.
TOO_SPECIFIC: three independent primary trials on two continents and two nutrient classes, plus the umbrella review that converts their nulls into a field verdict; not one paper's limitation.

DATA_SCARCITY: P-740 already collected erythrocyte fatty acids at baseline and endpoint and P-756 already collected 24-hour food records, so the data for the closure analysis exist; the absence is analytic.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: achieved-exposure and CACE analyses are established methodology in nutrition and cardiology trials, which is why their absence from MCI nutritional trials is a defect in this literature; the record asserts the absence for the named corpus papers, not for methodology at large, and its closure test is a re-analysis rather than a novel technique.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: each cited trial's own report is quoted as lacking the analysis - P-740's appraisal states no adherence figure, interim biomarker or per-protocol analysis exists; P-724's lists adherence and bioavailability as unmeasured; P-756 measured intake but reports no exposure-conditioned outcome estimate.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: this is analysis of MCI intervention data inside the corpus, not drug development or trial regulation.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the universal clause is deliberately narrow - 'no nutritional MCI trial here reports a cognitive or clinical effect estimated as a function of achieved exposure' - and was checked against every cited paper including P-713, which verifies exposure but produces no cognitive estimate, and P-756, which measures intake but reports no exposure-conditioned outcome; the record states P-713's partial closure on its face rather than claiming a clean absence.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every quoted paper's own text uses the gap's vocabulary (erythrocyte n-3, adherence, bioavailability, habitual intake, serum homocysteine); no leg rests on an inferential bridge.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: all quantitative quotes are results-field values (adjusted p values, RBC EPA percentages, intake means, homocysteine credible intervals); the only interpretive quotes are labelled as appraisals in their supports field.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked against the T08 theme gap file and the corpus gap list by keyword (adherence, achieved dose, per-protocol, compliance, omega-3, n-3, anthocyanin, supplement, nutrition). (1) MINE-G-004 is the closest and is scoped, in its own first line, to 'comparative-effectiveness syntheses of non-pharmacological interventions in POOLED dementia+MCI populations', and its missing covariate is session-completion or observed attendance in reminiscence/exercise syntheses; the papers it independently checked are P-642, P-655, P-683, P-705, P-673, P-674, P-679, P-692, P-615 - not one nutritional trial, and none of them measures a biological exposure marker. This record concerns primary pharmaconutritional trials and a biochemically measured exposure, and its closure test is an instrumental-variable re-analysis of a single existing trial rather than a network meta-regression. (2) ACTOR-G-009 (closed) concerns an undefined 'multi-ingredient' arm in a nutritional network meta-analysis - a composition-reporting defect, not an exposure-verification defect. (3) ACTOR-G-052 concerns glucose-lowering drugs needing a non-diabetic MCI control arm to separate glycaemic from neuroprotective effects - a comparator-design gap in a different intervention class. (4) ACTOR-G-044/045/046/053/056/074 concern absent endpoints or absent trials (dementia incidence, hearing intervention, sleep RCT, GABA+gamma, IVR control, CCT incidence) and none concerns whether a delivered exposure was verified. (5) G-CAND-22/23/43/44 are rejected per-paper limitation dumps. No existing record states that assignment is being read as exposure in MCI nutrition trials.

gaps.gap_statement: MCI INTERVENTION TRIALS EXCLUDE DEPRESSION AT ENROLMENT AND THEN MEASURE DEPRESSION AS AN OUTCOME, SO THE MOOD NULL ACCUMULATED IN THIS PACK IS A PROPERTY OF THE ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA RATHER THAN OF THE INTERVENTIONS - AND NO TRIAL REPORTS THE FRACTION OF ITS COHORT SITTING INSIDE THE SCALE'S NON-CLINICAL BAND, WHICH IS WHAT WOULD LET A READER SEE IT (baseline means and dispersions are printed, e.g. P-743's 4.00 (2.59) versus 6.33 (2.49) on the PHQ-9; the floor fraction is not). Three independent trials in this pack, in three countries with three unrelated interventions, each report a null depression outcome and each explain that null, in their own text, by their own exclusion of depressed participants. P-743 (Korea, nurse-delivered self-efficacy programme, n = 30) found depression the single non-significant outcome among five and its authors read it as a floor effect, with experimental-arm depression running 2.5 to 4.0 inside the PHQ-9 NON-DEPRESSION band of 0 to 4. P-712 (China, internet-assisted self-management, n = 68) reports 'no significant improvement in depression, attributing this to the exclusion of patients with severe depression'. P-740 (Taiwan, 24-month omega-3 RCT, n = 163) excluded every major DSM-IV-TR psychiatric disorder including major depression, ran baseline GDS means of 3.50 to 5.30 on a 30-point scale, and returned GDS at adjusted p = 0.57; its appraisal states plainly that 'the mood endpoint was built to fail'. P-724 supplies a fourth mood null (no TIME by TREATMENT interaction on any of three DASS-21 subscales) with no baseline mood distribution recoverable at all. THE ABSENCE THAT MATTERS IS NOT THE NULL BUT THE UNINTERPRETABILITY OF THE NULL: a scale administered to a cohort selected to sit at its floor cannot fall further, so these four results carry no information about whether the interventions affect mood, yet they enter narrative syntheses and abstracts as outcome results. WHY THIS ENDPOINT AND NOT ANOTHER: P-690's own framing states that depressive symptoms 'are among the most common neuropsychiatric features of MCI and a potential risk factor for progression to dementia, yet interventions are usually evaluated against cognition alone', so the endpoint being nullified by design is simultaneously the most prevalent comorbidity of the condition and a candidate modifier of its trajectory. THE CORPUS'S ONE ENRICHED TRIAL SHOWS WHAT IS BEING SUPPRESSED AND WHY IT IS NOT SETTLED: P-690 recruited older adults with BOTH MCI and depressive symptoms and produced the largest mood effect in the pack (GDS-30 9.10 +/- 4.10 versus 13.82 +/- 3.34 at three months, and median 6.00 versus 13.00 at six months) - but it allocated by community rather than at random, so site is 'perfectly aliased with treatment assignment' and it cannot settle the question it is the only trial positioned to ask. CLOSURE TEST: a randomised trial of a group-delivered non-pharmacological MCI intervention that ENROLS on a mood threshold (for example GDS-30 at or above 11, or PHQ-9 at or above 5) with a mood scale as the PRE-SPECIFIED PRIMARY endpoint and power computed for it, an attention-matched comparator, and the baseline mood distribution and the proportion of participants above the scale's floor reported; N >= 120 is implied by P-690's between-arm separation. A cheap partial closure is available immediately and is taken by none of the four null trials: report the baseline distribution of the mood scale and the fraction of the cohort inside its non-clinical band, so that a reader can tell a floor from an inert intervention. SCOPE AND EXCEPTIONS (mandatory): (a) stated for the intervention trials in this 30-paper pack, not asserted for corpus trials outside it; (b) P-689 is the counter-instance and is recorded as such - it obtained a significant depression difference (GDS 5.63 +/- 2.78 versus 7.38 +/- 2.86, t = -2.15, p = 0.037) in a cohort with no mood enrolment criterion, but it is non-randomised with a waiting-list comparator, its mood outcomes are self-reported with no blinding, and its own appraisal states the GDS result would not survive Bonferroni correction across roughly 21 comparisons; (c) the record does NOT claim that no MCI trial has ever enriched for depressive symptoms - P-690 did, and its non-randomised design, not its absence, is what leaves the question open; (d) outside the pack, P-675's review of group reminiscence in intact/MCI older adults records eight of seventeen trials enrolling participants with depressive symptoms and thirteen finding a between-group difference - a mood-enriched, depression-primary literature that does not separate MCI from intact participants and so does not meet the closure test.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern in which an objective-function or measurement framing is biased at the design stage rather than the analysis stage - the same shape as the curated 'progression is modelled, reversion is not' record, transposed to endpoints: the endpoint the field most plausibly moves is the one it makes unmovable before measuring. It is non-obvious because each trial's concession looks like an ordinary limitation in isolation and only becomes a structural finding when three unrelated trials are seen to make the same concession about the same endpoint; and because the corpus contains both halves of the demonstration - a floor-level cohort producing a null (P-740, GDS means 3.50 to 5.30 on a 30-point scale) and a symptom-enriched cohort producing a large effect on the same instrument family (P-690, GDS 9.10 versus 13.82) - so the mechanism is exhibited within the corpus rather than assumed. It also names a closure step that costs nothing (report the baseline mood distribution and the fraction inside the non-clinical band), which distinguishes it from a call for a new trial alone.
gaps.closure_criteria: A randomised trial of a group-delivered non-pharmacological MCI intervention that ENROLS on a mood threshold (for example GDS-30 at or above 11, or PHQ-9 at or above 5) with a mood scale as the PRE-SPECIFIED PRIMARY endpoint and power computed for it, an attention-matched comparator, and the baseline mood distribution and the proportion of participants above the scale's floor reported; N >= 120 is implied by P-690's between-arm separation. Partial closure: any of the null trials reporting the baseline distribution of the mood scale and the fraction of the cohort inside its non-clinical band.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern in which an objective-function or measurement framing is biased at the design stage rather than the analysis stage - the same shape as the curated 'progression is modelled, reversion is not' record, transposed to endpoints: the endpoint the field most plausibly moves is the one it makes unmovable before measuring. It is non-obvious because each trial's concession looks like an ordinary limitation in isolation and only becomes a structural finding when three unrelated trials are seen to make the same concession about the same endpoint; and because the corpus contains both halves of the demonstration - a floor-level cohort producing a null (P-740, GDS means 3.50 to 5.30 on a 30-point scale) and a symptom-enriched cohort producing a large effect on the same instrument family (P-690, GDS 9.10 versus 13.82) - so the mechanism is exhibited within the corpus rather than assumed. It also names a closure step that costs nothing (report the baseline mood distribution and the fraction inside the non-clinical band), which distinguishes it from a call for a new trial alone.
gaps.critic_falsification: Excluding participants with major depression from an MCI trial is defensible and standard - depression is a reversible cause of cognitive impairment, so admitting it contaminates the cognitive primary endpoint - and a reviewer can argue the field is not making an error but a correct trade-off, with the mood scale carried only as a safety and covariate measure that was never meant to be an efficacy endpoint. If that is the intended status, the record reduces to a reporting complaint. Two things keep it standing: the trials themselves present these nulls in abstracts and discussions as outcome findings rather than as safety monitoring (P-712's discussion offers the exclusion as an explanation for a result it nonetheless reports), and P-690 shows the trade-off is escapable by enrolling the comorbid population and powering for it. But the strength of the record depends on that reading of intent, which the papers do not state explicitly.

gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: MCI INTERVENTION TRIALS EXCLUDE DEPRESSION AT ENROLMENT AND THEN MEASURE DEPRESSION AS AN OUTCOME, SO THE FIELD'S ACCUMULATED MOOD NULL IS A PROPERTY OF THE ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA RATHER THAN OF THE INTERVENTIONS - AND NO TRIAL REPORTS THE BASELINE MOOD DISTRIBUTION THAT WOULD LET A READER SEE IT. Three independent trials in this pack, in three countries with three unrelated interventions, each report a null depression outcome and each explain that null, in their own text, by their own exclusion of depressed participants. P-743 (Korea, nurse-delivered self-efficacy programme, n = 30) found depression the single non-significant outcome among five and its authors read it as a floor effect, with experimental-arm depression running 2.5 to 4.0 inside the PHQ-9 NON-DEPRESSION band of 0 to 4. P-712 (China, internet-assisted self-management, n = 68) reports 'no significant improvement in depression, attributing this to the exclusion of patients with severe depression'. P-740 (Taiwan, 24-month omega-3 RCT, n = 163) excluded every major DSM-IV-TR psychiatric disorder including major depression, ran baseline GDS means of 3.50 to 5.30 on a 30-point scale, and returned GDS at adjusted p = 0.57; its appraisal states plainly that 'the mood endpoint was built to fail'. P-724 supplies a fourth mood null (no TIME by TREATMENT interaction on any of three DASS-21 subscales) with no baseline mood distribution recoverable at all. THE ABSENCE THAT MATTERS IS NOT THE NULL BUT THE UNINTERPRETABILITY OF THE NULL: a scale administered to a cohort selected to sit at its floor cannot fall further, so these four results carry no information about whether the interventions affect mood, yet they enter narrative syntheses and abstracts as outcome results. WHY THIS ENDPOINT AND NOT ANOTHER: P-690's own framing states that depressive symptoms 'are among the most common neuropsychiatric features of MCI and a potential risk factor for progression to dementia, yet interventions are usually evaluated against cognition alone', so the endpoint being nullified by design is simultaneously the most prevalent comorbidity of the condition and a candidate modifier of its trajectory. THE CORPUS'S ONE ENRICHED TRIAL SHOWS WHAT IS BEING SUPPRESSED AND WHY IT IS NOT SETTLED: P-690 recruited older adults with BOTH MCI and depressive symptoms and produced the largest mood effect in the pack (GDS-30 9.10 +/- 4.10 versus 13.82 +/- 3.34 at three months, and median 6.00 versus 13.00 at six months) - but it allocated by community rather than at random, so site is 'perfectly aliased with treatment assignment' and it cannot settle the question it is the only trial positioned to ask. CLOSURE TEST: a randomised trial of a group-delivered non-pharmacological MCI intervention that ENROLS on a mood threshold (for example GDS-30 at or above 11, or PHQ-9 at or above 5) with a mood scale as the PRE-SPECIFIED PRIMARY endpoint and power computed for it, an attention-matched comparator, and the baseline mood distribution and the proportion of participants above the scale's floor reported; N >= 120 is implied by P-690's between-arm separation. A cheap partial closure is available immediately and is taken by none of the four null trials: report the baseline distribution of the mood scale and the fraction of the cohort inside its non-clinical band, so that a reader can tell a floor from an inert intervention. SCOPE AND EXCEPTIONS (mandatory): (a) stated for the intervention trials in this 30-paper pack, not asserted for corpus trials outside it; (b) P-689 is the counter-instance and is recorded as such - it obtained a significant depression difference (GDS 5.63 +/- 2.78 versus 7.38 +/- 2.86, t = -2.15, p = 0.037) in a cohort with no mood enrolment criterion, but it is non-randomised with a waiting-list comparator, its mood outcomes are self-reported with no blinding, and its own appraisal states the GDS result would not survive Bonferroni correction across roughly 21 comparisons; (c) the record does NOT claim that no MCI trial has ever enriched for depressive symptoms - P-690 did, and its non-randomised design, not its absence, is what leaves the question open.

gaps.gap_statement: The MCI endpoint event that prevention and progression trials are powered on has had its RELIABILITY measured exactly once in this corpus, and it is only fair: blinded three-member committees reviewing the same case dossiers agreed with the examining site investigator on 71.0 per cent of them (Cohen's kappa 0.327 for MCI due to AD), agreement fell to 40.5 per cent on cases the investigator had himself diagnosed as MCI at two consecutive visits, and 41 of 96 trial endpoint events (42.7 per cent) came from participants whose own investigator did not think an endpoint had been reached. Nothing in the MCI intervention literature carries that number forward. Effect estimates, event-count power calculations and heterogeneity attributions all treat the conversion event and the MCI label as measured without error: the corpus's only conversion-endpoint review attributes its inability to pool to 'heterogeneity of interventions, populations, and outcomes' and never to ascertainment, and the syntheses and trials feeding this literature take the label as whatever their source studies said or as a single screening cut-off. The consequence is directional and under-appreciated: nondifferential endpoint misclassification attenuates conversion hazard ratios toward the null, so the borderline negative that anchors the field's prevention evidence (multidomain lifestyle HR 0.75, 95 per cent CI 0.55-1.02, p = 0.06) cannot presently be distinguished from a real effect degraded by endpoint noise, and no trial reports what its event count or its hazard ratio would be under an alternative adjudication rule. The gap is the missing propagation, not the missing measurement.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'Prognostic models treat central nervous system markers as absolute ground truth' and the ground-truth arm of 'no consensus on whether current MCI diagnostic criteria are compatible with computational models': it challenges the ground-truth assumption with a measured number rather than asserting an absence. It is non-obvious for two reasons. First, the corpus already contains the number and still nothing downstream uses it - the failure is propagation, which is invisible to any keyword search for the topic. Second, the direction of the consequence is counter-intuitive: nondifferential endpoint misclassification pushes conversion hazard ratios toward 1, so the finding at risk is the field's PESSIMISTIC one (P-882's HR 0.75, CI 0.55-1.02), not an inflated positive. That inverts the usual reading of endpoint noise as something that flatters results.
gaps.closure_criteria: Either (a) a re-analysis of an existing MCI intervention or prevention trial that holds an adjudication record - TOMMORROW's 648 dossiers are available through Vivli - reporting the primary effect estimate (HR or risk difference) under at least two ascertainment rules (investigator-only versus wide-net committee) plus a probabilistic bias analysis over the observed misclassification matrix, with the resulting change in the point estimate and interval stated; or (b) a prospective MCI prevention trial with N>=1,000 that pre-specifies duplicate independent endpoint adjudication on a random 20 per cent of dossiers, reports Cohen's kappa with 95 per cent CI for the MCI->dementia transition, and reports its primary hazard ratio both crude and corrected for the measured misclassification rate. Either would convert the reliability number from a process statistic into a term in the effect estimate.
gaps.modality: Clinical/neuropsychological adjudication (CDR, neuropsychological battery, investigator diagnosis); no imaging or digital modality
gaps.task_type: T6 (intervention outcome) with the endpoint drawn from T2 (MCI->dementia conversion) and T1 (NC->MCI)
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern 'Prognostic models treat central nervous system markers as absolute ground truth' and the ground-truth arm of 'no consensus on whether current MCI diagnostic criteria are compatible with computational models': it challenges the ground-truth assumption with a measured number rather than asserting an absence. It is non-obvious for two reasons. First, the corpus already contains the number and still nothing downstream uses it - the failure is propagation, which is invisible to any keyword search for the topic. Second, the direction of the consequence is counter-intuitive: nondifferential endpoint misclassification pushes conversion hazard ratios toward 1, so the finding at risk is the field's PESSIMISTIC one (P-882's HR 0.75, CI 0.55-1.02), not an inflated positive. That inverts the usual reading of endpoint noise as something that flatters results.
gaps.critic_falsification: The kappa I use to motivate the gap was measured on the WRONG transition for the trials the gap targets. P-866 adjudicated the NC->MCI-due-to-AD transition in genotype-selected, cognitively unimpaired volunteers - a boundary judgement that is intrinsically harder than the MCI->dementia conversion that P-882's four included studies score, where functional decline is more overt. A reviewer can fairly argue that dementia-conversion adjudication reaches a much better kappa, that the attenuation on HR 0.75 is therefore small, and that the record has imported a number from an adjacent and harder task. P-866 prints no MCI->dementia figure, so I cannot rebut this from the corpus; the honest position is that the size of the attenuation is unknown, which is itself part of the gap but weakens the specific claim about P-882's borderline null. Secondary objection: kappa is prevalence-sensitive, and in a cohort where events are rare a low kappa can coexist with high raw agreement (71.0 per cent here), so the raw number may overstate how much information the endpoint loses.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no modality or method combination is proposed anywhere in the record; the missing object is a statistical propagation step, not a pairing.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the absence clause is scoped to PROPAGATION precisely because P-866, which the record cites, does perform the MEASUREMENT. The record states this on its face and makes P-866 the partial closer. Likewise P-882's harmonisation call is quoted and explicitly distinguished rather than being contradicted by it.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: P-866 is named as the partial closer with what it leaves open (a kappa for the NC->MCI transition only, no misclassification-adjusted effect estimate, no MCI->dementia figure).

DATA_SCARCITY: the data already exist. TOMMORROW's 648 dossiers and the investigator-versus-committee cross-tabulation are published and the trial data are available through Vivli, and any trial that ran an adjudication committee already holds its own disagreement matrix; no new cohort is required.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: misclassification-adjusted survival analysis and sensitivity analysis for outcome misclassification are mature statistical methods, which is exactly why this is an APPLICATION failure inside the MCI intervention literature rather than a missing method. Stated openly, and the closure criterion below is an application of existing methods, not a request for new ones.
TOO_SPECIFIC: the gap spans a phase 3 trial endpoint, the corpus's only conversion-endpoint review, a 21-trial synthesis and a primary trial - four papers, four roles, one construct.
RESTATEMENT: distinguished by id from ACTOR-G-033, G-04, ACTOR-G-022, ACTOR-G-044 and G-NEW-1042-A in why_new.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: the construct's own vocabulary appears in every cited block - adjudication/agreement/kappa in P-866, conversion criteria and harmonisation in P-882, 'determined according to the description' in P-814, the MoCA cut-off as the whole MCI ascertainment in P-815. No leg rests on a paper that never mentions the construct.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: each quote is tagged with the field it came from. The kappa, the 40.5 per cent and the 42.7 per cent are reported measurements; the 'operationalised reliably enough' and 'what can be improved' sentences are labelled as digest appraisal and are used only to establish the absence of a propagation step, never as measured findings.

NOT_IN_SCOPE: the record is about how this corpus's own intervention and prevention evidence is measured and read, which is the T08 theme; the operator has confirmed records at the same level (ACTOR-G-022, G-023, G-044). It proposes no drug-development or trial-commissioning activity outside the corpus.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked by id against the theme file and a grep of all 535 statements in existing_gaps.md for kappa / inter-rater / interrater / adjudicat / label noise / ground truth: zero hits, so no existing record uses the reliability construct at all. Nearest neighbours checked individually: (1) ACTOR-G-033 says the MCI/conversion label is operationalised NON-COMPARABLY across studies and asks for one cohort held fixed while the label definition is varied - that is WHICH definition is used, between studies, with the consequence framed as classifier AUC/SHAP artefact. This record is about how reliably ONE fixed definition is applied by trained raters to the SAME dossier, measured as kappa, with the consequence framed as trial event count and hazard-ratio attenuation. Different quantity, different design to measure it, different downstream target. (2) G-04 (no consensus whether Petersen-style criteria suit computational models) is a criteria-design question, not a measured-reliability question. (3) ACTOR-G-022 (results reported on cognitive rating scales with no anchor to disease course) is about the meaning of the OUTCOME SCALE; this is about the ascertainment of the EVENT. (4) ACTOR-G-044 (no corpus study shows any intervention prevents MCI-to-dementia progression, anchored on the same P-882 null) is a result-level absence; this record supplies a specific, testable reason that null is uninterpretable, and cites P-882 for that role rather than restating G-044's claim. (5) G-NEW-1042-A (trials rarely correct for short-term practice effects) is a within-person retest gain on a continuous score, not between-rater disagreement on a binary event. (6) ACTOR-G-023, MINE-G-002, MINE-G-004 and G-349 are about indirect comparisons, durability pooling, adherence conditioning and outcome-battery harmonisation respectively - none touches ascertainment reliability. existing_records_core.md contains no VF/IA/CF/conflict mentioning kappa or adjudication.

evidence_quotes.supports: That the corpus's conversion-endpoint review enumerates its heterogeneity sources without endpoint ascertainment among them.

evidence_quotes.supports: That the remedy this literature does name is definitional harmonisation, which is a different quantity from how reliably any harmonised definition can be applied to a case - the distinction the gap turns on.

gaps.gap_statement: MCI intervention studies do not state, in advance or afterwards, how large a change on their own primary instrument would have to be to matter to a patient, and the one corpus synthesis that does apply published minimal clinically important differences finds its statistically significant pooled effects fall below them and says so. Without that interpretive threshold every conclusion in this literature is unbounded in one direction: a positive cannot be shown to be clinically meaningful (P-850 benchmarks its 2.1-point MoCA gain only against an unsourced '1-2 point' range from other trials; P-879 benchmarks a within-group d = 0.91 against FINGER and MAPT figures that are intervention-minus-control differences), a null cannot be shown to have excluded a clinically important effect (P-875's MoCA mean difference 1.06, 95 per cent CI -0.55 to 2.68, is reported as a negative trial without any statement of what size of benefit the interval rules out), an equivalence or non-inferiority claim cannot be specified at all (P-846 concludes 90 min/wk is comparable to 240 min/wk with no margin defined anywhere), and economic evaluation is blocked outright (P-849's cost per KQOL-AD point has no threshold to be compared against because that instrument's minimal important change in MCI is unknown). The MoCA is the modal primary endpoint across this pack; two corpus trials do invoke a MoCA threshold - P-257 runs an MCID responder analysis and P-815 cites a sourced 1-2 point clinically meaningful change (Zotcheva et al. 2022) - but neither pre-specifies or derives it in MCI, and the pack's own trials apply none. The absence is not that thresholds do not exist - P-873 uses published MMSE and ADAS-Cog values - but that this literature neither pre-specifies nor applies them, and P-873 demonstrates the test is decisive when it is applied, reversing a significant pooled result into one 'not demonstrated to be clinically meaningful'.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'Explainable AI relies on descriptive feature attribution without proving it provides actionable clinical reasoning' - a utility-and-interpretation critique rather than an existence claim - and the endpoint-substitution arm of the rubric. It is non-obvious because the corpus already contains the demonstration that the test is decisive: P-873 reaches significance on four outcomes and then, by applying published MMSE and ADAS-Cog thresholds, concludes the effects are not shown to be clinically meaningful. So this is not speculation about what an interpretive threshold would do to the field's results; it is an observed reversal in one corpus paper, with five papers in the same pack showing what happens in its absence, including the two failure modes a reader would not predict - the improvised external benchmark (P-850) and the cross-design benchmark (P-879). The record is also carefully NOT a claim that MCIDs do not exist, which is the trap the EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE code punishes.
gaps.closure_criteria: An anchor-based minimal clinically important difference for MoCA change over 3-12 months in a criterion-diagnosed MCI cohort of N>=200, derived against a patient-reported and an informant-reported global rating of change (and triangulated with a distribution-based minimal detectable change from a test-retest subsample), reported with a confidence interval and separately for MoCA total and for the memory index; followed by a re-reading of the corpus's MoCA-based MCI intervention trials against it, stating for each positive trial whether its point estimate and lower interval bound clear the threshold, and for each null trial whether its upper bound excludes it. A parallel derivation for KQOL-AD in MCI would close the economic arm that P-849 identifies.
gaps.modality: Neuropsychological and quality-of-life instruments (MoCA, MoCA-J, MMSE, ADAS-Cog, KQOL-AD, EQ-5D); no imaging or digital modality
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern 'Explainable AI relies on descriptive feature attribution without proving it provides actionable clinical reasoning' - a utility-and-interpretation critique rather than an existence claim - and the endpoint-substitution arm of the rubric. It is non-obvious because the corpus already contains the demonstration that the test is decisive: P-873 reaches significance on four outcomes and then, by applying published MMSE and ADAS-Cog thresholds, concludes the effects are not shown to be clinically meaningful. So this is not speculation about what an interpretive threshold would do to the field's results; it is an observed reversal in one corpus paper, with five papers in the same pack showing what happens in its absence, including the two failure modes a reader would not predict - the improvised external benchmark (P-850) and the cross-design benchmark (P-879). The record is also carefully NOT a claim that MCIDs do not exist, which is the trap the EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE code punishes.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is that fixing the threshold would legitimise the wrong endpoint rather than repair anything. P-850's own limitations concede that 'The use of MoCA as the primary outcome, while widely accepted, is a screening tool', and a 30-point screen administered twice is arguably not an instrument on which a clinically important difference is a coherent quantity at all - in which case the correct response is to abandon MoCA as a treatment endpoint, not to derive an MCID for it, and this record would be pointing at a symptom while naming the wrong cure. A second, narrower objection: two of the six legs (P-846's missing benchmark and P-879's cross-design comparison) rest on digest appraisal fields rather than on those papers' own words, so a verifier checking the source PDFs could find that either paper does discuss clinical importance in text the digest truncated - both digests carry explicit truncation markers - which would reduce the record from six papers to four.
fp_codes_cleared: EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: conceded on the face of the record. MMSE (2-4 points) and ADAS-Cog (2-3 points in MCI) thresholds exist in the wider literature and P-873 applies them. The asserted absence is (a) non-application within this intervention literature and (b) two instruments for which the corpus's own papers state the threshold is unavailable in MCI - KQOL-AD, stated verbatim by P-849, and MoCA change, for which no paper in the pack cites any value. The closure criterion is an anchor-based derivation plus a re-reading, not a request for a method that does not exist.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the record's own cited paper P-873 is the counterexample, is named as the partial closer, and the absence clause is written around it before any negative is asserted.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: P-873 is listed as the partial closer with exactly what it leaves open - MMSE and ADAS-Cog only, EVOO only, MCI and dementia pooled, no MoCA threshold, and no pre-specification since the comparison is post hoc.

RESTATEMENT: separated by id from ACTOR-G-022, G-349, G-023, MINE-G-004, G-NEW-1042-A, G-044 and G-033 in why_new, with the separation argued in both directions (what would close each, and what would not).
COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no modality or method pairing is proposed.

TOO_SPECIFIC: six papers across four intervention classes - dietary polyphenol, high-intensity functional training, herbal medicine with a health-economic arm, acupuncture plus deep TMS, and a multimodal community programme - all sharing one missing interpretive layer.

DATA_SCARCITY: an anchor-based MoCA MCID in MCI requires only an existing cohort with serial MoCA and a patient or informant global rating of change; several trials in the pack already hold serial MoCA on 60-450 participants. Nothing here is limited by data that cannot be collected.

NOT_IN_SCOPE: the record is about how this corpus's own intervention results are read and reported, which is the T08 theme; it proposes no drug development. Confirmed corpus records at the same level of analysis exist (ACTOR-G-022, G-023).

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper's own block uses the construct's vocabulary - MCID and 'clinically meaningful' in P-873, 'clinical-importance benchmark' and 'non-inferiority margin' in P-846, 'minimal change ... still unknown' in P-849, the '1-2 point' benchmark sentence in P-850, the mean difference and interval in P-875, and the FINGER/MAPT comparability sentence in P-879. No leg is an inferential bridge from a paper silent on the topic.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: every quote is tagged with its source field. P-873's MCID sentences are reported comparisons against published thresholds, not author assertions of importance; the P-846, P-879 and P-873-rarity quotes are labelled as digest appraisal and carry only the absence claim, never a measured finding.
gaps.dedup_note: Grepped all 535 statements in existing_gaps.md for 'minimal clinically important', 'clinically meaningful', 'MCID', 'minimal detectable change' and 'anchor-based': zero hits. No corpus gap uses the construct. Nearest neighbours checked by id: (1) ACTOR-G-022 says intervention results are reported as change on a cognitive rating scale with no anchor to DISEASE COURSE - no conversion endpoint, no functional endpoint beyond 30 days, no committed biomarker trajectory. That is EXTERNAL anchoring: does the scale change mean the disease was altered. This record is the WITHIN-instrument interpretability threshold: is the scale change large enough to matter to the patient on the scale's own units. The two are separable in both directions - P-873 performs the MCID test with no disease-course anchor whatsoever, and a trial could anchor to conversion and still not know its MCID - and this record covers three consequences G-022 does not touch: the null side (what a negative interval excludes), the equivalence side (no non-inferiority margin can be specified), and the economic side (no ICER threshold). (2) G-349 asks for a harmonised primary outcome BATTERY across the three most-cited reviews so effects can be POOLED - a comparability problem between studies, not an interpretability problem within one. (3) ACTOR-G-023 is about indirect comparison and unfalsifiable treatment hierarchies. (4) MINE-G-004 is about conditioning effects on achieved adherence. (5) G-NEW-1042-A is about practice-effect correction, i.e. the size of the artefact, not the size of the benefit that would matter. (6) ACTOR-G-044 says no intervention is shown to prevent conversion - a result-level absence about a different endpoint. (7) ACTOR-G-033 is about the label definition. None of these would be closed by an anchor-based MoCA MCID study, and this record would not be closed by any of their closure tests.

gaps.gap_statement: Exercise-in-MCI reviews issue dose prescriptions - 52 weeks, two to three sessions a week, 'moderate intensity' - while the intensity/volume variable those prescriptions rest on is not on a common scale and has never been fitted on one; the only fitted dose dimension in the corpus is weekly session frequency (P-698: 0.264 per session, 52.70 per cent of between-study variance; intensity not coded). Across one review's 29 charted trials, intensity is reported in mutually non-convertible units (per cent of maximal heart rate, absolute beats per minute, two different Borg scales with different ranges, per cent VO2max), so no dose-response function can be estimated even in principle from the pooled literature; a second review does not carry intensity as a column at all and records that the source literature does not agree on what the word denotes; a third states the intensity controversy twice while quantifying no dose-response and still recommending modalities at 'moderate intensity'; and the one meta-analysis that attempted prescription moderators reports that the resistance-training, intensity, session-time, high-frequency and long-duration strata all failed its own subgroup criteria for want of studies. The gap is not that the optimal dose is unknown - that is every review's stated limitation. It is that the field's dose guidance encodes a monotone dose-response that has never been estimated on a common metric, and that the one trial in this pack which randomised dose inside a single protocol found no gradient across a 2.7-fold contrast (90 versus 240 min/wk was not detectably different on 19 of 20 outcomes) with its single significant between-dose difference favouring the LOWER dose. So the prescriptions are derived from an uncalibrated between-study exposure and the only direct randomised test points the other way.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern of a measurement never calibrated across settings (the vendor-shift and cross-language gold gaps) and of an assumption nobody tests, applied to the exposure rather than the outcome. It is non-obvious in two ways. First, it separates a real structural claim from the generic limitation the corpus has already rejected once: 'optimal dose is unknown' is a per-paper limitation (G-CAND-322, rejected), whereas 'the dose variable cannot be placed on one axis, so no dose-response can be fitted even with more trials' is a property of the literature that more trials would not fix. Second, it does not rest on absence alone - it carries a direct falsifying observation. P-846 randomised the exposure inside one protocol across a 2.7-fold contrast that straddles the WHO thresholds the reviews cite, and found no gradient with the one significant difference favouring the lower dose. An absence claim paired with a within-study randomised contradiction is stronger evidence than either alone.
gaps.closure_criteria: A meta-regression over MCI exercise RCTs (>=25 trials) in which every trial's prescribed intensity is first converted to a single physiological metric - MET-minutes per week, or per cent heart-rate reserve with a published Borg-to-HRR mapping applied and the conversion assumptions stated - and total prescribed weekly volume entered as a continuous covariate, reporting the fitted slope on global cognition with a confidence interval, the residual heterogeneity explained, and a sensitivity analysis excluding trials whose intensity cannot be converted. A confirmatory second arm would be a within-trial randomised three-level dose contrast (for example 90, 150 and 240 min/wk) in criterion-diagnosed MCI, N>=250, powered for a trend test rather than for pairwise superiority, with a pre-specified equivalence margin. Closure requires either a fitted non-flat slope, which would license the field's prescriptions, or a flat one, which would retire them.
gaps.modality: Structured exercise interventions (aerobic, resistance, mind-body, multicomponent, dance, high-intensity functional training) with neuropsychological outcomes; no imaging or digital modality
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern of a measurement never calibrated across settings (the vendor-shift and cross-language gold gaps) and of an assumption nobody tests, applied to the exposure rather than the outcome. It is non-obvious in two ways. First, it separates a real structural claim from the generic limitation the corpus has already rejected once: 'optimal dose is unknown' is a per-paper limitation (G-CAND-322, rejected), whereas 'the dose variable cannot be placed on one axis, so no dose-response can be fitted even with more trials' is a property of the literature that more trials would not fix. Second, it does not rest on absence alone - it carries a direct falsifying observation. P-846 randomised the exposure inside one protocol across a 2.7-fold contrast that straddles the WHO thresholds the reviews cite, and found no gradient with the one significant difference favouring the lower dose. An absence claim paired with a within-study randomised contradiction is stronger evidence than either alone.
gaps.critic_falsification: P-839, P-845, P-814 and P-834 are syntheses of a partly shared pool of primary exercise trials, so they are four readings of one literature rather than four independent observations, and the record's breadth is weaker than its paper count implies. More seriously, a reviewer may reasonably hold that this belongs inside the family MINE-G-004 already nominates for merge with ACTOR-G-039 - 'nominal versus received dose' - on the ground that non-convertible nominal units and unmeasured received dose are two faces of the same failure to define exposure, in which case this should be folded in as the exercise-class leg rather than stand as its own record. The distinction I draw (units of the prescribed variable versus the gap between prescribed and delivered) is real but fine, and it is the operator's call. Finally, the falsifying leg is thin: P-846 is one 12-week trial in one modality with an over-recruited sample, no equivalence test and a baseline imbalance on the very outcome carrying its largest between-dose effect (TMT A pre-test means differ by 7.09 s), so its null is compatible with a real gradient that a two-occasion design could not detect.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no modality or method pairing is proposed. The missing object is a common exposure metric and a fitted dose-response, not a combination.

TOO_SPECIFIC: five papers from four independent author groups spanning dance, general exercise, executive-function-focused exercise and high-intensity functional training, at three evidence tiers (scoping review, narrative review, meta-analysis, RCT).

DATA_SCARCITY: not data-limited. The remedy is a unit conversion applied to trial characteristics already charted in these reviews plus a meta-regression, or a second within-trial randomised dose contrast; P-846 shows the latter is feasible at n=224 in 12 weeks.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: conceded openly. MET-minutes per week and per cent heart-rate-reserve are standard harmonisation metrics in physical-activity epidemiology, which is precisely why their absence from the MCI exercise syntheses is an application failure rather than a missing method. The record therefore claims non-application in this literature, not non-existence anywhere, and the closure test applies existing methods.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: P-834 is named as the partial closer - it attempted the prescription-parameter moderators and reports why they failed - and P-846 as the one direct randomised dose contrast, with what each leaves open stated.
RESTATEMENT: separated by id from ACTOR-G-039, MINE-G-004, G-CAND-322, MINE-G-002, ACTOR-G-023, G-349 and ACTOR-G-022 in why_new, in both directions.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the record asserts no 'no study does X' clause. Every negative is attributed to a named paper about its own analysis (P-845's unfitted dose-response, P-814's absent dose-response, P-834's failed strata), and the two papers that did attempt the analysis are cited as partial closers rather than as evidence of absence.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: intensity, dose or dose-response vocabulary appears in every cited block - the four charted unit types in P-839, 'dose-response ... has not been adequately established' in P-845, the intensity controversy in P-814, the named prescription strata in P-834, and the 90-versus-240 min/wk manipulation in P-846.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: each quote carries its source field. The P-839 units sentence and the P-845 'not a column' and P-846 'only numbers in the Discussion' sentences are digest appraisals and are labelled as such; the dose-response, intensity-controversy, recommendation, failed-strata and lower-dose sentences are the papers' own words.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: the record concerns how this corpus's own exercise-intervention evidence is measured and synthesised, which is the T08 theme; it proposes no drug or device development.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked by id against the theme file and by grep of existing_gaps.md for 'dose-response', 'exercise intensity', 'intensity of exercise', 'weekly dose', 'METs', 'Borg', 'incommensurable', 'common scale', 'harmonis', 'units'. Nearest neighbours: (1) ACTOR-G-039 - delivered electric-field dose never measured or modelled as exposure in MCI neuromodulation, dose-response analysed only on nominal parameters. That is RECEIVED versus NOMINAL dose, in a different intervention class, with cortical atrophy as the mechanism. This record is about the NOMINAL variable itself being reported in non-convertible units so that even a nominal dose-response cannot be fitted. (2) MINE-G-004 - no comparative-effectiveness synthesis conditions its effect estimate on achieved dose or observed adherence; its own text nominates a future merge into a 'nominal versus received dose' family. This record is explicitly NOT in that family: it concerns the metric of the prescribed dose, and would remain open even if every trial reported perfect adherence. (3) G-CAND-322 (rejected) records 'undetermined optimal dose/intensity' as one paper's limitation - the generic form this record deliberately does not restate. (4) MINE-G-002 is post-cessation durability pooling. (5) ACTOR-G-023 concerns indirect comparison between intervention TYPES and unfalsifiable hierarchies, not dose within a type. (6) G-349 asks for a harmonised primary outcome BATTERY - the dependent variable; this record concerns the independent variable. (7) ACTOR-G-022 concerns the meaning of the outcome scale. None of these would be closed by converting trial intensity prescriptions to a common physiological metric and fitting a dose-response, and this record would not be closed by any of their closure tests.

gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: Exercise-in-MCI reviews issue dose prescriptions - 52 weeks, two to three sessions a week, 'moderate intensity' - while the exposure variable those prescriptions rest on is not on a common scale and has never been fitted. Across one review's 29 charted trials, intensity is reported in mutually non-convertible units (per cent of maximal heart rate, absolute beats per minute, two different Borg scales with different ranges, per cent VO2max), so no dose-response function can be estimated even in principle from the pooled literature; a second review does not carry intensity as a column at all and records that the source literature does not agree on what the word denotes; a third states the intensity controversy twice while quantifying no dose-response and still recommending modalities at 'moderate intensity'; and the one meta-analysis that attempted prescription moderators reports that the resistance-training, intensity, session-time, high-frequency and long-duration strata all failed its own subgroup criteria for want of studies. The gap is not that the optimal dose is unknown - that is every review's stated limitation. It is that the field's dose guidance encodes a monotone dose-response that has never been estimated on a common metric, and that the one trial in this pack which randomised dose inside a single protocol found no gradient across a 2.7-fold contrast (90 versus 240 min/wk was not detectably different on 19 of 20 outcomes) with its single significant between-dose difference favouring the LOWER dose. So the prescriptions are derived from an uncalibrated between-study exposure and the only direct randomised test points the other way.
