gaps.gap_statement: The non-pharmacological MCI intervention evidence base is assembled almost entirely from bibliographic-database searches of PUBLISHED trials (P-698 is the exception in this literature, supplementing its search with ClinicalTrials.gov and ICTRP but reporting no capture fraction), while the field's own registry census establishes that only 8.28% of 2,609 registered MCI trials (2,064 interventional and 499 observational registrations) have shared any results at all. No synthesis in this literature estimates what fraction of completed MCI intervention trials its search actually captured, or how much of its positive signal survives the unreported remainder - and the syntheses that generate the headline claim do so by counting significance verdicts (19 of 20 trials positive in the home-based lifestyle review), which is precisely the pattern that near-total non-reporting of null trials would produce. The one synthesis that formally tested for asymmetry reports that trimming ALTERS its estimates but neither publishes the corrected values nor attempts registry retrieval. The absence matters because it is not the usual unquantified 'publication bias' caveat: the size of the missing fraction is already known and published inside this same corpus, and nobody has joined it to the effect estimates that clinical recommendations rest on.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard pattern of an assumption nobody tests - here the assumption that the published trial set represents the completed trial set - and it is not the generic caveat because the corpus itself already publishes the violating number. It is also a ground-truth/evidentiary-validity critique in the mould of the peripheral-vs-central-marker gold gap: the syntheses treat their retrieved set as the evidence, when the field's own census says it is at most one trial in twelve. Non-obvious because four of the six papers here DO write the words 'publication bias' - which is exactly why a keyword scan would call this addressed; what none of them does, and what P-1169 makes possible for the first time, is put a number on the missing fraction and propagate it. The consequence is concrete and directional: an evidence base of small (<100), university-sponsored, non-regulated trials with a 1-in-12 reporting rate is the configuration in which a 19/20 positivity rate carries almost no information about efficacy.
gaps.closure_criteria: A synthesis that starts from the registry rather than from the journals: take the WHO ICTRP / ClinicalTrials.gov set of MCI intervention trials recorded as COMPLETED with a cognitive primary endpoint (the completed subset of the 1,344 non-pharmacological trials P-1169 enumerates), determine for each whether results are available anywhere, report the capture fraction of the existing published syntheses against that denominator, and recover outcomes for the unreported arm by registry results-postings, investigator contact or a selection model. Primary reportable quantity: the pooled SMD on global cognition in the published-only set versus the retrieval-augmented set, with the difference and its interval. Closure requires that difference to be reported, whatever its sign; a null difference closes the gap as decisively as a large one.
gaps.modality: Clinical/Population - non-pharmacological intervention trials and their syntheses (home lifestyle, cognitive training, tDCS, sleep, exercise)
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold-standard pattern of an assumption nobody tests - here the assumption that the published trial set represents the completed trial set - and it is not the generic caveat because the corpus itself already publishes the violating number. The consequence is concrete and directional: an evidence base of small (<100), university-sponsored, non-regulated trials with a 1-in-12 reporting rate is the configuration in which a 19/20 positivity rate carries almost no information about efficacy.
gaps.critic_falsification: EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE is the strongest objection. Searching WHO ICTRP and ClinicalTrials.gov is mandated Cochrane practice, and there is a large external empirical literature on results-reporting rates and selection models; a curator could therefore rule that the method is not missing at all, that Cochrane-standard reviews of cognitive training in MCI already search registries, and that what this record documents is the below-standard search conduct of six particular non-Cochrane reviews - a quality observation about the corpus's sample of syntheses rather than a research gap. The defence is that the specific quantity (the MCI-intervention capture fraction and the resulting shift in the pooled estimate) has not been produced by anyone, but that defence rests on my not having found it rather than on a verified external search, and it cannot be settled from inside this corpus.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no modality or method combination is proposed; the missing object is a coverage/bias estimate for an existing literature.

RESTATEMENT: checked by id against ACTOR-G-022, G-023, G-044, MINE-G-002, MINE-G-004, G-349 and against the seven rejected single-paper 'publication bias' limitation records (G-CAND-22/24/30/48/190/193/194); the distinguishing element - a measured registry denominator propagated into the effect estimate - appears in none of them.

TOO_SPECIFIC: spans six independent syntheses across four intervention classes (home lifestyle, cognitive training, tDCS, sleep) plus the whole-registry census; not a property of one paper or one modality.

DATA_SCARCITY: the missing data are recoverable now - ICTRP records name sponsors and completion status, and selection-model or investigator-contact retrieval are established procedures. This is a methodological absence, not an inherent data limitation.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: P-1063 is listed as the partial closer, not omitted. Its Egger/trim-and-fill is an asymmetry test on its own 31 retrieved RCTs; it produces no capture fraction, contacts no registry, and its own digest records that the correction changes the answer without reporting the changed answer.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: this is not clinical-trial design or drug development; it is a property of the corpus's own evidence-synthesis products, the same class as the accepted ACTOR-G-023 and MINE-G-004.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the negative clause is deliberately narrow - no synthesis estimates its CAPTURE of completed trials or the effect of the unreported remainder. It is not 'no synthesis mentions publication bias' (four of the six do, and they are cited for exactly that) and not 'no synthesis tests asymmetry' (P-1063 does, and is cited as the partial closer).

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: every quote is tagged with the summary field it came from; the two load-bearing numbers (8.28% and 19/20) are both from results fields, not from significance or novelty fields.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: each cited paper's own text carries the record's vocabulary - P-1169 'results share'/'8.28%', P-1077 'significance voting', P-1063/P-1070/P-914/P-930 'publication bias'. No inferential bridge is asked of any paper.

G-CAND-22, G-CAND-24, G-CAND-30, G-CAND-48, G-CAND-190, G-CAND-193, G-CAND-194 are all single-paper limitation strings of the form 'Publication bias.' harvested from one review's limitations field and all were REJECTED as such - this record is the opposite construction: it takes a measured corpus-internal denominator (8.28%) and asks what it does to the effect estimates, which none of them do. ACTOR-G-022 is about the absence of a disease-course anchor for intervention endpoints (no conversion, no long-horizon function, no committed biomarker direction) - a question about WHICH endpoint, not about which trials are visible. MINE-G-004 is about conditioning an effect on achieved dose or observed adherence WITHIN included trials. MINE-G-002 is about the absent pooling of post-cessation timepoints. gaps.gap_statement: MCI intervention studies recruit only through routes that presuppose preserved illness awareness - self-presentation to a memory clinic, or a documented subjective memory complaint written into the eligibility criteria - while the two studies that actually asked MCI patients why they do not take up these interventions name cognitive anosognosia, low perceived risk and little perceived personal control as the leading barriers to ever starting. Awareness of one's own impairment is therefore a SELECTION variable for every efficacy estimate in this literature, and a plausible effect modifier, because it is a symptom of the disease being treated rather than an incidental preference. Yet no trial in this theme reports awareness or insight as a baseline characteristic, a covariate or a moderator, and none characterises those who declined; the barrier studies for their part quantify no barrier prevalence and measure no intervention outcome, so the two literatures cannot be joined. The absence matters because it is not the generic complaint that trial samples are volunteers: it identifies the specific, measurable variable on which the selection operates, and that variable is the one most likely to mark the patients with the most to gain from early intervention.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Structurally this is the handedness gap (NEW-G-21) transposed to the intervention literature: a disease-relevant variable that plausibly biases what the studies learn, is cheap to measure, and is entered by nobody as a stratifier or covariate. It also matches the gold pattern of a population everyone excludes, but with the excluding MECHANISM named and evidenced from the trials' own eligibility text rather than asserted - which is what separates it from the routine 'trial samples are volunteers' complaint. It is non-obvious because the exclusion is invisible in the trials: no protocol excludes anosognosic patients, so nothing in a trial report flags them; the exclusion happens upstream, in the requirement that the patient complained or presented, and it only becomes visible when the barrier literature is read against the eligibility criteria. The direction of the bias is specific and adverse: insight-preserved patients are the ones for whom self-managed home programmes, daily app practice and self-administered audio interventions - four of the delivery models here - are most likely to work.
gaps.closure_criteria: A community-screening-based MCI intervention study that reports both halves of the selection. (1) Reach: from a defined community screening frame of MCI-positive individuals (N >= 500 screened positive), report the number offered the intervention, the number who initiated, and a comparison of initiators versus decliners on a validated awareness/insight measure (for example patient-informant discrepancy or an anosognosia rating), plus age, education and cognitive severity. (2) Effect modification: within the enrolled arm, enter that awareness measure as a prespecified baseline covariate and report the intervention-by-awareness interaction on the primary cognitive endpoint with its interval. A study reporting a null interaction closes the gap as validly as one reporting a large one; what closes it is the estimate existing.

gaps.critic_falsification: The clause 'no trial reports insight or awareness as a baseline characteristic' is an inference from what the digests do not contain, and a digest is a summary - a baseline awareness measure could sit in a table that the summary never reproduced. That is materially weaker evidence than an author concession, and it is the load-bearing negative. A second objection: the two barrier studies are both from China (Nanjing tertiary hospital plus community screening; four central provinces), so the barrier profile on which the selection argument rests may be culturally specific and may not describe the populations of the Texan, Moscow, Israeli and Japanese intervention samples it is being read against; and both of the striking participation figures that would have sized the excluded stratum turn out to be background citations rather than measurements, so this corpus contains no measured estimate of how large the unreached group actually is.

ACTOR-G-083 asks whether temperament-aware RECRUITMENT STRATEGY has been validated against realised enrolment and retention - a question about whether a recruitment tool works; this record is about a confounder/selection variable that biases the efficacy estimate whether or not any recruitment tool is used. ACTOR-G-059 asks for anosognosia/metamemory measures as a PROGNOSTIC or screening tool for rapid conversion - the same construct in an entirely different role (predicting outcome, not gating trial entry). gaps.gap_statement: In MCI intervention research, cognition enters trials only as an EFFICACY variable and never as a SAFETY endpoint: no study in this evidence set pre-specifies a treatment-emergent cognitive-deterioration threshold, a non-inferiority margin on a cognitive scale, or tabulates cognitive adverse events by arm. The absence is not a resource limit but an endpoint-architecture choice, and the same literature demonstrates the missing rigour on other organ systems: P-1262 runs a 6-month double-blind placebo-controlled panel of cardiometabolic and inflammatory markers in 39 MCI participants explicitly to answer a safety objection, while P-1189 - a trial whose stated primary aim is safety and tolerability in an MCI population, using a subanesthetic dissociative anaesthetic - measured no cognitive outcome at all and lists 'formal safety monitoring of cognitive function' among the improvements not made. Consequence: in a population defined by proximity to a cognitive threshold, a drug- or programme-induced cognitive decrement cannot be detected as harm - it is scored as absence of efficacy - and the only cognitive-stability reassurance available (P-1200) is a post-hoc reading of an uncontrolled within-subject null in 14 patients. Harm is meanwhile asserted rather than measured: P-1235 ranks 21 regimens from 46 RCTs (3641 participants) as clinician guidance and calls acupuncture 'low-risk' in its importance field while naming adverse-event reporting as still needed, and P-1196 issues a supplementation ceiling of 800-2000 IU/day 'to avoid toxicity' while listing safety monitoring as absent and conceding it is undetermined whether some vitamin E components are harmful.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern of the XAI record ('descriptive attribution without proving it improves clinician decision-making') and of G-09 (discrimination proven, decision impact never tested): the field has built rigorous machinery pointed at the wrong question. The non-obvious part is the internal asymmetry - this is not a field that lacks safety methodology, it is a field that applies full pre-specified placebo-controlled safety methodology to the liver, the vasculature and the cytokine panel (P-1262) while leaving the target organ's function to be inferred from an efficacy null. The second non-obvious element is the direction-of-scoring problem: because cognition is an efficacy variable, a treatment-emergent decrement is recorded as a failed benefit rather than as a harm signal, so the harm is invisible by construction rather than by omission.
gaps.closure_criteria: An MCI intervention trial (any class) that pre-specifies a treatment-emergent cognitive-deterioration threshold on its cognitive scale (or a non-inferiority margin for a non-cognitive-target intervention), tabulates cognitive adverse events by arm alongside its efficacy result, and reports the proportion of participants crossing the deterioration threshold in each arm. A post-hoc within-subject null (as in P-1200) does not close it.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern of the XAI record ('descriptive attribution without proving it improves clinician decision-making') and of G-09 (discrimination proven, decision impact never tested): the field has built rigorous machinery pointed at the wrong question. The non-obvious part is the internal asymmetry - this is not a field that lacks safety methodology, it is a field that applies full pre-specified placebo-controlled safety methodology to the liver, the vasculature and the cytokine panel (P-1262) while leaving the target organ's function to be inferred from an efficacy null. The second non-obvious element is the direction-of-scoring problem: because cognition is an efficacy variable, a treatment-emergent decrement is recorded as a failed benefit rather than as a harm signal, so the harm is invisible by construction rather than by omission.
gaps.critic_falsification: EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE is the real threat. Cognitive safety monitoring is standard practice in some adjacent literatures - anticholinergic-burden and sedative-hypnotic trials in older adults, and anti-amyloid programmes where ARIA monitoring sits beside cognitive endpoints - so a reviewer could argue the corpus absence is a sampling artefact of a nutraceutical/non-pharmacological-heavy sample rather than a field-level blind spot. The record's defence is that P-1189 is not a sampling artefact: it is a purpose-built safety trial of a psychoactive drug in MCI that conceded in its own text that cognitive-safety monitoring was not performed. That single paper survives the external-literature objection; the corpus-wide framing may not, and a verifier should be prepared to narrow the record to the non-pharmacological and nutraceutical intervention classes if an external check finds cognitive-safety endpoints routine in pharmacological MCI trials.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no modality/method combination is proposed; this is an endpoint-architecture absence.
RESTATEMENT: no existing gap in the 534-statement list concerns safety endpoints in MCI intervention trials (grepped safety/adverse/harm/tolerab); the nearest records are efficacy-side.

TOO_SPECIFIC: the absence spans four intervention classes in this pack (glutamatergic drug, antioxidant supplement, acupuncture/moxibustion, Kampo herbal) plus a ketogenic-supplement RCT, not one protocol.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: P-1262 and P-1200 are named as partial closers on the face of the record rather than ignored - P-1262 closes the non-cognitive half and P-1200 supplies only an uncontrolled n=14 within-subject null; neither pre-specifies a cognitive harm criterion.

DATA_SCARCITY: the data are trivially available - every trial here already administers cognitive scales; what is missing is their pre-specification and reporting AS safety, which costs nothing extra to collect.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: partially mitigated rather than eliminated - see residual_risk. The claim is scoped as an absence in the checked corpus set, and is anchored on P-1189's own concession that cognitive-safety monitoring was not performed, which is a within-paper fact rather than a corpus-sampling inference.

NOT_IN_SCOPE: intervention trials are the declared scope of theme T08 and P-1169's registry census counts 2,609 registered MCI trials (2,064 interventional, 499 observational) - a registry count, not a corpus count; the gold set itself contains prospective-trial-design gaps (G-09, NEW-G-27).

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper uses the record's own vocabulary - P-1189 'safety monitoring of cognitive function', P-1196 'safety monitoring'/'toxicity', P-1235 'adverse events'/'low-risk', P-1262 'adversely affect'.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: the two quotes that sit in assertion fields (P-1235 'low-risk' in '### Why is it important?', P-1196's dose ceiling in '### What is the significance?') are labelled as assertions in the evidence entries, and their assertion status IS the point being made, not a measured finding being borrowed.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: checked against every cited paper. P-1200 does measure cognition and P-1262 does run a safety analysis; both are declared as partial closers and the absence clause is narrowed to pre-specified cognitive-deterioration criteria, non-inferiority margins and arm-level cognitive adverse-event tabulation, none of which any cited paper reports.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked against every T08 existing gap and grepped the full 534-statement list for safety / adverse / harm / tolerability: the only hits are G-CAND-76 (a rejected template line), G-CAND-232 (P-378's own limitation list) and ACTOR-G-058 (driving-safety prediction models) - none concerns cognitive safety as a trial endpoint. Distinct from ACTOR-G-022 (intervention results not anchorable to disease course) and ACTOR-G-044 (no intervention shown to delay conversion): both are about whether BENEFIT is real, this is about whether HARM is detectable, which no existing record addresses. Distinct from ACTOR-G-009 (undefined multi-ingredient arm), G-349 (outcome-battery harmonisation across reviews) and VF-30 (fragility of pooled efficacy estimates) - all efficacy-side. Distinct from NEW-G-27 (XAI decision-impact RCT) and G-09 (AI-vs-standard-of-care pragmatic trial), which concern AI deployment rather than intervention harm.

gaps.gap_statement: For orally administered nutraceutical and probiotic interventions in MCI, the dose reported is the dose SWALLOWED, never the dose DELIVERED, even though the corpus itself identifies host-dependent gut conversion as the reason these compounds fail in humans. P-1176 records that punicalagin has 18.17% oral bioavailability and is converted by the gut microbiota into ellagic acid and urolithins with three distinct metabotypes (0/A/B) - so the active moiety circulating in a participant is produced by that participant's own microbiome and differs between people - yet it names metabotype stratification as a future aspiration, not a completed measurement. On the probiotic side P-1198 records that across the nine human trials it appraised, NO gut-related parameter was measured in any MCI or AD study, so the gut-permeability / SCFA mechanism the field invokes is never verified in the humans dosed. The single trial that does open the gut (P-1246, LGG, n=169, double-blind) measures 16S taxonomic COMPOSITION and concedes shotgun metagenomics for functional resolution is still needed - composition is not exposure. Why it matters: without a measured circulating active metabolite, a null nutraceutical trial in MCI cannot be distinguished from a trial in which a large fraction of participants were never exposed, so compounds are being retired (or advanced) on evidence that carries no exposure information at all - and this is demonstrably fixable at this trial scale, because P-1262 verified delivered exposure in only 39 MCI participants, showing plasma 8:0 and 10:0 acids and ketones moved with arm assignment.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern of the OCT vendor-variance gap and of the peripheral-versus-central temporal-lag gap: it challenges the measurement that everything downstream rests on, rather than proposing a missing pairing. The non-obvious element is that the exposure is not merely unmeasured but is generated by the participant rather than the protocol - the compound tested in the animal model is not the compound circulating in the human, and which human converts it is a microbiome trait, so the intervention is effectively a different drug in different participants while being analysed as one arm. The record is also self-limiting in a way that strengthens it: the same corpus contains a trial (P-1262) that did verify delivered exposure at n=39, so the absence cannot be explained by cost or feasibility.
gaps.closure_criteria: An MCI nutraceutical or probiotic trial that measures the circulating active metabolite (or, for probiotics, a functional gut readout such as SCFA or shotgun-metagenomic pathway abundance) at baseline and endpoint in every participant, reports the delivered-exposure distribution by arm and by metabotype, and reports the cognitive effect as a function of achieved exposure alongside the intention-to-treat estimate. A 16S composition change or a pill count does not close it.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern of the OCT vendor-variance gap and of the peripheral-versus-central temporal-lag gap: it challenges the measurement that everything downstream rests on, rather than proposing a missing pairing. The non-obvious element is that the exposure is not merely unmeasured but is generated by the participant rather than the protocol - the compound tested in the animal model is not the compound circulating in the human, and which human converts it is a microbiome trait, so the intervention is effectively a different drug in different participants while being analysed as one arm. The record is also self-limiting in a way that strengthens it: the same corpus contains a trial (P-1262) that did verify delivered exposure at n=39, so the absence cannot be explained by cost or feasibility.
gaps.critic_falsification: Urolithin metabotype stratification is an established practice in the broader nutrition literature (metabotype 0/A/B was defined there and has been used as a stratifier in pomegranate and walnut trials), so a verifier checking outside this corpus may find that the general method is not missing at all - only its application to an MCI cognitive endpoint - which pushes the record toward EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE and toward being a narrower application gap than the claim's framing suggests. A second, independent objection: P-1198 (a 2022 mini-review appraising nine trials including an L. rhamnosus GG MCI study) and P-1246 (a 2022 L. rhamnosus GG RCT whose own background cites earlier LGG-in-MCI work from the same group) may not be fully independent sources - P-1198's LGG entry could be a sibling trial of P-1246's programme. Neither card declares a cross_paper_claim, and the participant counts do not match (P-1198 lists MCI arms of n=63/80/100/145 against P-1246's 169), but a verifier should confirm this before the two are counted as separate lines of evidence.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: nothing is proposed to be combined with anything; the missing quantity is a measurement of the delivered compound.

RESTATEMENT: no gap statement in the corpus list mentions bioavailability, metabotype, urolithins, gut parameters or target engagement; the two sibling records in the dose family are named explicitly and distinguished on quantity, mechanism, literature and closure test.
TOO_SPECIFIC: spans two intervention classes (polyphenol nutraceuticals, probiotics) and is corroborated in a third (vitamin E component isolation), not a single compound.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: P-1246 is carried on the face of the record as a partial closer with exactly what it leaves open (16S composition, not function), and P-1262 is carried as a feasibility proof rather than being silently ignored.
DATA_SCARCITY: the opposite - P-1262 demonstrates the assay burden is small at n=39, and urolithin/SCFA assays operate on the same fasting plasma and stool samples these trials already collect.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: mitigated but not eliminated - see residual_risk. The absence clause is scoped to MCI trials in this corpus, and the two anchor facts (P-1176's metabotype aspiration, P-1198's finding of zero gut parameters across nine appraised trials) are within-paper statements about the MCI literature, not inferences from corpus sampling.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: nutraceutical and probiotic intervention trials in MCI are squarely inside theme T08 and appear as C3 registry rows.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: each cited paper uses the record's own vocabulary - P-1176 bioavailability/metabotype/urolithins, P-1198 gut parameters/gut permeability, P-1246 functional resolution/metagenomics, P-1262 plasma 8:0 and 10:0 acids.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: the quantitative anchors (18.17%; the p=0.001 time-by-group interactions) come from results and key-findings fields, not from significance or novelty fields; P-1176's therapeutic framing is explicitly flagged as overclaim in its card and is NOT used - only its pharmacokinetic facts and its own future-work list are relied on.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: checked against all five cited papers. P-1246 measures the gut and P-1262 measures delivered exposure, so the clause is narrowed accordingly: what no cited paper reports is a measured circulating ACTIVE METABOLITE or a metabotype-stratified analysis in an MCI cohort. P-1262's exposure measurement is a medium-chain fatty acid, not a microbiome-converted metabolite, so it does not falsify the narrowed clause.
gaps.dedup_note: Grepped the 534-statement gap list for metabotype / bioavailab / target engagement / urolithin / polyphenol / probiotic / microbiome / gut: the sole hit is G-CAND-110 (a rejected EEG/EGG classifier limitation), so no existing record concerns nutraceutical exposure. DECLARED FAMILY MEMBERSHIP: this is a third sibling in the 'nominal versus received dose' family the curator already recognised - ACTOR-G-039 (delivered cortical electric field never modelled as exposure in MCI neuromodulation) and MINE-G-004 (achieved dose / adherence never conditioned on in non-pharmacological syntheses). It is not a restatement of either: the quantity is different (a host-microbiome-generated metabolite, not an anatomically attenuated field or an attendance count), the mechanism of loss is different (interindividual metabotype variation rather than atrophy or dropout), the literature is different (nutraceutical and probiotic trials), and the closure study is different. If the operator merges the family, this should become its dietary/oral arm rather than be discarded. Also distinct from ACTOR-G-009 (undefined multi-ingredient composition in nutritional NMAs) - that concerns what was in the ranked arm, this concerns what reached the bloodstream.

gaps.gap_statement: MCI intervention studies in this set that measure BOTH a blood or CSF mechanism biomarker and cognition report the two as separate results and do not test whether the mechanism change carries the cognitive change - so the mechanistic hypothesis cannot be disconfirmed by the trial that is presented as testing it. The dissociation is directly visible inside single studies in this set and always resolves the same way, with whichever endpoint moved becoming the paper's headline and the flat one demoted to a limitation: P-1243 titles its result 'Gamma neuromodulation improves episodic memory' on the strength of memory gains while recording 'no changes in plasma AD biomarkers'; P-1200 reports frailty and anorexia improvement as its finding while global CDR, CDR-SB and MoCA-J stayed flat; P-1252 reports serum PARP-1, 8-OHdG, NOS2, Abeta and p-tau restored to near-normal and concedes it has no cognitive outcome to correlate them with, leaving 'whether biomarker restoration translates to cognitive benefit' as an open problem. The same unfalsifiability propagates upward into synthesis: P-1187 pools 38 studies and issues an exercise PRESCRIPTION on a cytokine surrogate while listing 'linking cytokine reductions to cognitive endpoints' among its open problems. No cited study pre-specifies which endpoint is confirmatory, reports concordance between the biological and cognitive arms, or fits a mediation model; the closest linkage anywhere in the set is P-1246's unadjusted within-subgroup correlation between a taxon change and a cognitive change, which does not use the randomisation and is conceded to be correlational. Why it matters: the mechanism marker is the variable that selects which compounds and modalities advance to larger trials, and for fluid mechanism markers in this population it has not been shown to track the outcome it is standing in for. Two corpus RCTs do run the mediation test for imaging mechanisms: P-793 (computerised cognitive training) reports that PCC-precuneus connectivity change mediated the group effect on recall (bootstrap indirect CI 0.18 to 2.37), and P-760 (acupuncture, 40 aMCI, with serum metabolomics and gut metagenomics) ran a mediation analysis that did not support its chain; a merge into ACTOR-G-022 as its mechanism rung is the alternative the record's own critique anticipates.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern of the peripheral-versus-central decoupling gap (prognostic models treat one marker family as ground truth and never map its decoupling from the other) and of the objective-function-framing gaps: the defect is in what the study is structured to be able to conclude, not in its execution. The non-obvious element is the asymmetric reporting rule that makes the design unfalsifiable - across three studies with three different pairs of endpoints, the endpoint that moved became the title and the flat endpoint became a limitation, so no configuration of results could have counted against the mechanism. The evidence is unusually direct for an absence record: the dissociations are stated in the results fields of the papers themselves, not inferred from what is missing.
gaps.closure_criteria: An MCI intervention trial measuring a fluid mechanism biomarker (blood or CSF) and cognition in the same participants that pre-specifies which endpoint is confirmatory, reports concordance between biomarker and cognitive change, and fits a mediation or instrumental model using the randomisation. The imaging-mechanism mediation tests in P-793 and P-760 are the design precedent.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern of the peripheral-versus-central decoupling gap (prognostic models treat one marker family as ground truth and never map its decoupling from the other) and of the objective-function-framing gaps: the defect is in what the study is structured to be able to conclude, not in its execution. The non-obvious element is the asymmetric reporting rule that makes the design unfalsifiable - across three studies with three different pairs of endpoints, the endpoint that moved became the title and the flat endpoint became a limitation, so no configuration of results could have counted against the mechanism. The evidence is unusually direct for an absence record: the dissociations are stated in the results fields of the papers themselves, not inferred from what is missing.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is that the dissociations may be fully explained by power rather than by an untested causal step: P-1243 has 13 participants, P-1200 has 14, and P-1252's arms are 22 each - at those sizes a flat biomarker or a flat cognitive scale is the expected result whether or not the mechanism operates, so 'the two endpoints dissociate' may be a small-sample artefact rather than evidence that the link is unverified. That would not remove the absence (no mediation model is fitted in any of them) but it would considerably weaken the framing that the dissociation is informative, and it makes the record vulnerable to being merged into ACTOR-G-022 as a further symptom of the same surrogate-endpoint problem rather than kept as a separate gap. A verifier should decide whether the mediation-absence clause alone, stripped of the dissociation evidence, still clears the bar.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: nothing is proposed to be combined; the missing item is a pre-specified endpoint hierarchy and a mediation test between endpoints these studies already measure.

gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: MCI intervention studies that measure BOTH a mechanism biomarker and cognition report the two as separate results and never test whether the mechanism change carries the cognitive change - so the mechanistic hypothesis cannot be disconfirmed by the trial that is presented as testing it. The dissociation is directly visible inside single studies in this set and always resolves the same way, with whichever endpoint moved becoming the paper's headline and the flat one demoted to a limitation: P-1243 titles its result 'Gamma neuromodulation improves episodic memory' on the strength of memory gains while recording 'no changes in plasma AD biomarkers'; P-1200 reports frailty and anorexia improvement as its finding while global CDR, CDR-SB and MoCA-J stayed flat; P-1252 reports serum PARP-1, 8-OHdG, NOS2, Abeta and p-tau restored to near-normal and concedes it has no cognitive outcome to correlate them with, leaving 'whether biomarker restoration translates to cognitive benefit' as an open problem. The same unfalsifiability propagates upward into synthesis: P-1187 pools 38 studies and issues an exercise PRESCRIPTION on a cytokine surrogate while listing 'linking cytokine reductions to cognitive endpoints' among its open problems. No cited study pre-specifies which endpoint is confirmatory, reports concordance between the biological and cognitive arms, or fits a mediation model; the closest linkage anywhere in the set is P-1246's unadjusted within-subgroup correlation between a taxon change and a cognitive change, which does not use the randomisation and is conceded to be correlational. Why it matters: the mechanism marker is the variable that selects which compounds and modalities advance to larger trials, and in this population it has never been shown to track the outcome it is standing in for.

gaps.gap_statement: Joint-exposure MCI risk-factor studies adjudicate synergy - and issue their co-exposure targeting recommendations - on the multiplicative scale or on no scale at all, while the additive scale (relative excess risk due to interaction, attributable proportion, synergy index), which is the scale that determines how many MCI cases targeting the doubly exposed group would actually prevent, is left uncomputed. This is not a gap in method availability: the corpus already contains one demonstration that the two scales disagree in sign for an MCI outcome (P-678, CHARLS, 4420 cognitively intact adults: multiplicative product-term RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.67 to 1.37, null; additive RERI 1.08, 95% CI 0.25 to 1.91, significant, AP 0.20, S 1.33 - summaries.md Paper 678 block). No frontier joint-exposure study repeats it. P-828 declares a co-occurrence finding and a prevention recommendation with no interaction number of any kind; P-791 headlines a joint cell RR of 3.73 while its only interaction test is a null multiplicative product term (0.70, P = 0.113); P-807's stated objective IS the SES-by-lifestyle interaction yet it prints no interaction estimate, no population attributable fraction and no absolute risk difference; P-803's central effect-modification claim is never formally tested at all. Because a null multiplicative interaction is fully compatible with a large positive additive one, every 'target the co-exposed group' conclusion in this literature rests on the one scale that cannot license it.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard pattern of a framing/analysis assumption that invalidates the field's own conclusions - the same shape as 'Machine learning architectures force continuous, interval-censored multi-visit clinical trial data into artificial, discrete cross-sectional binary labels' and 'Prognostic models treat central nervous system markers as absolute ground truth'. It is non-obvious because the surface reading of these papers is that they DID test interaction (P-791 and P-881 print product terms), so the absence is invisible unless you ask which scale the conclusion is stated on. It spans four independent cohorts on four continents-worth of exposures (bone/muscle in Shanghai, residence x depression in a Chinese national panel, SES x lifestyle in Lombardy, sleep x metabolic syndrome in Tianjin/Shanghai) and it is actionable with data already collected: the joint cells exist in the published tables, and P-678 supplies a worked template inside this same corpus and literature.
gaps.closure_criteria: Re-analysis of at least one joint-exposure MCI risk-factor study (the joint cells in P-828, P-791, P-807 or P-803 already print the needed counts) reporting the relative excess risk due to interaction, attributable proportion and synergy index with confidence intervals alongside the multiplicative product term, and an absolute risk difference for the doubly exposed group. The gap closes when a frontier joint-exposure study states its targeting recommendation on the additive scale (P-678 is the corpus template).

It is non-obvious because the surface reading of these papers is that they DID test interaction (P-791 and P-881 print product terms), so the absence is invisible unless you ask which scale the conclusion is stated on. It spans four independent cohorts on four continents-worth of exposures (bone/muscle in Shanghai, residence x depression in a Chinese national panel, SES x lifestyle in Lombardy, sleep x metabolic syndrome in Tianjin/Shanghai) and it is actionable with data already collected: the joint cells exist in the published tables, and P-678 supplies a worked template inside this same corpus and literature.
gaps.critic_falsification: RERI, AP and S are three algebraic transformations of the same three joint-exposure risk ratios - the P-678 block itself says they 'reproduce from them directly'. A reviewer can therefore argue that for P-828, whose adjusted odds ratios for all three exposure groups are in its own Table 2, the additive interaction POINT ESTIMATE is already recoverable by any reader, making this a reporting-convention complaint rather than a research gap. The counter is that the point estimate is not the adjudicating quantity: the confidence interval for RERI requires the covariance matrix of the joint model, which is not recoverable from published cells, and it is the interval - not the point estimate - that decides whether the co-exposed group is a legitimate targeting unit. That counter holds for P-828, but it is weaker for P-791 and P-807, where the joint cells themselves are in figures or unprinted, and it means the record is better framed as 'the interval is never estimable' than as 'the quantity is never computed'.

gaps.gap_statement: The MCI prevalence figures this corpus treats as population base rates are produced almost entirely in samples selected on the capacity to attend and complete an in-person cognitive and physical assessment - the very capacity the outcome degrades - and none of the five cohorts examined here reports any quantity that would bound the resulting bias: no response or refusal count, no comparison of participants against non-participants on a variable available for both, and no selection-weighted prevalence set beside the unweighted one (elsewhere in the corpus P-898, a secondary analysis of the Chilean National Health Survey with complex-survey weighting, and P-785, HCHS/SOL with sampling weights, produce weighted MCI estimates from screen-defined MCI, without a weighted-versus-unweighted pair or a criterion diagnosis). Several of these authors concede the selection in words (P-828: volunteers at health checkups, 'This choice could constitute a selection bias'; P-803: older adults unable to complete a comprehensive geriatric assessment were excluded, 'the prevalence of MetS and MCI may be underestimated'); none measures it. The consequence is that the sampling frame moves the prevalence as far as the instrument does - 12.0% in a Shanghai health-checkup sample (P-828), 17.3% adjusted in a Taiwanese volunteer-recruited cohort with expert-consensus diagnosis (P-754), 19.4% in a Japanese municipal cohort where 2968 of 21,692 invited were analysed (P-825), 40.2% in a trial cohort recruited for healthy ageing (P-827) - so the definitional spread that ACTOR-G-017 attributes to the ascertainment rule is confounded with an unmeasured participation component, and the fix G-017 proposes (apply two definitions inside one cohort) cannot separate them. The same failure carries into incidence: P-737's authors state that participants who developed MCI or dementia may have been unable to complete clinical visits and dropped out, so new-onset MCI is underreported - outcome-dependent non-participation named by the authors, quantified by nobody.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard pattern of an assumption nobody tests that changes the ground truth downstream - the same shape as the peripheral-versus-central ground-truth gap and the interval-censoring gap. It is non-obvious because the papers look well-behaved: three of the five explicitly CONCEDE the selection, which reads as diligence and is exactly why nobody has noticed that the concession is never followed by a number. It spans five independent cohorts across Japan, Taiwan, mainland China and a five-country European trial, and the absence is directly checkable inside each paper rather than inferred from what the world literature does or does not contain. The closure design is cheap: the responder/non-responder linkage variables already exist in the municipal and national-programme registries these studies recruited from.
gaps.closure_criteria: For at least one of the cited prevalence cohorts, report the invitation, response and refusal counts, compare participants with non-participants on a variable held for both (registry age, sex, area deprivation, prior diagnoses), and print a selection-weighted MCI prevalence beside the unweighted one; for incidence, the analogous attrition-weighted rate.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold-standard pattern of an assumption nobody tests that changes the ground truth downstream - the same shape as the peripheral-versus-central ground-truth gap and the interval-censoring gap. It is non-obvious because the papers look well-behaved: three of the five explicitly CONCEDE the selection, which reads as diligence and is exactly why nobody has noticed that the concession is never followed by a number. It spans five independent cohorts across Japan, Taiwan, mainland China and a five-country European trial, and the absence is directly checkable inside each paper rather than inferred from what the world literature does or does not contain. The closure design is cheap: the responder/non-responder linkage variables already exist in the municipal and national-programme registries these studies recruited from.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is that this aggregates five separately-stated single-paper limitations, which is the pattern the ledger lint SOFT-flags, and that three of the five papers already concede the point in their own Limitations sections - so a reviewer can reasonably say the field is aware and the record adds only the observation that awareness is not quantification. The record's defence is the entanglement claim (frame and instrument move prevalence together and nobody has separated them), and that defence is weaker than it looks: P-827's frame is health-selected yet its prevalence is the highest in the set, which is fully explained by its MoCA <26 threshold alone and therefore does not by itself demonstrate that the frame contributes anything measurable. If a reviewer accepts that instrument choice explains the whole 12%-to-40% spread, this record collapses into ACTOR-G-017.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: nothing is being combined; this is a missing bias-quantification step inside single studies.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: the record makes no claim about the world literature, and deliberately does NOT assert that no probability-sampled criterion-diagnosis MCI prevalence study exists anywhere (enumerated-population cohorts of that kind do exist outside this corpus). The asserted absence is within-paper and verifiable: these five papers report prevalences without response accounting, non-participant comparison or a weighted estimate.
RESTATEMENT: see why_new - the nearest neighbours (G-017, G-033, G-016) are about the case definition and the measurement source, not the sampling frame.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the record names its own partial falsifier, P-791, which does run a weighted sensitivity analysis, and scopes the absence accordingly rather than claiming no one ever weights anything.
FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: P-791 is filed as the partial closer with the exact respect in which it falls short (item missingness, not frame participation; screen composite, not criterion diagnosis).

DATA_SCARCITY: not a scarcity problem - the non-participants are enumerated (21,692 invited in P-825; a national free physical-examination programme roster in P-828), so responder/non-responder comparisons are constructible from data the investigators already touched.
TOO_SPECIFIC: five independent cohorts, one shared omission.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: prevalence estimation for MCI is the centre of theme T09.

gaps.dedup_note: Grepped existing_gaps.md for 'volunteer', 'non-responder', 'response rate', 'participation', 'selection bias', 'sampling frame', 'weight' - the only hits are per-paper limitation stubs already marked rejected (G-CAND-195, G-CAND-242, G-CAND-252, G-CAND-320, G-CAND-327), none of which asserts a corpus-level absence of selection diagnostics. gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: The MCI prevalence figures this corpus treats as population base rates are produced almost entirely in samples selected on the capacity to attend and complete an in-person cognitive and physical assessment - the very capacity the outcome degrades - and not one of them reports any quantity that would bound the resulting bias: no response or refusal count, no comparison of participants against non-participants on a variable available for both, and no selection-weighted prevalence set beside the unweighted one. Several of these authors concede the selection in words (P-828: volunteers at health checkups, 'This choice could constitute a selection bias'; P-803: older adults unable to complete a comprehensive geriatric assessment were excluded, 'the prevalence of MetS and MCI may be underestimated'); none measures it. The consequence is that the sampling frame moves the prevalence as far as the instrument does - 12.0% in a Shanghai health-checkup sample (P-828), 17.3% adjusted in a Taiwanese volunteer-recruited cohort with expert-consensus diagnosis (P-754), 19.4% in a Japanese municipal cohort where 2968 of 21,692 invited were analysed (P-825), 40.2% in a trial cohort recruited for healthy ageing (P-827) - so the definitional spread that ACTOR-G-017 attributes to the ascertainment rule is confounded with an unmeasured participation component, and the fix G-017 proposes (apply two definitions inside one cohort) cannot separate them. The same failure carries into incidence: P-737's authors state that participants who developed MCI or dementia may have been unable to complete clinical visits and dropped out, so new-onset MCI is underreported - outcome-dependent non-participation named by the authors, quantified by nobody.

gaps.gap_statement: Modifiable-risk-factor epidemiology for MCI uses the MCI endpoint as a surrogate for dementia - papers conclude that acting on the exposure will 'delay dementia' from designs whose only outcome is MCI - yet the surrogate has never been validated in this literature, and in the two contrasts examined here that estimate the same exposure against BOTH endpoints (physical activity in P-733; rural residence in P-701), the signal is present at MCI and absent at dementia - a pattern that is not general, since P-733's own handgrip-strength exposure is associated with both (HR 0.94 for MCI, 0.95 for dementia) and P-1421 (SNAC-K, multistate) finds the reverse, with no biomarker predicting NC-to-MCI while NfL and p-tau217 predict MCI-to-dementia. P-733 (SHARE, 19,686 adults, mean 10.2 years) finds physical activity associated with incident MCI (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.74 to 0.98) but not incident dementia (HR 0.91, 0.78 to 1.07), and its own appraisal records that the two outcomes are ascertained so differently - a psychometric threshold applied at every wave versus whether a person says a doctor told them they have dementia - that the contrast may be measurement rather than biology. P-701 pools 35 rural studies and finds the rural excess concentrated in MCI and not in dementia, and names the discrepancy as its own open question. P-737 concludes that oral health can 'prevent MCI and delay dementia' while, in the digest's own inventory, no dementia endpoint appears anywhere in it. What is absent is the quantity that would license the substitution: only P-1005 (NACC, 43,630; atrial fibrillation) estimates one exposure's effect on the NC-to-MCI and the MCI-to-dementia transitions in one cohort under one diagnostic pipeline (women: HR 1.28 and 2.49), and no corpus risk-factor study reports a surrogate-validity statistic (proportion of the dementia effect explained by the MCI effect, or an equivalent). Until it does, every dementia-stage null in this literature is uninterpretable and every dementia-prevention claim built on an MCI endpoint is unsupported at its load-bearing link.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: This is the pattern the mining brief names directly - an endpoint everyone substitutes for the one that matters - and it matches the gold-standard clinical-utility gap (discrimination proven, decision impact never tested) in structure: the field has proven the association at the convenient endpoint and never tested that it transfers to the endpoint the public-health case is stated in. It is non-obvious because the two studies that DO measure both endpoints read as ordinary stage-specific findings ('the risk factor acts early'), which is precisely the interpretation the measurement asymmetry makes unavailable. It spans three independent evidence bases (a 14-country European panel cohort, a 35-study meta-analysis of rural prevalence, a Japanese municipal incidence cohort) plus a fourth paper that supplies the multi-state machinery, and the closure design is concrete and buildable from existing panel data.
gaps.closure_criteria: In one cohort observing both transitions under harmonised ascertainment, estimate the exposure's effect on NC-to-MCI and on MCI-to-dementia with confidence intervals and a stage-by-exposure test, and report a surrogate-validity statistic (the proportion of the dementia effect explained by the MCI effect, or an equivalent), so that the MCI endpoint can be licensed or not as a stand-in for dementia for that exposure.
gaps.actor_justification: This is the pattern the mining brief names directly - an endpoint everyone substitutes for the one that matters - and it matches the gold-standard clinical-utility gap (discrimination proven, decision impact never tested) in structure: the field has proven the association at the convenient endpoint and never tested that it transfers to the endpoint the public-health case is stated in. It is non-obvious because the two studies that DO measure both endpoints read as ordinary stage-specific findings ('the risk factor acts early'), which is precisely the interpretation the measurement asymmetry makes unavailable. It spans three independent evidence bases (a 14-country European panel cohort, a 35-study meta-analysis of rural prevalence, a Japanese municipal incidence cohort) plus a fourth paper that supplies the multi-state machinery, and the closure design is concrete and buildable from existing panel data.
gaps.critic_falsification: The record rests on only two observed instances of the MCI-present / dementia-absent asymmetry, and one of them (P-701) is a meta-analysis flagged for authors_overclaim whose own digest says its numbers are not calibrated prevalence estimates and whose pooled estimates carry I2 of 99.3 to 99.5 per cent - so the rural MCI-versus-dementia contrast there is arguably noise rather than a second instance, which would leave the empirical core of this record standing on P-733 alone. There is also a benign competing explanation the record cannot exclude: an exposure genuinely acting on the transition into MCI and not on the transition out of it would produce exactly this pattern, and P-733's own handgrip result (HR 0.94 for MCI and 0.95 for dementia, both significant) shows that not every exposure in that cohort diverges - which cuts against a pure measurement-artefact reading and means the gap is correctly framed as 'the two explanations have never been separated' rather than as 'the divergence is an artefact'.

The scarcity that DOES apply is narrower and is stated in the record: in oldest-old cohorts such as P-722's the MCI-to-dementia leg is swamped by competing mortality, which is a reason to specify the closure cohort's age structure, not a reason the question cannot be answered.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: this is about endpoint choice inside observational MCI risk-factor studies, which is the centre of theme T09; it is not a trial-design or drug-development question.

gaps.gap_statement: Routine-care MCI cohorts are conditioned on having received an MCI diagnosis, and P-1046 measures how small and how skewed that study base is: across 100% of US Medicare 2015-2019 only 6-8% of expected MCI cases carry the code (observed/expected 0.062-0.079), against 1.086-1.104 for dementia in the SAME data, with capture patterned by race (Black 0.039 vs non-Hispanic White 0.098) and income (dual-eligible 0.056 vs Medicare-only 0.085). Every claims/EHR/referral MCI estimate in this pack - drug effects on progression (P-1002 N=14,269 OMOP; P-1012 N=342 memory-clinic records), transition probabilities (P-1106 NACC), national association estimates (P-1028 NIS) - is therefore computed inside a roughly 7% slice selected on care-seeking and clinician coding, yet no study models the probability of being diagnosed, reweights an effect estimate by it, or anchors a coded-MCI cohort to an adjudicated population sample. This matters because the MCI-specific magnitude makes MCI real-world evidence structurally unlike the dementia real-world evidence whose methods it borrows: for dementia the same instrument shows essentially complete case capture, so a generic 'EHR generalisability' caveat is proportionate there and describes a 93% missing study base here - and these are the estimates now used to plan disease-modifying-therapy access and detection infrastructure.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern of a quantified structural transfer failure (the EEG single-site/no-multi-site-replication gap; the 'prognostic models treat CNS markers as ground truth' gap) rather than a missing-modality combination. It is non-obvious because 'EHR studies may not generalise' is exactly the boilerplate every one of these papers already writes: the content that is not boilerplate is the within-data MCI-versus-dementia asymmetry (0.062-0.079 vs 1.086-1.104) showing the problem is more than an order of magnitude worse for MCI than for the dementia real-world evidence whose methods and reviewer expectations MCI studies inherit, and the fact that the missingness runs along the same race and income axes as the social exposures and access variables these studies model as covariates.
gaps.closure_criteria: A study linking a population-based cohort with adjudicated MCI (an HRS/ADAMS-style consensus adjudication, or a community cohort such as WHICAP, Rotterdam or SLAS) to the same individuals' claims or EHR records, with N >= 1,000 adjudicated MCI cases, that (1) fits and reports a model for the probability of receiving an MCI diagnosis code, giving its discrimination and the covariates that drive it, and (2) re-estimates at least one exposure-to-progression association (for example a drug class as in P-1002/P-1012, or a cardiometabolic exposure) twice - unweighted in the coded-MCI subset and inverse-probability-of-diagnosis weighted to the full adjudicated MCI population - reporting both estimates with confidence intervals and the ratio between them.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern of a quantified structural transfer failure (the EEG single-site/no-multi-site-replication gap; the 'prognostic models treat CNS markers as ground truth' gap) rather than a missing-modality combination. It is non-obvious because 'EHR studies may not generalise' is exactly the boilerplate every one of these papers already writes: the content that is not boilerplate is the within-data MCI-versus-dementia asymmetry (0.062-0.079 vs 1.086-1.104) showing the problem is more than an order of magnitude worse for MCI than for the dementia real-world evidence whose methods and reviewer expectations MCI studies inherit, and the fact that the missingness runs along the same race and income axes as the social exposures and access variables these studies model as covariates.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE at the method level: inverse-probability-of-selection weighting and formal selection-bias frameworks for EHR and claims cohorts are an established biostatistics literature applied in other diseases, so a reviewer can argue this is a known method nobody has bothered to run on MCI rather than an unrecognised research gap. A second, sharper objection attacks the number this record is built on: P-1046's 'expected' rate is not observed, it is a probit model fitted to HRS 2000-2016 using the Langa-Kabeto-Weir telephone/proxy classification and transported onto Medicare. If that classification over-calls MCI relative to consensus criteria, the 6-8% capture figure - the entire quantitative spine of the gap - is inflated, and the MCI/dementia asymmetry could partly reflect that the same model calls dementia more accurately than MCI rather than that clinicians code MCI less often.

Listed as partial closers rather than ignored.

TOO_SPECIFIC: the gap covers the whole routine-care MCI evidence stream in this pack (drug effects, transitions, national associations, cost), not one paper's limitation.

gaps.gap_statement: This frontier's MCI risk epidemiology repeatedly reports a fused endpoint - 'MCI-or-dementia', 'cognitive impairment/dementia' - and then markets the resulting instrument or effect estimate as MCI-specific, while the same corpus shows the two components are not exchangeable on any quantity that has been measured within a single study: P-888's adjudicated AKI exposure is significant for probable dementia and for the composite but NOT for MCI alone; P-1046's diagnosis capture in one Medicare dataset is 0.062-0.079 for MCI against 1.086-1.104 for dementia; P-1137 finds the MCI stage adds only 7.6% inpatient and 9.1% primary-care cost while the AD-dementia diagnosis carries GBP 20,199 and a 5-year IRR of 7.2. The specific unmet need is a stage-resolved estimate: no study reports one exposure's effect on the NC->MCI transition and on the MCI->dementia transition as two numbers WITH an explicit test of the difference and per-arm event counts (P-1005 and P-1421 report both transition estimates with confidence intervals in one cohort, without the stage-difference test). Until that exists, an 'MCI risk factor' cannot be distinguished from a dementia risk factor measured earlier, and MCI-stage prevention and early-detection policy - the justification for P-977's coverage agenda and P-1046's detection agenda - is being targeted using effect sizes whose MCI component is either null, unreported, or not separated at all.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the pattern the brief names directly - an endpoint everyone substitutes for the one that matters - and the gold-standard data-structure critique (interval-censored multi-visit data forced into binary labels). It is non-obvious because a composite endpoint is normally defended as a legitimate power-gaining convention for ordered stages of one disease; the content that is not obvious is that this corpus already contains, inside single studies, the three demonstrations that would invalidate the convention here - the components differ in effect size (P-888), in observation process (P-1046) and in cost (P-1137) - and that the field nonetheless labels a composite-validated instrument 'MCI-specific (not just dementia-specific)' and offers it for prodromal-stage prevention targeting.
gaps.closure_criteria: One longitudinal cohort in which both transitions are observed (NACC, WHICAP, Rotterdam or SLAS all already hold such data) that fits the same exposure model twice - incidence of NC->MCI and progression MCI->dementia - and reports both effect estimates with confidence intervals, the event count in each arm, and an explicit test of the difference (a stage-by-exposure interaction term, or a multi-state / competing-transition formulation with transition-specific covariate effects), with at least 100 incident-MCI events so the prodromal arm is not the underpowered one. For risk indices specifically: report AUC and PPV for the incident-MCI-alone outcome alongside the composite, in the same validation cohort.
gaps.modality: Clinical/Population (trial cohort, population survey, administrative claims, biobank)
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the pattern the brief names directly - an endpoint everyone substitutes for the one that matters - and the gold-standard data-structure critique (interval-censored multi-visit data forced into binary labels). It is non-obvious because a composite endpoint is normally defended as a legitimate power-gaining convention for ordered stages of one disease; the content that is not obvious is that this corpus already contains, inside single studies, the three demonstrations that would invalidate the convention here - the components differ in effect size (P-888), in observation process (P-1046) and in cost (P-1137) - and that the field nonetheless labels a composite-validated instrument 'MCI-specific (not just dementia-specific)' and offers it for prodromal-stage prevention targeting.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is that a composite endpoint is a deliberate and defensible design when the components are ordered stages of one disease process - MCI-or-dementia is arguably the textbook case - so the 'substitution' framing may be describing justified standard practice rather than a blind spot, and a reviewer could reasonably answer that the composite is the clinically relevant event and that stage-resolved effects are a refinement, not a missing prerequisite. A second objection cuts at my best single piece of evidence: P-888's MCI-alone arm is null on 19 events with no a priori power for the question, so treating that null as evidence that the exposure acts stage-specifically is reading equivalence out of a non-significant result - exactly the error this corpus flags in P-961's aided-versus-normal-hearing comparison. If P-888's null is simply low power, the non-exchangeability case rests mainly on ascertainment (P-1046) and cost (P-1137), neither of which is an exposure effect.
fp_codes_cleared: UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the clause was deliberately narrowed after checking the record's own citations. It does not claim nobody separates MCI from dementia (four cited papers do); it claims nobody reports both transition-specific exposure effects with an adequately powered MCI arm and a formal test of the difference. P-888 and P-1119 are named in the record as the closest attempts and what each leaves open is stated.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: P-1119 is the nearest candidate closer and is listed as such, with its disqualifying features (cross-sectional, no effect sizes reported, no between-stage test) named rather than hidden.
RESTATEMENT: distinguished by id from ACTOR-G-040, G-033, G-017, G-027 in why_new, with the disjoint paper set and different closure test stated.
COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no 'combine X with Y' clause; the missing object is a stage-resolved estimate in one cohort.

DATA_SCARCITY: not a data limitation - NACC (P-1106), WHICAP (P-954), Rotterdam (P-950) and SLAS (P-939) already observe both transitions in this corpus; the missing item is a reporting and testing step.
TOO_SPECIFIC: spans six papers and three distinct quantity types (effect size, ascertainment, cost) across trial, survey, claims, cohort and biobank designs.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: within corpus scope; all cited papers are corpus T2/T4/T6 clinical-population records.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: each cited paper's own text uses the construct - P-888 'composite', P-939 'combined MCI+dementia outcome', P-1028 'no stratification by MCI vs dementia severity', P-1119 'shared risk factors for MCI and dementia', P-1137 'not MCI per se'.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: the two quotes drawn from author-side importance/significance fields (P-939 'MCI-specific', P-1137 'main cost driver') are tagged as assertions in the evidence entries and are used as evidence of FRAMING and of the paper's own reading, never as measured head-to-head results; all quantitative claims come from Results or Problems fields.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked against ACTOR-G-040 (adjacent-stage CONTRASTS in diagnostic classifiers: easy extreme contrasts inflate claimed readiness relative to the hard SCD-vs-MCI boundary). That record is about cross-sectional classification performance and sampling of contrast groups; this record is about prognostic and etiologic effect estimation in observational epidemiology, a disjoint paper set (P-888/P-939/P-1028/P-1046/P-1119/P-1137 appear in none of it), a different mechanism (fusion of two transitions into one event, not selection of easy contrast groups) and a different closure test (a stage-by-exposure interaction, not an isolated hard boundary). Also checked ACTOR-G-033 (conversion label non-comparable ACROSS studies via follow-up windows and prevalent-MCI criteria; this is fusion WITHIN one study's endpoint), ACTOR-G-017 (case-definition heterogeneity), ACTOR-G-027 (death as a competing event - a different estimand defect), ACTOR-G-044 (no intervention prevents progression), G-NEW-1046-A and the whole theme file T09_epidemiology_risk_existing_gaps.md, which contains nothing on composite or fused endpoints.
