gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: This frontier's MCI risk epidemiology repeatedly reports a fused endpoint - 'MCI-or-dementia', 'cognitive impairment/dementia' - and then markets the resulting instrument or effect estimate as MCI-specific, while the same corpus shows the two components are not exchangeable on any quantity that has been measured within a single study: P-888's adjudicated AKI exposure is significant for probable dementia and for the composite but NOT for MCI alone; P-1046's diagnosis capture in one Medicare dataset is 0.062-0.079 for MCI against 1.086-1.104 for dementia; P-1137 finds the MCI stage adds only 7.6% inpatient and 9.1% primary-care cost while the AD-dementia diagnosis carries GBP 20,199 and a 5-year IRR of 7.2. The specific unmet need is a stage-resolved estimate: no study reports one exposure's effect on the NC->MCI transition and on the MCI->dementia transition as two numbers, with adequate events in the MCI arm and an explicit test of the difference. Until that exists, an 'MCI risk factor' cannot be distinguished from a dementia risk factor measured earlier, and MCI-stage prevention and early-detection policy - the justification for P-977's coverage agenda and P-1046's detection agenda - is being targeted using effect sizes whose MCI component is either null, unreported, or not separated at all.

gaps.gap_statement: The corpus has already MEASURED how incomplete and how socially differential administrative MCI ascertainment is - P-1046 puts US Medicare MCI detection at 0.062-0.079 of expected (about 92 percent undiagnosed) against dementia detection of 1.086-1.104 in the SAME claims, and shows detection varying from 0.039 (Black) and 0.048 (Hispanic) to 0.098 (non-Hispanic White) and 0.056 (dual-eligible) vs 0.085 (Medicare-only) - yet no corpus study that uses an administratively or hospital/death-record ascertained MCI endpoint as the OUTCOME of an exposure-effect model reports that endpoint's sensitivity, benchmarks its observed case count against an expected count, or propagates the known sensitivity into the estimate by quantitative bias analysis. The consequence is not merely a wider interval, it is a directional one: when detection probability differs more than twofold across the same socioeconomic, educational and racial strata that are themselves studied as MCI risk factors, a coded-MCI outcome estimates the effect of an exposure on BEING DIAGNOSED with MCI rather than on having it, so both a positive and a null MCI result from such a cohort are uninterpretable as statements about the disease stage. P-1217 is the working instance - 87 incident MCI cases against 1,103 incident dementia cases among the same 125,594 UK Biobank participants over a median 11.8 years, an ordering inverted relative to every directly ascertained cohort in this corpus (P-888 SPRINT, expert-panel adjudication: MCI 3.1 vs 1.6 per 100 person-years against probable dementia 3.0 vs 0.8; P-1175's pooled literature inputs likewise put MCI incidence roughly an order of magnitude above AD incidence in the 65+ population) - and it still publishes a first-in-field choline-MCI association and a protective intake range off that endpoint. Downstream, MCI case counts derived this way are the dominant term in attributable-burden and cost models (P-1175: about 1.6 million MCI vs about 110,000 AD cases, US$18,000 million vs US$1,200 million), where the MCI incidence input has to be imported as a single literature constant because no primary ascertainment exists. Absence asserted for this corpus record only.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern of the OCT vendor-shift and peripheral-vs-central-ground-truth gaps: it attacks a ground-truth assumption rather than a missing modality pairing, and it names WHY the absence matters - the bias is differential, so it is directional, and it lands on exactly the socioeconomic and racial gradients that this literature reports as risk factors. Non-obvious because both halves are already in the corpus and have never been put together: the corpus contains the measured sensitivity (P-1046) and it contains the cohorts that inherit it (P-1217), and it contains the adjudicated benchmark that shows the coded ordering is inverted (P-888, MCI incidence at or above dementia incidence). The failure is visible as arithmetic, not interpretation: 87 versus 1,103 in the same 125,594 people is the reverse of the true ordering by a factor of order twenty, and no paper reports that ratio as a validity check. It is also actionable with data already collected - UK Biobank holds both the 87 coded MCI cases and touchscreen cognitive testing on 64,819-75,651 of the same participants.
gaps.closure_criteria: In a cohort that holds BOTH a coded/administrative MCI endpoint and a directly administered cognitive assessment on the same participants (UK Biobank is the concrete case: the 87 ICD-coded incident MCI cases sit inside the 64,819-75,651 participants with touchscreen cognitive testing; a Medicare-linked HRS sample would serve equally), a study that (a) estimates sensitivity and positive predictive value of the coded MCI endpoint against a criterion classification, reported overall and within race-ethnicity, education and dual-eligibility/deprivation strata, and (b) re-estimates at least one published exposure-MCI hazard ratio under probabilistic bias analysis using those stratum-specific operating characteristics, reporting how far the point estimate and its interval move and whether the exposure's MCI-versus-dementia stage contrast survives correction. A burden-model variant closes the downstream half: propagate the same sensitivity distribution through an MCI-attributable case and cost estimate and report the resulting interval alongside the point estimate.
gaps.modality: C5 Clinical/Population (administrative claims and hospital/death-record linked cohort epidemiology; burden modelling)
gaps.task_type: T4 risk-factor association (with T6 burden/cost estimation downstream)
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern of the OCT vendor-shift and peripheral-vs-central-ground-truth gaps: it attacks a ground-truth assumption rather than a missing modality pairing, and it names WHY the absence matters - the bias is differential, so it is directional, and it lands on exactly the socioeconomic and racial gradients that this literature reports as risk factors. Non-obvious because both halves are already in the corpus and have never been put together: the corpus contains the measured sensitivity (P-1046) and it contains the cohorts that inherit it (P-1217), and it contains the adjudicated benchmark that shows the coded ordering is inverted (P-888, MCI incidence at or above dementia incidence). The failure is visible as arithmetic, not interpretation: 87 versus 1,103 in the same 125,594 people is the reverse of the true ordering by a factor of order twenty, and no paper reports that ratio as a validity check. It is also actionable with data already collected - UK Biobank holds both the 87 coded MCI cases and touchscreen cognitive testing on 64,819-75,651 of the same participants.
gaps.critic_falsification: The two anchor numbers come from different health systems and different cohort designs, and the record transfers a bias parameter across that gap. P-1046's 0.062-0.079 detection ratio and its race and dual-eligibility gradient are properties of US Medicare fee-for-service and Advantage billing behaviour in beneficiaries aged 65 and over; P-1217 is UK Biobank inpatient and death-record linkage in a cohort recruited at 40-70. A reviewer can argue that P-1217's 87 MCI cases are explained by its young baseline age and by MCI simply never generating an NHS inpatient episode, without P-1046's US coding-behaviour or disparity structure applying at all - in which case the endpoint is under-captured but not necessarily DIFFERENTIALLY so, and the directional half of the claim, which is the part that makes this more than G-017, weakens to an attenuation argument. The record therefore needs the closure study to estimate the sensitivity IN the cohort being corrected, not to import P-1046's parameters; and a second objection is that P-1165, with a well-powered directly ascertained MCI arm of 136 events, still returns a largely null MCI result, which shows that at least one stage dissociation in this pack survives good ascertainment and cannot be blamed on measurement.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: contains no 'combine modality X with Y' clause; it is a bias-analysis and endpoint-validity gap within a single existing design.

RESTATEMENT: differentiated by id above against G-017, G-NEW-1046-A, G-016, G-033, G-027, G-07 and G-350. The distinguishing content is the use of an ALREADY MEASURED and socially differential sensitivity as bias parameters, and the directional (not merely attenuating) consequence.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: the closest corpus papers were checked individually. P-1046 measures the deficit but fits no exposure model. P-888 and P-1165 avoid the problem by adjudicating or by annual CDR rather than correcting for it. P-961 (NACC, marginal structural Cox with IPW) applies causal weighting for time-varying CONFOUNDING with a clinically adjudicated MCI outcome, not bias analysis for outcome misclassification. P-1217 concedes the undercount and applies Heckman selection models, which address selection into the analytic sample, not outcome-endpoint sensitivity.
TOO_SPECIFIC: not narrow - it applies to every corpus study taking MCI as an outcome from claims, hospital or death-record coding, and to the burden and cost models that consume the resulting rates.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: all five anchor papers are corpus papers and the subject is the corpus's own MCI endpoint, not trial design or drug development.

DATA_SCARCITY: the data already exist. UK Biobank holds the coded outcome and the cognitive testing on the same participants; the bias parameters are already published inside this corpus (P-1046). This is a methodological gap doable today, not a data limitation.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: the METHOD (quantitative bias analysis for outcome misclassification) plainly exists in the external epidemiology literature, and ICD validation studies exist for DEMENTIA. The record does not claim the method is unknown - it claims, scoped to this corpus record, that it has not reached the MCI-outcome cohort literature, and P-1046 (which first quantified the MCI-specific detection deficit at population scale) and P-1217 (which published an uncorrected coded-MCI association in 2025 while conceding the undercount) are the corpus evidence for that scoping. The claim is deliberately about MCI, where sensitivity is about 0.07 and differential, not about dementia, where P-1046 measures detection at 1.086-1.104.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper's own vocabulary carries the construct - P-1046 'undiagnosed', 'detection', observed/expected; P-1217 'MCI case ascertainment from hospital/death records likely undercounts cases'; P-1175 'no China-wide MCI annual cost data' and 'literature-derived MCI incidence'; P-888 'adjudicated incident MCI ... expert panel adjudication'. No inferential bridge is asked of any paper.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: the load-bearing quantities are taken from Results, Methods and Problems fields. The one quote drawn from a significance field (P-1217 'First longitudinal study ...') is cited explicitly as an author CLAIM, which is what the record needs it to be, not as a measured result.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the absence clause is scoped to studies that use an administratively or record-coded MCI endpoint as the outcome of an exposure-effect model. P-888 (adjudicated) and P-1165 (annual CDR) fall outside that clause by construction and are labelled partial closers; P-1046 fits no exposure model. None of the record's own citations falsifies it.

MISASSIGNED_MEASUREMENT_FAMILY: the two arms of the contrast were checked for what they are computed OVER - P-1046 and P-1217 read ICD codes generated by a healthcare encounter, P-888 and P-1165 read a cognitive assessment administered on a protocol schedule to every participant. These are genuinely different ascertainment families, not two instances of one.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked against every T09 existing-gap record and by grepping the 534-statement corpus list for ascertain/ICD/administrative/registry/misclassif/self-report/burden/cost. Nearest neighbours and why this is not a restatement: (1) ACTOR-G-017 - 'MCI case status is operationalised at least four incompatible ways across this corpus ... yet no study applies two or more definitions to the SAME cohort to quantify how much of an effect estimate is attributable to the ascertainment rule'. G-017 is about definitional PLURALITY across studies and its closure is a two-definition re-analysis. This record is about a single definition whose SENSITIVITY has already been measured inside the corpus (P-1046, about 0.07 for MCI against about 1.09 for dementia in the same data) and is DIFFERENTIAL across the exact strata that are studied as risk factors, so the unmet act is quantitative bias analysis with stratum-specific bias parameters and the resulting claim is about the DIRECTION of the bias, neither of which G-017 states. (2) G-NEW-1046-A - extends P-1046's observed/expected MEASUREMENT to non-US populations; this record asks that the measurement already in hand be USED by the cohorts that inherit the bias. (3) ACTOR-G-016 - measurement-source bias (self vs informant vs objective) within MCI participants; that is exposure/instrument source, not outcome-ascertainment completeness. (4) ACTOR-G-033 - label operationalisation and follow-up windows inside ML conversion models, framed around AUC/SHAP artefacts; this record is exposure-effect estimation in cohort epidemiology, not prediction-model quality. (5) ACTOR-G-027 - death as a competing event in MCI-to-AD prognostic models; different bias (competing risk, not outcome misclassification) and different design family. (6) G-07 and G-350 - health-economic ICER/WTP records; neither concerns the ascertainment quality of the MCI incidence input to a burden model. No existing record cites P-1046 alongside a cohort that uses coded MCI as an outcome.

gaps.gap_statement: The MCI and SCD case definitions used across this corpus's affective-risk-factor literature contain a subjective-cognitive-complaint criterion, and the one corpus study that measures what that criterion actually carries finds it carries affect rather than cognition. P-862 (N=1536, five diagnostic stages, 1028 paired informants) reports that participant-reported complaints had no relation to measured cognition in ANY diagnostic group (B = -0.001, 95% CI -0.217 to 0.215, p=0.993) while informant report did (B = -0.777, 95% CI -0.947 to -0.608, p<0.001), and that in the cognitively unimpaired the complainers' higher scores tracked depression and anxiety instead. The exposure of this literature (depressive/anxious symptoms) and the outcome's case definition (a label one of whose conditions is self-reported decline) therefore share one measurement channel. NO corpus study re-estimates an affective-exposure -> MCI effect on the same participants under a complaint-inclusive versus a complaint-free case definition, so the fraction of the published depression/anxiety -> MCI association that is criterion contamination rather than risk is unknown and is unbounded upward. This matters because that association is the corpus's leading psychiatric prevention target (P-912 consolidates depression as the strongest supported psychiatric risk factor; P-843 pools it across 87 prospective cohorts), and a prevention target defined partly out of the outcome's own definition is not modifiable in the sense the recommendation assumes.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'Prognostic models treat central nervous system markers as absolute ground truth' and the XAI-utility gold - it attacks the ground-truth standard rather than adding a missing modality. The non-obvious part is that the corpus already contains the measurement that undermines the criterion (P-862's null) and the corpus already recognises criterion circularity in one of the very papers concerned (P-785), but nobody has connected the measurement to the effect estimates: the field reads P-862 as a paper about which informant to ask, not as a paper that invalidates one clause of the outcome definition used by P-785, P-831, P-843 and P-912. It also proposes a bounded, computable quantity (the ratio of two odds ratios estimated on one cohort) rather than a call for more work.
gaps.closure_criteria: In one cohort that holds a validated affective measure AND two independent channels for the cognitive-complaint criterion - P-862's design (memory clinic, N>=1500, 1028 patient-informant dyads on the identical 12-item instrument) or HCHS/SOL-INCA (N=6140, symptom scales plus an algorithmic MCI label) - estimate the odds ratio for MCI given the affective exposure TWICE on the same participants and the same covariates: (a) with MCI defined by the standard criteria including the self-reported-complaint condition, and (b) with that condition replaced by informant report, or dropped so the label rests on objective performance and function alone. Report the ratio of the two odds ratios with a bootstrap 95% CI, and the reclassification table showing which participants change label. A ratio whose interval excludes 1 establishes that the published affective-risk estimates are partly a definitional artefact and gives the field the correction factor it currently lacks. Falsification: a ratio interval containing 1 in a cohort of this size closes the gap and licenses the existing estimates.

gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is that this is ACTOR-G-016 (measurement-source bias never quantified within the same MCI participants) recombined with ACTOR-G-017/G-033 (case definitions never varied on a fixed cohort) and narrowed to one exposure class - an operator who reads gap families broadly should merge it into G-016 as the affective-exposure instance rather than mint a new record. The second objection is a transfer problem in the anchor: P-862 is a tertiary memory-clinic sample of people who already self-selected by seeking help, so the complaint criterion had in effect already been satisfied by referral, and a null for self-report there may not transfer to the community cohorts (P-785, P-843) where the criterion actually does the selection work. Third, the record cannot establish the SIGN of the contamination. The under-inclusion limb previously rested on P-883's '24% non-complaining impaired patients', which was struck on 2026-09-14: that figure came from a fabricated block and the real paper reports the opposite (anosognosia assessed clinically, 'none of the patients presented this symptom'). The sign is therefore unestablished on narrower evidence than before, and the real P-883 cuts the other way on the record's central thesis in its own cohort - complaint scores DID separate PD-MCI from PD-nMCI (Cognition 31.3 vs 0, r = -.542) and did NOT track mood (depression P = .939, anxiety P = .397, neither correlated with the analysed PDQ-39 scores), where P-862 found the reverse. That contrast is a reason to run the test, not a substitute for it rather than assuming an answer, but it does mean 'unbounded upward' is a statement about what is unknown, not a prediction.

gaps.dedup_note: Checked against every existing gap that touches measurement or case definition. ACTOR-G-016 (self-report/informant/objective sources used interchangeably, disagreement never analysed) is the closest: it is about source disagreement as such, and P-862 actually goes some way to CLOSING it by analysing the disagreement; this record is the downstream claim G-016 does not make - that one of those sources sits inside the OUTCOME DEFINITION of a different literature and therefore biases a specific effect estimate in a known direction. ACTOR-G-017 and ACTOR-G-033 concern ascertainment-rule variation ACROSS studies and its effect on frequency estimates and on ML AUC/SHAP rankings; neither names the complaint criterion, neither concerns an epidemiological exposure effect, and neither proposes an exposure-specific two-definition re-estimation. ACTOR-G-018 is depression dichotomisation versus continuous severity - a specification issue, not a definitional-overlap issue. ACTOR-G-038 is reverse causation of psychosocial SHAP importances in cross-sectional ML - a causal-direction claim about model interpretation, not a measurement-overlap claim about a case definition. ACTOR-G-019 is bidirectionality and within/between-person variance. Theme-file gaps checked: ACTOR-G-072, ACTOR-G-046, G-NEW-1041-A, MINE-G-001, MINE-G-004 - none concerns the complaint criterion.

gaps.gap_statement: This corpus's neuropsychiatric and behavioural prognostic studies enter their exposure as a single fixed baseline value of a symptom class that is episodic and remitting, even where repeated measurements were collected, and no study re-fits the same model with the exposure specified as a visit-updated time-varying covariate with a paired difference test; P-1142 (811 ADNI MCI) is the affective-exposure demonstration nearest to it, entering longitudinal depressive-symptom trajectory classes with the baseline GDS-15 in one Cox model, without the paired baseline-versus-time-varying contrast. The one corpus study that fits BOTH specifications on one cohort finds the baseline specification carries no prognostic signal at all: P-1138 (74 probable MCI-LB, median three visits, up to 8.8 years) reports decline steepening with accumulating features (-1.1 ACE-R points/year per feature, p<0.001; visual hallucinations -2.1/year; cognitive fluctuations -3.4/year) while its baseline-only sensitivity analysis is flat, and it measures the churn that explains why - a 25.5% annual probability of a new feature appearing. Two consequences follow that the field has not registered. First, the null affective results in this corpus cannot currently be read as true nulls, because attenuation from a mis-specified exposure and a genuine absence of effect are indistinguishable under a baseline-fixed design. Second, and more damaging to the field's stated purpose, MODIFIABILITY cannot be estimated from an exposure held fixed at baseline: a design that never observes the exposure change cannot estimate what changing it would do, yet 'modifiable risk factor' is exactly the claim this literature makes.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'Machine learning architectures force continuous, interval-censored multi-visit clinical trial data into artificial, discrete cross-sectional binary labels' - a data-structure critique of how the exposure is represented rather than a missing-modality complaint. Its non-obvious element is the direction of the argument: the corpus already contains a clean, quantified refutation of the universal specification (P-1138's null baseline arm), sitting in a paper nobody reads as a methodological result because it is filed as a Lewy-body clinical study. The record also converts a vague call for longitudinal work into a specific paired estimate on an open dataset, and it identifies a claim the field cannot make at all under its current designs - modifiability from a fixed exposure - which is stronger than saying the estimates are noisy.
gaps.closure_criteria: Re-fit an existing multi-wave cohort that already holds repeated affective or behavioural measurements - PPMI is the concrete instance (P-997: 423 at baseline, 315 retained at year 5, annual NPS instruments for depression, anxiety, apathy, psychosis and impulse-control disorders) - with the SAME outcome, the SAME covariates and the SAME estimation method under two exposure specifications: (a) baseline-fixed NPS presence, and (b) time-varying / cumulative NPS as a covariate updated at each visit. Report the decline-rate coefficient or hazard ratio under each with a paired test of the difference and its confidence interval, plus the change in discrimination, and pre-specify what magnitude of difference would count. Extend to the affective exposures specifically by repeating on a cohort with repeated depression/anxiety scales. Falsification: if the two specifications give statistically indistinguishable coefficients in a cohort of PPMI's size, the baseline convention is vindicated for this exposure class and the gap closes.

gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern 'Machine learning architectures force continuous, interval-censored multi-visit clinical trial data into artificial, discrete cross-sectional binary labels' - a data-structure critique of how the exposure is represented rather than a missing-modality complaint. Its non-obvious element is the direction of the argument: the corpus already contains a clean, quantified refutation of the universal specification (P-1138's null baseline arm), sitting in a paper nobody reads as a methodological result because it is filed as a Lewy-body clinical study. The record also converts a vague call for longitudinal work into a specific paired estimate on an open dataset, and it identifies a claim the field cannot make at all under its current designs - modifiability from a fixed exposure - which is stronger than saying the estimates are noisy.
gaps.critic_falsification: The motivating demonstration may be a power artefact rather than a specification result. P-1138's baseline-only arm is a SENSITIVITY analysis in a 74-case single-region cohort with a median of three visits, and the digest reports no estimate, interval or test for that arm at all - only that it did not predict. A null in a small sensitivity analysis is as consistent with insufficient power as with mis-specification, and if it is the former the record loses the fact that distinguishes it from a generic call for longitudinal work. Compounding this, P-1138's own limitation list concedes that cognitive fluctuations 'partly reflect cognitive state itself, risking circularity', and fluctuations carry the strongest coefficient (-3.4/year) in the time-varying arm - so part of the time-varying arm's advantage may be definitional rather than prognostic, which would cut the contrast from both ends. A secondary objection is the overlap with ACTOR-G-019, whose >=3-wave joint model would incidentally supply most of what this record asks for.

gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: This corpus's neuropsychiatric and behavioural prognostic studies enter their exposure as a single fixed baseline value of a symptom class that is episodic and remitting, even where repeated measurements were collected, and no study re-fits the same model with the exposure specified as time-varying. The one corpus study that fits BOTH specifications on one cohort finds the baseline specification carries no prognostic signal at all: P-1138 (74 probable MCI-LB, median three visits, up to 8.8 years) reports decline steepening with accumulating features (-1.1 ACE-R points/year per feature, p<0.001; visual hallucinations -2.1/year; cognitive fluctuations -3.4/year) while its baseline-only sensitivity analysis is flat, and it measures the churn that explains why - a 25.5% annual probability of a new feature appearing. Two consequences follow that the field has not registered. First, the null affective results in this corpus cannot currently be read as true nulls, because attenuation from a mis-specified exposure and a genuine absence of effect are indistinguishable under a baseline-fixed design. Second, and more damaging to the field's stated purpose, MODIFIABILITY cannot be estimated from an exposure held fixed at baseline: a design that never observes the exposure change cannot estimate what changing it would do, yet 'modifiable risk factor' is exactly the claim this literature makes.

gaps.gap_statement: Follow-up horizon is an estimand-defining parameter of the psychiatric-risk-for-MCI literature and it is never modelled as one. In the corpus's only quantitative synthesis of modifiable exposures for INCIDENT MCI in cognitively normal older adults (P-843; 87 prospective cohorts, 225,584 participants), the same exposure is significant or null according to which follow-up window its pool covers - the significant pools include 'the six-year anxiety pool, the three-year depression odds-ratio pool, the five-year depression hazard-ratio pool' while the null pools include 'the four-year anxiety pool, the six-year depression pool'. These are separate estimands and must NOT be merged into a contradiction; the gap is that the parameter separating them is discarded rather than estimated. A +/-1-year matching rule cut 87 studies to 20, and no band stratification or meta-regression on follow-up duration was pre-specified. The absence is consequential because the SLOPE of a pooled effect against follow-up horizon is the one discriminator between a prodrome and a cause that this literature can compute from data it already holds: an exposure that is a prodromal manifestation should show its association decay as the horizon lengthens, whereas a causal exposure should not. Both P-843 and P-831 name the prodrome-versus-risk-factor question as unresolved, and P-912 lists it as open, yet the corpus contains no estimate of the decay slope - so 'depression is a modifiable risk factor for MCI' is published without the test that would separate it from a marker of pathology already present.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern that challenges 'the fundamental temporal assumptions' of the field and asks for mathematical evidence of a temporal structure, rather than naming a missing combination. The non-obvious element is that the corpus's own numbers already show the two affective exposures behaving in OPPOSITE temporal directions - depression significant at three and five years and null at six, anxiety null at four and significant at six - which is precisely the dissociation a prodrome-versus-cause test would be designed to detect, and which the review that printed both never comments on. It also proposes a falsifiable quantity (the slope of log effect on follow-up years, with a pre-specified band stratification) on data that exists, rather than a call for new cohorts.
gaps.closure_criteria: A meta-regression of the log effect size on follow-up duration as a continuous moderator, fitted separately for depression and for anxiety, across the FULL assembled prospective-cohort set that P-843 already screened (87 studies, 225,584 participants) rather than the 20-study window-matched subset, with the effect-measure family (OR versus HR) entered as a covariate so that measure and horizon are not confounded; reported as the slope with a 95% CI, alongside a pre-specified band stratification (<=3, 4-6, >6 years) and a test of between-band heterogeneity. An individual-participant-data version in a single large multi-wave cohort, estimating the exposure's hazard ratio at successive horizons from one fitted model, would be stronger still. INTERPRETATION FIXED IN ADVANCE: a significantly negative slope for depression with a non-negative slope for anxiety establishes the prodrome-versus-cause dissociation both P-843 and P-831 name as unresolved; a flat slope for both closes the gap and licenses the horizon-pooled reading the field currently assumes.

gaps.critic_falsification:
[T10_sleep_mood_behaviour_p1-gap-03] The pattern the record is built on may be nothing but the effect-measure confound. In P-843 the significant depression pools are an odds-ratio pool at three years and a hazard-ratio pool at five, and the null is at six - so window and effect measure vary together across the pools, and the constituent study sets differ as well. A reader could argue that with seven significant and seven null pools drawn from overlapping cohorts (the digest notes seven pools rest on Geda 2014 plus Krell-Roesch 2021a and that 55.2 per cent of included studies come from a single country), the apparent horizon-dependence is sampling noise in a small, non-independent study set, and that the decay slope would be uninterpretable however it came out. That objection does not remove the gap - it argues the closure test must carry the effect-measure covariate and a leave-one-cohort-family-out sensitivity analysis, which the closure criteria now specify - but it does mean the record's motivating pattern is suggestive rather than established, and it must not be written up as evidence that depression IS a prodrome.

[T13_evidence_synthesis_p2-gap-02] The strongest objection: methodologists may hold that +/-1-year outcome-ascertainment matching is a legitimate standardisation (reducing genuine heterogeneity) rather than an artificial constraint, so the 67-study exclusion could be defended as rigor, making the gap a criticism of one paper's analysis plan rather than a field-level absence. The rebuttal inside the record is that no corpus study offers the window-stratified alternative either, and P-843's own verdict flips show the choice of window is outcome-determining - but an operator could still rule this TOO_SPECIFIC for a single-paper practice. Secondary: an external methodological paper on follow-up-window sensitivity in dementia-incidence pooling may exist (EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE risk for the generic method), which would leave open only the MCI-specific application.

gaps.gap_statement: In the corpus sleep-MCI association studies the OUTCOME is a single-session cognitive screener (MoCA-BJ in P-1159, TICS-10 at 1 SD below the age-group mean in P-891, a two-item screening operationalisation in P-803) while the EXPOSURE is exactly the state that acutely depresses performance on the attention, processing-speed and delayed-recall items those screeners score. None of these studies records the participant's sleep on the night before, or sleepiness at the time of, the cognitive assessment; none adjusts for it; and none re-tests screener-defined MCI cases after a rested night or against a diagnosis that does not come from a single screening session. Their odds ratios therefore cannot separate a disease association from a same-session state effect on the measuring instrument - a third reading that is neither the causal nor the reverse-causal reading these papers do discuss, and that does not require either. This matters because these are the estimates that make sleep a 'modifiable target': P-930 turns them into 'sleep disturbance as a modifiable risk factor in MCI', P-891 into 'quantitative targets for sleep health guidance', and P-1159 into a case for 'positioning sleep assessment within cardiology care pathways'. Note the direction: because the exposure is habitual sleep (PSQI over the preceding month, CHARLS trouble-sleeping over the past week), a habitually poor sleeper is more likely than a good sleeper to be sleep-degraded on any single test day, so the expected bias runs WITH the reported association rather than toward the null - which is the opposite of what the generic 'recall and misclassification bias' concession in P-891 implies.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches two gold patterns at once: the ground-truth/temporal-assumption pattern (prognostic and risk models treating a proxy label as the disease state) and the calibration-across-setting pattern. It is non-obvious because these papers LOOK like they have covered the bias space: they discuss causality, reverse causality, recall bias and residual confounding, so a reader ticks the methodological boxes and moves on. The pathway they miss is the one that needs no causal story at all - poor sleep lowering the score on the instrument that defines the outcome, in the same session. The direction argument sharpens it further: because the exposure is habitual sleep rather than a single night, the misclassification is expected to be correlated with the outcome, which invalidates the implicit 'misclassification biases toward the null' defence that a generic recall-bias concession invokes. The gap is also cheap to close - the missing variable is a two-item sleepiness rating and a prior-night sleep question at the assessment visit - which is what makes an uncorrected 1.39x pooled risk estimate and a care-pathway recommendation hard to defend.
gaps.closure_criteria: In a single cohort of N >= 300 community or clinic participants including >= 100 who meet a screener threshold for MCI, with cognitive status independently adjudicated (clinical consensus or biomarker-anchored) and habitual sleep measured by both questionnaire and >= 7 nights of actigraphy: administer the cognitive screener twice in counterbalanced order - once after a documented habitual night and once after a documented short/disturbed night (or with prior-night actigraphy and a same-session sleepiness scale recorded at each administration) - and report (a) the sleep-MCI odds ratio with and without adjustment for test-session state, (b) the proportion of screener-defined MCI cases that reclassify as non-MCI on the rested administration, and (c) the same association re-estimated against the adjudicated diagnosis. The gap closes if the association survives (a) and (c) with the reclassification rate in (b) quantified; it is confirmed if a material fraction of the odds ratio is attributable to test-session state.

gaps.critic_falsification: The exposure in all three studies is HABITUAL sleep (PSQI over the preceding month; CHARLS trouble-sleeping over the past week), not the previous night, so the state pathway is not direct: it requires that habitual poor sleepers are also disproportionately sleep-degraded at the assessment session. That link is plausible but is itself unmeasured in every paper cited, including mine. If the day-to-day correlation between habitual sleep quality and test-day state is weak, the contamination is small and the gap shrinks to a reporting nicety rather than a threat to the estimates. A second, weaker objection: acute sleep-deprivation-and-cognition experiments exist in the wider literature, so a reviewer applying EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE could argue the principle is established - the reply is that this record is not asking for the principle to be demonstrated but for it to be propagated into the risk-factor estimates that these papers convert into screening and guidance recommendations, which is a within-paper methodological absence, not a corpus-sampling artefact.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no combine-X-with-Y clause. The record asks for a control variable and a re-analysis within existing designs, not for a new modality pairing.

DATA_SCARCITY: the missing data are not scarce - prior-night sleep and same-session sleepiness are one or two extra questions at a visit that already administers a 30-item screener and a 19-item PSQI; CHARLS-type surveys and single-centre clinic studies could both collect them at negligible cost.

TOO_SPECIFIC: the absence spans three independent cohorts on three different screeners (MoCA-BJ, TICS-10, a two-item operationalisation) in three different sampling frames (hospital CHF, national survey, community), plus the 188-study landscape of P-963.
RESTATEMENT: differentiated by id above against ACTOR-G-072, G-046, G-038, G-018 and MINE-G-001.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: this is measurement validity inside corpus risk-factor studies, the same territory as the accepted G-018, G-038 and MINE-G-001 records; it is not trial design or drug development.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: each cited paper's own vocabulary carries the construct - P-1159 names MoCA-BJ and PSQI in its methods field, P-891 names its screening-based MCI operationalisation and its self-report sleep bias, P-803's digest names its two-item screening operationalisation, P-963 quantifies questionnaire dominance. P-963 is a measurement review and reports no cognitive-outcome state control; P-930 reports intervention effects on sleep, not off-state cognitive endpoints; P-823 has no results at all. None of the record's own citations does the thing the record says is absent.

ACTOR-G-072 (sleep measurement heterogeneous, no core outcome set, no harmonised protocol) is about how the sleep EXPOSURE is measured across studies; this record is about the cognitive OUTCOME instrument being moved by that exposure - a different quantity, and one a core outcome set for sleep would not fix. gaps.gap_statement: In this corpus's cardiometabolic-comorbidity work on MCI, the exposure is always an ever/never diagnosis code or prescription-class flag and never the achieved level of control of the condition (HbA1c, LDL, blood pressure) modelled as a time-varying quantity - every one of the five frontier studies concedes the omission in its own limitation field. This matters because a coded diagnosis is not a modifiable quantity, only control is, so these studies cannot support the secondary-prevention recommendations they issue; and because without that intermediate the corpus reports the disease and its own treatment with opposite signs on the same axis (hyperlipidemia HR 1.21 for AD dementia in P-1151 against lipid-modifying and antihypertensive drugs among the classes associated with REDUCED progression in P-1157, and antihypertensive classes at aHR 0.96-0.98 in P-999) with nothing measured that could separate a real protective drug effect from confounding by indication or from patients whose condition was simply better controlled. The one frontier study that does substitute measured metabolic quantities for the binary reverses the answer: in P-688's three-year T2DM cohort HbA1c went null after adjustment while hypoglycaemic-episode burden carried the association. ABSENCE ASSERTED FOR THIS CORPUS ONLY.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'a data-structure violation' and 'a measurement never calibrated across settings' - specifically the gold entry that criticises forcing continuous clinical data into an artificial discrete label, transposed to the exposure side. It is non-obvious in three ways. First, the absence is not that anyone forgot: all five papers name it themselves, so the gap is that a five-paper literature has converged on the same known mis-specification without any of them fixing it. Second, the consequence is a sign reversal, not a precision loss - the corpus tells a clinician both that hyperlipidemia raises AD-dementia hazard and that lipid-modifying drugs lower progression hazard, which are near-collinear exposures in real care. Third, the corpus already contains the falsifying experiment in miniature: the only frontier paper that measured a control marker (P-688) found it null after adjustment while an unmeasured-in-every-other-paper quantity (hypoglycaemic-episode burden) carried the signal - so the substitution is not predicted to be a null exercise.
gaps.closure_criteria: An MCI cohort drawn from an EHR or claims system with linked laboratory results (e.g. a TriNetX/Optum lab-linked extract, a national primary-care database, or NACC linked to VA labs), N >= 5,000 incident-MCI patients with at least two pre-index and two post-index measurements of HbA1c, LDL and systolic blood pressure. Fit a marginal-structural or target-trial-emulation Cox model of 5-year MCI-to-all-cause-dementia conversion in which the exposure is the achieved-control trajectory (time-varying), and report (a) the hazard ratio for achieved control within the ever-coded stratum, and (b) how the ever-coded diagnosis hazard ratio and the treatment-class hazard ratio move when achieved control is entered - both estimated in the SAME cohort and reported side by side. Closure requires the disease-code and drug-class estimates to be reported from one cohort with the control measure present, not two cohorts with it absent.
gaps.task_type: T2 (MCI-to-dementia conversion), with T4 risk-association arms

gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest argument against: the broader (non-corpus) literature has substantial work on glycaemic control and cognitive decline - ACCORD-MIND and the large cohort studies relating HbA1c and glucose trajectories to dementia incidence - so a reviewer may code this EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE on the grounds that 'achieved control predicts dementia' is a settled question. My defence is that the unmet quantity here is narrower and is genuinely a corpus-record absence: not whether HbA1c predicts dementia in the general population, but whether the ever-coded-diagnosis hazard reported for an EXISTING MCI cohort survives adjustment for achieved control, estimated with the drug-class hazard in the same cohort so the sign discordance can be attributed. A reviewer who judges that narrowing to be a distinction without a difference should reject this record, and I would not argue the point past that. A second, weaker objection: P-1106's hazard ratios are stated in the corpus record to sit 'in the manuscript tables' and are not reproduced in its digest, so it is possible that P-1106 reports more of the disease-versus-drug contrast than the corpus can see; the record scopes its claims about that paper to the corpus record for exactly this reason.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: this is not 'combine modality X with Y'. It concerns the specification of one existing exposure variable inside models that already exist, using laboratory data already held by the same EHR and claims systems these five studies used.

RESTATEMENT: differentiated by id against ACTOR-G-017, G-018, G-027, G-033, G-039, G-052, MINE-G-004, G-351, G-CAND-351 and G-NEW-1043-A in the why_new field; none of them concerns achieved cardiometabolic control as an exposure, and none carries the disease-versus-treatment sign discordance.

TOO_SPECIFIC: the record spans three condition classes (glycaemia, lipids, blood pressure) and four independent data families (TriNetX, Optum, NACC, Taiwan VGH), not a single paper or a single disease.

DATA_SCARCITY: the missing data are routine laboratory results that already sit in the systems these studies queried. P-1151's own improvement field asks for 'time-dependent biomarker modelling' and P-999's asks to 'incorporate dose/adherence, blood-pressure trajectories and laboratory measures' - both treat the data as available, not scarce.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the absence clause is scoped to what each cited paper states about itself, and the one paper that partially falsifies a broader version (P-688, which does measure HbA1c) is named as a partial closer inside the record rather than cited as support. No clause of the form 'no study measures HbA1c' is asserted.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every claiming paper's quote uses the construct's own vocabulary - laboratory variation, blood pressure control, dose, medication duration, time-varying treatment - taken from that paper's problems or improvement field, not inferred from an unrelated result.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: the two quotes used as measured findings (P-1151 HR 1.21, P-688 adjusted OR 1.663 p=0.098) come from the results fields and carry their intervals; the limitation quotes are labelled and used only as evidence of the absence, never as findings.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: the closure design is an observational re-analysis in cohorts the corpus already contains, not drug development or trial design.
gaps.dedup_note: Checked against the 8 records in T11_comorbidity_existing_gaps.md and grepped existing_gaps.md for ICD / comorbid / diabet / hypertens / HbA1c / medication / polypharm / claims / severity / dose / treated / glyc / LDL / blood pressure / lipid. (1) ACTOR-G-017 and ACTOR-G-033 are about the MCI/conversion OUTCOME label being operationalised incompatibly; this record is about the EXPOSURE variable and never touches case definition. (2) ACTOR-G-018 is the structural sibling in a different exposure family - depression dichotomised at a scale cut-off, with a severity inversion observed at one Korean centre; it says nothing about cardiometabolic conditions, ever-coded diagnoses, or the disease-versus-treatment sign discordance, and its evidence base and closure test are disjoint from this one. (3) ACTOR-G-039 is nominal-versus-delivered dose for neuromodulation electric fields - the same family of 'nominal exposure is not received exposure' but a different literature, different quantity and different closure test; MINE-G-004 already proposes that a 'nominal versus received dose' gap family be recognised, and this record is a third member, not a duplicate of either. (4) ACTOR-G-052 asks for an RCT of glucose-lowering drugs with an MCI-without-diabetes control arm to isolate neuroprotective from glycemic effects - a trial-design gap about drug mechanism; this is an observational exposure-definition gap about whether the reported comorbidity hazard is an effect of the disease or of its poor management, and neither closes the other. (5) ACTOR-G-027 (death as competing risk) and G-351 / G-CAND-351 / G-NEW-1043-A (AF and anticoagulation claims pathways) are on different axes. (6) Nothing in existing_records_core.md covers this: the only comorbidity entry is KA-02, a CHF predictor-surprise assumption. (7) The pack's own reader lead proposes P-1151 vs P-1157 as an opposite-signed CONFLICT; this record is not that conflict, it is the statement that the corpus holds no measurement that could resolve it, and the two are complementary rather than duplicative.

evidence_quotes.supports: The paper naming the missing specification itself, in its own improvement field.

evidence_quotes.supports: That the corpus's own multi-state medication model cannot separate the drug from the condition it is prescribed for.

gaps.gap_statement: The dementia-SUBTYPE dissociation that turns the comorbidity literature from a risk association into a mechanism claim - diabetes tracking vascular dementia, hyperlipidemia tracking Alzheimer's dementia - is estimated in this corpus entirely against clinician-assigned ICD subtype labels in cohorts with no amyloid, tau or autopsy confirmation, and the exposure is itself one of the cues that pushes a coder toward a vascular rather than an AD label. The corpus therefore has no bound on exposure-dependent outcome misclassification for the one result it reads mechanistically. Two further corpus facts show the field is aware of the hole and has not filled it: P-1081, the largest EHR conversion cohort (59,782 veterans), avoids subtype claims by using an all-cause endpoint and lists 'disease-specific (AD vs vascular) endpoints' as unfinished; and P-946, the only corpus study that puts routine cardiometabolic history and biologically measured amyloid status in one model at the MCI stage, offers hypertension and diabetes as candidate predictors and does not retain either in its MCI model. ABSENCE ASSERTED FOR THIS CORPUS ONLY.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern that challenges a ground-truth standard - the entry criticising prognostic models for treating CNS markers as absolute ground truth, and the entry on MCI case definitions being misaligned with computational models. The non-obvious step is the direction of the bias: this is not generic outcome misclassification, which would attenuate toward the null, but misclassification that is a FUNCTION OF THE EXPOSURE. A patient carrying a coded vascular risk factor is more likely to have their dementia coded vascular, which manufactures exactly the dissociation P-1151 reports and reads mechanistically. The corpus supplies the check and it comes back negative: P-946 offers hypertension and diabetes to a model with a biologically measured amyloid endpoint at the MCI stage and retains neither, while hypertension enters only at the dementia stage where clinical labelling and vascular burden are most entangled. Cross-corpus, the largest routine-data cohort (P-1081) declines the subtype endpoint outright and names it as unfinished, which is a paper-declared statement of the absence rather than a miner's inference.
gaps.closure_criteria: A cohort of MCI patients with BOTH a clinically or ICD-assigned dementia-subtype endpoint AND an independent aetiological anchor (amyloid PET or CSF Abeta42/40 and p-tau, plasma p-tau217, or autopsy), N >= 500 MCI cases with >= 150 incident dementia events and recorded diabetes / hyperlipidemia / hypertension status. Re-estimate the exposure-specific hazards twice in the same cohort - once against the clinical subtype label, once against the biomarker-defined aetiology - and report the change in the diabetes-versus-hyperlipidemia subtype contrast between the two specifications, together with a quantitative bias analysis (e.g. probabilistic sensitivity analysis over differential subtype-misclassification probabilities) showing what degree of exposure-dependent mislabelling would erase the dissociation. Closure requires the two endpoint definitions to be compared within one cohort, not across studies.
gaps.modality: C5 Clinical/Population (EHR, claims, memory-clinic cohorts) with amyloid PET as reference standard
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern that challenges a ground-truth standard - the entry criticising prognostic models for treating CNS markers as absolute ground truth, and the entry on MCI case definitions being misaligned with computational models. The non-obvious step is the direction of the bias: this is not generic outcome misclassification, which would attenuate toward the null, but misclassification that is a FUNCTION OF THE EXPOSURE. A patient carrying a coded vascular risk factor is more likely to have their dementia coded vascular, which manufactures exactly the dissociation P-1151 reports and reads mechanistically. The corpus supplies the check and it comes back negative: P-946 offers hypertension and diabetes to a model with a biologically measured amyloid endpoint at the MCI stage and retains neither, while hypertension enters only at the dementia stage where clinical labelling and vascular burden are most entangled. Cross-corpus, the largest routine-data cohort (P-1081) declines the subtype endpoint outright and names it as unfinished, which is a paper-declared statement of the absence rather than a miner's inference.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest argument against is EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE. Clinicopathological correlation studies relating vascular risk factors to autopsy-confirmed dementia neuropathology do exist outside this corpus, and a reviewer may hold that the general question - does clinical dementia-subtype labelling misclassify pathology, and does that distort risk-factor estimates - is long settled, making the corpus absence a sampling artefact. My narrowing is that the unmet item is the specific re-estimation of the P-1151 diabetes-versus-hyperlipidemia subtype CONTRAST under an aetiologically anchored endpoint in one cohort with a bias analysis attached, not the general clinicopathological question; but that narrowing is a judgement call and a reviewer who rejects it should reject the record. A second, sharper objection concerns P-1150: NACC diagnoses are expert consensus at ADRCs with biomarker and autopsy subsets available, so if P-1150's full paper contains a biomarker-confirmed subgroup the 'no aetiological anchor anywhere' framing weakens - which is why P-1150 is scoped out of the claiming set and flagged for checking. A third: P-946's negative is weak evidence. It is a stepwise selection outcome in 410 patients at one Korean centre with no split-sample or resampling, so 'cardiometabolic history carries no amyloid information in MCI' is not established by it and the record must not be read as asserting that.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no 'combine X with Y' clause. The record asks that one existing estimate be re-derived against a validated endpoint in one cohort, plus a bias analysis.

RESTATEMENT: differentiated by id against G-01, ACTOR-G-014, G-017, G-025, G-033, G-037 and G-NEW-1047-A in why_new, and against sibling candidate T11_comorbidity_p1-gap-01. None concerns the aetiological validity of a dementia-subtype endpoint in comorbidity survival models.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: P-1151 and P-1081 are cited only for quotes in the construct's own vocabulary (ICD-diagnosis bias, aetiology-specific endpoint, EHR outcome misclassification, biomarker modelling). gaps.gap_statement: In cardiometabolic comorbidity cohorts the MCI label is assigned from a single cognitive screen administered while the patient is an inpatient for the index disease, and not one of these studies re-tests the same patients after clinical stabilisation to report how many labels persist. This is not a criterion-heterogeneity problem: even a perfectly standardised MoCA<26 applied identically everywhere would still be contaminated here, because the acute-illness severity that depresses an in-admission screen (decompensation, hyper/hypoglycaemia, hospital sleep disruption, sedatives) is the same quantity that drives the exposures under test - PSQI sleep quality, HOMA-IR, glycaemia, insulin-signalling analytes. The corpus's own preoperative-screening review states the confound outright (cognitive deficits detected in inpatient settings may reflect acute illness such as delirium rather than MCI, with prevalence spanning 25.5-69.0 per cent across settings) and the acute-heart-failure study concedes it has no delirium screen at all, yet every downstream number in this literature - the 58 per cent CHF prevalence, the 53-61 per cent ward prevalences in T2DM, the OR 1.257 per PSQI point, the OR 1.741 for HOMA-IR, the nomogram C-index 0.863 - is estimated against that unvalidated label with the transient component sitting in both the exposure and the outcome.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'Prognostic models treat central nervous system markers as absolute ground truth' and 'a measurement never calibrated across settings' - it attacks the ground truth itself rather than a missing modality. The non-obvious part is the direction of the bias: this is not generic noise in the outcome, it is a shared cause. Acute-illness severity depresses the in-admission MoCA/MMSE AND raises HOMA-IR, worsens PSQI, disturbs glycaemia and perturbs the insulin-signalling analytes being proposed as markers, so the contamination is correlated between exposure and outcome and inflates rather than attenuates the reported associations. That also explains a pattern nobody in the pack comments on: ward MCI prevalences of 53-61 per cent in T2DM and 58 per cent in CHF sit at or above the top of P-757's cross-setting range. And the gap is closable with the patients these studies already have - it is a within-study omission, not a data-scarcity problem.
gaps.closure_criteria: A prospective cohort of at least 200 patients admitted to a cardiology or endocrinology ward who receive, during the admission, (a) the same screen the cited studies use (MoCA or MMSE) and (b) a validated delirium instrument (CAM or 4AT), and who are re-tested at least 3 months after discharge with multi-domain neuropsychological testing plus a functional/informant criterion. Primary endpoint: the proportion of in-admission MCI labels that persist as stable MCI at re-test, with kappa and the positive predictive value of the in-admission screen for stable MCI. Secondary endpoint: re-estimation of at least one published in-admission association from this literature (e.g. the PSQI OR 1.257 per point, or the HOMA-IR OR 1.741) against both the in-admission label and the post-stabilisation label, reporting the change in the point estimate.
gaps.modality: C5 Clinical/Population (MoCA/MMSE cognitive screens in disease-specific inpatient cohorts), with C3 Molecular/Fluid analytes estimated against the same label
gaps.task_type: T1 (MCI detection / risk nomograms) and T4 (association studies)

And the gap is closable with the patients these studies already have - it is a within-study omission, not a data-scarcity problem.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is that the shared-cause argument is my inference, not any cited paper's measurement. No paper in this set reports that its MoCA/MMSE scores changed after stabilisation, and none reports a correlation between acute-illness severity and the screen score, so the claim that the bias inflates rather than attenuates the associations is a mechanism I am asserting from clinical plausibility. A defender could reply that MoCA<26 in a stable-phase CHF or T2DM ward admission is a reasonable proxy for chronic impairment, that the 58 and 61 per cent prevalences reflect genuinely high burden in these high-risk groups rather than transient dysfunction, and that P-1159's and P-1085's cohorts were not acutely decompensated at testing. That reply cannot be checked from the digests either - which is itself the gap, but it does mean the record's directional claim about the bias is weaker than its claim about the missing measurement, and the gap statement should be read as anchored on the latter.

P-757 names the confound but is a review whose own problems field records that no preoperative primary study existed to include.

TOO_SPECIFIC: the defect spans eight papers, two disease areas (heart failure, type 2 diabetes), two instruments (MoCA/MoCA-BJ and MMSE), four independent T2DM centres and two countries; it is a shared blind spot, not one paper's limitation.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: the validity of the MCI label is the corpus's central construct; nothing here is trial design or drug development.

RESTATEMENT: differentiated by id against ACTOR-G-033, G-047, G-020, G-048, G-054 and G-001 in why_new, on the specific ground that this is a timing-of-measurement defect that survives criterion standardisation.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: the claim is deliberately not 'nobody anywhere has ever re-tested cognition after acute illness'. It is that each of these six primary studies could have re-tested its own patients and reported the persistence rate, and none did, so the quantity needed to interpret their own published effect sizes does not exist for their own cohorts. That is the methodological within-paper form the brief prefers over a structural corpus-absence claim.

DATA_SCARCITY: the opposite - these are hospitalised patients under routine cardiology/endocrinology follow-up, so a 3-month post-discharge re-test is among the cheapest possible additions to the existing protocols.
COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no combine-X-with-Y clause anywhere; the missing item is a second measurement of an existing variable, not a new modality pairing.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every cited paper's own block carries the gap's vocabulary - hospitalised/inpatient and cross-sectional MoCA in P-1085/P-1206/P-1212/P-1219, delirium explicitly in P-751 and P-757, and P-1111 and P-920 are cited only as partial closers on quotes that are about cognitive re-assessment and delirium.

gaps.gap_statement: Diabetes-restricted MCI biomarker studies estimate every contrast inside the diabetic population, so an analyte's position on the diabetes axis is never separated from its position on the cognition axis: no study in the cluster reports the marker in non-diabetic MCI. The cluster's own data show this is decisive rather than merely tidy. P-1219, the only paper here carrying a non-diabetic arm, reports serum RBP HIGHER in diabetes-without-MCI than in healthy controls and LOWER in diabetic MCI than in diabetes-without-MCI - opposite directions along the two axes - and then publishes a within-diabetes cut-off of 38.90 mg/L (sensitivity 0.703, specificity 0.539) whose meaning depends entirely on where non-diabetic MCI sits relative to that cut-off, which is not measured. Under one reading low RBP indexes neurodegeneration; under the other it indexes partial normalisation of a diabetes-induced elevation, in which case the cut-off tracks metabolic control rather than cognition. This matters because the cluster's outputs are clinic-facing: a cut-off read this way is not transportable to any population with a different diabetes case-mix, a patient whose glycaemic control changes can cross it with no change in cognition, and the therapeutic targets these papers nominate (BVR-A activation, CDR1as/alpha-Syn modulation, Gal-3 acting through its TREM2-ligand link to AD neuroinflammation) are assigned to the cognition axis on evidence that cannot separate the two.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern in which prognostic work treats a marker's meaning as fixed and the record challenges the ground-truth mapping instead of asking for another modality. Two things make it non-obvious. First, the decisive evidence is a direction reversal that the cluster's own paper reports and does not comment on: RBP goes UP with diabetes and DOWN with MCI, so a low value is ambiguous between two clinically opposite readings, and the ambiguity is invisible if you only ever look inside diabetes. Second, it identifies a case where the field's own stated fix is the wrong fix - P-1212 asks for healthy controls and P-1250 asks for non-diabetic replication, and neither would resolve the interaction that the published cut-offs depend on. The closure design is cheap, uses assays these groups already run, and produces a single interpretable number (the interaction term).
gaps.closure_criteria: A single-assay-run four-cell study (T2DM+MCI, T2DM+cognitively normal, non-diabetic MCI, non-diabetic cognitively normal), at least 100 participants per cell, MCI adjudicated identically in all four cells, reporting for at least one of the cluster's analytes (serum RBP, plasma BVR-A, Gal-3 or CDR1as): the diabetes main effect, the cognition main effect, and the diabetes-by-cognition interaction term with its p-value; plus the sensitivity and specificity of the published within-diabetes cut-off (e.g. RBP 38.90 mg/L) when applied to the non-diabetic MCI versus non-diabetic normal contrast. A significant interaction with a non-transportable cut-off confirms the marker is reading the metabolic axis; parallel main effects with a transportable cut-off closes the gap the other way.
gaps.modality: C3 Molecular/Fluid (plasma/serum analytes) in C5 disease-restricted clinical populations
gaps.task_type: T1 (MCI detection within a comorbid population)
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern in which prognostic work treats a marker's meaning as fixed and the record challenges the ground-truth mapping instead of asking for another modality. Two things make it non-obvious. First, the decisive evidence is a direction reversal that the cluster's own paper reports and does not comment on: RBP goes UP with diabetes and DOWN with MCI, so a low value is ambiguous between two clinically opposite readings, and the ambiguity is invisible if you only ever look inside diabetes. Second, it identifies a case where the field's own stated fix is the wrong fix - P-1212 asks for healthy controls and P-1250 asks for non-diabetic replication, and neither would resolve the interaction that the published cut-offs depend on. The closure design is cheap, uses assays these groups already run, and produces a single interpretable number (the interaction term).
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is that these papers never claim disease-specificity, so the missing cell is not their burden: each is explicitly a screening tool FOR the diabetes clinic, and within that clinic every patient is diabetic, so a cut-off that separates MCI from non-MCI among diabetics is exactly the quantity the intended user needs, whatever axis it is physiologically reading. On that reading the record demands a mechanistic identification the clinical claim does not rest on. Two things blunt the objection but do not remove it - the papers do import cognition-axis mechanisms (TREM2 neuroinflammation, neuroprotection, alpha-Syn) to justify the markers and nominate therapeutic targets from them, and a cut-off that tracks metabolic control will drift with case-mix across diabetes clinics even for the within-clinic use. But a curator could reasonably rule that this is a mechanistic-interpretation caveat on P-1219 rather than a research gap, or merge it into ACTOR-G-020 on the grounds that both are missing-reference-arm problems. A second, smaller risk: P-1219's healthy controls are described only as healthy, and if they were in fact cognitively unscreened the direction reversal I build on is less clean than stated.
fp_codes_cleared: FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: P-1219 is named as the partial closer and its exact shortfall stated (three cells of four, no non-diabetic MCI contrast reported). No other paper in the cluster carries a non-diabetic arm at all.
TOO_SPECIFIC: four analytes, four cohorts, three centres, one shared design omission; the statement is about the design class, not about serum RBP.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: this is biomarker measurement and MCI case definition inside the corpus's core scope; no drug development or trial design is involved.

RESTATEMENT: separated by id from ACTOR-G-020, G-021, G-052 and G-NEW-1053-A in why_new, with the specific ground that G-020's missing cell is non-diabetic NORMAL and this record's is non-diabetic MCI, and that G-020's remedy is already partly satisfied in P-1219 without resolving the problem.

gaps.gap_statement: The QALY gain that prices every MCI-stage intervention is set by WHICH RESPONDENT rates the health state, and no corpus economic claim is reported under more than one reporter convention. In the corpus's only paired self-report/proxy-report utility measurement spanning MCI to severe dementia (P-1031, 289 Thai patients; duplicated in the corpus as P-802), the utility gradient does not merely shrink between reporters, it changes direction over the exact range early intervention is sold on: patient self-report is flat-to-rising from MCI (0.91) to mild dementia (0.93) while caregiver proxy-report falls from 0.87 (MCI) to 0.33 (severe dementia). The reporter is also not a free choice - self-report is 'only feasible in MCI/mild dementia (floor effect for severe cases)', so patient-side values are structurally missing exactly where the two channels diverge most, and that missingness is never treated as informative. Because the benefit of delaying MCI-to-dementia progression is the area between two utility trajectories, its magnitude, and at the MCI-to-mild-dementia boundary its sign, is fixed by a reporter convention that no corpus study adjudicates within patients, tests as a sensitivity analysis, or even names as an assumption when a value claim is made (P-960's modelled disease-modifying-therapy cost savings; P-1075's -0.18 disclosure disutility). This is why the corpus's missing MCI cost-effectiveness models (G-07, G-350) are not merely undone but currently underdetermined: the input parameter has two readings that disagree about whether MCI-stage decline costs health at all.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches two gold patterns at once: the ground-truth/endpoint assumption pattern ('Prognostic models treat central nervous system markers as absolute ground truth...') and the clinical-utility pattern where a number is proven in one frame and never checked in the frame that matters. It is non-obvious because both values are printed one line apart in the same abstract and read as an ordinary, well-known patient-proxy discrepancy; what is not obvious is (a) that the two channels disagree about the DIRECTION of the gradient over the precise MCI-to-mild-dementia range on which every early-intervention value argument is denominated, and (b) that the disagreement cannot be resolved with the data as collected, because the patient channel is unobtainable at the severe end - so the corpus cannot even bound the error. It also spans three papers with three distinct measurement families (patient self-completion, caregiver proxy completion, societal TTO/DCE) rather than restating one paper's limitation.
gaps.closure_criteria: A cost-utility analysis of an MCI-stage intervention (multidomain lifestyle programme or progression-slowing therapy) on a single cohort of >= 200 patients spanning MCI to moderate dementia, with EQ-5D-5L (or an equivalent preference-based instrument) collected from the patient AND a paired proxy at every visit, reporting: (i) within-patient agreement (ICC and Bland-Altman) at each severity stratum, with stratum n and dispersion printed; (ii) the incremental cost per QALY computed separately under the self-report and the proxy-report utility sets; (iii) whether the adopt/reject decision at a stated willingness-to-pay threshold flips between the two; and (iv) a missing-not-at-random sensitivity analysis for the strata in which patient self-report cannot be obtained. A decision flip would establish that MCI-stage value claims are reporter-determined; agreement within the WTP threshold would close the gap.
gaps.modality: Clinical/population - preference-based health-state utility (EQ-5D-5L, TTO/DCE), self-report vs caregiver proxy-report
gaps.actor_justification: Matches two gold patterns at once: the ground-truth/endpoint assumption pattern ('Prognostic models treat central nervous system markers as absolute ground truth...') and the clinical-utility pattern where a number is proven in one frame and never checked in the frame that matters. It also spans three papers with three distinct measurement families (patient self-completion, caregiver proxy completion, societal TTO/DCE) rather than restating one paper's limitation.
gaps.critic_falsification: The sign reversal rests on a single conference abstract, and its own digest records that the seven utility values carry no dispersion, no stratum denominators and no statistical test. The 'reversal' across MCI (0.91) and mild dementia (0.93) is a 0.02 difference on two undenominated means and could easily be noise. If it is noise, the honest claim collapses from 'the gradient reverses direction' to 'the gradient is much shallower under self-report' - which is the ordinary, externally well-documented patient-proxy discrepancy, and the record then becomes a weaker restatement of ACTOR-G-016 in an economic setting. A second, independent MCI-to-dementia cohort printing both channels with denominators would decide this, and none exists in the corpus.

NEAREST is ACTOR-G-016 (confirmed_open, operator score 7.0): 'MCI is the condition in which self-report validity is most compromised, yet no study in this corpus quantifies measurement-source bias WITHIN the same MCI participants'. Four differences, stated plainly so the operator can merge if they disagree: (1) CONSTRUCT - G-016's named constructs are sleep, mood, function and memory, and its six cited papers (P-654, P-657, P-635, P-667, P-663, P-630) are prevalence and instrument studies; none is a utility or economic record. This record's construct is a preference-based health-state utility, which is not a symptom measure but a decision-analytic input with a defined role in an ICER. (2) CONSEQUENCE - G-016 treats source disagreement as unquantified measurement bias; here the disagreement determines the SIGN of the quantity being priced, so it is an estimand problem, not a measurement-error nuisance. (3) A FEATURE G-016 HAS NO ANALOGUE FOR - the reporter choice is forced by an instrument floor (patient self-report is unobtainable in severe dementia), making the missingness structural and informative; nothing in G-016's evidence involves a channel that cannot be administered. (4) CLOSURE TEST - G-016 closes on a within-subject agreement statistic; this closes on a decision flip in an ICER at a stated WTP threshold. Against G-07: G-07 says the cost-effectiveness MODEL is missing; this says the INPUT that model would take is reporter-indeterminate - different object, and this record explains why G-07 is underdetermined rather than merely undone. Against G-350: G-350 proposes harmonising national WTP with 'Thailand-style EQ-5D-5L utility across the MCI-dementia continuum from P-1031' - i.e. it consumes exactly the values this record contests, so the two are complementary, not duplicative. Against MINE-G-004: that record is about effect estimates not being conditioned on achieved dose or adherence in intervention syntheses - a different quantity (delivered dose) and a different literature (network meta-analyses).
