gaps.gap_statement: The corpus's per-person savings figure for slowing MCI-stage progression is a within-person association estimate that the same cohort's own observed spending trajectory does not display, and nobody has reconciled the two estimands. Both numbers come from GERAS-US. P-1093 fits a GLM relating MMSE change to outcomes and reports that natural 36-month progression in MCI 'was associated with a 5.1-point BASQID decline, +1,050 hours total caregiver time and +$8,504 societal costs', then prices a 30 percent slowing at about 1.5 BASQID points, 315 hours and $2,638 per person. P-1000, the primary 36-month follow-up of the same cohort, reports the observed trajectory: 'Total societal costs were higher at baseline and then broadly stable: approximately $2,430 to $2,007 per month for MCI and $4,063 to $3,392 for mild dementia' - monthly spend FELL across the window in which MMSE and function declined. The two are not formally contradictory (one is conditional on within-person MMSE change, the other a marginal mean subject to differential dropout and pandemic disruption), but the figure carried forward into value arguments is always the modelled one, and the analysis that would say which estimand a payer should price - a joint model of cost and cognition with a dropout submodel - is named as future work by P-1000 itself and has not been run. This matters because it is the quantity the whole MCI-stage intervention case is denominated in: P-960 repeats the same shape of claim from a different source ('modelling of a hypothetical disease-modifying treatment delaying MCI-to-AD progression suggested cost savings'), so the corpus's cost-offset argument rests entirely on modelled associations that have never been checked against observed spend in any cohort.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold data-structure pattern - the critique that 'Machine learning architectures force continuous, interval-censored multi-visit clinical trial data into artificial, discrete cross-sectional binary labels' - by attacking the estimand rather than a number. It is non-obvious because both papers are individually sound and are cited approvingly in this corpus, and neither headline is wrong: the tension only appears when the marginal trajectory and the conditional association are read as answers to the same payer question, which is how the savings figure is used. It spans a cohort pair plus an independent review rather than restating one paper's limitation, and its closure test is named by one of the cited papers itself, which makes it actionable rather than aspirational.
gaps.closure_criteria: A joint or shared-parameter longitudinal model fitted to GERAS-US, or to an equivalent MCI-stage cohort with at least five repeated cost and cognition measurements and n >= 500, that (i) models monthly societal cost and MMSE trajectory simultaneously with an explicit dropout submodel (inverse-probability-of-censoring weighting or a shared random effect), (ii) reports the estimated cost consequence of a 20-30 percent reduction in the rate of cognitive decline under BOTH the within-person association estimand and the marginal population-trajectory estimand, each with a confidence interval, and (iii) states whether the two agree within those intervals. Closure requires an explicit statement of which estimand is being offered to payers; a demonstration that the marginal cost trajectory stays flat under a realistic slowing scenario would show the published per-person savings are not payer-observable.
gaps.modality: Clinical/population - longitudinal societal cost, caregiver time and MMSE in an observational early-AD cohort
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold data-structure pattern - the critique that 'Machine learning architectures force continuous, interval-censored multi-visit clinical trial data into artificial, discrete cross-sectional binary labels' - by attacking the estimand rather than a number. It is non-obvious because both papers are individually sound and are cited approvingly in this corpus, and neither headline is wrong: the tension only appears when the marginal trajectory and the conditional association are read as answers to the same payer question, which is how the savings figure is used. It spans a cohort pair plus an independent review rather than restating one paper's limitation, and its closure test is named by one of the cited papers itself, which makes it actionable rather than aspirational.
gaps.critic_falsification: The two results may not be in tension at all. A genuine within-person association between MMSE decline and cost is entirely compatible with a flat or falling marginal cost trajectory if the sickest and costliest participants left the study first - and the attrition is documented and large, with P-1093's outcome analysis set at 222 of 617 enrolled and P-1000 conceding pandemic disruption and differential dropout. A reviewer who holds that the within-person estimand is simply the correct one for projecting a treatment effect, and that the marginal trajectory is a known survivorship artefact, would reduce this record to 'the authors did not run a sensitivity analysis they had already flagged as future work' - a single-paper limitation rather than a gap. The record survives that objection only if one accepts that a payer pays the marginal trajectory, not the conditional coefficient, and that nobody has shown the two coincide.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no combine-X-with-Y clause. The record concerns two estimands computed on one dataset.

DATA_SCARCITY: does not apply. GERAS-US already carries baseline plus 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 and 36-month assessments with direct medical, direct non-medical and indirect cost categories - exactly the repeated-measures structure a joint model needs. No new collection is required.

RESTATEMENT: distinguished from ACTOR-G-019 (shared failure mode, different domain, papers and consequence) and from G-07 in why_new. If the operator judges the shared within-person/marginal mechanism decisive, the correct disposition is to merge the two into a single estimand-family record rather than to discard the GERAS evidence.

TOO_SPECIFIC: partially applies and is owned here. The core contrast is anchored on one cohort. It is not trivially narrow because GERAS-US is the corpus's only longitudinal MCI-stage cost dataset, its savings figure is the corpus's per-person value anchor, and P-960 shows an independent source issuing the same modelled-savings form of claim.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: neither cited paper reports the reconciliation. P-1093's own open problem asks for the treatment-effect linkage and P-1000's improvement list asks for the joint model, so both authors record it as undone.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: MODERATE and flagged for external search before any G5 sign-off. Joint modelling of longitudinal cost and clinical outcome is a known methodological literature, and GERAS sister analyses in Europe may have gone further. The claim is scoped to this corpus and to the specific reconciliation of a published per-person saving against observed spend in the same cohort; an external GERAS-EU or IDEAS analysis fitting a dropout-aware joint cost-cognition model would close it.

gaps.gap_statement: The depression / neuropsychiatric-symptom endpoint that MCI intervention syntheses pool and rank treatments on has never had its measurement properties established in an MCI population, and the syntheses pool self-report and informant-rated instruments together in exactly the population where the two should be expected to diverge. P-776 ran a PROSPERO-registered, four-database, grey-literature-inclusive, no-language-restriction search to April 2021 and recovered six diagnostic-accuracy studies (all 2006-2011) supplying nine tools, each validated in exactly one study, concluding that it cannot say which tool is most accurate in MCI; the observer-rated instrument the field treats as its reference (HAM-D) has never been validated in MCI at all, and no tool has been validated across MCI subtypes. Downstream, P-838 generates a three-way exercise ranking for MCI depression by pooling GDS-15, GDS-30, CSDD, HADS and CES-D onto one standardised scale - four patient self-report scales plus one informant-rated scale (CSDD) - and P-832 pools neuropsychiatric-symptom scales across AD and MCI trials to SMD 0.82 while naming scale heterogeneity as a driver of its own I2 of 86.1%. WHY IT MATTERS: because the population is defined by cognitive impairment, informant-rated instruments exist precisely because self-report is expected to degrade there; so instrument choice is a candidate moderator of every affective effect estimate in MCI, an SMD pooled across the two families is uninterpretable in magnitude, and a null in this literature cannot be distinguished from instrument insensitivity. P-776 records depression prevalence ranging from 3.1 to 51 per cent across its included studies despite similar reference standards, i.e. the ascertainment spread is already an order of magnitude wide before any pooling happens.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'a calibration or transfer failure across language, education, device or setting' - here the transfer is across cognitive status, from the general geriatric population where these scales were validated into MCI where they are used routinely. It is also the prompt's 'a measurement never calibrated across settings' and 'an endpoint everyone substitutes for the one that matters'. It is non-obvious because the defect is invisible inside the syntheses that commit it: P-838 and P-832 report clean-looking SMDs with GRADE ratings and never touch measurement validity, and P-776 - the one paper that looked - sits in a different literature (diagnostic accuracy) that never cites them. The record joins a documented, dated emptiness to two named consumers that depend on it, which is what separates it from a generic 'outcome heterogeneity' complaint.
gaps.closure_criteria: A diagnostic-accuracy validation of at least two depression instruments (one self-report, one informant-rated, e.g. GDS-15 and CSDD) against a structured clinical interview in a criterion-diagnosed MCI cohort (N >= 150), reporting sensitivity/specificity, the self-report-versus-informant agreement (kappa or ICC) and its dependence on cognitive severity; plus a re-pooling of an MCI depression-outcome meta-analysis (P-838 or P-832) stratified by instrument family, reporting whether the pooled SMD and its sign survive within each family.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern 'a calibration or transfer failure across language, education, device or setting' - here the transfer is across cognitive status, from the general geriatric population where these scales were validated into MCI where they are used routinely. It is also the prompt's 'a measurement never calibrated across settings' and 'an endpoint everyone substitutes for the one that matters'. It is non-obvious because the defect is invisible inside the syntheses that commit it: P-838 and P-832 report clean-looking SMDs with GRADE ratings and never touch measurement validity, and P-776 - the one paper that looked - sits in a different literature (diagnostic accuracy) that never cites them. The record joins a documented, dated emptiness to two named consumers that depend on it, which is what separates it from a generic 'outcome heterogeneity' complaint.
gaps.critic_falsification: The standardised mean difference is designed to absorb between-instrument scaling, so a reviewer can argue that pooling GDS-15 with CSDD requires only that both track the same latent change, not that they be interchangeable in units - in which case unknown accuracy would degrade precision rather than invalidate the estimate. The record's force therefore depends on the instruments differing in MCI-specific sensitivity, which P-776 establishes as UNKNOWN rather than as demonstrated; the strongest counter is that an unknown is not automatically a gap. What keeps the record standing is that the divergence has a mechanism, not merely a possibility: informant-rated scales exist because self-report is expected to fail under cognitive impairment, and P-776's 3.1-to-51-per-cent prevalence spread under similar reference standards shows the ascertainment is already unstable. A secondary weakness is that P-832's population is AD and MCI pooled, so its leg speaks to the affective endpoint across the AD/MCI continuum rather than to MCI alone.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: does not propose combining any modality or method with another. The absence named is a measurement-validity study of a single instrument family in a single population.
RESTATEMENT: distinguished by id above from G-349, ACTOR-G-072, MINE-G-004, ACTOR-G-038, MINE-G-001 and ACTOR-G-009, none of which concerns instrument accuracy in MCI.
TOO_SPECIFIC: spans two distinct literatures (diagnostic accuracy of affective instruments; non-pharmacological intervention synthesis) and three papers with three unrelated author teams and topics.

DATA_SCARCITY: the closure study is an ordinary diagnostic-accuracy study in an MCI cohort; P-776 records 275 records excluded for lacking a reference-standard depression diagnosis and 73 for not reporting accuracy, so the cohorts and the instruments exist and only the reference-standard design is missing. This is an unrun study, not unobtainable data.

EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE: P-776 is itself the external-literature check - PROSPERO-registered, four databases plus a structured grey-literature search, from inception to 25 April 2021, with no language restriction, returning six studies. The absence is field-level as of that date, not an artefact of this corpus's sampling.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: no paper in the pack reports diagnostic accuracy for any affective instrument in MCI; P-838, P-832 and P-790 all consume the scales without validating them, and P-776's 'What can be improved' names the missing programme rather than delivering it.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: each cited paper's own text carries the construct - P-776's subject IS depression-tool accuracy in MCI, P-838's digest names the five pooled instruments explicitly, and P-832's authors name scale differences as a heterogeneity source in their own limitations paragraph. No inferential bridge is used.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: every quote is tagged with the summary field it came from. The load-bearing quotes sit in Results, Key findings and author-stated limitations. The one quote from an importance field (P-776's 'Clinicians use the GDS, the PHQ-9, the CSDD and the Beck inventory in this population as a matter of routine') has been left OUT of the evidence list and is not relied on.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the absence clause is deliberately NOT 'no instrument has ever been validated in MCI' - P-776 reports nine tools each validated once, and that is stated on the face of the claim. The clause asserted is the weaker and true one: no tool has comparative accuracy evidence sufficient to choose among them, the HAM-D has none at all, and none has subtype-level validation - all three stated by P-776 itself.

MISASSIGNED_MEASUREMENT_FAMILY: the two families asserted (patient self-report vs informant-rated) are taken verbatim from P-776's own instrument taxonomy, and the specific cross-family instance (CSDD informant-rated pooled with GDS-15/GDS-30/HADS/CES-D self-report in P-838) is checked instrument by instrument against that taxonomy.

gaps.gap_statement: The MCI intervention literature issues practice recommendations from the wrong interval. Every pooled estimate in this pack is reported as a confidence interval around a random-effects mean under I2 of 68 to 93 per cent; the confidence interval locates the mean of a scatter of true effects, whereas the quantity a recommendation is about - what a new programme in a new clinic would produce - is the prediction interval. In the two corpus syntheses whose prediction interval is actually recoverable, it crossed zero into substantial harm both times: P-680's pooled global-cognition SMD of 1.165 (95% CI 0.741 to 1.589, I-squared 88.045 per cent) carries a prediction interval of -0.747 to 3.077, and P-698's SMD of 0.76 (I-squared 83 per cent) carries -0.63 to 2.15. Both papers computed the interval, printed it, and then issued a confident positive conclusion from the confidence interval alone - P-680's digest records that the authors 'do not carry it into their conclusion'. P-711 states the same inferential point explicitly for its own pooled proportion and reports no prediction interval at all. WHY IT MATTERS: this is not a request for more caution, it is a claim that the field has never measured the size of its own problem. Nobody has recomputed the prediction interval across the MCI intervention meta-analyses and reported what fraction of the positive pooled estimates - the ones that drive modality rankings, dose recommendations and guideline text - still exclude zero when expressed as the quantity the recommendation is actually about. Both existing instances say the answer would bite, and the analysis needs no new participants: tau-squared and k are already published in every forest plot.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern 'Machine learning architectures force continuous, interval-censored multi-visit clinical trial data into artificial, discrete cross-sectional binary labels' - a critique of the quantity the pipeline computes rather than of the data it computes on. It is non-obvious because the defect is invisible from the abstracts: both papers report a statistically significant positive pooled effect with a confidence interval excluding zero, and only the body text carries the interval that contradicts it. The record is also actionable without any new data collection, which is what the DATA_SCARCITY verdict on ACTOR-G-001/002 marks as the difference between a data limitation and a methodological gap.

It is non-obvious because the defect is invisible from the abstracts: both papers report a statistically significant positive pooled effect with a confidence interval excluding zero, and only the body text carries the interval that contradicts it. The record is also actionable without any new data collection, which is what the DATA_SCARCITY verdict on ACTOR-G-001/002 marks as the difference between a data limitation and a methodological gap.

It is non-obvious because the defect is invisible from the abstracts: both papers report a statistically significant positive pooled effect with a confidence interval excluding zero, and only the body text carries the interval that contradicts it. The record is also actionable without any new data collection, which is what the DATA_SCARCITY verdict on ACTOR-G-001/002 marks as the difference between a data limitation and a methodological gap.
gaps.critic_falsification: P-680 and P-698 are both exercise-in-MCI meta-analyses published within a year of each other and almost certainly share primary trials, so they are not two independent demonstrations of the pattern - the 'both times' clause rests closer to one evidence base than to two, and P-711's leg supplies the principle rather than a third measured interval. The stronger objection, though, is conceptual: a reviewer can hold that a wide prediction interval is the arithmetically necessary consequence of I2 at 83-88 per cent, that high heterogeneity in this literature is already recorded many times over, and that the prediction interval is therefore a symptom of a known problem rather than an unexplored absence - in which case the record reduces to 'report your heterogeneity properly', which is guidance rather than a research gap. The reply is that the audit is quantitative and has an unknown answer (what fraction of the field's positive estimates survive), but the reply concedes that the record's value is contingent on that fraction being interesting, which nobody yet knows.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: proposes no combination of modalities or methods; the absence is a re-analysis of already-published pooled estimates.
DATA_SCARCITY: explicitly not - tau-squared, k and the pooled estimate are printed in every forest plot in this literature, so the audit is computable today from published material.
TOO_SPECIFIC: the statistic in question governs every pooled estimate in the MCI intervention literature, and the record's closure test is a field-level audit rather than one paper's fix.
RESTATEMENT: zero hits for 'prediction interval' across the 534 existing statements; distinguished by id from MINE-G-002, MINE-G-004, G-349 and ACTOR-G-024 above.
EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: all three cited papers use the term 'prediction interval' in their own digests, and two print their own values; no construct is imported by the miner.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: every quote is field-tagged. The numeric values come from Results and Key findings; the interpretive quotes are tagged as coming from the problems / improvements fields and are used only to establish that the papers themselves did not let the interval govern the conclusion, which is a statement about the papers' own text, not a measured finding.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: the claim deliberately does NOT say that no MCI synthesis reports a prediction interval. Two of the three cited papers report one, which is stated on the face of the claim. It is further disclosed here that P-838's digest names 'Fig. 3 (predictive interval plot)' as present in that paper although its contents are not recoverable from the extract - so at least one further corpus synthesis produces the statistic. The asserted absence is narrower and survives that: no corpus study re-expresses its clinical recommendation against a prediction interval, and none reports what fraction of MCI intervention pooled estimates would survive being so expressed.
NOT_IN_SCOPE: the object is meta-analytic reporting of MCI intervention effects, squarely inside the corpus scope; no clinical-trial design or drug-development question is raised.

gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: The MCI intervention literature issues practice recommendations from the wrong interval. Every pooled estimate in this pack is reported as a confidence interval around a random-effects mean under I2 of 68 to 93 per cent; the confidence interval locates the mean of a scatter of true effects, whereas the quantity a recommendation is about - what a new programme in a new clinic would produce - is the prediction interval. In the two corpus syntheses whose prediction interval is actually recoverable, it crossed zero into substantial harm both times: P-680's pooled global-cognition SMD of 1.165 (95% CI 0.741 to 1.589, I-squared 88.045 per cent) carries a prediction interval of -0.747 to 3.077, and P-698's SMD of 0.76 (I-squared 83 per cent) carries -0.63 to 2.15. Both papers computed the interval, printed it, and then issued a confident positive conclusion from the confidence interval alone - P-680's digest records that the authors 'do not carry it into their conclusion'. P-711 states the same inferential point explicitly for its own pooled proportion and reports no prediction interval at all. WHY IT MATTERS: this is not a request for more caution, it is a claim that the field has never measured the size of its own problem. Nobody has recomputed the prediction interval across the MCI intervention meta-analyses and reported what fraction of the positive pooled estimates - the ones that drive modality rankings, dose recommendations and guideline text - still exclude zero when expressed as the quantity the recommendation is actually about. Both existing instances say the answer would bite, and the analysis needs no new participants: tau-squared and k are already published in every forest plot.

merged_2026_09_22.reason: Both state that pooled MCI-intervention syntheses report the confidence interval and never the prediction interval, and that in the two syntheses where a PI is recoverable it crosses zero; identical anchor set (P-680, P-698, P-711) and the same P-680 SMD 1.165 worked example.

gaps.gap_statement: Across three MCI evidence-synthesis literatures - exergaming, rapid cognitive screening, and social determinants of neuropsychiatric symptoms - and for the tDCS syntheses P-705 and P-832 specifically, the estimate that is cited for MCI is a mixture in which MCI is the minority stratum and is not separately estimated. For cortical stimulation more broadly the MCI-only estimate does exist in the corpus (P-461, an MCI-only network meta-analysis of 19 RCTs / 599 MCI participants; P-520, an MCI-only rTMS meta-analysis of 12 studies / 329 MCI participants, SMD 0.83), so the claim for that literature is confined to the two tDCS-inclusive pools named. P-705 pools 426 MCI with 648 AD participants for tDCS, never produces an MCI estimate, and still concludes that tDCS may prevent MCI developing into AD; its own descriptive strand points the opposite way for AD, and its digest identifies the stratified analysis as the paper's single most consequential missing step because 'MCI is the stage at which prevention is plausible'. P-832's NIBS synthesis has 'only a small number of studies on MCI patients, and only one of these investigated the use of tDCS'. P-699 pools 166 MCI with 350 dementia participants for exergaming and names diagnosis-stratified analysis as its own open problem. P-757 finds ten of its 23 rapid-screen accuracy studies pooled MCI and dementia patients without delineating the groups. P-790's eighteen-study map contains exactly one MCI-only study. WHY IT MATTERS: MCI is the stage on which the entire prevention rationale for these interventions and screens rests, and it is the stage at which effects are most likely to differ from dementia - earlier disease, more reserve, different ceiling effects on the instruments used. Yet where the split is possible the papers have not run it and where it is impossible the reviews have not said what the MCI-only estimate would need. For P-705 and P-699 this is an UNRUN ANALYSIS on denominators already printed in their own tables, not missing data; for P-757 and P-790 the dilution originates in the primary studies and is repairable only by primary-level reporting.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold pattern of a ground-truth / population assumption that nobody tests - the same shape as 'Prognostic models treat central nervous system markers as absolute ground truth' - here the untested assumption is that an intervention or screen behaves identically at the MCI and dementia stages, an assumption the papers make silently by pooling and which P-705's own descriptive strand contradicts. It is non-obvious because every one of these papers passes surface inspection: each names MCI in its title, each reports its diagnostic composition honestly in a table, and the defect only appears when the composition is read against the conclusion. The record is also actionable: for two of the four legs it is a re-analysis on denominators the papers already print.
gaps.closure_criteria: For P-705 and P-699: the diagnosis-stratified re-analysis on the denominators printed in their own tables, reporting the MCI-only pooled estimate with its interval. For rapid screening (P-757) and NPS social determinants (P-790): primary studies reporting MCI and dementia accuracy or effect separately. The gap closes for a literature when an MCI-only estimate with an interval is published for it.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold pattern of a ground-truth / population assumption that nobody tests - the same shape as 'Prognostic models treat central nervous system markers as absolute ground truth' - here the untested assumption is that an intervention or screen behaves identically at the MCI and dementia stages, an assumption the papers make silently by pooling and which P-705's own descriptive strand contradicts. It is non-obvious because every one of these papers passes surface inspection: each names MCI in its title, each reports its diagnostic composition honestly in a table, and the defect only appears when the composition is read against the conclusion. The record is also actionable: for two of the four legs it is a re-analysis on denominators the papers already print.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection is that pooling MCI with AD or dementia is a deliberate and defensible transitivity assumption rather than an oversight: for a stage-agnostic mechanism such as cortical stimulation or an exergame, the trialists and the reviewers may hold that the intervention acts on the same substrate at both stages, in which case the pooled estimate is the intended quantity and the 'missing' MCI estimate is simply a less precise version of it. P-705's own descriptive strand pointing the other way for AD is a hint, not a tested interaction, so the record cannot demonstrate that the strata differ - only that nobody has checked. A second and separate weakness is that P-705 and P-832 are both neuromodulation syntheses of overlapping years and plausibly share primary tDCS trials, so the record has four independent legs rather than the five papers it cites; and for the P-757 and P-790 legs the pooling happens inside the primary studies, so those two reviews could not have run the split even had they wanted to, which weakens the 'unrun analysis' framing to a 'unreported primary data' framing for half the record.
fp_codes_cleared: COMBINATORIAL_GAP: no combine-X-with-Y clause. The absence is a stratified estimate within an existing evidence base.

DATA_SCARCITY: explicitly not for the P-705 and P-699 legs - the per-diagnosis participant counts are printed in the papers' own tables and only the analysis is missing. The record states openly that the P-757 and P-790 legs are different in kind and need primary-level reporting.

TOO_SPECIFIC: four independent legs across four distinct literatures - cortical stimulation, exergaming, rapid cognitive screening, social determinants of neuropsychiatric symptoms - and two distinct task families (intervention efficacy and diagnostic accuracy).
RESTATEMENT: distinguished by id above from G-CAND-114 (rejected single-paper limitation), MINE-G-004 (adherence, caveat only), ACTOR-G-044 (endpoint, not population) and NEW-G-22.

FIELD_ALREADY_ADDRESSED: scoped explicitly. MCI-restricted syntheses DO exist elsewhere in this pack - P-833 (VR combined intervention), P-834 (exercise and executive function), P-836 (VR detection) and P-838 (exercise and depression) are all MCI-only - so the claim is confined to the four named literatures and is not asserted corpus-wide. This scoping is on the face of the claim.

EVIDENCE_TOPIC_DRIFT: every leg is evidenced by the paper's own statement of its own diagnostic composition or its own open problem; the MCI-versus-dementia construct appears in each cited paper's own vocabulary.

EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT: quotes are field-tagged. The composition facts come from sample-size and key-findings fields; the P-705 interpretive quotes are tagged as coming from 'What can be improved?' and are used to establish that the split is feasible on printed data, which is a statement about the paper's own tables rather than a measured effect. No comparative magnitude is claimed anywhere in this record.

UNIVERSAL_NEGATIVE_FALSIFIED_BY_OWN_CITATIONS: checked against every cited paper. None of P-705, P-832, P-699, P-757 or P-790 reports a diagnosis-stratified estimate or an interaction test, so no cited paper falsifies the absence clause. P-832 reports a diagnosis SUBGROUP only for the NPS analysis in AD, which the digest instructs must not be propagated, and reports none for MCI.

gaps.gap_statement: Exercise-intervention intensity is reported across the MCI evidence base in at least four mutually incommensurable units - percentage of maximal heart rate, absolute beats per minute, two different Borg scales with different ranges, and percentage of VO2max - so intensity cannot be harmonised across studies even in principle (P-839's own charting of 29 dance-intervention studies), and no corpus synthesis quantifies the cost of that incommensurability: no unit cross-walk table exists in the corpus, no corpus study reports the same trial's intensity in two units to anchor a conversion, and no corpus meta-analysis treats intensity as an analysable continuous moderator. P-846 shows the contrast that becomes possible when dose IS operationalised - a 90 vs 240 min/wk head-to-head RCT that was null between doses on 19 of 20 outcomes - but its dose axis is weekly time, not intensity; P-848's 34-study network meta-analysis takes exercise type, never dose or intensity, as its network dimension. The field's most policy-relevant question for non-pharmacological MCI trials - what intensity, not just what type or duration - is therefore unanswerable by corpus synthesis, and P-846's null between a 2.7-fold duration difference raises the untested hypothesis that intensity, not duration, carries the effect. (A prior claim element that P-846's protocol lists heart-rate and Borg targets was not verifiable from the digest and is dropped pending source-PDF confirmation; closure part (1), a dual-unit anchor measurement, may additionally exist in external exercise-science literature, in which case the open core is the MCI-specific intensity-moderated synthesis.)
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard measurement-standardisation pattern (vendor-device variance in OCT; multi-site standardisation in EEG) transposed to the intervention-dose axis, and the gold-standard data-structure critique pattern (incommensurable units blocking synthesis). It is non-obvious because P-846 looks like a dose study - the corpus superficially appears to have dose-response evidence - but its dose axis is time only, and the intensity axis that actually defines a prescription is never analysable. The record scopes the absence to what synthesis needs (a cross-walk plus a moderated estimate), not to the trivially true claim that units differ.
gaps.closure_criteria: A two-part closure: (1) a methodological anchor study measuring the same exercise session's intensity simultaneously in percent maximal heart rate, absolute bpm, Borg CR10, Borg 6-20 and percent VO2max in >=30 older adults with MCI, publishing the between-unit conversion functions with prediction intervals; (2) an individual-participant-data or trial-level meta-analysis of MCI exercise RCTs with intensity entered as a continuous moderator after conversion, reporting a dose-response curve for cognitive outcomes with the duration dimension held separate. Part (1) alone does not close the gap; the gap closes when a cross-study intensity dose-response estimate exists.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold-standard measurement-standardisation pattern (vendor-device variance in OCT; multi-site standardisation in EEG) transposed to the intervention-dose axis, and the gold-standard data-structure critique pattern (incommensurable units blocking synthesis). gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection: external exercise-science literature (ACSM guidelines literature, cardiac-rehabilitation dose meta-analyses) has published intensity unit cross-walks for older adults, so part (1) of the closure test may already exist outside the corpus, demoting that half to EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE and leaving only the MCI-specific moderated synthesis half genuinely open. gaps.original_claim_before_narrowing: Exercise-intervention intensity is reported across the MCI evidence base in at least four mutually incommensurable units - percentage of maximal heart rate, absolute beats per minute, two different Borg scales with different ranges, and percentage of VO2max - so intensity cannot be harmonised across studies even in principle, and no corpus synthesis quantifies the cost of that incommensurability: no cross-walk table between units exists, no corpus study reports the same trial's intensity in two units to anchor a conversion, and no dose-response meta-analysis in the corpus uses intensity as an analysable moderator at all. P-839 documents the four-unit problem inside its own 29-study chart of dance interventions; P-846 shows the contrast that becomes possible when dose IS quantified (90 vs 240 min/wk head-to-head, null between doses on 19 of 20 outcomes); P-848 ranks five exercise types while never entering dose as a network node. The result is that the field's most policy-relevant question for non-pharmacological MCI trials - what intensity, not just what type or duration - is unanswerable by synthesis, while the corpus demonstrates on paper after paper that pooling is blocked precisely at intensity.

gaps.gap_statement: Psychotic-symptom prevalence in MCI - the number that decides whether these patients are flagged for antipsychotic exposure or excluded from trials - is instrument-dependent by a factor of roughly three and a half (hallucinations 1.47%, 95% CI 0.9-2.41, across the 31 studies using NPI/NPI-Q vs significantly higher rates across the 5 studies using other instruments: Behave-AD, CERAD-Behavioural and comparable schedules), no validated psychosis scale exists for the pre-dementia population in the corpus, no cognitively healthy comparator arm exists in the pooled evidence so the specificity of low rates to MCI is unknown, and P-844 names the missing instrument itself ('the lack of a validated scale that could be used in the pre-dementia population may have an impact on the measure of the prevalence of psychotic symptoms in MCI patients'). No corpus study develops, validates or head-to-head compares psychosis ascertainment instruments in an MCI cohort, so the field cannot say whether MCI psychosis is genuinely rare or merely under-ascertained by instruments designed for dementia populations.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard measurement-standardisation pattern (no validated scale for the population the measurement is applied to; instrument-dependence quantified but never resolved) and carries a quantified anchoring statistic (3.5-fold) rather than a bare absence. It is non-obvious because the corpus superficially has a complete prevalence line (36 studies, pooled CIs), and the gap only becomes visible through the instrument-split subgroup inside that synthesis; the healthy-comparator half adds a specificity absence that is easy to miss entirely.
gaps.closure_criteria: A validation study in one MCI cohort (>=150 MCI participants plus >=100 cognitively healthy controls) administering at least two existing psychosis schedules (e.g. NPI-Q and Behave-AD) plus a gold-standard clinical interview, reporting inter-instrument agreement (kappa), sensitivity/specificity against the interview, and the prevalence ratio between instruments - establishing whether MCI psychosis is rare or under-ascertained, and whether the 3.5-fold split is instrument artefact. A validation with a healthy comparator arm additionally closes the specificity half.

gaps.gap_statement: STAGE-ASYMMETRIC EVIDENCE WITH BACKWARD EXTRAPOLATION: the two frontier fluid/metabolic evidence syntheses that anchor the 'stress-endocrine and bioenergetic disruption is EARLY in the AD course' narrative both derive that early-stage claim from their AD-stage arms, while their own systematic searches show the MCI-stage arm is null or too small to analyse - and neither synthesis, nor any other corpus record, tests whether these markers actually change BEFORE the MCI-to-AD transition. Specifics, all from the reviews' own numbers: P-1195 (1H/31P-MRS meta-analysis, literature searched 1989-2021) pools 40 MCI 1H-MRS studies but its 31P bioenergetic arm contains 8 AD studies and exactly 1 MCI study, so every pooled bioenergetic result (increased PME and Pi, decreased PCr/Pi) is AD-only and its own gaps field concedes 'no MCI-stage 31P analysis'; it nevertheless concludes that neuroinflammation and oxidative stress 'may occur early in AD, likely preceding neuron loss' and advances bioenergetics as a treatment avenue. P-1202 (PRISMA systematic review of CSF HPA-axis hormones, searched to July 2022) finds CSF cortisol elevated in AD in 5 of 7 studies, but at the MCI stage most studies found NO significant difference (1 of 4 positive), ACTH rests on 2 AD-stage studies, and CRH is inconclusive; it nevertheless frames HPA dysregulation as a proposed mechanism 'driving AD progression from MCI to dementia' and suggests CSF cortisol 'could complement AD diagnosis and staging'. The one MCI-stage metabolic effect that IS established in this pack cuts the other way and is itself thin: GSH significantly reduced in MCI (4 studies) but NOT in AD - so the only stage-resolved oxidative marker does not behave as a monotone early-to-late trajectory. WHY IT MATTERS: an AD-stage elevation with an MCI-stage null is equally consistent with the marker being a LATE CONSEQUENCE of neurodegeneration as with it being an early driver - the two readings dictate opposite uses (staging biomarker vs early-intervention target), and both reviews name therapeutic targeting (hypercortisolemia, bioenergetics) that only makes sense on the early-driver reading. For a corpus whose object is the MCI stage, the bioenergetic (31P) and neuroendocrine (HPA) pathways therefore have no interpretable MCI-stage evidence base at all: any MCI trial or biomarker panel built on them would be designed from AD-stage data extrapolated backward across exactly the stage boundary in question. CLOSURE CRITERIA: either (a) an adequately powered MCI-stage cross-sectional base - a multi-site 31P-MRS study in MCI vs matched HC (N >= 100 per arm, or >= 5 poolable studies) reporting PME/Pi/PCr-Pi effect sizes with 95 per cent CIs, plus a pooled CSF-cortisol MCI-vs-HC estimate from >= 5 studies with cognitively assessed controls; or, decisively, (b) a longitudinal MCI cohort with baseline 31P-MRS and CSF (or validated blood-equivalent) cortisol and >= 3-year conversion follow-up, testing whether marker change PRECEDES the MCI-to-AD transition (hazard ratio or time-lag estimate with CI). STATUS: candidate, pending_human_review, gate_verified=false.

gaps.gap_statement: The corpus's leading clinically-deployable MCI risk stratifier, the cognition-plus-hippocampal-volume index Cog_Vol (P-1226: Cog_Vol < 101 predicts 94.1% 2-year conversion in amyloid-elevated MCI; >= 340 predicts ~0% at 4 years), has never been combined with blood p-tau217 - the single best-performing blood biomarker in the corpus's own 150-study meta-analysis (P-1231: AUC 0.97-0.98) - and the combination is exactly what P-1226 names as its own next step ('p-tau217 was not included so tau status of high-risk subjects is unknown'; open problem: 'Inclusion of p-tau217/tau biomarkers to characterise high-risk subgroups'). The untested question is not whether either marker works but whether the cheap, already-validated index gains intermediate-band resolution from the blood marker: P-1226's own limitation is that subjects in the intermediate Cog_Vol band (102-266, ~60% risk) 'cannot be individually classified', and no corpus study reports whether p-tau217 resolves that band. This is a concrete, one-cohort, already-named-by-the-authors absence in the corpus's clinical-deployment pathway.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard clinical-utility pattern (discrimination proven, decision impact never tested: the corpus's best index cannot resolve the band where decisions are made) while avoiding the deprecated combinatorial template because the reason the combination is critical is stated by the corpus itself (P-1226's own limitation and open problem), not manufactured by the miner. It is non-obvious because both components are celebrated results in the same corpus and same population, which makes their never having been crossed a genuine structural observation about how the corpus's validation pathway fragments by modality.
gaps.closure_criteria: One MCI cohort (>=200 participants) with baseline cognition, hippocampal volumetry and plasma p-tau217: compute a Cog_Vol-style index, report conversion (2-4 years) within each index band stratified by p-tau217 (binary at a pre-specified cut-off and as a continuous covariate), and report the intermediate band's reclassification (category-free net reclassification improvement or band-level risk shift with CI). gaps.gap_statement: The corpus's exercise-cytokine-cognition chain is missing its end: P-1187's systematic review of 38 studies (25 animal, 11 human) synthesises exercise effects on inflammatory markers by vote-counting only, reports no pooled effect size, records 'no standardised cytokine panel' as a field problem, and - per its own improvement list - lacks 'longer follow-up to link cytokine changes to cognitive trajectory'; in humans the mechanism claim is already weak at the marker level (only 53.9% of human studies reduced pro-inflammatory proteins and only 23% raised anti-inflammatory ones), yet the downstream rationale ('Neuroinflammation is a strong driver of MCI-to-AD progression and a modifiable target') is used to justify exercise prescription. No corpus study in this chain reports the association between cytokine change and cognitive change measured in the same participants (P-1301, a 76-participant MCI physical-plus-cognitive training trial, measures cytokine reductions and cognition in the same people but does not report the association; P-1320, 74 MCI, measures cytokines and p-tau181 with no cognitive endpoint), so the inflammatory-mediation pathway by which exercise is supposed to protect cognition in MCI is asserted by narrative and never estimated.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard clinical-utility pattern transposed to mechanism: a treatment pathway (anti-inflammatory exercise prescription) is recommended while its mechanistic core (marker change relates to cognitive change) is never estimated - discrimination-style evidence is absent not for performance but for the mediating process itself. It is non-obvious because P-1187 superficially supports the mechanism (70.8% of animal studies show marker improvement), and the gap only becomes visible through the human-vs-animal split in its own vote counts and the endpoint-link entry on its own improvement list; the record scopes the claim to within-cohort estimates so it cannot be falsified by the cross-literature narrative the field actually uses.
gaps.closure_criteria: An MCI exercise RCT (>=150 participants, >=6 months) measuring a pre-specified cytokine panel (>=4 analytes with assay harmonisation) at baseline and follow-up alongside a standard cognitive composite, reporting (a) the correlation or mediation estimate between cytokine change and cognitive change with CI, and (b) a biomarker-responder stratification (cognitive change in cytokine-responders vs non-responders). The gap closes only when a within-cohort association estimate exists; a pooled cytokine-effect meta-analysis alone does not close it.

gaps.gap_statement_pre_2026_09_22: The corpus's entire exercise-cytokine-cognition chain is missing its middle and its end: P-1187's systematic review of 38 studies (25 animal, 11 human) synthesises exercise effects on inflammatory markers by vote-counting only, reports no pooled effect size, records 'no standardised cytokine panel' as a field problem, and - per its own improvement list - lacks 'longer follow-up to link cytokine changes to cognitive trajectory'; in humans the mechanism claim is already weak at the marker level (only 53.9% of human studies reduced pro-inflammatory proteins and only 23% raised anti-inflammatory ones), yet the downstream rationale ('Neuroinflammation is a strong driver of MCI-to-AD progression and a modifiable target') is used to justify exercise prescription. gaps.gap_statement: The MCI reversion rate - the number used to counsel patients and to argue MCI is an unstable trial-entry state - is reported across the corpus under non-interchangeable measurement schemes, and the two scheme parameters that produce the largest divergences (estimand type and assessment cadence) have never been quantified within any single cohort. The corpus HAS quantified two other knobs: diagnostic-criteria choice (P-986: Petersen 43.4% vs modified NP 48.3% head-to-head in one Swedish cohort, person-time incidences 63.0 vs 76.2/1000 person-years, sensitivity range 42.1% to 54.7%) and practice effects (P-971: adjustment cuts ADNI reverters from 80 to 57). But cumulative diagnosis-change proportions (P-1133: 18.17% at 2 years in ADNI; P-975: 32.8% first-year EMCI under annual testing; P-932: 7% over a single 6-year test-retest interval) and modelled instantaneous transition probabilities (P-1135: 2% at baseline rising to a maximum of 8% by year 10, on an overlapping ADNI-sourced sample) differ by more than a factor of two against the maximum - and up to roughly nine-fold against the baseline-year value - on quantities the corpus papers themselves cross-cite as one construct. No corpus study reports the diagnosis-change proportion and the multistate transition probability side by side on the same data, and none re-estimates reversion under thinned or confirmation-requiring visit schedules, so the roughly 5% to 55% spread in published reversion rates cannot be decomposed into population biology versus measurement scheme - if the two estimands are in fact commensurable, which is itself untested.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches two gold-standard patterns: the interval-censored-data structural critique (gold: ML architectures force continuous, interval-censored multi-visit data into artificial discrete labels - here the epidemiological twin of that critique) and the measurement-robustness pattern (gold: EEG single-site AUC without multi-site replication - promising numbers whose measurement scheme was never varied). It is non-obvious because the corpus appears to already have a complete reversion-methodology line (criteria head-to-head, practice-effect adjustment, definition-component sensitivity); the two unquantified knobs only become visible when the two ADNI-sourced papers are put side by side, and the record explicitly credits the addressed knobs so the absence claim is exactly scoped.
gaps.closure_criteria: In one multi-visit MCI cohort (>=300 MCI participants, >=4 annual visits; ADNI or an annual memory-clinic cohort suffices - no new data collection needed), report reversion simultaneously as (a) 1-, 2- and 3-year diagnosis-change proportions, (b) a two-consecutive-visit-confirmed reversion proportion, (c) person-time incidence, and (d) a multistate-model instantaneous transition probability; then re-estimate (a)-(d) after artificially thinning the visit schedule to biennial and triennial. Publish the between-scheme spread with confidence intervals as a conversion table between estimands and cadences.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches two gold-standard patterns: the interval-censored-data structural critique (gold: ML architectures force continuous, interval-censored multi-visit data into artificial discrete labels - here the epidemiological twin of that critique) and the measurement-robustness pattern (gold: EEG single-site AUC without multi-site replication - promising numbers whose measurement scheme was never varied). It is non-obvious because the corpus appears to already have a complete reversion-methodology line (criteria head-to-head, practice-effect adjustment, definition-component sensitivity); the two unquantified knobs only become visible when the two ADNI-sourced papers are put side by side, and the record explicitly credits the addressed knobs so the absence claim is exactly scoped.
gaps.critic_falsification: A methodologist could object that a 2-year cumulative proportion and an instantaneous transition probability are different quantities by construction, so the P-1133/P-1135 divergence is a units mismatch rather than a research gap. The rebuttal inside the record is that the corpus itself treats them as one construct (P-1135 is explicitly framed against P-1133's favourable-reversion narrative, and both feed the same reversion consensus line), and no paper supplies the conversion that would make them commensurable - but an operator could still rule the gap partially a reporting-convention complaint. Secondary risk: an external (non-corpus) multistate methods paper may already report both estimands on one cohort, which would demote the estimand half to EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE and leave only the cadence half open.

gaps.gap_statement: Biomarker-decision evidence in the MCI pathway has only been gathered where the patients are not: the corpus's study of clinician-and-care-partner decision factors around AD biomarker testing (P-857) samples exclusively from three dementia-specialist referrals at one academic health system (87.7% White non-Hispanic, mean 16.8 years education, 65 patients), while the corpus's own health-services measurement shows 99.9% of 226,756 US primary care clinicians diagnose significantly below expectation (detection rate 0.08; over a quarter of panels contain not a single diagnosed MCI patient) - so the setting holding the overwhelming majority of undetected MCI cases has no decision-making evidence at all. P-857's own limitation paragraph names the fix ('primary-care and community memory-clinic sampling, where biomarker awareness is presumably lower') and the corpus holds no study that follows it. The amyloid-therapy era makes this an access-critical absence: treatment is indicated at the MCI stage, detection fails in primary care, and the factors that govern biomarker uptake are known only in the specialist straw that excludes the population at issue.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard population-exclusion pattern (a population everyone excludes - here the primary-care population where ~92% of expected MCI is undiagnosed) and the gold-standard clinical-utility pattern (testing decisions are made daily while the factors governing them are measured only in a straw sample that excludes the deciders' setting). It is non-obvious because the two papers are adjacent in the corpus and neither links to the other: the detection paper quantifies where the patients are, the decision paper measures factors where the patients are not, and the mismatch only becomes visible when the referral-bias limitation is read against the detection statistics. Both papers are corpus-internal so EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE risk is confined to the combination, which is the actual claim.
gaps.closure_criteria: A decision-factor study (dyadic or clinician survey, >=200 participants or >=100 clinicians) recruited from primary care or community memory clinics - the settings P-858 shows carry the undetected burden - measuring the same factor domains P-857 measured (clinical utility, clinician authority, cost, insurance, awareness), with racial/ethnic and education composition reported and stratified analysis; reporting whether the specialist-clinic factor ranking (utility and authority dominant, cost and insurance lowest) reproduces where biomarker awareness is presumably lower and cost may bind harder. Closure requires the setting contrast, not merely another specialist-sample replication.

gaps.gap_statement: Cross-national survey-cohort MCI risk models report 'external validation' that shares its exposure and outcome instruments with the training cohort, so the validation does not test transportability of the measurement - and the corpus's own example states it directly: the CHARLS-trained COPD-specific MCI risk model (P-893) validates on HRS while reusing self-reported COPD and the same screening-based cognitive-impairment (AACD-style) outcome definition, so 'external' validity is 'partially shared-method', and the model is further restricted to survey variables alone (no spirometry, no oxygen saturation, no inflammatory markers, no imaging) capping AUROC at 0.722-0.782 with the physiological predictors' incremental value unknown. This is a reusable methodological blind spot: any corpus or field claim that a survey-variable MCI model 'externally validates' conflates population transportability with instrument transportability, and no corpus study separates the two - P-824, the corpus's other survey-cohort model (CHARLS-developed, validated in CLHLS and RuLAS with different outcome instruments), is the opposite configuration and also does not decompose instrument from population transportability, so neither the shared-instrument nor the changed-instrument validation isolates the measurement axis.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard domain-shift/measurement-vulnerability pattern (vendor devices in OCT; language families in speech) transposed to the validation-design axis: the shift at issue is in the measurement instruments themselves, and the corpus's own 'external validation' practice is shown by its own worked example to be blind to it. It is non-obvious because 'externally validated on HRS' reads as strong evidence in this literature; the gap only becomes visible when the validation's instrument inventory is compared against the training cohort's. The record is scoped to a named, quotable worked example rather than a corpus-wide universal negative.
gaps.closure_criteria: A validation-decomposition study: fit the survey-variable model on CHARLS (or comparable), then validate on one cohort sharing the instruments (HRS-style) and one cohort with clinically adjudicated MCI and instrumented exposures (spirometry or biomarkers), reporting AUROC in each and the delta attributable to instrument change versus population change (e.g. by also running the adjudicated-outcome cohort with self-report-only features). Closure requires the instrument-vs-population decomposition, not a single new validation cohort.
gaps.modality: Clinical/Population (survey cohorts) + Molecular/Fluid or Clinical instruments as comparator
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold-standard domain-shift/measurement-vulnerability pattern (vendor devices in OCT; language families in speech) transposed to the validation-design axis: the shift at issue is in the measurement instruments themselves, and the corpus's own 'external validation' practice is shown by its own worked example to be blind to it. It is non-obvious because 'externally validated on HRS' reads as strong evidence in this literature; the gap only becomes visible when the validation's instrument inventory is compared against the training cohort's. The record is scoped to a named, quotable worked example rather than a corpus-wide universal negative.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection: P-893's shared-method statement is the digest's own appraisal vocabulary rather than a paper-declared limitation in those words, so an operator could rule the record's sharpest sentence an interpreter's framing (EVIDENTIAL_OVERSTATEMENT adjacent) even though the underlying facts (same self-report exposure, same screening-based outcome) are printed. Secondary: epidemiological methods literature on transportability may already formalise the population-versus-instrument decomposition (EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE risk for the generic method); the corpus-scoped framing confines the claim to what MCI survey-cohort modelling has done.

gaps.gap_statement: Novel brief MCI screening channels (oculomotor measures, binocular near-point of convergence, brief visuo-construction tests) are proposed in the corpus with at most one partial head-to-head benchmark against the standard cognitive screens they claim to improve on - P-1006 (GARD, 679 participants) reports paired AUROCs of 0.752 for demographics plus eye movements against 0.767 for demographics plus MMSE and 0.840 combined, without confidence intervals, a decision-analytic contrast or a prognostic subset - and otherwise without one: P-988's own limitation field states there was 'no head-to-head accuracy comparison with standard cognitive screens'; P-998 evaluates receded near point of convergence against an MMSE-derived label without comparing NPC against MMSE-based screening as a test; and the one corpus paper that did run the head-to-head (P-991, three brief tests including a language-independent MMSE alternative, n=622 memory-clinic participants) found none of the three reliably discriminated all four groups or predicted progression (VVT: sensitivity 62.1% / specificity 83.1% for AD vs rest; 'no test predicted progression adequately') - a ceiling result that makes the absence of head-to-head evidence for the newer channels consequential rather than academic. The corpus therefore cannot answer which brief channel, if any, a clinic should adopt in place of MMSE/MoCA, and its own one rigorous comparison suggests the ceiling is low.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard clinical-utility pattern transposed to test adoption: channels are proposed and threshold-evaluated in isolation while the decision (which test to administer) requires the paired comparison that the corpus's own papers name as missing, and the corpus's one rigorous comparison quantifies a ceiling that makes the newer channels' isolation-nested claims uninterpretable. It is non-obvious because P-998 superficially looks like an MMSE comparison (MMSE supplies its label), and the gap only becomes clear once the label-vs-comparator distinction is drawn; the record credits P-991 explicitly so the absence cannot be read as 'no head-to-head evidence exists at all'.
gaps.closure_criteria: One memory-clinic or community cohort (>=300 participants across MCI and controls, one reference-standard adjudication) administering the novel channel (e.g. NPC or saccadic measure) AND a standard screen (MMSE or MoCA) to the same participants, reporting paired accuracies (AUC with CI, sensitivity/specificity at pre-specified thresholds), decision-analytic contrast (net benefit or misclassification cost ratio), and, in a subset with follow-up, both tests' prognostic value for progression. Closure requires the paired design; separate single-channel accuracy studies do not close it.
gaps.modality: Behavioural/digital (oculomotor, binocular vision, brief cognitive instruments)
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold-standard clinical-utility pattern transposed to test adoption: channels are proposed and threshold-evaluated in isolation while the decision (which test to administer) requires the paired comparison that the corpus's own papers name as missing, and the corpus's one rigorous comparison quantifies a ceiling that makes the newer channels' isolation-nested claims uninterpretable. It is non-obvious because P-998 superficially looks like an MMSE comparison (MMSE supplies its label), and the gap only becomes clear once the label-vs-comparator distinction is drawn; the record credits P-991 explicitly so the absence cannot be read as 'no head-to-head evidence exists at all'.
gaps.critic_falsification: The strongest objection: an operator may hold that P-991's ceiling is specific to its three tests and its Vienna memory-clinic distribution, so the absence of head-to-head evidence for other channels could reflect rational triage rather than neglect - a field may reasonably decline to benchmark a channel whose signal size (P-998's NPC threshold, P-988's unquantified marker) is plainly below the incumbent. The rebuttal inside the record is that P-988's own limitation field names the missing comparison as a limitation, i.e. the field itself treats it as owed, not as triaged-away. Secondary: P-988 and P-991 are clinical-outcome-adjudicated single sites, so the ceiling value itself may not generalise (EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE risk is low for the comparative-design absence but real for the ceiling's magnitude).

The corpus therefore cannot answer which brief channel, if any, a clinic should adopt in place of MMSE/MoCA, and its own one rigorous comparison suggests the ceiling is low.

gaps.gap_statement: The frontier's chronic-disease MCI screening nomogram family (CKD P-1078, T2DM P-1085/P-1212, memory-clinic P-1118, outpatient conversion P-1155) derives absolute-risk tools in samples whose MCI proportion is 50-61 percent - or an artificially exact 49/49 balance in P-1155 - and reports calibration and decision-curve net benefit only at that derivation case-mix, while framing the tools as early-screening instruments for deployment settings where the corpus's own community data (P-1108, CLHLS) put the 3-year MCI rate at 14-16 percent. No paper in the family recalibrates its intercept/baseline risk to a deployment prevalence or re-computes decision-curve net benefit there. Because a nomogram outputs an absolute probability and net benefit is prevalence-dependent by construction, the family's absolute-risk outputs would be expected to overpredict by up to roughly 3-4-fold in the claimed screening populations (the derivation-to-deployment prevalence ratio; P-1155's nomogram is calibrated to an artificial 50 percent prevalence by construction) - but the actual inflation magnitude is unmeasured, which is exactly the absence: no family member reports calibration-in-the-large, observed-to-expected ratio, or net benefit at deployment prevalence. A same-case-mix external validation would not close this; the missing evaluation is the prevalence-transported one.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches two gold patterns at once: a calibration/transfer failure across setting (gold: 'a calibration or transfer failure across language, education, device or setting') and a clinical-utility failure (net benefit claimed where it was never evaluated). It is non-obvious because every paper in the family individually reports 'good calibration and net benefit' - the defect is invisible per-paper and only appears when the derivation prevalences (50-61 percent, or artificial 49/49) are set against the corpus's own measured community rate (14-16 percent, P-1108). The mechanism is deterministic, not speculative: absolute risk and DCA net benefit are prevalence-dependent by construction.

gaps.dedup_note: Checked against the full existing-gaps list and the T15 theme file. G-14 (open) covers calibration under domain shift but enumerates its axes as cross-scanner, cross-site, cross-modality dropout - case-mix/prevalence shift is not among them, and these clinical/tabular nomograms involve no scanner at all. NEW-G-23 asks for ECE/reliability-diagram reporting; this family DOES report in-distribution calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow, calibration curves), so NEW-G-23 does not capture the absence - the missing piece is recalibration and net-benefit evaluation at deployment prevalence. ACTOR-G-015 (sex/ancestry calibration loss) and ACTOR-G-029 (assay-platform calibration loss) are different shift axes. ACTOR-G-038 (reverse causation of cross-sectional SHAP importances) and ACTOR-G-033 (label operationalisation) critique features and labels, not absolute-risk transportability. The rejected G-CAND single-paper 'no external validation' limitations (e.g. G-CAND-33, G-CAND-207) are not this gap: an external validation in another 50-percent-prevalence clinic would satisfy them and still leave this absence open.

gaps.gap_statement: Claims-based MCI burden and progression estimates are published as policy-facing numbers with no validation of the administrative phenotype against clinical assessment and no propagation of measured code-validity error into the estimates - even though the corpus now contains a direct measurement (P-816) showing that ICD-code-only MCI/ADRD phenotyping discriminates barely above chance (AUROC 0.54, medications-only 0.56, against a chart-review reference standard, free text alone 0.94). P-1015's headline outputs (30.9% three-year MCI-to-AD conversion; cost trajectories offered for budget forecasting and long-term-care capacity planning) rest on an administrative phenotype the paper itself concedes is unvalidated, ascertainment-biased and contaminated (about 20% of 'new-onset MCI' already carried an AD diagnosis at or before MCI onset), and its year-one conversion rate (15.0%) sits at the top of the 3-15% annual range its own literature review reports - a rate consistent with, though not demonstrative of, ascertainment-shifted case capture. No claims-based MCI burden or progression study in the corpus validates its phenotype in a subsample or applies quantitative misclassification bias analysis, and the transport of P-816's measured near-chance validity from US academic EHR coding to Japanese claims coding is itself untested; the misclassification magnitude is therefore measured in one setting and propagated nowhere, so unpropagated phenotype error could dominate the very numbers health systems are being invited to plan with.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard 'temporal or ground-truth assumption' family (prognostic models treating an unvalidated standard as ground truth) and the NEW-G-23 calibration pattern (a measured deficiency that no one carries into their reported numbers). Non-obvious because the two legs live in different corpus themes - an EHR-methods paper and a health-economics claims paper - and the connection (the corpus has already measured the magnitude of the error that the burden literature leaves unpropagated) only appears when they are read together. The universal-negative clause survives its own citations: P-816 measures validity but is not a burden/progression study and propagates nothing; P-1015 declares the validation open in its own text.
gaps.closure_criteria: A claims-based MCI burden or progression study (N >= 1,000 new-onset MCI cases) that either (a) validates its claims phenotype against clinical assessment or chart review in a random subsample of n >= 100, reporting sensitivity, specificity and PPV of the code definition, or (b) applies quantitative probabilistic bias analysis using an externally measured validity coefficient - and in either case republishes its conversion probabilities and expenditure estimates as bias-adjusted ranges alongside the naive estimates, with competing-mortality adjustment.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold-standard 'temporal or ground-truth assumption' family (prognostic models treating an unvalidated standard as ground truth) and the NEW-G-23 calibration pattern (a measured deficiency that no one carries into their reported numbers). Non-obvious because the two legs live in different corpus themes - an EHR-methods paper and a health-economics claims paper - and the connection (the corpus has already measured the magnitude of the error that the burden literature leaves unpropagated) only appears when they are read together. The universal-negative clause survives its own citations: P-816 measures validity but is not a burden/progression study and propagates nothing; P-1015 declares the validation open in its own text.
gaps.critic_falsification: The transport step is the weak joint: P-816's AUROC 0.54 is measured for US EHR ICD codes against chart-documented diagnosis at two Boston academic hospitals, while P-1015's phenotype is Japanese medical plus long-term-care claims, where LTC insurance certification gives coding a different incentive structure - so the measured near-chance validity may not transfer, and an operator could rule that using it as the record's anchor is itself an inferential bridge. Separately, validation studies of dementia claims codes (PPV studies) exist in the external literature, and an operator may judge the record close enough to ACTOR-G-017 to merge rather than confirm as a new gap.

gaps.gap_statement: The MCI care-delivery literature in this corpus documents defective care processes in three independent national settings - patients unable to name their own diagnosis (Ireland: 21% used the term MCI, 25% attributed problems to a pathological cause, 60% said causes were not discussed), specialists absorbing referral inflow without accepting coordination responsibility (US: 92% receive ongoing-management referrals, 46% see themselves as coordinator), and non-uniform diagnosis and treatment across centres (Italy: 121 neurologists, 203 patients) - yet no corpus study, and none the corpus evidences in the MCI population, links any measured care-process variable to any patient or carer outcome, and all three papers concede exactly this in their own open-problem fields. The absence matters because the literature issues normative conclusions ('suboptimal and inconsistent MCI management') and improvement agendas (disclosure protocols, coordination roles, standardised national guidance) with no evidence about which process deficits actually change prognosis, function, wellbeing or carer burden - an empirically unanchored quality agenda at the moment disease-modifying therapy makes the MCI care pathway consequential. Caveat carried: dementia-population care-coordination trials exist outside the corpus and may be argued to cover the coordination leg by transfer; the MCI-specific disclosure-comprehension and practice-concordance legs are the defensible core.
gaps.evidence_for_open_status: Matches the gold-standard 'clinical-utility failure' family (a quantity is measured and acted on rhetorically while its decision/outcome impact is never tested - the XAI gold gap has this exact shape) and spans three papers from three countries and three professional vantage points (patients/carers, specialist physicians, centre-level practice), each independently conceding the same missing link in its own text. Non-obvious because each paper reads as a complete descriptive study on its own; the shared blind spot - a whole health-services literature issuing improvement agendas with no outcome anchor - only appears at pack level.
gaps.closure_criteria: A multi-centre longitudinal study (>= 2 centres, >= 200 MCI patients, >= 2 years follow-up) that measures a defined care-process exposure at baseline - disclosure comprehension (e.g. patient ability to name and causally attribute the diagnosis), presence of a named care coordinator, or centre-level guideline concordance - and tests its association with pre-specified outcomes (time to dementia diagnosis, functional decline, patient wellbeing, carer Zarit burden), adjusted for baseline severity; or a cluster-randomised trial of a standardised disclosure or coordination protocol with the same endpoints.
gaps.actor_justification: Matches the gold-standard 'clinical-utility failure' family (a quantity is measured and acted on rhetorically while its decision/outcome impact is never tested - the XAI gold gap has this exact shape) and spans three papers from three countries and three professional vantage points (patients/carers, specialist physicians, centre-level practice), each independently conceding the same missing link in its own text. Non-obvious because each paper reads as a complete descriptive study on its own; the shared blind spot - a whole health-services literature issuing improvement agendas with no outcome anchor - only appears at pack level.
gaps.critic_falsification: EXISTS_IN_EXTERNAL_LITERATURE is the live threat: dementia care-coordination trials with patient outcomes exist outside the corpus (collaborative-care and care-navigator RCTs in dementia populations), and if an operator judges those transferable to MCI the coordination leg collapses to a corpus-sampling artifact; the record survives only if MCI-specific process-to-outcome linkage (disclosure comprehension and practice concordance especially) is genuinely absent externally, which was not verifiable here. Secondarily, G-NEW-1064-A's statement text is empty in the corpus gap list, so a merge rather than a new record may be the right disposition.

Single-paper limitation (lint soft-flag): three independent papers, three countries, each conceding the absence in its own limitations/open-problems fields.

gaps.original_claim_before_narrowing: The MCI care-delivery literature in this pack documents defective care processes in three independent national settings - patients unable to name their own diagnosis (Ireland: 21% used the term MCI, 60% said causes were not discussed), specialists absorbing referral inflow without accepting coordination responsibility (US: 92% receive ongoing-management referrals, 46% see themselves as coordinator), and non-uniform diagnosis and treatment across centres (Italy: 121 neurologists, 203 patients) - yet no study links any measured care-process variable to any patient or carer outcome, and all three papers concede exactly this in their own text. The absence matters because the field is issuing normative conclusions ('suboptimal and inconsistent MCI management') and improvement agendas (disclosure protocols, coordination roles, standardised national guidance) with no evidence about which process deficits actually change prognosis, function, wellbeing or carer burden - an unfalsifiable quality agenda at the moment disease-modifying therapy makes the MCI care pathway consequential.
